23438 Finance Officer (Migrant Protection, Return and Reintegration Programme for Sub-Saharan Africa (MPRR-SSA))
jobs.description:
Under the overall supervision of the Deputy Regional Director – Management (DRD-M) in Dakar, and the direct supervision of the Project Finance and Budget Officer – Migrant Protection, Return and Reintegration Programme for Sub-Saharan Africa (MPRR-SSA) in close coordination with the Senior Regional Programme Coordinator (MPRR-SSA), the Finance Officer (MPRR-SSA) will assist the Project Finance and Budget Officer (MPRR-SSA) in the programmes budget, accounts, and financial reports of all the implementing Country Offices (COs), provide support to the programmatic unit of the MPRR-SSA team in the areas of financial monitoring and reporting. The Finance Officer (MPRR-SSA) will work closely with the European Commission Compliance Unit in IOM Global Office Brussels, Regional Office, as well as central units at Headquarters (HQ).

The MPRR-SSA is an EU-funded programme that is implemented in 16 countries of sub-Saharan Africa, including Burkina Faso, Côte d’Ivoire, Cameroon, Chad, Ethiopia, Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Mali, Mauritania, Niger, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, Senegal, Somalia, and Sudan.

**Responsibilities**

1. Assist the Project Finance and Budget Officer (MPRR-SSA) to monitor and oversee the financial management of all activities, including oversight of financial expenditure and accountability, and undertake financial analysis of all activities in the offices implementing the MPRR-SSA programme.
2. Assist the Project Finance and Budget Officer (MPRR-SSA) to oversee and coordinate the preparation and review of EU financial reports in accordance with IOM regulations and EU regulations and established procedures.
3. In coordination with the Senior Regional Programme Coordinator (MPRR-SSA), Project Managers, the Regional Office (RO) Coordination Unit, Global Office Brussels, and Resources Management Officers (RMOs), prepare budget reports, proposals, and revisions in the Project Information and Management Application (PRIMA).
4. Contribute to the budget control process and analyse variances between the budget and actual expenditures for MPRR-SSA projects.
5. Contribute to the creation of draft general instructions and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to ensure compliance with the general instructions of IOM and relevant permanent instructions in the areas of general administration, finance, Supply Chain, Information and Communications Technology (ICT), and Human Resources (HR).
6. Contribute to the capacity building initiatives to train local staff on EU and IOM’s administrative/financial policies and procedures.
7. As assigned by the Project Finance and Budget Officer (MPRR-SSA), undertake travel to offices in view to building financial management capacity of administrative and finance staff in the field.
8. Provide support to the Project Finance and Budget Officer (MPRR-SSA) in facilitating the financial audit of the MPRR-SSA programme in accordance with the donor agreements.
9. Assess monthly financial reports and advise on resolving anomalies and unusual trends.
10. Provide advice and guidance to Country Offices (COs) in the Region with management of implementing Partners (IP) under the MPRR-SSA programme.
11. Contribute to ensure compliance with all administrative and financial rules, instructions, regulations, and procedures related to the EU-funded project(s).
12. In coordination with the Project Finance and Budget Officer (MPRR-SSA) and upon approval of the Regional Financial Comptroller, undertake duty travel to the CO to increase capacity building in financial reporting in relation to assigned projects.
13. Perform other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, Auditing, or related fields from an accredited academic institution with two years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with four years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Experience in accounting, financial management and reporting;
- Experience in preparing clear and concise financial and management reports;
- Experience working in and with international institutions;
- Experience with internal control assessment, internal or external audit;
- Previous work experience in the region is an advantage;
- Previous working experience in emergency operations is an advantage; and,
- Experience with EU budgeting rules is mandatory.

**Skills**

- Knowledge of International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS);
- Knowledge of the IOM/UN accounting system, software, and procedures, Common System regulations, policies, and procedures is a distinct advantage;
- Familiarity with financial oversight and public administration is an advantage; and,
- Knowledge of MS Office products and good computer literacy skills are required.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English and French is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

jobs.title: Global Finance and Compliance Business Partner
jobs.description:
**Location:** United Kingdom (preferred), or other approved locations where HelpAge International is legally able to employ staff (Ethiopia, Italy, Jordan, Kenya, Spain, Tanzania, Türkiye and Zimbabwe)

**Department:** Business Support Team

**Reports to (Line Manager):** Director of Finance & Business Support

**Responsible for (Line managing):** N/A

**Grade:** E- [https://helpage.sharepoint.com/:x:/r/sites/external/HR/Global%20Finance%20%26%20Comp%20BP-Grade%20E%20Salary%20Ranges.xlsx?d=w430eb70dde154b1ea879aac96f47c68f&csf=1&web=1&e=IgX0R7](https://helpage.sharepoint.com/:x:/r/sites/external/HR/Global%20Finance%20%26%20Comp%20BP-Grade%20E%20Salary%20Ranges.xlsx?d=w430eb70dde154b1ea879aac96f47c68f&csf=1&web=1&e=IgX0R7)

**Contract Type:** Open ended

**About HelpAge**

HelpAge International works with a diverse global network of around 200 organisations across 99 countries to promote the rights of older people to lead dignified, healthy and secure lives.

Through partnership and collaborations, we work to ensure the inclusion of older people across society and strive to deliver a just and fair world for everyone as they get older. Our work is driven by our desire to achieve real impact for older people, to be inclusive, to work in partnership and to learn from our shared experience.

## **About the Job**

The Global Finance & Compliance Business Partner provides high-quality financial business partnering support and oversight to assigned programmes and organisational initiatives.

The role supports managers in ensuring compliance to policy in areas of budgeting, proposal development, donor compliance, and financial reporting. The post holder will help colleagues make informed financial decisions while ensuring compliance with organisational, donor, and regulatory requirements.

The role also lead the internal audit planning and implementation, compliance, and assurance activities across corporate and partner financial reporting.

## Key areas for impact/influence and responsibilities

**Financial Business Partnering**

- Build strong relationships with budget holders and managers, providing proactive financial advice, support and oversight.
- Support managers in understanding financial compliance and managing risks.
- Contribute to financial decision-making through analysis, insight and challenge.

**Budgeting, Forecasting and Financial Planning**

- Support the preparation of programme budgets, and financial plans with a view to ensuring compliance with policy.
- Monitor expenditure against approved budgets and provide timely feedback on variances, risks and mitigation
- Contribute to organisational financial planning processes and reporting cycles.
- Support grant managers and programme teams in understanding donor rules and compliance requirements.
- Monitor and advise on cost recovery, co-funding requirements, and financial risks associated with grants.

**Partner Financial Management**

- Support financial oversight of implementing partners in line with HelpAge’s partner-led approach.
- Review partner financial reports and supporting documentation.
- Support partner financial assessments, capacity strengthening initiatives, and compliance reviews.
- Audit selected partner organisations in line with agreed audit plan

**Compliance and Audit**

- Analyse monthly management information prepared for senior management and provide audit and assurance on them
- Support the design of relevant financial reports, dashboards and performance reports needed to manage performance and risk.
- Support the annual external audit preparation and process.
- Develop and propose an annual internal audit plan for review and approval by the Audit & Risk Committee, ensuring appropriate oversight and safeguards to maintain the independence of internal audit activities.
- Develop and maintain Internal Audit Procedures to ensure best practice and that the audits address specific areas of identified risk withing corporate accounts and programmes/partners activities
- Coordinate and implement the approved internal audit plan in accordance with established procedures and appropriate independence safeguards. At the conclusion of each audit, communicate findings to Director of Finance and Business Support Department or partner organisation, document management responses and agree corrective action plans.
- Monitor and report on the implementation of any recommendations;

Skills and experience required

**Essential**

- Professional accounting qualification or equivalent audit certification and experience.
- Significant experience in financial management, budgeting and financial reporting.
- Experience working within an NGO, charity or similar organisation.
- Strong understanding of donor-funded programmes and donor compliance requirements.
- Experience in financial audit, compliance, and investigation.
- Good communication, stakeholder management, and relationship-building skills.
- Strong Excel and financial systems skills.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities and work collaboratively across teams.

**Desirable**

- Experience supporting partner-led programming and partner financial management.
- Experience preparing donor budgets and donor financial reports.
- Knowledge of UK charity finance requirements.
- Knowledge of Charity SORP and auditing standards
- Experience using MS Business Dynamics or similar accounting systems.
- Experience supporting finance process improvements and risk management.

## Key Behavioural Competencies

Working Collaboratively with Others: Work collaboratively, building mutual trust and respect, with external organizations and partners to achieve our strategic aims and objectives; being accountable for the work we do together.

Adaptability and Flexibility: Adapt to new directions or opportunities arising within the organisation and in our work area; being flexible in our role, constantly using the feedback to learn more and evolve further.

Supporting and Facilitating Change: Lead behavioural and cultural change through embracing a supportive, collaborative and highly inclusive environment where everybody feels supported, respected and engaged.

Extend HelpAge’s Reach and Impact: Extend HelpAge’s reach and impact by creating and identifying new business development opportunities and building relationships with new partners.

Diversity and Inclusion: Lead and promote a culture of including the voices of older people across our support, convening and thought leadership roles, in a way that is transformative, empowering and highly inclusive of those marginalised by gender, economic status, disability and other factors of discrimination.

Leading Others (for managers): Demonstrate strong leadership to own unit/department and manage people in a well and reputable manner. Create an atmosphere of trust and an enabling environment where staff can contribute their best and develop their potential.

**Policies and Code of Conduct**

As a HelpAge International employee, you are expected to comply with all organisational policies and standards, and to conduct yourself in a manner consistent with our values at all times.

This includes, but is not limited to:

- Code of Conduct
- Safeguarding Policy and Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA)
- Anti-Fraud and Bribery Policy
- Anti-Bullying, Harassment and Sexual Harassment Policy
- Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Policy
- Raising a Concern (Whistleblowing) Policy
- Social Media Policy

All staff are required to familiarise themselves with these policies, complete any mandatory training, and adhere to them throughout their employment with HelpAge International.

**Safeguarding**

HelpAge International is committed to safeguarding the communities with which we work, our partners, staff and any others who we come into contact with. The post holder will also be responsible for:

- Preventing harm and abuse from our people, operations and programmes to anyone that encounters our work.
- Reporting all safeguarding incidents you see, hear, hear about or suspect, using our internal reporting mechanism.
- Complying with all safeguarding framework policies and practices.
- Completing mandatory training courses relating to our safeguarding policy framework and complying with HR vetting procedures.

**SAFER RECRUITMENT**

All employments at HelpAge International will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate screening checks, which can include misconduct disclosure schemes and terrorism finance checks.

jobs.title: MOZAMBIQUE - DEPUTY COUNTRY DIRECTOR FOR PROGRAMS (M/F) - CABO DELGADO
jobs.description:
## ABOUT US

**Desired start date: ASAP**
**Duration of the mission: 6 months**
**Location: CABO DELGADO**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## ABOUT THE MISSION

Solidarités International (SI) has been providing life-saving assistance in northern Mozambique since March 2019, initially responding to Cyclone Idai. As the crisis in Cabo Delgado escalated, SI began operations in Mueda in July 2021 and progressively expanded to other northern districts including Nangade, Muidumbe, Palma and, more recently, Mocímboa da Praia. By 2022, SI had established a coordination office in Pemba and operational bases in Mueda and Palma.

Following the closure of the Palma base, SI opened a new base in Mocímboa da Praia in July 2023 to support urgent returnee needs. Today, SI operates from Pemba, Mueda and Mocímboa da Praia, covering not only the northern districts (Mueda, Mocímboa da Praia, Nangade, Muidumbe and Palma) but also additional districts further south, such as Metuge, Chiúre, Mecúfi and Ancuabe.

At the beginning of 2025, major BHA funding cuts forced a significant restructuring, reducing the mission from approximately 140 to around 50 staff and prompting a reorganisation of operations to maintain essential activities. This restructuring coincided with a deterioration of the security situation in Cabo Delgado, with renewed attacks, increased displacement and unpredictable access since mid-2024.

In early 2026, the mission entered a new phase with the confirmation of significant short-term emergency funding, alongside the launch of a major 3-year development-oriented WASH/FSL/Education project in Consortium. This shift requires strengthened programmatic oversight to manage simultaneous emergency and longer-term interventions within a rapidly evolving operational context.

Despite these challenges, SI continues to deliver principled, needs-based assistance across Cabo Delgado with the support of key donors such as ECHO, SDC, CDCS, IFSAN, UNICEF and WFP.

Projects and activities include:

\- Rapid Response Mechanism to shocks (conflict, natural disasters, epidemics): multisectoral WASH / Food / Shelter-NFI assistance through CVA or in-kind distributions

\- WASH: rehabilitation of large water networks, water points construction/rehabilitation, WASH in schools and health facilities, rainwater harvesting systems, sanitation and hygiene promotion

\- FSL: seeds and equipment distributions, support to cooperatives, cash-for-work and income-generating activities

\- Shelter/NFI: mainly emergency shelter and NFI through RRM

Around 50 staff in total across the mission in April 2026, but it will increase in May/June with the new funding.

SI operates 3 bases:

• Pemba (Coordination / Operational Base): 27 staff

• Mueda (Operational Base): 19 staff

• Mocímboa da Praia (Operational Sub-base): 4 staff

• Chiure (Operational Sub-base) to be opened: 6 staff

The DCDP is based in Pemba and covers operations in all bases of SI in Mozambique.

## ABOUT THE JOB

**GENERAL OBJECTIVE:**

The Deputy CD for Programs (DCDP) is responsible for the overall supervision, quality and strategic orientation of Solidarités International programmatic operations and MEAL systems in Cabo Delgado. S/he ensures effective, high-quality and compliant implementation of programmes in line with SI strategy and donor requirements. S/he supervises Program Managers and the MEAL Manager, supports adaptive programming, and works closely with the Area Coordinator and field teams to strengthen coordination, accountability and operational continuity.

**THE MAIN CHALLENGES:**

1- Major mission restructuring following BHA funding cuts in early 2025, with reduced staffing and evolving organisational set-up, followed by a rapid increase of funding in 2026, including short-term emergency grants and a multi-year development project
2- Short implementation timelines for emergency projects (6 months) requiring strong planning, monitoring and adaptive management
3- Volatile and unpredictable security context requiring continuous analysis and flexible programming
4- Multi-base programme (Pemba, Mueda, Mocímboa da Praia, Chiure) with limited resources and high coordination needs
5- High workload linked to simultaneous project closures, scale-up of emergency response and launch of new projects
6- Strengthening and maintaining relationships with local authorities and coordination bodies in a sensitive operational environment

**PRIORITIES FOR THE 2/3 FIRST MONTHS:**

1- Ensure structured supervision of ongoing programmes across all bases and also the suppervision of the technicall departments (WASH, FSL, RRM Co, and MEAL)
2- Strengthen MEAL systems and ensure effective use of monitoring data and accountability mechanisms for programmatic decision-making
3- Ensure quality closure of ending projects and structured launch of new projects (Apri-May 2026)
4- Reinforce program compliance with donor requirements and internal procedures
5- Clarify roles, workflows and coordination mechanisms between Program, MEAL and Support departments
6- Lead and coordinate proposal development with Project Managers, Technical Coordinators and the Grants Department
7- Strengthen representation and collaboration with provincial and district authorities, clusters and key partners

**SECURITY CONSTRAINTS:**

Security level 2 in Pemba with limited constraints.

Mueda and Mocímboa da Praia are security level 3, with more restrictions. Movements and activities depend on local conditions and Security Department guidance.

The security situation remains volatile, with unpredictable insurgent attacks and evolving dynamics involving armed actors. Close monitoring of the context is required for daily movement validation. Travel to field bases is mainly via UNHAS flights.

## YOUR PROFILE

**DIPLOMA AND EXPERIENCE:**

Diploma : Master in humanitarian action, development, international law or any other technical area related to the humanitarian sector

Experience in the humanitarian sector : 3/4 years

Experience on a similar position : 3/4 years

**SKILLS:**

TECHNICAL SKILLS

1. Strong Project Cycle Management skills
2. Solid background or experience in at least one technical
3. Strong understanding of MEAL systems and accountability mechanisms, with ability to ensure effective use of monitoring data for programmatic decision-making
4. Good knowledge of donor compliance and reporting requirements

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS

1. Strong information management capacity and ability to coordinate multiple activities across bases
2. Strong planning, prioritisation and organisational skills
3. Ability to represent SI with authorities, partners and coordination bodies
4. Strong analytical capacity and ability to adapt programming to evolving contexts
5. Capacity to supervise and structure teams in a complex operational environment

**LANGUAGE:**

1. English (mandatory)
2. Portuguese (strong asset)
3. Spanish or Italian (asset)

## SI WILL OFFER YOU...

**A salaried position:**
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 3300 gross per month (3000 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 750.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

Pemba is a coastal city with good living conditions for expatriates, including stable water and electricity and reliable 4G internet. There is no curfew, and walking is allowed during the day. SI provides comfortable office and guesthouse facilities close to amenities.

The position is based in Pemba, with frequent visits to the bases. Field bases are reachable by UNHAS flight in less than one hour. Living conditions in field locations are basic but functional.

jobs.title: Programme Coordinator - PALESTINE (H/F/X)
jobs.description:
**Working environment:**

The French Red Cross (FRC) has been present in Palestine since November 2022, based in Ramallah and working in close partnership with the Palestine Red Crescent Society (PRCS). Initially established to implement a five-year AFD-funded project supporting the institutional and pedagogical development of Ibn Sina College of Health Professions in Nablus, the Delegation has progressively expanded its portfolio to support PRCS across key health and humanitarian priorities.

The Delegation currently combines longer-term institutional and capacity-strengthening programmes with support to PRCS's response to the evolving humanitarian context, particularly in emergency medical services, first aid, rehabilitation and disability inclusion, and health education. This includes support to PRCS through CDCS-funded EMS/First Aid programmes, rehabilitation activities, and the continued implementation of the AFD-funded Ibn Sina College project. The overall approach is centred on capacity building, technical expertise, knowledge transfer and institutional strengthening, increasingly through delegated implementation by PRCS while maintaining FRC technical, programme, financial and donor oversight.

The programme portfolio is implemented in a highly volatile operational environment, characterised by severe humanitarian needs in Gaza, increasing access and protection constraints in the West Bank, and significant pressures on Palestinian health and emergency-response systems. The Delegation therefore needs to balance longer-term development and capacity-strengthening objectives with the ability to adapt programmes to rapidly changing humanitarian and operational priorities.

**Position**

For a Programme Coordinator position, the role sits at the centre of this portfolio: ensuring strategic coherence across programmes, supporting and overseeing PRCS-led implementation, maintaining strong donor and partner relations, ensuring smooth and proactive coordination between programme and support teams through all steps of the project cycle, supporting positive team coordination including through the supervision of the Project Manager, identifying opportunities for programme development and funding, and ensuring that FRC's support remains relevant, technically sound and adaptable to the changing Palestinian context.

**MISSIONS AND ACTIVITIES**

Reporting to the Head of Delegation, the Programme Coordinator will :

- contribute to the development and implementation of the operational strategy of the Delegation,
- ensure the monitoring and steering of the implementation and development of programmes,
- and contribute to the representation of the Delegation to partners, humanitarian coordination bodies and other relevant stakeholders.

1. Lead on all aspects of programmatic design and projects implementation (working closely with all relevant technical experts and counterparts as well as in constant coordination with PRCS), and actively contribute to the strategic & operational positioning and development of the Delegation in support of the Head of Delegation.
2. Coordinate the development and writing of new quality Project Proposals and Concept Notes, in coordination with the Palestine Red Crescent Society (PRCS) and in line with the Delegation's annual operational programming validated by the FRC.
3. Support the programme team in the planning, implementation, monitoring, evaluation and quality and timely narrative and financial reporting of projects, in line with FRC's international strategy and MEAL obligations (processes and tools) in the country of intervention.
4. Contribute to the representation of the FRC and the development of partnerships in support of the Head of Delegation.
5. Ensure good coordination and support of project and programme teams for quality project management.
6. Contribute to good partnership relations and the capacity building of the PRCS, as well as to any further support activities that the position may require.

**Reporting relationship**: Head of Delegation

**Managing and Operational links :**

- The incumbent will manage the FRC Delegation’s technical programme/project in the field of health, in coordination with partners, Health and NSD Logistics regional experts, and under the supervision of technical advisors from HQ. At the time of posting, the FRC Delegation is considering ad hoc technical staff support rather than long term in-country technical programme teams. The development of projects and portfolio through the Programme Coordination position will impact the Delegation organigram.
- The incumbent will be the direct line manager of a national Project Manager, focused on the AFD project (see context section above)

**Collaborates internally with :**

- All the delegation & FRC HQ support services (Desk, Finance, Logistics, MEAL, Technical departments, Compliance & Audit, Security Management, etc.)

**Collaborates externally with :**

- PRCS counterparts and management team
- Ibn Sina College Project Manager
- AFD Project Manager
- Counterparts and colleagues within the Red Cross Red Crescent Movement
- Technical experts and consultants supporting project development and implementation

**Profile**

**1/ Qualifications and experience**

***Experience :***

- At least five (5) years’ experience in the same type of position - **mandatory**
- Previous experience in programme coordination positions - **mandatory**
- Previous experience in supervising staff and supporting their professional and technical development -
- Experience and/or knowledge in communicating with various partners and donors - **mandatory**
- Experience in developing new projects (concept note, proposal, budget, logframe, etc) - **mandatory**
- Experience in donor reporting and contract management - **mandatory**
- Experience working with local partners and partner-implemented projects / programmes - **mandatory**
- Experience working with the Red Cross Red Crescent Movement - **mandatory**
- Previous experience managing projects with AFD and CDCS is a strong asset
- Experience in the MENA region and specifically in Palestinian context is a strong asset
- Background in health or in health projects (including emergency medical services, nurse sciences, pre-hospital care, first aid, etc.) is a strong asset

***Education*** :

- Studies in humanitarian or development studies, or any equivalent field
- Mastery of the project cycle and project management tools
- Knowledge of the different humanitarian sectors
- Mastery of the humanitarian coordination system
- Knowledge of the main donors and rules

**2/ Competencies**

Mandatory job requirements

- Organisational capacity
- Coordination capacity
- Strong writing and synthesis skills (for both proposals and reporting contributions)
- Effective capacity in grant management
- Effective capacity in MEAL procedures and processes
- Strong communication and diplomatic skills in multicultural work environments
- Teamwork skills (active listening, proactivity and consensus building)
- Experience in team management
- Initiative and ability to work efficiently and effectively without close supervision

Valued skills

- Proficiency in Office (Word, Excel, Powerpoint), networking (Google-Suite/Google Workspace)
- Expertise in identifying and implementing jointly capacity-improvement plans
- Experience facilitating trainings and accompanying staff to strengthen their expertise
- In-depth knowledge of the Red Cross Red Crescent Movement’s National Society Development approaches, especially through a Programme Coordination and Development lens

Skills related to the specific environment of the mission:

- Flexibility and quick adaptability
- Restraint, patience and diplomacy in institutional relations
- Ability to work within a coordination team and in functional link with the project and field teams
- Ability to work with a multicultural team
- Resilience to stress and high workload
- **International driving licence mandatory**

Languages

- English and French mandatory (oral and written); Arabic would be an asset.

**Conditions of employment:**

- Type of status: expatriate
- Type of contract: Fixed-term contract under French law
- Salary: According to the classification of the position on the CRf grid and the experience of the candidate
- Per diem: daily per diem which varies according to the country
- Leave: 10 to 15 days minimum every 6 months - Airfare paid at 100% by CRF for home travel
- Health coverage: CFE + Mutuelle MSH (covered 100%) - covered at 75% by the CRF
- MedEvac/repatriation insurance: YES
- Other insurances: Provident insurance (death and disability)

**SUMMARY**

- Location: Ramallah- PALESTINE
- Duration: 12 months (renewable)
- Starting date : December 2026
- Mandatory driving licence

The French Red Cross reserves the right to close a recruitment before the closing date of the advertisement and the application deadline. Thank you for your understanding.

If we do not contact you within 3 weeks, please consider that we will not consider your application.

Female candidates are encouraged to apply.

**Online training**

To learn more about the Red Cross Movement, we invite you to follow two online training courses, free of charge and accessible to all. W.O.R.C. (World of Red Cross and Red Crescent): this course covers topics such as the origin and history of the Movement, its fundamental principles, the emblem, the International Federation, the ICRC and the national societies. Stay Safe aims to develop a common culture of security management within the Movement. You can find these courses on the International Federation's Learning Platform: [https://ifrc.csod.com/client/ifrc/default.aspx](https://ifrc.csod.com/client/ifrc/default.aspx)

## **We unlock power with coastal communities**

Blue Ventures connects coastal communities restoring the ocean, providing the resources and partnerships they need to unlock their power and turn local action into global impact. We link communities with allies, knowledge and influence to create unstoppable waves of change.

Together, we’re placing communities at the centre of solutions to sustain fisheries, manage ecosystems and redefine how the world protects the ocean.

Blue Ventures’ Partner Network team is responsible for identifying, selecting, and supporting civil society organisations and NGOs that work with coastal communities around the world. The role requires frequent travel to remote communities, flexibility to accommodate weather- and tide-dependent schedules, and the ability to work effectively across multiple time zones.

jobs.title: Chef de projet
jobs.description:
INTERSOS est une Organisation Humanitaire Non Gouvernementale, à but non lucratif, qui a l’objectif d’assister les victimes de désastres naturels et de conflits armés. INTERSOS base son action sur les valeurs de la solidarité, de la justice, de la dignité humaine, de l’égalité des droits et des opportunités pour tous les peuples, du respect des diversités, de la cohabitation, de l’attention aux groupes sociales les plus vulnérables.

## **Termes de référence**

**Intitulé du poste** : Chef de projet

**Code :** SR-38-10313

**Pays :** République du Congo

**Lieu d’affectation** : Bukavu

**Date de prise de fonction** :01/12/2026

**Durée du contrat** : 12 mois ( jusqu'au 14.10.2027)

**Sous la supervision de :** Coordinateur Programme

**Supervision de :** Personnel du projet

**Lieu d'affectation:** sans famille

## **Contexte général du projet**

La situation humanitaire en RDC reste complexe et s'est globalement détériorée ces dernières années, constituée de multiples crises qui se chevauchent, en particulier dans les provinces de l'Est du pays, qui font face à une violence endémique et à des conflits armés. L'insécurité a entraîné des déplacements massifs et répétés. L'impact de la violence sur les civils est une souffrance majeure avec des violations régulières des droits de l'homme et du droit international humanitaire, y compris des attaques ciblées contre des civils et une forte prévalence de la violence sexiste.
INTERSOS est présent en RDC depuis 2010 et travaille actuellement en Ituri, Nord Kivu, Sud Kivu à travers des programmes de protection, de santé, Wash et sécurité alimentaire en partenariat avec les agences UN et avec des fonds donnés par ECHO, AICS, SV et autres bailleurs.

Ce projet, financé par le Fonds Humanitaire RDC à hauteur de 960 000 USD, vise à renforcer la sécurité et le bien-être des populations touchées par les crises au Sud-Kivu à travers 40 aires de santé. Il s'appuie sur le soutien aux initiatives communautaires, en particulier les associations féminines, afin de faciliter un accès sécurisé, confidentiel et équitable à des services de protection adaptés.

## **Objectif général de la position**

Le chef de projet assure un engagement constant entre les différents services de soutien afin d'assurer un soutien rapide à l'équipe de projet.
Le chef de projet est titulaire du budget pour l'ensemble de la subvention/du budget du projet et supervise/surveille de près la planification financière, la planification des liquidités et l'utilisation du budget/le suivi du taux d'épuisement.

La gestion financière/budgétaire est la responsabilité finale du chef de projet pour le projet spécifique et il / elle doit s'assurer que cela va de pair avec un cadre logique serré et un suivi du plan de travail.

## **Principales responsabilités et tâches**

**Principales responsabilités**

- Assurer la planification, la mise en œuvre et le suivi/évaluation et fixer les objectifs tels qu'ils sont inclus dans la description du projet. Signaler tout écart important par rapport au plan de mise en œuvre du programme et aux dépenses estimées ; Alertez le personnel concerné.
- Garantir une gestion financière efficace en tant que principal détenteur du budget du projet, conformément au modèle d'INTERSOS et à la réglementation des bailleurs de fonds.
- Gestion d'équipe et des ressources humaines (personnel et bénévoles)
- Fournir des rapports de qualité sur les activités du projet, y compris les conclusions en termes d'impact et de changements au niveau des bénéficiaires atteints par le projet, des rapports conformes et cohérents conformément à INTERSOS et aux exigences des donateurs, en collaboration avec l'Unité des subventions du siège
- Développer une compréhension claire du programme INTERSOS et de la stratégie pays au sein de l'équipe de projet – s'assurer également que l'équipe apporte sa contribution et son retour d'information en temps opportun sur les questions stratégiques.
- Soutenir la coordonnatrice de programme dans l'élaboration de programmes ou de projets.
- Veiller à ce que la prestation du programme soit conforme aux normes techniques minimales d'INTERSOS et des bailleurs de fonds, et rechercher des conseils et des outils de la section technique et du département MEAL.
- Assurer une vue d'ensemble claire des acteurs et des services dans la zone d'intervention, en permettant le développement et la mise en œuvre de partenariats et de voies d'orientation.
- Activités de soutien administratif et de bureau (ententes, modifications, rapports signés, communications, etc.), en veillant à ce que le cycle de documentation soit à jour et en veillant à ce que les exigences de tous les services soient harmonisées et traitées.

**Responsabilités et tâches détaillées**

- Assurer la mise en œuvre intégrale et en temps opportun de la proposition de projet telle qu'approuvée, en respectant de manière proactive les délais de production de rapports :
- Lancement du projet et présentation/partage du projet avec les équipes
- Examiner et préparer un plan d'activités détaillé avec l'équipe
- Vérification du ciblage des bénéficiaires

**Gestion financière et approvisionnement**

- Préparer, suivre et mettre en œuvre le plan financier et d'approvisionnement
- Préparer le plan financier
- Approbation de tous les achats/contrats et allocations de lignes budgétaires
- Vérifier les écritures comptables dans les feuilles de calcul comptables INTERSOS (JOURNAL) : vérifier les allocations des lignes budgétaires, l'état des dépenses budgétaires par rapport à la livraison réelle et le plan financier pour la période de mise en œuvre restante du projet
- S'assurer que pour tous les achats/contrats de biens/services/fournitures, les directives d'approvisionnement INTERSOS correctes sont appliquées et correctement documentées, en coordination avec les départements des finances et de la logistique.
- Vérifier la liste des dépenses avant de finaliser les rapports financiers intermédiaires et finaux.
- Assume la responsabilité finale de la vérification de l'exhaustivité et de l'exactitude de tous les documents justificatifs.

**Gestion du personnel**

- Convenir et établir des lignes de signalement et de communication claires
- Recrutement de l'équipe, liaison avec le département RH pour sécuriser les dossiers RH à jour.
- Coaching permanent des équipes sur le terrain pour travailler sur la qualité de la livraison.
- Gère et évalue le rendement du personnel du projet.
- Organisez des réunions hebdomadaires et mensuelles avec l'équipe pour examiner la planification et discuter des principales préoccupations sur lesquelles se concentrer pour la période à venir.
- Vérification continue/rapide de la qualité des données collectées et reçues du personnel sur le terrain.
- S'assurer que les équipes respectent les règles et les directives d'INTERSOS à la mission et adhèrent au code de conduite et à la charte des valeurs d'INTERSOS.

**Suivi et évaluation**

- Assurer le suivi et la vérification du ciblage des bénéficiaires.
- En appliquant une approche de gestion axée sur les résultats, surveiller les résultats du projet, en plus des extrants et des activités, y compris les changements au niveau des ménages et de la communauté réalisés dans le cadre du projet.
- Effectuer (si les conditions de sécurité le permettent) des visites sur le terrain afin de fournir des conseils techniques et une supervision à l'équipe et de suivre l'avancement et la qualité des différentes activités du projet.

**Rapports**

- Assurer des rapports de qualité sur les réalisations par le biais de brefs briefings quotidiens, d'une planification mensuelle et hebdomadaire présentée par rapport à des rapports de performance hebdomadaires et mensuels contenant des informations quantitatives et qualitatives claires relatives aux activités.
- Obtenir des rapports réguliers par équipe et compiler, examiner et analyser les rapports sur une base mensuelle qui seront reflétés dans l'outil d'évaluation de projet INTERSOS.
- Préparer des rapports d'avancement ad hoc à l'intention des donateurs et des rapports provisoires et finaux de projet exigés par les fonctionnaires ; Préparer des rapports narratifs provisoires et finaux à l'intention du donateur en temps opportun et de manière qualitative, en examinant les réalisations par rapport aux résultats et aux extrants, et en reflétant clairement les leçons apprises dans des recommandations pour les programmes futurs.
- Assume la responsabilité finale de tous les documents d'appui (moyens de vérification) et des documents généraux du projet.
- Fournit régulièrement des produits de communication (y compris des photos) sur le projet à utiliser par le service de communication d'INTERSOS dans différents points de vente.

**Coordination et représentation**

- Aider le coordonnateur de programme et les coordonnateurs techniques à assister aux réunions du groupe et veiller à ce que les faits saillants et les informations pertinentes pour la zone d'intervention fassent l'objet d'un rapport en temps opportun.
- Participer à des réunions régulières avec les représentants des donateurs et faciliter les visites sur le terrain des missions des donateurs (lorsque les conditions de sécurité le permettent), en coordination avec le coordonnateur du programme.
- Assurer le partage systématique de l'information et de la mise à jour avec la coordonnatrice du programme
- S'acquitter de toutes autres tâches connexes qui pourraient lui être confiées.

## **Profil requis**

**Education**

- Diplôme universitaire du niveau du commerce en sciences sociales, en sciences politiques, en relations internationales, en aide humanitaire et dans une discipline apparentée

**Expérience Professionnelle**

- Minimum de 3 ans d'expérience professionnelle dans la gestion de projets/programmes humanitaires, y compris la gestion financière et les responsabilités logistiques
- Minimum 1 an d'expérience dans la mise en œuvre de programmes de protection, expérience en protection monitoring sera un atout et protection de l'enfance.
- Expérience de l'établissement et du maintien de relations de collaboration avec les donateurs et les homologues gouvernementaux, ainsi qu'en matière de conformité et de production de rapports auprès des bailleurs de fonds.
- Expérience dans des situations d'urgence complexes

**Exigences Professionnelles**

- Solides compétences en matière de représentation et de négociation
- Compétences en administration, en finances et en gestion budgétaire
- Connaissances essentielles en informatique (Word, Excel et Internet)
- Pensée analytique, capacité d'analyse et compétences en élaboration de programmes stratégiques

**Langues**

- Langue de travail de la mission essentielle
- Connaissance multilingue souhaitable

**Exigences personnelles**

- Capacité à assurer une livraison rapide et de qualité dans un environnement stressant
- Capacité à respecter les échéanciers et la hiérarchie
- Solides compétences interpersonnelles : communication, diplomatie
- Leadership, gestion et développement des personnes
- Organisation et résolution de problèmes
- Engagement envers les principes d'INTERSOS

## **Conditions générales et avantages :**

- **Fourchette de salaire :** 10 - 3.362€ - 3.792€ monthly gross
- **Rémunération**: La rémunération mensuelle pour chaque poste est définie conformément à la grille salariale et à la grille de fonctions standard internationales d'INTERSOS, en tenant compte de l'expérience du candidat sélectionné. Elle est communiquée lors de l'entretien avec les ressources humaines, ou en tout état de cause lors de la première étape du processus de sélection.
- **Hébergement :** Shared Guesthouse
- **R&R :** Le personnel d'INTERSOS tenu de travailler pendant des périodes prolongées dans des lieux d'affectation soumis à des conditions périlleuses, stressantes et difficiles bénéficie d'une période régulière et obligatoire de repos et de récupération (R&R). Cette mesure vise à protéger sa santé et son bien-être et à garantir une performance de travail optimale lors de la reprise de ses fonctions, tout en préservant la capacité opérationnelle de l'Organisation. Les avantages liés au R&R ne constituent pas une compensation financière pour le degré de pénibilité et d'insécurité d'un lieu d'affectation. Admissibilité : les membres du personnel recrutés en tant que personnel international de terrain dont le contrat indique un lieu d'affectation R&R comme lieu d'affectation principal et dont la durée du contrat est égale ou supérieure à 4 mois civils. R&R : il consiste en 7 jours de récupération psychophysique toutes les 8/10/12 semaines, selon le lieu d'affectation. Une indemnité de 1 000 € y est associée.
- **Congés annuels :** 2,5 jours par mois
- **Assurance médicale:** Assurance accidents et décès ; assurance responsabilité civile ; remboursement des vaccins, du certificat médical et du test PCR pour le déploiement ; soutien psychosocial sur demande pour le travailleur humanitaire.
- **Transport:** Vols A/R pour l'humanitaire. Pour toute mission d'une durée d'au moins 9 mois, un billet d'avion supplémentaire vers le pays de résidence et le retour sur le lieu de mission est pris en charge par l'Organisation pour le travailleur humanitaire.
- **Visa:** INTERSOS prend en charge les frais et l'assistance pour l'obtention du visa pour le travailleur humanitaire.
- **Formation d’intégration :** Cours d'orientation en ligne : chaque nouveau membre du personnel reçoit une formation préparatoire avant le départ, adéquate pour fournir les informations nécessaires relatives à la structure d'INTERSOS et aux principaux processus décisionnels et outils de travail, afin de faciliter son intégration au sein de l'Organisation.
- **Remarque 1 :** INTERSOS applique une « politique d'apprentissage et de développement » (Learning & Development Policy) qui inclut la possibilité de bénéficier de formations et de participer à des formations internes et externes. La priorité sera accordée au personnel travaillant pour INTERSOS depuis plus de deux ans.
- **Remarque 2 :** La classification des lieux d'affectation avec accompagnement, R&R et sans accompagnement est soumise à des critères de sécurité, d'accès aux services de santé et d'éducation, et n'est pas négociable.

jobs.title: Humanitarian Affairs Officer (NOB)
jobs.company: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
jobs.description:
**The duty station is Rasuwa, Nepal.**

**Background**

The Humanitarian Affairs Officer, UNOCHA, position is established to support the humanitarian response to the floods affecting Rasuwa and surrounding disaster-affected areas of Nepal. The position is intended to reinforce UN field-level coordination during the immediate response period, working closely with government authorities, UN agencies, NGOs, humanitarian partners, and affected communities. Under the direct supervision of the RCO/OCHA Bidur Hub lead and the overall supervision of the Resident Coordinator’s Office Nepal and the Head of OCHA’s Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific (ROAP), the incumbent will work in close collaboration with the UN Resident Coordinator, Government and relief/recovery partners to support the formulation of strategies of engagement in support of the mandate of OCHA at both managerial and operational levels.

The Humanitarian Affairs Officer will provide on-site humanitarian coordination in flood-affected areas, with a particular focus in Rasuwa and Nuwakot. The incumbent will help ensure that operational agencies and local authorities have a common understanding of priority needs, response activities, constraints and gaps, and that field-level issues requiring attention are communicated promptly to relevant coordination and decision-making structures. The role is operational and field-facing and requires regular travel to affected communities and response locations. The incumbent will also be responsible for providing advice and support to the Resident/Humanitarian Coordinator and operational partners to consider the priorities of the most vulnerable communities in humanitarian and early recovery planning.

**Duties and Responsibilities**

1.) Ensures effective humanitarian coordination at field level in support of national authorities
•Provide a visible and sustained OCHA /RCO coordination presence in Rasuwa and other designated flood-affected areas.
•Facilitate and support field coordination meetings with local authorities, UN agencies, NGOs, Red Cross/Red Crescent actors and other operational partners.
•Promote complementarity among responders, identify duplication and gaps, and support practical follow-up on agreed coordination actions.
•Maintain regular liaison with affected communities and relevant local structures so priority concerns can inform coordination discussions.
•Support field partners to steer a collective approach to Accountability to Affected People (AAP). This means joint community consultations, harmonized messaging in local languages, and shared feedback and complaint mechanisms, whose findings inform response planning and are followed up with communities. Work with the PSEA Network and agency focal points so that these channels are safe and accessible for reporting sexual exploitation and abuse, and that survivor-centred referral pathways are in place and known to communities and responders.

2.) Monitoring, assessment and analysis of humanitarian needs
•Monitor humanitarian conditions, priority needs, access constraints, emerging risks and response coverage through regular field visits and engagement with partners.
•Support or participate in inter-agency rapid assessments and field missions as required.
•Consolidate field observations and partner inputs into concise situation updates, analysis and recommendations for OCHA and humanitarian leadership.
•Flag critical gaps, underserved locations and operational bottlenecks requiring coordinated action.

3.) Support to operational response and emergency preparedness
•Promote timely coordination around immediate life-saving priorities and evolving operational requirements following the floods.
•Support contingency and preparedness discussions where continuing rainfall, landslides, access disruption or other hazards may affect communities or response operations.
•Encourage partners to integrate relevant humanitarian policies and principles, protection considerations, accountability to affected people and inclusion in field-level response planning.

4.) Information sharing, reporting and coordination support
•Maintain regular information exchange between responders in affected areas and coordination structures at national and regional levels.
•Support partners to engage women, persons with disabilities, older persons and marginalized groups in response decisions, using safe and inclusive channels that also serve as entry points for PSEA reporting and referral.
•Track how community feedback is acted upon across partners, and flag recurring concerns, including SEA risks, to coordination forums and the PSEA Network so the response can adjust.
•Prepare meeting records, action points, field updates, briefing notes and inputs to humanitarian reporting products.
•Support mapping of operational presence, needs and response gaps in collaboration with information management colleagues and partners.
•Track agreed actions and follow up with responsible partners to support timely implementation

5\) Partnership, advocacy and enabling humanitarian access
•Build constructive working relationships with local and district authorities, humanitarian organizations, civil society and community representatives.
•Identify operational or coordination issues that may impede assistance and elevate them through appropriate channels.
•Provide field evidence and analysis to support advocacy on priority humanitarian needs, equitable assistance and effective response coverage.

**Work implies frequent interaction with the following:**
Staff at all levels within RCO/OCHA Bidur Hub, UN RCO Nepal and Regional Offfice for Asia and the Pacific . Representatives of Nepal National Disaster Management Organizations, other UN agencies and other organizations that work on disaster risk managemet and related issues.
**Results Expected:**
Provides sound analytical inputs and advice that contributes to improving institutional capacity and articulates humanitarian response to the Nepal 2026 Flash Flood with a special focus in Rasuwa. Provides timely delivery of assigned tasks, maintains partnerships and interacts effectively with colleagues internally and externally.

**Competencies**

**Core Competencies**

- **Achieve Results:**
LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact
- **Think Innovatively:**
LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems
- **Learn Continuously:**
LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences
- **Adapt with Agility:**
LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands
- **Act with Determination:**
LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results
- **Engage and Partner:**
LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration
- **Enable Diversity and Inclusion:**
LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

**People Management**

Show Managerial Courage
• Face up to organizational and people problems
• Not be afraid to take decisions and action when and as needed
• Not hold back anything that needs to be said, respectfully and diplomatically
• Address conflict in a timely manner, not allow conflicts in teams to linger
• Help others through emotional or tense situations, tactfully bringing disagreements into the open and finding solutions all can endorse

Demonstrate Empathy and Emotional Intelligence
• Genuinely care about people; demonstrate empathy with the joys and pains of others
• Enable the wellbeing of the team(s)
• Read a group’s emotional currents and power relationships, identifying influencers, networks, and organizational dynamics; adapt leadership styles at the appropriate times
• See the positive in people, situations, and events

Motivate and Direct
• Create and communicate a compelling vision and purpose
• Align people and resources with organizational vision, strategy, objectives
• Understand and proactively build the team/organization culture

Build an Enabling Workplace
• Create a working environment where people are engaged and want to do their best; empower and enable team members to perform and have a positive workplace experience
• Promote honesty, openness, trust and psychological safety and create opportunities to innovate and learn
• Encourage collective action and integration

Build Capability
• Identify and develop talent in individuals, providing positive support to enable them to achieve their potential
• Foster learning or development of others by giving feedback, guidance, and support; support career development of others
• Have willingness and ability to delegate to help people learn, including from failure

Manage Performance and Ensure Accountability
• Ensure regular conversations with people about work
• Provide positive and constructive feedback
• Discuss poor performance in a timely manner
• Provide praise and recognition, as well as ensure accountability

Lead with Humility
• Be authentic and transparent, act with integrity
• Be accessible and available to team members they lead
• Encourage debate and discussion, creating a culture where people are comfortable to challenge senior leaders and feel listened to
• Be modest, giving credit for success to others and admit own shortcomings

**Cross Functional & Technical competencies**

**Business Management**
**Operation Management**
• Ability to effectively plan, organise and oversee different parts of corporate operations, simultaneously and in an integrated way, in order to convert the organisation’s assets into the best results in the most efficient way. Knowledge of relevant concepts and mechanisms

**Partnership management**
**Emerging partnerships**
**•** Ability to engage with emerging partners, develop and manage a strategy and develop approaches to developing and managing these new strategic partnerships

**Communications**
**Advocacy strategy and implementation**
• Ability to create and implement advocacy strategies which lead to impactful change

**Required Skills and Experience**

**Education:**

- Advanced University degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Humanitarian, Environmental Science, Social Science, Climate Change, International Development, Business Administration, Public Administration, or related field is required, or;
- A first level university degree (bachelor’s degree or equivalent) in the above-mentioned fields with additional 2 years of relevant experience will be given due consideration in lieu of master’s degree.

**Experience:**

- Minimum 2 years (with master’s degree) or 4 years (with bachelor’s degree) of relevant working experience at the national or international organization in disaster management, humanitarian or in related thematic area is required.
- Relevant experience with a UN agency or comparable humanitarian organisation is required.
- Experience in crisis/emergency relief management, and humanitarian/ emergency field coordination is required.
- Excellent liaison, interpersonal and general communications skills; Ability to work with minimum supervision in a multi-cultural environment; Coordination and Information Management skills; Training and or capacity building skills; Presentation skills;
- Excellent command of MS Office suite applications (Word, Excel, Access, PowerPoint).
- Excellent oral and written command of Nepali and English is required. Knowledge of another UN language is desirable.
- Experience coordinating field-based humanitarian response, including engagement with government authorities and humanitarian partners, is highly desirable.
- Knowledge of Nepal, including local institutions and coordination arrangements, is highly desirable.

jobs.title: HQ Programme Support Officer
jobs.description:
**PROJECT´S GENERAL INFORMATION**

***Location:** Based in either Honduras or Colombia*

***Will report to:** Regional Director*

**PROGRAM OVERVIEW:**

Founded in 1977, GOAL is an international humanitarian response agency working with vulnerable communities in more than 60 countries. GOAL aims to increase the resilient wellbeing of the world’s poorest people and focuses on those who are excluded or marginalised, particularly those who are vulnerable due to socio-economic status, gender or age. See our website at: [https://www.goalglobal.org](https://www.goalglobal.org)

**OBJECTIVE OF THE POSITION:**

The Programme Support Officer will play a vital role in the support of GOAL’s country programmes and will be part of the HQ Operations Team. Working in a fast-paced environment and undertaking tasks which will touch on a wide range of GOAL’s overseas programmes and HQ functions, they will be responsible for a broad and varying range of duties including grant management and country support.

**PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES/ROLES**

**Grant & Data Management**

- Provide support to Desk officers in the administration and management of GOAL’s portfolio of grants or other country programme related tasks
- Lead on operational data management for the countries/region supported
- Support the Desk Officer in developing donor submissions (concept notes, proposals, reports, amendments).

**Information Management**

- Providing support to Desk Officers to improve integrity and ensure the Grant Management System is up to date
- Support the maintenance of key departmental systems including the internal SharePoint page and grant management system.
- Manage and input data into GOAL’s key systems, including grants management system

**Coordination and Representation**

- Support the desk team on any donor coordination, communication and representation needs
- Lead on donor portal management for the region, supported by the Desk Coordinator (DC)
- Support on any business development strategies with FBD and other key stakeholders
- Coordinate bilaterally and across departments on projects to ensure alignment and efficiency.

**Operational Process Management**

- Work with the Communications Department and country programme teams to develop and submit high quality case studies, stories of change or success stories and media input.
- Emergency support - Providing general support for Desk during emergency response, including sitreps and GMS support.
- Support management of Partnership data, reporting, and contracts.
- Lead on regional documentation management, administration and filing across all GOAL systems

**MINIMUM REQUIRED PROFILE**

***Professional Studies:***

- Professionals in Business Administration, Project Management, or related fields.

***Professional experience:***

- Some previous experience working in an INGO either in a field-based or HQ role.
- Good understanding and or relevant experience in the core job responsibilities noted above including: Grant and Data Management, Information Management, Coordination and representation, and Operational Process Management.
- An understanding of GOALs mission, values and strategy
- Adept in Microsoft Applications like Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.
- Fluency in English and Spanish with excellent writing and analytical skills.

***Desired competencies:***

- Demonstrable knowledge and experience of major institutional donors (USAID, ECHO, Irish Aid, FCDO, UN agencies), including familiarity key donor priorities, compliance, monitoring and evaluation guidelines.
- Good knowledge and experience of GOAL’s thematic programmes or sectors (including health, nutrition, wash & resilience), and/or donors (including USAID, ECHO, FCDO and Irish Aid)
- Experience with Dynamics 365, SharePoint, Power BI, and grant management systems.
- Fluency in French

**COORDINATION**

- The professional will coordinate with the Regional Director.

**RESOURCES**

1. The incumbent will receive logistical support (computer) and transportation, when required for project activities.
2. The employee will have a physical space available to work in the GOAL office.

**SAFEGUARD**

Children and adults in vulnerable situations must be protected to the greatest extent possible from deliberate or inadvertent actions and failures that put them at risk of abuse, sexual exploitation, injury and any other harm. One of the ways GOAL shows this ongoing commitment to protection is to include rigorous background checks and benchmark checks in the selection process for all candidates.

**RESPONSIBILITY WITHIN GOAL**

Along with our safeguarding policy, GOAL is an equal opportunity employer and has a set of integrity policies. Any candidate who gets offered a job with GOAL is expected to adhere to the following key areas of responsibility:

- Comply with GOAL's policies and procedures regarding safeguarding, Code of Conduct, health and safety, data protection and confidentiality, principles of no harm, and unacceptable behavior protocols.
- Report any concerns about the well-being of a child or adult in a vulnerable situation, or any irregularities within our programming area.
- Report any concerns about inappropriate behavior by a GOAL staff or partner.

jobs.title: Emergency Coordinator
jobs.description:
Field-based contract - 12 months (Renewable)

To fulfill its mission of assistance to victims of conflicts, epidemics or natural disasters, MSF Switzerland has created an Emergency Pool, of which, members are experienced individuals capable of evaluating a situation, opening, closing, and coordinating emergency projects.

The successful candidate is expected to:

- Work in all contexts set by the Emergency cell (Ecell)
- Have the flexibility to work in different positions depending on your profile
- Work in emergency contexts in collaboration with regular cells
- Fill gaps in regular projects if/when needed

Duty Station

Any country, either whether the Emergency Cell has activities, where an assessment is being conducted or where OCG has a regular mission that requires support.

On call, as Emergency Coordinator you should be available within 48 hours for rapid and short interventions. You will be part of a core group of medicals, para-medicals, and support staff responsible for responding to:

- Epidemic outbreaks
- Nutritional crises
- Displaced populations and/or refugees’ camps
- Conflict contexts
- Natural disasters
- Exploratory missions
- Short gap filling in the field on regular missions

Job Description (but not limited to)

- Implementation of and participation in exploratory missions and evaluations, upon request of the Ecell
- Definition, implementation (or modification) of the operational strategy of an emergency mission
- Identification and management of the tools, resources and means necessary for the implementation and management of an emergency intervention
- Coordination of the emergency mission in collaboration with the FCO/PMR/MedCo/Ecell: evaluation of needs and situation, definition of strategy and activities
- Networking and negotiation with all pertinent actors to enable access, security and implementation of activities.
- Coordination and supervision of the staff in the mission
- Management of material and financial resources for the emergency intervention
- Management of the entire mission’ security
- Reporting on the interventions, explorations and activities pertaining to the mission
- In accordance with the headquarters, you can be mandated (or requested) to coordinate activities, under the responsibility of a Head of Mission in the country where the section is already working
- You can be asked to intervene within the framework of certain MSF trainings and to take part in local, national, and international meetings

Your Profile

Required:

- 24 months of field experience with MSF in a coordination role (12 months in a HOM role) and at least one mission in an emergency context with MSF. at least one mission in an emergency context with MSF.
- Fluency in both French and English is highly desirable
- Expertise in analyses of unstable contexts / crises situations
- Capacity to quickly evaluate an emergency on ground and to propose an appropriate strategy of intervention.
- General knowledge of MSF in emergency management
- Proven management skills with emphasis on team-leadership/human resources
- Knowledge and experience in security management in insecure contexts
- Commitment to the aims and values of MSF
- A flexible and solution-oriented mentality and the ability to be decisive in chaotic circumstances,
- Proven skills in negotiation, diplomacy and decision-making skills
- Proven capacity for coordination and organization
- Ability to prioritize work, manage teams and clearly communicate decisions.
- Capacity to work in a volatile, insecure context and deal with stress.
- PSP Training (at minimum ERT training)

Preferred:

- Medical / Paramedical background preferable.
- Experience in Public Health programs

Desirable:

- Ability to work as part of a multi-cultural and multi-disciplinary team
- Availability, flexibility, mobility
- Other languages represent an advantage: Arabic, Spanish, Portuguese

Terms of Employment

- Field-based contract, fixed-term for one year, renewable.
- Duration of direct interventions in the field: from 4 weeks to 3 months (certain flexibility is asked in case of needs)
- Travel arrangements and visa requirements will be taken in charge by MSF. MSF will provide per diem and accommodation when under assignment, but not between assignments.

**We encourage applications from people of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, backgrounds, religions, beliefs, abilities, and all other characteristics of diversity.**
**MSF does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of discrimination or harassment, including Sexual harassment.**

jobs.description:
## نبذة عن مؤسسة ماري للأبحاث والتنمية (MRD)

مؤسسة ماري للأبحاث والتنمية (MRD) هي مؤسسة غير ربحية مرخّصة تعمل في سوريا ، وتهدف إلى تعزيز بناء السلام، والحوار المدني، والحماية، والدعم النفسي والاجتماعي، والمساعدة القانونية، وسبل العيش، وتعزيز قدرة المجتمعات على الصمود.

تعمل المؤسسة بالتعاون الوثيق مع المجتمعات المحلية والشركاء الدوليين لتمكين الفئات الأكثر ضعفاً، بما في ذلك الناجون والناجيات من الاحتجاز والتعذيب، وأسر المفقودين، والنساء، والشباب.

## المسمى الوظيفي

مساعد/ة حماية ومناهضة العنف القائم على النوع الاجتماعي.

## مكان العمل

دمشق / دير الزور، على أن يتم تعيين موظف/ة واحد/ة في كل مركز.

## المسؤول المباشر

منسق/ة المشاريع، مع توفير الدعم والإشراف الفني من منسق/ة الحماية والعنف القائم على النوع الاجتماعي.

## الهدف من الوظيفة

يتولى/تتولى مساعد/ة الحماية والعنف القائم على النوع الاجتماعي دعم تنفيذ أنشطة الحماية ومناهضة العنف القائم على النوع الاجتماعي على مستوى المراكز، بما يضمن تقديم خدمات آمنة وسرية تراعي احتياجات الناجين والناجيات وحقوقهم وكرامتهم.

كما يساهم/تساهم في متابعة الحالات، وتنفيذ جلسات التوعية، وتيسير الإحالات الآمنة إلى الخدمات المتخصصة، وتعزيز مشاركة المجتمع المحلي، وذلك وفقاً للمعايير الدولية للحماية وسياسات الحماية المعتمدة لدى المؤسسة.

## المهام والمسؤوليات الرئيسية

- المساهمة في تحديد حالات الحماية والعنف القائم على النوع الاجتماعي، واستقبالها، وتقييم احتياجاتها، ومتابعتها وفق الإجراءات المعتمدة.
- دعم إدارة الحالات وتقديم الخدمات التي تراعي احتياجات الناجين والناجيات، مع ضمان احترام رغباتهم وحقوقهم وخصوصيتهم، وتنفيذ الإحالات الآمنة وفق إجراءات التشغيل القياسية المعتمدة.
- تنظيم وتيسير جلسات توعية حول الوقاية من العنف القائم على النوع الاجتماعي، وحقوق المرأة، وحماية الطفل، والخدمات المتاحة للفئات المستهدفة.
- التعاون مع فرق التعبئة المجتمعية لتعزيز مسارات الإحالة وآليات الحماية المجتمعية.
- توثيق الحالات والأنشطة بدقة، وحفظ السجلات والبيانات بطريقة آمنة وسرية، بما يضمن حماية المعلومات الشخصية وفق السياسات المعتمدة.
- التنسيق مع فرق المساعدة القانونية والدعم النفسي والاجتماعي لضمان تقديم خدمات متكاملة تستجيب لاحتياجات المستفيدين والمستفيدات.
- المشاركة في التدريبات وجلسات الإشراف الفني والإرشاد المهني وجلسات استخلاص الدروس.
- الالتزام بمبادئ الحماية والسرية وعدم التمييز واحترام الكرامة الإنسانية، وسياسات المؤسسة المتعلقة بالحماية من الاستغلال والانتهاك والإساءة، ومبدأ عدم التسبب بالضرر.

## المؤهلات والمتطلبات

- شهادة جامعية في العمل الاجتماعي، أو علم النفس، أو الحقوق، أو أحد التخصصات ذات الصلة.
- خبرة عملية لا تقل عن سنتين في مجال الحماية أو برامج العنف القائم على النوع الاجتماعي.
- معرفة جيدة بالمبادئ التوجيهية للاستجابة للعنف القائم على النوع الاجتماعي، بما يشمل السرية، والسلامة، والاحترام، وعدم التمييز.
- الإلمام بمسارات الإحالة وآليات تقديم الخدمات التي تراعي احتياجات الناجين والناجيات وتحفظ حقوقهم وكرامتهم.
- امتلاك مهارات جيدة في التواصل والتيسير وإدارة جلسات التوعية.
- إجادة اللغة العربية تحدثاً وكتابةً.
- تعتبر معرفة اللغة الإنجليزية ميزة إضافية.

## ملاحظات

- سيتم تعيين موظف/ة واحد/ة في كل من مركزي دمشق ودير الزور.
- يُشترط الالتزام بالمعايير المهنية والأخلاقية وسياسات المؤسسة، والتعامل باحترام وسرية مع جميع المستفيدين والمستفيدات.

**Job Title: Psychologist**

**Job location: Syria – Idleb**

**Reports to: Admin Officer**

**JOB SUMMARY**

The psychologist is responsible for providing psychological, educational, and rehabilitative support for children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and their families, and to develop comprehensive and individualized intervention plans based on scientific assessment, implemented in collaboration with a multidisciplinary team.

**MAIN DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

The psychologist has the following responsibilities and duties:

· Conduct comprehensive psychological and behavioral assessments using standardized and approved tools and reports.

· Participate in the diagnosis of autism spectrum disorders in collaboration with the specialized team.

· Develop Individualized Education Plans (IEPs), follow up on their implementation, and modify them as needed.

· Deliver individual and group therapy sessions based on scientific strategies (e.g., Applied Behavior Analysis, Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, Play Therapy…).

· Provide psychological counseling and support to the parents of children, encouraging their active participation in the therapeutic plan.

· Document all therapy sessions and evaluation reports and update them regularly.

· Work within a multidisciplinary team (teachers, speech therapists, occupational therapists…) and maintain ongoing coordination.

· Contribute to building the capacity of the staff through internal guidance or training sessions.

· Conduct awareness workshops for parents and the local community about autism and the role of families.

· Adhere to ethical and professional standards in the practice of psychology.

· Participate in regular meetings and report on case development and service quality improvement.

**QUALIFICATIONS AND SKILLS**

Should have the following skills, education, and experience:

· A minimum of a bachelor’s degree in psychology (Master’s degree or a specialized diploma in Child Psychology or Clinical Psychology is preferred).

· At least two years of experience working with children with autism spectrum disorder.

· Strong knowledge of psychological assessment methods and standardized tools.

· Familiarity with modern therapeutic techniques used in autism treatment.

· Ability to communicate effectively with children and their families.

· Strong teamwork skills and the ability to coordinate within a multidisciplinary team.

· High documentation skills and proficiency in using computers.

· Empathy, patience, and the ability to work with children with special needs.

· Good analytical and organizational skills.

· Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

· Commitment to humanitarian and professional values

**ABOUT MEDGLOBAL**

MedGlobal is a global humanitarian non-profit organization providing medical and health education services to people in need, including refugees and displaced persons, in disaster and underserved regions. The organization is composed of medical and public health professionals from diverse backgrounds.

**CODE OF CONDUCT**

MedGlobal Code of Conduct reflects the profession’s core set of beliefs and values of care, respect, trust, and integrity. These beliefs and values are fundamental to MedGlobal employees, volunteers, interns, consultants, and contractors to guide their practice and conduct. The Code is organized into categories, as follows:

· Always act with fairness, honesty, integrity, and openness; respect the opinions of others and treat all with equality and dignity without regard to gender, race, color, creed, ancestry, place of origin, political beliefs, religion, marital status, disability, age, or sexual orientation.

· Provide a positive and valued experience for those receiving services within and outside MedGlobal.

**CHILD PROTECTION POLICY**

Child abuse in all forms is unacceptable to MedGlobal, which recognizes its responsibility to protect children from harm in all areas of its work. MedGlobal is committed to ensuring a child-safe environment and is applying a zero-tolerance approach towards any kind of child abuse and exploitation.

**DISCRIMINATION, ABUSE AND HARASSMENT POLICY**

MedGlobal provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and expressly prohibits and will not tolerate any form of discrimination, abuse, harassment (sexual or otherwise), based upon race, ethnicity, religion, national origin, gender, age, marital status, citizenship status, disability, or military status. MedGlobal employees and related personnel must under no circumstances take part in any form of discrimination, harassment, or abuse (physical, sexual or verbal), intimidation or exploitation, or in any other way infringe the rights of others inside or outside the organization.

**Job Title: Special Education Facilitator**

**Job location: Syria, Idleb**

**Report to: Admin Officer**

The special education facilitator is responsible for the Ddagnosis of the needs of children with disabilities or learning difficulties, designing and implementing individualized educational programs that meet those needs, and providing academic, behavioral, and social support within an inclusive educational environment that respects individual differences.

• Prepare and develop an Individualized Education Plan (IEP) in collaboration with the multidisciplinary team.

• Conduct individual or group rehabilitation sessions based on the objectives of the educational plan.

• Use and adapt a variety of teaching strategies (visual, auditory, sensory) according to the type of disability.

• Modify activities and adapt the environment to suit the child’s abilities.

• Document academic, educational, and developmental progress through regular reports and systematic observations.

• Support and guide teachers and facilitators in implementing effective educational strategies.

• Collaborate with parents to implement programs at home and enhance the learning environment.

• Develop and implement behavior modification plans when needed.

• Participate in regular meetings and reviews of each child’s Individualized Education Plan.

Should have the following skills, education, and experience:

• Bachelor’s or master’s degree in special education or a related field (such as Classroom Teaching, Psychological
