jobs.title: Project Director, Preconception Nutrition & Care, India
jobs.description:
**Employment Type:** Project, Full Time

**Title:** Project Director, Preconception Nutrition & Care, India

**Location:** New Delhi, India

**Deadline for submission:** October 31, 2025 (Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis and the position may be closed once a suitable candidate is identified.)

**About us**

Nutrition International (NI) is a global organization dedicated to delivering proven nutrition interventions to those who need them most. Working in partnership with countries, donors, and implementers, our experts conduct cutting-edge nutrition research, support critical policy formulation, and integrate nutrition into a broader development agenda. For more than 30 years now, we have focused on delivering low-cost, high-impact, nutrition interventions to people in need, driven by our mission to achieve a world where everyone, everywhere, is free from malnutrition and able to reach their full potential. Our work is guided by a dedicated and talented team of experts working globally, regionally and within countries to end malnutrition worldwide.

If you are a motivated and passionate individual who shares our conviction that a better world is possible through improved nutrition, wants to leave the world a little better than they found it, and is looking to be part of a team with a clear vision, we want to hear from you. Please consider applying for the position below which is being advertised for an anticipated project.

**About the Project**

The Preconception Nutrition and Care project is an exciting new initiative in India. It aims to change how families begin: by reaching couples of reproductive ages with nutrition, health interventions and counselling before pregnancy, so that women enter pregnancy healthier and better nourished. Healthier beginnings lead to better maternal and birth outcomes. The project takes a systems-based approach. It brings together service delivery, evidence generation, learning and government partnership, so that preconception care becomes integrated into overall health system delivery. At the heart of the project is a commitment to putting the nutritional needs of women and couples at the center of design and implementation. The project aims to generate evidence and learning from implementation, and to use it to shape national dialogue on preconception nutrition and care.

**About you**

You will have PhD or MD degree from a recognized university in one of the following areas: nutrition, public health, reproductive health and/or a related field, with atleast 10-12 years of work experience with international NGOs, UN agencies or similar working on public health, reproductive health, nutrition related programs with at least 5 years of senior level experience in project management. You will also have demonstrated the experience in managing complex partnerships with multiple stakeholders, including government bodies, NGOs, and international organizations.

Fluency in English is essential. Knowledge of Hindi and /or local languages of project states would be an advantage.

**About the role**

The Project Director will lead this work from New Delhi. You will head a small, focused team, guide a range of implementing partners and engage with state and national government. You will also be the primary voice of the project with the donor, government, research bodies and the private sector. You will work closely with Nutrition International’s Maternal Newborn Health and Nutrition and Health Economics and Nutrition Financing portfolios, as well as colleagues in the Asia Regional Office and headquarters in Ottawa.

This is a rare opportunity to lead a high-visibility project, with full accountability for results, partnerships and resources. You will help set the direction for how India, and the wider region, approaches nutrition and care before pregnancy. **In this role you** **will be responsible to:**

- Serve as the primary point of contact for donor/s, national government representatives and strategic partners to lead evidence-based negotiations on project priorities, scope, and deliverables
- Facilitate shared understanding of project scope, goals and deliverables and among project staff, partners and stakeholders.
- Guide the implementation of project activities and ensure project staff and partners are executing the project according to the approved project plan.
- Manage relations with partners, service providers and consultants of the project, according to Nutrition International’s policies. This includes the development of terms of reference, service provided and consultant/firm selection, contracting, monitoring and end of contract processes.
- Oversee and work closely with government stakeholders and partners to develop detailed annual workplans that clearly define the strategies, activities and resources (time, budget and equipment etc.) required for effective implementation of the project; and update workplans regularly to ensure the timely completion of activities and achievement of the deliverables
- Cultivate and manage strong, collaborative relationships with implementing partners, government authorities, donors and other key stakeholders. Ensure open communication channels and a shared understanding of the project’s goals, responsibilities, and timelines.
- Identify and engage with potential new partners that align with the project's objectives, ensuring their capacities complement the project's needs and strategies.
- Ensure monitoring and learning strategies and systems are applied within the project in collaboration with the Monitoring, Data and Learning sub-unit.
- Ensure a monitoring plan is developed and followed by the project team and partners. Ensure monitoring data is analyzed and used for course correction as needed.
- Ensure that the project has a comprehensive staffing strategy with the appropriate composition of team members to ensure adequate oversight and quality assurance of all work within the project.
- Manage project staff contracts and consultants in a timely manner and according to local legislation and Nutrition International policies.
- Provide financial oversight for the full scope of the project. Maintain oversight on all sub-grants within the project and their associated budget(s) and ensure that partners establish appropriate financial procedures and tools required to be in alignment with Nutrition International requirements and standards
- Develop regular cash flow projections and monitor expenditure and review variance analysis to ensure the project operates within its budget parameters.
- Ensure all project funds are managed according to established accounting policies, procedures and donor regulations.
- Ensure donor stewardship with our committed donors to sustain relationships. Build and strengthen relationships with key project stakeholders and partners to ensure the project is harmonized with other donors funded project/programs and facilitates government leadership and ownership.
- Establish mechanisms for regular communication within the project team, Country leadership and across partners and with Nutrition International leadership to maximize opportunities for program integration and to elevate issues or risks

**For more detailed information about the role**, please click on the attached [**Job Description**](https://nutritionintl.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/M365_PC-JobPostings/IQCMxQN_qQI_RamHX3ndj8Y8AdbDdsV4w2nPzLuvsWJGOi8?e=BUbcaY)

jobs.title: Officer, M/E
jobs.description:
**JOB SUMMARY**

The role of the Officer Monitoring and Evaluation (M/E) is to implement the M/E work plan and contribute to achieving and improving the quality of the program/project. The Officer M/E will provide support by collecting and managing the program's/project's output and outcome data. Officer M/E also plays a key role in data analysis and carrying out M/E activities in the field. The Officer M/E will provide support to the program’s M/E function in the field through working closely with the field staff to ensure the quality of the program/project.

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential function with or without reasonable accommodation.

**MAIN TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

**IMC’s policies, guidelines, and procedures**

- Mainstream the Global M/E Guidelines across all related M/E activities at the field level and ensure the guidance notes for monitoring and evaluation are functional at the field level.
- Apply and adapt existing Global M/E Guidelines, tools, and templates at the relevant stages of the project cycle.
- Actively promote the Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) standards within IMC and amongst its beneficiaries.
- Contribute to the creation of a positive image and overall credibility of the organization, notably through the application of the Code of Conduct, ethics, values, and standpoint with regards to internal and external actors.

**Project design and planning**

- Participate in needs assessments by organizing the training for enumerators on assessment methodology, tools, respondent’s selection, and supervise field team to ensure field level data integrity.
- Ensure that M/E activities are participatory.
- Support in developing results framework and log frame, including indicators, for simple projects.

**M/E system**

- Ensure that different components of the M/E system are functional and relevant and maintain IPTT to track output, outcome, and impact indicators and their measurement in the different sectors of relevance.
- Support M/E department in development of databases for all programs by using available technologies.
- Organize and lead data collection activities following the data collection and reporting flow put in place for a project.
- Use tools for tracking project's progress and bottlenecks and develop simple data collection tools based on monitoring indicators.
- Maintain effective M/E system (ensure data collected translates to the M/E Framework/IPTT).
- Conduct regular field visits.
- Conduct periodic data analysis and triangulate data from other M/E exercises.

**Data quality management**

- Conduct periodic data quality audits to assess the quality of collected data for indicators.
- Mitigate data pitfalls, issues, and ensure that strategies for quality data are in place.
- Report data quality issues to the M/E Manager/Coordinator.
- Adhere to the fundamental concepts of data quality.
- Conduct on-site routine data quality audits at community levels.
- Assess the quality of collected data for indicators.
- Provide supportive supervision on data quality at facility and community-levels.

**Sampling**

- Implement probability and non-probability sampling techniques as and when appropriate after consulting with manager.
- Develop sampling frame and carry out sampling following instructions (manager, guidelines).

**Qualitative and quantitative techniques**

- Use different qualitative and quantitative methods of data collection including structured/semi structured interviews, key informant interviews, in-depth interviews, group discussions, focus group discussions and direct observations as an M/E tool.
- Conduct trainings on qualitative techniques for data collection for M/E staff, program staff, and interviewers.
- Develop and use key qualitative tools (observation checklists, guide for group discussion and interviews) for monitoring purposes.
- Apply the different interview techniques (structured/semi-structured) and use appropriate questionnaires for monitoring purposes as and when appropriate
- Conduct regular and ad-hoc (when required) site visits to monitor data collection processes to ensure data quality.

**Mobile and manual data collection**

- Determine the appropriate data collection tool based on the purpose, advantages and disadvantages of mobile data collection techniques.
- Install and configure mobile data collection tools (OKD collect, Kobo collect, ONA collect, etc.) on smart phones or tablets
- Design simple questionnaire using XLS form and configure mobile phones and tablets for mobile data collection.
- Use smart phones/tablets for data collection
- Provide training to M/E staff and enumerators on mobile data collection mechanisms and software, and provide technical support and troubleshooting during all stages of mobile data collection, ensuring data is transferred from mobile devices and the devices are securely stored (sign in/sign out system for enumerators) and ensuring devices are charged
- Data analysis, including use of statistical software
- Perform data cleaning and ensuring data integrity before data analysis.
- Organizing and overseeing data entry and data consolidation.
- Perform descriptive univariate and bivariate data analysis using Excel Pivot tables or statistical software.
- Interpret frequency tables, bi-variate cross tables, the mean and median.

**Evaluation design**

- Contribute to the preparation of project evaluation and facilitating the field level work.
- Use and supervise quantitative, qualitative, and mixed methods of data collection in evaluation.

**Techniques for presenting information**

- Communicate clearly the findings of monitoring activities and reviews against targets set by the project.
- Compile data and indicators at the project's level for reporting in a clear and concise manner, providing all required information.
- Develop information products to share results of data analysis and monitoring.
- Drafting reports of assessments and surveys

**Knowledge Management and Learning**

- Organize the documentation of the project's M/E activities, results, and processes.
- Organize secondary data (internal and external sources).

**Cross-cutting themes**

- Monitor the general context through regular field visits and report issues affecting beneficiaries and intra-community relations.
- Ensure data collected is representative of population and demonstrate an understanding of social dynamics.
- Document the needs of target populations, including people of different sex, age, and vulnerability status, into all M/E systems and activities.
- Support or lead in the implementation of analyses and assessments of the impact of sex on outcomes, as required, including staff capacity building on tools and protocols; data collection; data analysis; and report writing.
- Ensure tools and systems are in place for learning and decision making on the needs of crisis-affected groups, including disaggregation of all data, development of mainstreamed and specific indicators, specific research questions, and targeted recommendations in reports

Perform other duties as assigned. The duties and responsibilities listed in this document are representative of the nature and level of work assigned and not necessarily comprehensive.

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

- Typically, bachelor’s degree in social sciences, public health, statistics, or international development, with experience in M/E. Equivalent combination of relevant education and experience may be substituted as appropriate.
- Typically, 3+ years of relevant and progressive experience with a humanitarian organization in implementing and overseeing monitoring and evaluation systems.
- Knowledge of data pitfalls, issues, and strategies for assessing the quality of collected data.
- Knowledge of commonly used probability and purposive sampling techniques and different methods of qualitative and quantitative data collection and analysis.
- Knowledge of descriptive univariate and bivariate data analysis using Excel Pivot tables or other advanced analysis software.
- Knowledge of indicators and their measurement in the different sectors of relevance.
- Understand the concept of participatory monitoring, evaluation and needs assessment.
- Excellent proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, Outlook, and PowerPoint.
- Strong training facilitator/presentation skills.
- Effective communication and interpersonal skills.
- Have analytical, conceptual, and strategic thinking skills.
- Manage performance by setting clear goals.
- High-level English proficiency (Speaking – Reading – Writing)
- High-level MISSION’S LANGUAGE proficiency (Speaking – Reading – Writing).
- Travel: 0-25%

**Ethical Conduct at International Medical Corps**

As part of a global, humanitarian team dedicated to saving lives, easing suffering, and building self-reliance, International Medical Corps staff are responsible for adhering to our *Code of Conduct and Ethics* and for knowing and abiding by International Medical Corps policies and standards. All staff play a vital role in preventing violations of our *Code of Conduct and Ethics*, including conflicts of interest, fraud, corruption, and any kind of exploitation or abuse. International Medical Corps is also committed to providing a safe and healthy work environment free of harassment, bullying, and other misconduct, enabling staff to build and maintain professional, respectful working relationships.

International Medical Corps prioritizes safeguarding the populations with whom we work from exploitation, neglect, or abuse of children and adults at risk, and/or any form of trafficking in persons. International Medical Corps is committed to engaging members of crisis-affected communities to participate in meaningful ways in a crisis response, including making informed decisions about the assistance they receive, mitigating potential risks, and holding us accountable for the commitments we make. All staff are expected to support International Medical Corps’ culture of accountability toward our stakeholders, particularly the crisis-affected communities and individuals we serve.

As part of International Medical Corps’ commitment to a speak-up culture and as one of the primary ways we collectively hold ourselves accountable for complying with the ethical principles and standards of conduct outlined in the *Code of Conduct and Ethics,* all staffare required to report suspected or actual misconduct or violations of organizational policies. Our *Code of Conduct and Ethics* and *Whistleblower Policy* prohibit any form of retaliation against whistleblowers or individuals who report a concern in good faith. Staff who violate these protections may be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment or contractual relationship with International Medical Corps.

**Equal Opportunities**

International Medical Corps is proud to provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national or ethnic origin, age, disability or status as a veteran.

jobs.title: 23246 Programme Officer (Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E)) (P)
jobs.description:
Launched in August 2021 with funding from the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), the Better Regional Migration Management (BRMM) Programme is IOM’s flagship labour migration programme in the East and Horn of Africa (EHOA). The programme supports efforts to strengthen labour migration governance, promote fair and ethical recruitment, enhance the protection of migrant workers and their families, and expand access to safe, orderly and regular labour migration pathways. Building on earlier phases, the current BRMM FY26–27 framework focuses on operationalising skills-to-employment, skills mobility and ethical recruitment systems for safe labour migration in the EHOA. It prioritises scalable and evidence-based interventions that improve access to decent work, strengthen national and regional labour migration systems, and contribute to reducing reliance on irregular migration routes. The programme will be implemented in four priority countries—Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia and Uganda—while continuing to support regional cooperation through the Regional Ministerial Forum on Migration (RMFM), Regional Economic Communities and relevant national institutions. It places particular emphasis on vulnerable groups, including youth, women, returnees, refugees and migrant workers, and supports interventions related to labour market information systems, public employment services, skills development and recognition, bilateral labour migration agreements, ethical recruitment, migrant protection, reintegration and engagement with countries of destination, including the Gulf States. A strong monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning approach, together with communication and visibility efforts, will support adaptive management, donor accountability and the documentation of results and lessons learned.

Under the overall supervision of the EHOA Regional Director and direct supervision of the Regional Program Management Officer, Labour Mobility and Human Development, the Programme Officer (Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E)) will be responsible for the implementation of the M&E aspects of the BRMM program in line with the expectations of the donors.

**Responsibilities**

1. Lead and be responsible for the overall Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) function of the BRMM project, including the development, updating and implementation of the project M&E plan, results framework, data collection tools, quality assurance mechanisms and monitoring procedures.
2. Provide regular technical M&E support to implementing missions, including guidance on data collection, activity monitoring, results tracking, reporting requirements, data quality and the accurate reflection of M&E plans in mission-level action plans.
3. Lead the collection, consolidation, analysis and use of BRMM project monitoring data to track progress against agreed indicators, inform programme decisions, identify implementation gaps and ensure that programme-related datasets are accurate and up to date.
4. Prepare BRMM biannual and annual reports by compiling, verifying and analysing inputs from implementing missions, ensuring that reported results are evidence-based, consistent with donor requirements and aligned with the project results framework.
5. Review and provide technical guidance on activity concept notes, mission activity reports and related workplans, ensuring that M&E requirements, indicators, targets, verification methods and follow-up actions are clearly and accurately reflected.
6. Undertake monitoring visits to implementing missions, as required, to assess progress, verify reported results, support corrective actions and provide hands-on guidance on the implementation of BRMM M&E processes.
7. Design, coordinate and conduct surveys, outcome monitoring exercises, impact assessments and other learning or evidence-generation activities when required by programme needs or requested by the donor.
8. Support adaptive management, learning and accountability by tracking risks, assumptions, lessons learned and emerging results; ensuring responsible data management; and providing evidence-based recommendations to improve BRMM implementation, reporting and donor accountability.
9. Perform such other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in Monitoring and Evaluation, Development Studies, Social Sciences, Statistics, Economics, Public Policy, Migration Studies, International Relations, Law, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with two years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with four years of relevant professional experience.
- Specific training or certification in Monitoring and Evaluation, Results-Based Management, data analysis, research methods, or impact assessment would be an advantage.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Experience in leading Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) functions for complex projects, including the development and implementation of M&E plans, results frameworks, indicators, data collection tools, quality assurance mechanisms and monitoring procedures;
- Demonstrated experience in Project Cycle Management (PCM), Results-Based Management (RBM), monitoring data collection, consolidation, analysis and use of evidence to inform programme implementation, reporting and adaptive management;
- Experience in providing technical M&E support to implementing missions or field teams, including guidance on activity monitoring, results tracking, data quality, reporting requirements and the integration of M&E plans into action plans;
- Experience in preparing high-quality donor reports, including biannual and annual reports, by compiling, verifying and analysing inputs from implementing partners or missions and ensuring alignment with results frameworks and donor requirements;
- Experience in reviewing activity concept notes, activity reports, workplans and related documentation to ensure that M&E requirements, indicators, targets, verification methods, risks, assumptions and follow-up actions are clearly reflected;
- Experience in conducting monitoring visits, surveys, outcome monitoring exercises, evaluations, impact assessments or other evidence-generation activities to assess progress, verify results and support programme learning;
- Experience in maintaining programme datasets, ensuring responsible data management and producing evidence-based recommendations to strengthen implementation, accountability, learning and donor reporting; and,
- Experience in labour migration, migrant protection, ethical recruitment, bilateral labour migration agreements, skills mobility or related migration governance programming would be an advantage.

**Skills**

- Strong communication and coordination skills, including the ability to present M&E findings clearly, provide practical guidance to implementing missions, and communicate evidence-based recommendations to programme teams, management and donors;
- Strong analytical skills, including the ability to collect, verify, consolidate and interpret quantitative and qualitative data for reporting, learning and decision-making;
- Excellent report-writing skills, including the ability to prepare evidence-based donor, biannual and annual reports aligned with results frameworks and reporting requirements;
- Ability to provide technical M&E guidance and capacity support to implementing missions, including on activity monitoring, data quality, reporting and the integration of M&E requirements into concept notes and action plans; and,
- Ability to conduct monitoring visits, surveys, outcome monitoring, impact assessments and learning exercises to support adaptive management and donor accountability.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) or a relevant EHoA languages is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

jobs.title: Consultant.e Power BI Developer – Industrialisation des rapports Business Intelligence
jobs.description:
**Titre : Consultant.e Power BI Developer – Industrialisation des rapports Business Intelligence**

**Date : 15/10/2029**

**Référence : ​HULO-TDR-BAR-2026-004​**

Cet appel à candidatures est ouvert à tous les consultants éligibles, en accord avec les procédures et principes de hulo.

**Contexte de la consultance :**

La Coopérative hulo, créée en juin 2021, est la première Société Coopérative Européenne (SCE) opérant dans le secteur humanitaire. Son objectif est d'accroître l'impact de l'aide humanitaire en renforçant les liens et la solidarité entre les acteurs de la logistique humanitaire et en améliorant les performances grâce à la mise en commun des ressources et de l'expertise en matière de logistique et de chaîne d'approvisionnement.

Hulo développe son écosystème Data afin de renforcer ses capacités en matière de Data Science, Business Analytics et Business Intelligence (BI). Le département Business Analytics & Research (BAR) développe et maintient notamment des rapports Power BI destinés aux équipes internes et aux organisations participant aux initiatives de hulo.

Certains rapports BI sont actuellement à l'état de prototype. Ils nécessitent des améliorations fonctionnelles et techniques, ainsi que la prise en compte des retours des utilisateurs, avant de pouvoir être déployés en production.

En parallèle, hulo souhaite structurer et industrialiser son environnement de développement BI. L'objectif est de disposer de processus et d'outils permettant de développer, tester, déployer et maintenir les rapports de manière plus standardisée, fiable et efficace.

Dans ce contexte, hulo souhaite recruter un.e consultant.e Power BI Developer pour accompagner le département BAR dans la finalisation des rapports existants et la mise en place d'un environnement adapté à leur développement et à leur maintenance à long terme.

L'environnement technique concerné s'appuie notamment sur :

- Microsoft Power BI
- Microsoft Fabric
- Microsoft Power Platform
- Microsoft SharePoint

**Perimètre général du travail attendu du.de la Consultant.e :**

L'objectif principal de cette consultance est d'améliorer la maturité opérationnelle de l'environnement Business Intelligence de hulo, en finalisant les rapports prioritaires et en mettant en place les pratiques et outils nécessaires à leur industrialisation.

La mission s'articulera autour de deux axes complémentaires.

**Axe 1 – Finalisation et mise en production des rapports BI:**

- Prendre connaissance des rapports Power BI existants et de leur niveau de maturité
- Échanger avec les équipes BAR et les utilisateurs concernés afin de recueillir et analyser leurs retours
- Identifier les écarts entre les prototypes actuels et les besoins opérationnels
- Améliorer les rapports sur les plans fonctionnel, visuel et technique
- Vérifier la cohérence des indicateurs, des mesures DAX, des filtres et des interactions, en fonction du périmètre de chaque rapport
- Améliorer les performances et la fiabilité des rapports lorsque cela est nécessaire
- Vérifier les règles d'accès aux données et les paramètres de partage applicables
- Organiser les tests et la validation avec les utilisateurs
- Préparer et réaliser le déploiement en production des rapports validés
- Documenter les rapports finalisés et les principaux choix techniques.

Les rapports à traiter seront priorisés conjointement avec hulo au démarrage de la mission.

**Axe 2 – Industrialisation du développement et de la maintenance BI:**

Le.la consultant.e devra analyser l'environnement existant et proposer puis mettre en place une organisation technique permettant de standardiser le cycle de vie des rapports BI.

Les travaux pourront notamment couvrir :

- La structuration des espaces de travail et des environnements de développement, de test et de production, en fonction des capacités disponibles dans l'environnement Microsoft de hulo
- La définition d'un processus de développement, de validation et de publication des rapports
- La mise en place de pratiques de gestion des versions et de suivi des modifications
- La standardisation des conventions de nommage, de la documentation et des éléments réutilisables
- L'amélioration de l'organisation des modèles sémantiques, des connexions aux sources de données et des dépendances entre rapports
- L'utilisation des fonctionnalités de Microsoft Fabric et de Power BI permettant de faciliter les déploiements et la maintenance
- L'identification des usages pertinents de Microsoft Power Platform pour automatiser certaines tâches ou étapes du processus BI
- L'utilisation de SharePoint pour organiser l’extranet donnant accès aux rapports BI
- La définition de bonnes pratiques en matière de sécurité, de gestion des accès, de tests et de contrôle qualité
- La préparation d'une documentation et le transfert de compétences à l'équipe BAR.

Le.la consultant.e devra privilégier les fonctionnalités et licences déjà disponibles chez hulo, en identifiant clairement les éventuels prérequis techniques ou financiers supplémentaires.

La mission ne consiste pas à reconstruire l'ensemble de l'écosystème BI de hulo, mais à mettre en place une approche pragmatique, adaptée aux besoins actuels et réutilisable pour les développements futurs.

Les taches décrites peuvent être menées à bien à 100% en distanciel.

**Qualifications et expérience:**

- Expérience confirmée en développement de rapports et de tableaux de bord Power BI
- Maîtrise de Power Query, du langage DAX et de la modélisation des données
- Expérience avec les pipelines de déploiement Power BI ou Fabric et les outils de gestion de versions
- Connaissance des modèles sémantiques partagés et des pratiques de gouvernance BI
- Expérience dans la gestion de rapports utilisés par plusieurs organisations ou catégories d'utilisateurs
- Expérience dans l'optimisation des performances et la fiabilisation des rapports BI
- Bonne connaissance de Microsoft Fabric et de son intégration avec Power BI
- Expérience dans la structuration d'environnements de développement, de test et de production
- Bonne connaissance des mécanismes de déploiement, de gestion des versions et de maintenance des solutions BI
- Maîtrise de Microsoft Power Platform, notamment pour l'automatisation de processus lorsque cela est pertinent
- Expérience avec SharePoint pour la gestion d’un extranet
- Bonne compréhension des enjeux de sécurité des données, de gestion des accès et de partage des rapports
- Capacité à recueillir les besoins des utilisateurs et à les traduire en améliorations fonctionnelles et techniques
- Capacité à produire une documentation claire et à transférer ses compétences à une équipe interne

**Management et lignes hiérarchiques**

Ce · tte consultant·e sera placé·e sous la responsabilité du directeur du département « Business Analytics & Research » et travaillera de concert avec un Data Scientist et un analyste métier.

**Processus de contractualisation :**

Le.la Consultant.e séléctionné.e sera contractualisé.e par hulo sur deux tranches :

- 1 tranche ferme pour une durée estimée de 10 à 15 **jours**,
- 1 tranche optionnelle pour une durée estimée de 20 à 30 jours

**Calendrier**

Tranche ferme - Novembre – décembre 2026

Tranche optionnelle - Février - Juin 2027

Sans obligation de travailler à temps plein pour hulo durant cette période.

**Candidature**

Hulo appelle à candidater pour la provision des services décrits ci-dessus. Les Consultant.e.s intéressé.e.s devront soumettre :

- Un CV présentant les compétences et expériences pertinentes
- Une proposition technique décrivant l'approche proposée pour les deux axes de la mission
- Une proposition financière indiquant le taux journalier et le coût total de la mission
- Des références ou exemples de missions comparables, si disponibles

**Critères de sélection:**

Les candidatures seront évaluées selon les critères suivants.:

- Expertise Power BI
- Expertise Microsoft Fabric
- Industrialisation et maintenance
- Maîtrise de Power Platform et SharePoint
- Compréhension des besoins métier
- Documentation et transfert de compétences
- Rapport qualité-prix

jobs.title: Responsable Eau Hygiène et Assainissement (EHA)
jobs.description:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

MSF recrute en urgence des Responsables Eau Hygiène et Assainissement, notamment dans le cadre des projets médicaux déployés face à l'épidémie Ebola en cours en République Démocratique du Congo.

**Votre mission**

En tant que responsable Eau Hygiène et Assainissement (EHA), vous avez pour mission d’assurer la mise œuvre des activités
d’approvisionnement en eau, de gestion des eaux usées, de lutte anti vectorielle et de gestion des déchets dans les structures de santé
supportées par MSF. De plus, vous êtes amené·e à apporter les secours non médicaux, dans votre domaine, aux populations déplacées
en raison de conflits, catastrophes naturelles, etc. Vous êtes responsable de la bonne mise en œuvre et du suivi des activités EHA au
sein de chaque projet/mission. Le tout selon les normes universelles de santé et les procédures MSF.

**Principales responsabilités :**

- Réaliser les évaluations en collaboration avec les équipes médicales, identifiant les besoins en eau, hygiène et assainissement ;
- Assurer la quantité et la qualité de l’eau dans toutes les activités du projet et pour nos bénéficiaires ;
- En collaboration avec l’équipe médicale, vous participez à l’hygiène hospitalière et mettez en place la lutte contre les vecteurs de maladies ;
- Dimensionner les ouvrages sanitaires (douches, latrines, etc.), les systèmes de traitements des eaux usées ainsi que leurs évacuations ;
- Assurer le suivi et la mise en œuvre de la gestion des déchets hospitaliers selon les recommandations MSF ainsi que le dimensionnement des zones à déchets pour les structures de santé ;

**Activités :**

- Gérer le matériel EHA du projet : achat, installation, maintenance et suivi ;
- Gérer les infrastructures du projet : construction et travaux de réhabilitation, interventions techniques dans le domaine de l’eau-hygiène et assainissement ;
- Encadrer et former les équipes logistiques, personnel national et/ou expatrié·e ;
- Apporter le support logistique EHA aux équipes médicales ;
- Participer à la définition des orientations opérationnelles et des objectifs logistiques du projet en collaboration avec les équipes médicales et le coordinateur du projet

**Profil recherché**

**Formation / Expériences :**

- Hydraulicien·ne, spécialiste en traitement de l’eau, gestion environnementale, hydrogéologue, Ingénieur·e/technicien·ne en assainissement et/ou autres qualifications techniques en rapport avec les domaines d’activité : gestion des déchets, lutte anti-vectorielle ou en contrôle infectieux.
- Au moins deux ans d’expériences professionnelles dans le domaine de l’EHA.
- Des compétences en encadrement ou en formation sont un plus.
- Une expérience à l’international et dans le milieu humanitaire est un atout.

Aptitudes :

- Disposition à travailler au sein d'équipes multiculturelles et pluridisciplinaires.
- Diplomatie, pédagogie, flexibilité, dynamisme.
- Bonnes capacités d’adaptation et d’organisation.

**Langues :**

- Français courant
- Anglais (B1)

**Disponibilité** : Engagement de **3 à 12 mois.** Missions de 3 mois pour les projets déployés face à l'épidémie Ebola en cours en République Démocratique du Congo.

**IMPORTANT : la durée de mission sur ce contexte est inférieure à 6 mois, de l'ordre de 3 mois. Merci d'indiquer durée de mission = 6 mois dans le formulaire de candidature, même si vous vous intéressé.e à un départ en RDC sur les projets de lutte contre Ebola.**

**Ce que nous offrons**

- Salaire en fonction de l'ancienneté et de l'expérience pertinente
- Prise en charge des frais liés à la mission (transport, visas, logement, vaccins, etc.).
- Assurances santé, rapatriement, retraite.
- Perspectives d’évolution : formations, accompagnement et développement de carrière dans un large éventail de contextes humanitaires.

**Pourquoi vous ?**

Vous êtes rigoureux·se, engagé·e, stratégique, à l’écoute, et vous souhaitez mettre vos compétences au service de populations en situation de vulnérabilité.

**Pour postuler :**

Merci de déposer votre candidature complète sur notre site, à ce lien (candidature spontanée) : [Responsable Eau Hygiène et Assainissement (EHA) | Médecins sans frontières](https://www.msf.fr/agir/rejoindre-nos-equipes/decouvrir-nos-metiers/responsable-eau-hygiene-et-assainissement-eha)

*Les candidatures féminines sont fortement encouragées.*

**Date limite de dépôt de candidatures :** 15 décembre 2026

jobs.title: 23411 Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse and Sexual Harassment (PSEAH) Officer (P)
jobs.description:
The Global Assisted Voluntary Return (AVR) program aims to provide AVR to migrants in the United States, receiving countries, and the Western Hemisphere, ensuring that returns are safe, dignified, and based on the migrants’ free, prior, and informed consent. Additionally, the program offers independent, needs-based post-arrival assistance at the request of countries of origin or receiving countries, always with the explicit consent of the migrants.

Addressing the Prevention of and Response to Sexual Exploitation and Abuse and Sexual Harassment (PSEAH) is a priority within IOM and a strong contributor to United Nations (UN) and Inter-Agency Standing Committee (IASC) efforts at both the global and country levels.

IOM’s PSEAH strategy focuses on five key pillars: 1) Leadership and Organizational Culture;2)Institutional Accountability and Transparency; 3) Capacity-Development, Training, and Communication; 4) Quality and Accessible Victim Assistance; 5) Partnership and Coordination.

Under the direct supervision of the Chief of Mission or Head of Office and in close coordination with the Regional PSEAH Officer and the global PSEAH Unit at Headquarters, as well as relevant thematic specialists within the Country Office, Regional Office, and HQ, the PSEAH Officer will be responsible and accountable for supporting IOM’s PSEAH prevention and response efforts at the country level, providing technical oversight and management support, in line with a victim-centred approach. The PSEAH Officer will also be an active member of the inter-agency PSEA Network or Task Force in-country.

**Responsibilities**

**COORDINATION:**

- Facilitate the development of an operational PSEAH Work Plan, in line with IOM and United Nations (UN) strategic frameworks, and in coordination with the global PSEAH Unit, Regional PSEAH Officer, and senior management of the Country Office.
- Facilitate the inclusion of PSEAH within the IOM Country Office Strategy, Crisis Response Plans/Migrant Response Plans, or other appeals as appropriate; ensure Sexual Exploitation and Abuse and Harassment (SEAH) risks are considered in the Country Office risk register and that PSEAH is mainstreamed in proposal development, programming, monitoring and evaluation, and budgeting; develop PSEAH programming and liaise with relevant donors.
- Contribute to the in-country interagency PSEA Network (support in the development of the collective PSEA workplan, risk management plan, PSEA Strategies, Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) for an inter-agency Community-Based Complaint Mechanism, etc.) and actively participate in IOM internal coordination initiatives.
- Provide technical support in collection, analysis, and use of data related to PSEAH efforts, in line with relevant IOM data protection standards, to showcase trends, results, and impact.
- Showcase PSEAH results and good practices through internal and external reporting, visibility materials, and knowledge-sharing initiatives in coordination with global and regional PSEAH teams.

**PREVENTION:**

- Undertake assessments to identify potential SEAH risks and define appropriate mitigation measures; in coordination with relevant units, ensure that risk mitigation measures are embedded within IOM programming, operations, and administration.
- Develop a PSEAH training plan for the Country Office and coordinate, organize, and deliver PSEAH trainings for IOM personnel, implementing partners, and key institutional stakeholders; support the work of PSEAH focal points within the country to deliver key messaging and trainings as appropriate.
- On a regular basis, compile and report data on the number of IOM personnel and partners trained in-country on PSEAH in coordination with HR. Oversee the registration of all participants within the IOM system and the timely issuance of certificates.
- Continually share key messages on PSEAH, including information on reporting requirements and support mechanisms at the country and global levels in close coordination with relevant colleagues.
- Develop, localize, contextualize, and implement communication and awareness-raising strategies and tools to ensure appropriate PSEAH messaging and understanding of prohibited behaviors, reporting channels, and available assistance.
- Map existing Country Office community engagement projects and work with project/programme managers to gather community inputs, insert PSEAH messages, and strengthen and/or establish safe and accessible reporting channels.

**RESPONSE:**

- Support the development and mapping of country-specific interagency victim assistance pathways and/or existing IOM programmes to refer victims/survivors for assistance; ensure up-to-date information on available assistance services is accessible in all areas where IOM operates in country; coordinate with gender-based violence and/or child protection colleagues to support the strengthening of victim services within the country and/or programming.
- Safely respond to SEAH disclosures and coordinate referrals for victim/survivor assistance in line with country, regional, or global support mechanisms and ensure coordination with the Regional PSEAH Officer and the global SEAH case management team.
- Regularly monitor safety and other risks for SEAH victims/survivors in coordination with the Regional PSEAH Officer and the global SEAH case management team; adjust response to mitigate risks; ensure regular assessment of victims’/survivors’ needs.
- Undertake duty travel as required.
- Perform such other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in law, International Relations, Psychology, Social Sciences, Development Studies and Planning, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with two years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with four years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Professional experience in the fields of sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, protection, child protection, gender-based violence, accountability to affected populations (AAP), gender mainstreaming and/or humanitarian affairs;
- Experience in management of sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, child protection or gender-based violence cases;
- Strong coordination experience within the UN system and amongst interagency partners, including governments, Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs), and communities;
- Experience in developing and facilitating trainings, in particular capacity-building, and communication materials to promote behavior change;
- Experience in undertaking risk assessments, in coordination with relevant offices, communities, partners, and UN and other key stakeholders;
- Experience in proposal development and the creation of standard operating procedures and tools; and,
- Experience in mainstreaming PSEAH, gender-based violence, child protection, protection, gender, or accountability to affected populations.

**Skills**

- Demonstrated ability to work across a wide variety of sectors/teams on cross-cutting themes;
- Good written and oral communication skills, effective in representation and liaison with external partners;
- Ability to organize work, work independently and prioritize work under pressure, coordinate multiple tasks, maintain attention to detail, and coordinate with a variety of stakeholders;
- Ability to work with affected individuals with empathy, sensitivity and a victim-centred approach;
- Knowledge and understanding of IOM’s institutional approach on PSEAH and Ethics and related strategies, policies, rules and regulations; and,
- Ability to work with and maintain strict confidentiality, when necessary.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English and French is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

jobs.title: Trainer for "The Use of GIS in Humanitarian Operation" - Only Local Candidates from Madrid
jobs.description:
**Location:** Madrid, Spain - due to budget limitation we can only consider applicants from Madrid
**Training Dates:** 9–10 November 2026
**Daily Schedule:** 09:00 AM – 4:00 PM
**Delivery Mode:** In-person
**Participants:** 2 professionals
**Engagement:** Short-term training consultancy

## Project Overview

Accordemy® is seeking an experienced GIS trainer and consultant to deliver a two-day, in-person professional development program titled **"The Use of GIS in Humanitarian Projects"** in Madrid, Spain.

The program aims to strengthen participants' ability to apply Geographic Information Systems (GIS) in humanitarian operations, project planning, land and asset management, risk assessment, and evidence-based decision-making.

The training should emphasize practical applications, real-world scenarios, and the effective use of geospatial information to support humanitarian project implementation and management.

## Proposed Training Topics

The program is expected to cover:

1. **GIS Applications in Humanitarian Projects** — GIS for humanitarian planning, coordination, needs assessment, and operational management.
2. **Geospatial Data Collection and Management** — Spatial datasets, data integration, mapping layers, and geographic information management.
3. **Spatial Analysis and Risk Assessment** — Identifying vulnerable areas, assessing geographic risks, and supporting project prioritization.
4. **Land and Asset Mapping** — Mapping land parcels, infrastructure, resources, and project-affected locations.
5. **GIS for Evidence-Based Decision-Making** — Spatial suitability assessment, comparison of alternatives, and management decision support.
6. **GIS Visualization and Reporting** — Thematic maps, dashboards, analytical outputs, and communicating geographic findings to stakeholders.
7. **AI Integration with GIS** — Practical applications of artificial intelligence, automation, and emerging geospatial technologies.
8. **GIS Data Security and Stakeholder Information Management** — Data privacy, access control, secure sharing, and responsible management of sensitive geographic information.
9. **Practical GIS Exercises** — Hands-on demonstrations and case studies relevant to humanitarian and development projects.

The final training outline will be agreed upon with the selected consultant, considering their technical expertise and recommendations.

## Consultant Qualifications

Candidates should demonstrate:

- Strong professional experience in Geographic Information Systems and spatial analysis.
- **Proficiency in ArcGIS and proven experience teaching or delivering professional training using ArcGIS.**
- Experience designing and delivering instructor-led GIS training programs.
- Ability to explain technical GIS concepts clearly to professionals and managers.
- Practical knowledge of GIS applications in humanitarian assistance, international development, land management, or related fields.
- Familiarity with AI-assisted geospatial analysis and GIS data management practices.
- Excellent English communication and presentation skills.
- Availability to deliver the training in person in Madrid on the specified dates.

Experience working with humanitarian organizations, development agencies, NGOs, or international institutions would be an advantage.

## Expected Deliverables

- A finalized two-day training outline.
- Instructor-led delivery with practical demonstrations.
- Relevant training presentations, exercises, and example datasets.
- Hands-on activities that allow participants to apply the concepts.
- Supporting technical reference materials, where appropriate./

jobs.title: Grants Manager Lebanon
jobs.description:
**Position**: Grants Manager Lebanon

**Location**: Beirut, Lebanon

**Reporting Relationship**: Country Head of Programmes

**Family Duty Station**: NO

**Starting date**: ASAP

**Application deadline**: 15/11/2026

**Contract Type**: Expatriate (International)

**Working Context**

WeWorld has been working in Lebanon since 2006 and is currently supporting vulnerable refugee, IDP and host community populations through WASH, Food Security and Livelihoods, Local Economic Development, Education and Social Cohesion in Bekaa, Baalbek-Hermel, Akkar, Saida and Beirut. Our interventions span immediate emergency response and recovery in view of building preparedness and longer-term resilience for populations affected by conflict and/or displacement. The operation is run by over 50 employees, divided in three offices (Beirut, Zahle and Saida). We work closely with local partners, including NGOs and institutional actors at different levels, and are part of large consortia with other actors.

**Purpose of the Role**

The **Grants Manager** is responsible for leading and overseeing country-level grants management processes, from funding opportunity identification and proposal development to donor reporting, grant amendments and closeout, ensuring quality, timeliness and compliance with donor requirements and WeWorld procedures.

Reporting to the Country Head of Programmes, the Grants Manager operates with a high degree of autonomy within agreed priorities and delegated authority, while ensuring alignment with the country strategy and internal approval procedures.

The role provides functional coordination to Project Managers and relevant technical and support departments, ensuring clear responsibilities, effective collaboration and timely delivery of grants-related outputs. This coordination does not imply direct line management of Project Managers, who remain responsible for project implementation and the accuracy of their respective contributions.

The Grants Manager is also responsible for strengthening grants management systems, tools and procedures, identifying compliance risks and escalating issues requiring strategic or management decisions to the Country Head of Programmes.

**Main Tasks and Responsibilities**

**Proposal Development and Fundraising**

- Contribute to the development and regular review of the country fundraising strategy with the Country Head of Programmes and Senior Management Team, translating donor mapping, funding trends, programme priorities and pipeline analysis into recommendations on funding opportunities and donor engagement
- Build and maintain a donor database and an updated funding pipeline
- Proactively identify, assess and share opportunities aligned with WeWorld’s strategy and goals in Lebanon
- Lead and own proposal development processes, including grant writing, setting realistic calendars, allocating and agreeing contributions, functionally coordinating Project Managers and other contributors, and consolidating inputs. Be accountable for the quality, coherence, completeness and donor compliance of the final proposal package, ensuring appropriate technical and financial review, internal approval and timely submission. The Country Head of Programmes will provide strategic oversight and approval in line with WeWorld’s procedures
- Ensure learning from implementation and WeWorld’s programmatic strategy are duly taken into account when writing proposals
- Keep WeWorld’s profile up to date and adequately archive all proposal-related documents in WeWorld’s SharePoint files

**Compliance and Reporting**

- Own and regularly update the Grants Tracker and reporting calendar, ensuring clear responsibilities, internal deadlines and visibility of grant obligations, deliverables and compliance risks
- Develop, maintain and oversee the application of guidelines and workflows for proposal development, donor reporting, grant amendments and closeout
- Support the MEAL department and Project Managers with partner due diligence processes and implementation monitoring
- Lead the donor reporting process through functional coordination of Project Managers and relevant departments, setting internal deadlines, consolidating and reviewing inputs, and ensuring consistency between narrative and financial reports. Be accountable for the quality, completeness and donor compliance of report packages and their timely submission following the required internal reviews and approvals
- Provide guidance and build the capacity of Project Managers on grants management, reporting and donor requirements; monitor follow-up on agreed actions and escalate unresolved gaps or delays to the Country Head of Programmes

**Project Cycle Management**

- Coordinate grants-related preparation and follow-up for project kick-off, review and closeout meetings with Project Managers and relevant departments, ensuring grant conditions, reporting obligations, roles and deadlines are understood and tracked, under the strategic oversight of the Country Head of Programmes
- Coordinate guidance on donor compliance throughout implementation, maintain oversight of grants-related risks and corrective actions, and escalate significant issues to the Country Head of Programmes.
- Coordinate routine donor communication on grants matters within delegated authority, seeking approval for commitments or changes requiring management authorization
- Ensure the Project archiving system is up to date: conduct periodic reviews of project documentation, ensuring proper uploading and archiving by the Project Managers
- Coordinate the preparation, review and submission of grant amendment requests with Project Managers and Finance, ensuring their quality and compliance with donor procedures and obtaining the required internal approvals

The duties and responsibilities set forth above are not exhaustive and the role holder may be required to perform additional duties requested by the Line Manager. Proper handover must be ensured before the end of the assignment.

**ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENTS**

**Qualifications and Knowledge**

- Master’s degree or equivalent in International Cooperation or a related field
- Good computer skills are required
- Knowledge of institutional donor procedures (AICS, EU, AFD, UN)
- Fluency in both written and verbal English is mandatory
- Fluency in both written and verbal Italian is mandatory

**Professional experiences**

- At least 4 years of specific experience in the field of international cooperation
- At least 3 years of specific experience in Grants management
- Proven experience in independently managing proposal development, donor reporting and compliance processes, including coordination of contributions from multiple stakeholders
- Experience working with institutional donors such as AICS, EU, OCHA and UN agencies

**Skills and Abilities**

- Strong grant writing, donor compliance and functional coordination skills, with the ability to independently manage grants processes, coordinate contributors and ensure timely delivery and quality standards
- Excellent organizational and time management skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and tight deadlines
- Sound judgement, problem-solving and decision-making skills, including the ability to identify risks and escalate issues requiring management decisions
- Strong leadership, planning and teamwork skills, with the ability to influence and coordinate colleagues across different functions
- Proactive and dynamic attitude
- Ability to adapt and work under constraint, under pressure and in complex and multicultural contexts
- Interpersonal skills and intercultural approach
- Good listening and communication skills
- Good negotiation and conflict resolution skills
- Strong commitment to the Mission of WeWorld, genuine interest in international cooperation development topics
- Demonstrates integrity with regards to NGO values and ethical standards
- Displays cultural, gender, religion, nationality and age sensitivity and adaptability
- Treats all people fairly without favouritism

**Desirable requirements**

- Knowledge of Arabic would be considered an asset
- Previous work experience in Lebanon would be considered an asset

**WHAT WE OFFER**

**Type of contract**: a 6 (six) month contract, renewable subject to funding availability

**Economic conditions**: according to WeWorld Expatriates Compensation Policy Base Salary (2.840€ - 3.440€ monthly) + Contributions reflecting role complexity and hardship level of the duty station + Housing contribution

**Wellbeing & Inclusion**: One day of paid menstrual leave per month. We promote a positive and inclusive work environment based on psychological safety, respect, and team empowerment.

**Flight ticket**: One round-trip air ticket every 12 months of service (between country of residence and duty station)

**Health insurance**: covered

**Family Duty Station**: NO

**R&R**: NO

**Equal Opportunities**

We are dedicated to fostering an inclusive and respectful workplace where everyone has equal access to opportunities. Employment decisions are based on merit, qualifications, and organizational needs, without regard to gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, ethnicity, nationality, religion or belief, age, family or parental status, disability or any other status protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Case Management Officer
jobs.company: International Network For Aid Relief and Assistance
jobs.description:
**ABOUT INARA:**

International Network for Aid, Relief and Assistance (INARA) is a U.S.-registered 501(c)(3) humanitarian organization founded in 2015 by Arwa Damon. Established in response to critical gaps in the humanitarian system, INARA works to support children affected by conflict, displacement, and natural and human-induced disasters who are often unable to access sustained medical and psychosocial care.

INARA delivers integrated, child-centered programming that combines life-saving interventions with long-term recovery support. The organization focuses on children facing complex and overlapping vulnerabilities, including injury, trauma, disability, and exclusion from essential services. Through a multidisciplinary approach, INARA provides access to medical treatment, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), and coordinated case management, ensuring continuity of care beyond the immediate emergency phase.

INARA delivers integrated, child-centered programming across multiple sectors to support children affected by crisis. Its interventions include comprehensive medical and rehabilitative care, providing specialized treatment and long-term follow-up; mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), offering trauma-informed and community-based services; and livelihood and economic empowerment initiatives that strengthen household stability. INARA also supports education in emergencies by creating safe and inclusive learning environments, implements water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) interventions to improve health conditions, and maintains a rapid emergency response capacity to deliver immediate medical, psychosocial, food, and non-food assistance during acute crises.

## Vision

A world where every child has the agency to create a dignified life.

## Mission

Fostering a future where we empower children to shape their own dignified lives.

## Purpose

Enhancing children’s capacity to shape their own fulfilling futures through integrated health, empowerment, and community-driven interventions.

**JOB SUMMARY:**

Under the responsibility of the Country Director the Case Management Officer is responsible for overseeing and coordinating comprehensive care and support services for patients. This role involves assessing patients’ needs, developing care plans, and collaborating with internal and external stakeholders to ensure the delivery of high-quality and culturally competent services. The officer will be an integral part of a multidisciplinary team, working to enhance the overall well-being and outcome of target population.

## **Key Responsibilities**

Include and may not be limited to:

**Assessment and Planning:**

- Conduct comprehensive assessments of clients' physical, emotional, social, and financial needs.
- Develop tailored care plans in collaboration with clients, families, and relevant stakeholders.
- Regularly review and adjust care plans to ensure relevance and effectiveness.
- Work with a multidisciplinary team to integrate various perspectives into the assessment and planning process.
- Facilitate crisis intervention planning, anticipating potential emergencies.
- Demonstrate cultural sensitivity in the assessment and planning process.

**Coordination and Collaboration:**

- Establish effective communication channels with healthcare professionals, social services, and other relevant organizations.
- Coordinate and liaise with agencies, organizations, and external healthcare service providers to ensure a seamless continuum of care for clients.
- Facilitate collaboration among different stakeholders involved in the client's care journey.
- Act as a central point of contact for information exchange between relevant parties.
- Advocate for streamlined communication to enhance the efficiency of care coordination efforts to ensure accurate identification and addressing of the patient’s needs.
- Support and engage in regular team meetings to discuss patients’ progress, challenges, and adjustments to care plans.
- Ensure that all relevant parties are informed promptly of changes in care plans and patients' needs.
- Utilize effective communication strategies to address potential conflicts or challenges in the coordination process.
- Maintain up-to-date knowledge of local social services and healthcare resources to enhance collaboration efforts.
- Provide operational and administrative support across departments when needed to ensure seamless field and office execution.

**Patients Support and Education:**

- Provide emotional support and practical assistance to patients and their families throughout their care journey.
- Educate patients on available resources, services, and self-care strategies to empower them in decision-making.
- Foster a supportive environment for patients to actively participate in their care plans.
- Ensure patients are well-informed about their medical conditions, treatment options, and recovery expectations.
- Tailor supportive services to address the unique needs and preferences of each client.
- Collaborate with patients to set realistic goals and milestones within the care plan.
- Regularly assess clients' understanding of their health situation and adjust education efforts accordingly.
- Assist patients in accessing necessary services.
- Provide information on community support groups, workshops, or relevant events to enhance clients' well-being.
- Foster a compassionate and empathetic approach to patient support, recognizing the emotional challenges they may face.

**Cash Distribution- when needed**

- Cash distribution to the beneficiaries
- Documentation of receipts
- Confirmation of the bank details.
- Follow up if any payment hasn’t been received by the beneficiaries

**Program Development:**

- Participate in the development of educational materials and resources for patients and their families.
- Implementation of quality improvement initiatives to enhance patient care outcomes.
- Collect and analyze data to evaluate the effectiveness of case management interventions.
- Stay updated on current trends, best practices, and evidence-based approaches in physical health case management.

**Documentation and Reporting:**

- Maintain accurate and up-to-date patients’ records, ensuring confidentiality and compliance with regulations.
- Document interventions, assessments, and coordination efforts in a systematic and organized manner.
- Generate regular reports on patients’ progress, outcomes, and any changes to care plans.
- Ensure that all documentation aligns with INARA's standards and policies.
- Provide detailed and accurate information for internal and external reporting requirements.
- Collaborate with the administrative team to streamline documentation processes.
- Implement a robust filing system to retrieve and reference patients’ records as needed easily.
- Conduct regular audits of documentation to identify any discrepancies or areas for improvement.
- Prepare reports for supervisory review, ensuring clarity and completeness.
- Communicate effectively with the team regarding any updates or changes in documentation procedures.

## **Requirements & Qualifications**

- Bachelor’s degree in social work, Psychology, Nursing, paramedical specialty or a related field. Master’s degree is a plus.
- Strong interpersonal and communication skills.
- Ability to work collaboratively in a multidisciplinary team.
- Knowledge of local social services and healthcare resources.
- Familiarity with relevant laws and regulations governing patient care.
- Proven experience in case management and care coordination
- Experience working with vulnerable and multicultural populations including refugees and children with medical needs.

jobs.description:
**London UK**

**£45,728 to £61,034 per annum pro rata inclusive**

The London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine (LSHTM) is one of the world’s leading public health universities. Our mission is to improve health and health equity in the UK and worldwide; working in partnership to achieve excellence in public and global health research, education and translation of knowledge into policy and practice.

The UK-Public Health Rapid Support Team (UK-PHRST) has an exciting opportunity to recruit a Research Fellow or Assistant Professor in Epidemiology.

UK-PHRST is a partnership between the UK Health Security Agency, and international research partners, led by LSHTM. UK-PHRST supports partners in LMICs to prepare for, prevent, detect and respond rapidly to disease outbreaks.

Based in the Department of Infectious Disease Epidemiology & Dynamics, the post-holder’s responsibilities will range from providing direct operational support to outbreak response, to co-identification, development and implementation of substantial research and capacity strengthening projects. As a member of the UK-PHRST deployable team, the post-holder must be prepared to travel overseas at short notice for periods of typically 6-8 weeks, most frequently to ODA-eligible countries.

The post-holder must have a postgraduate degree, ideally a doctoral degree (for Research Fellow) or a doctoral degree (for Assistant Professor) in epidemiology, and expertise in the control of infectious disease, including outbreak investigation and response.

The post is full-time 35 hours per week, 1.0 FTE and fixed-term until 31 March 2029 with the possibility of a two-year extension, subject to funding. The post is funded by the NIHR and is available from 01 October 2026.

The salary will be on the LSHTM salary scale, for Research Fellow Grade 6 in the range £45,728 -£51,872 or for Assistant Professor Grade 7 in the range £53,317 - £61,034 per annum pro rata (inclusive of London Weighting). The post will be subject to the LSHTM terms and conditions of service. Annual leave entitlement is 30 working days per year, pro rata for part time staff. In addition to this there are discretionary “Wellbeing Days”. Membership of the Pension Scheme is available. The post is based in London at LSHTM.

Applications should be made on-line via our [jobs website](https://jobs.lshtm.ac.uk/). Online applications will be accepted by the automated system until 10pm of the closing date. Any queries regarding the application process may be addressed to jobs@lshtm.ac.uk Please quote reference EPH-EPED-2026-07.

The supporting statement section should set out how your qualifications, experience and training meet **each** of the selection criteria. Please provide one or more paragraphs addressing each criterion. The supporting statement is an essential part of the selection process and thus a failure to provide this information will mean that the application will not be considered. An answer to any of the criteria such as "Please see attached CV" will not be considered acceptable.

Closing date for the receipt of applications is **Monday 26 October 2026.**

The London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine is committed to being an equal opportunities employer. We believe that when people feel respected and included, they can be more creative, successful, and happier at work. While we have more work to do, we are committed to building an inclusive workplace, a community that everyone feels a part of, which is safe, respectful, supportive and enables all to reach their full potential.
