jobs.title: Executive Director Partnerships, Advocacy, Engagement & Resource Mobilisation
jobs.description:
Would you like to shape how one of the world’s leading humanitarian organisations builds partnerships, and mobilises resources needed to support people affected by displacement?

This is an opportunity to bring your leadership, external engagement and resource mobilisation experience to a mission with human impact. As Executive Director for Partnerships, Advocacy, Engagement & Resource Mobilisation (PAER) at the Danish Refugee Council (DRC), you will strengthen DRC’s voice, relationships and funding base - positioning DRC as a trusted partner and advocate for displaced people.

You will join DRC at an important time for the humanitarian sector, as needs continue to rise while funding and humanitarian space are under increasing pressure. As a member of the Executive Management Team, you will help set DRC’s strategic direction and lead a broad global portfolio spanning strategic partnerships, institutional and private fundraising, advocacy, external communications, press, international representations, and asylum and refugee rights.

**About the job**

Reporting to the Secretary General, you will set direction for DRC’s global partnerships, advocacy, engagement and resource mobilisation agenda. Working closely with the Executive Management Team, country leadership, and senior functional leaders, you will expand high-level relationships with institutional donors, global foundations, private contributors, private-sector partners to secure more sustainable and flexible funding.

You will harness DRC’s global advocacy, communications and press efforts across countries, regions, representations and headquarters, strengthening DRC’s position as a relevant influencing and dialogue partner for donors, political stakeholders, peers and the wider humanitarian system. You will also oversee DRC’s representations in Geneva, Brussels and Berlin, as well as our representative presence in London, and provide leadership for the Asylum & Refugee Rights department and its specialised expertise in asylum procedures, refugee rights and legal aid.

You will lead and develop leaders across the PAER portfolio, foster collaboration across the organisation, and ensure sound people planning, employee well-being and financial management. Based at DRC’s headquarters in Copenhagen, you will represent DRC internally and externally, communicate its priorities with clarity and build trusted relationships across cultures, sectors and geographies.

The impact you will make:

- Shape DRC’s global strategy and PAER agenda as a member of the Executive Management Team, helping translate organisational priorities into coordinated action.
- Expand institutional and private partnerships to secure more sustainable and flexible funding for DRC’s humanitarian mission.
- Strengthen DRC’s global advocacy, communications and influence on displacement-related agendas with donors, policymakers and humanitarian partners.
- Lead DRC’s international representations with a focus on external relations, and its asylum and refugee rights portfolio, connecting specialist expertise with global engagement.
- Develop senior leaders and promote effective collaboration, people management and financial stewardship across the PAER portfolio.

**About you**

You are a purpose-driven executive who combines political judgement, entrepreneurial energy and strong relationship-building skills. You understand the global humanitarian and development landscape and can translate opportunities into lasting partnerships, influence and income. You are an inclusive, inspiring and empowering leader with the ability to create momentum across a complex international organisation.

What you will bring: ​​​​​​​

- Senior-level experience building institutional and private partnerships in the international humanitarian or development sector.
- Deep knowledge of humanitarian funding to forced displacement and related global policy priorities.
- A proven record in resource mobilisation, high-level advocacy, external engagement and policy dialogue.
- Political acumen and credibility with senior government, donor, foundation and private-sector stakeholders.
- Executive leadership experience and an inclusive, entrepreneurial and high-integrity leadership style.

All employees in DRC should master DRC's core competencies: Communicating, Taking the lead, Collaborating, Striving for excellence and Demonstrating integrity.

**We offer**

Contract length: Permanent
Work location: Lyngbyvej 100, 2100 Copenhagen Ø, just by Ryparken station
Salary and conditions will be in accordance with the agreement between DRC and Lederaftalen between Dansk Arbejdsgiverforening and Lederne (agreement for managers), which can be found here: www.lederne.dk. This is a national position for which local terms and conditions apply.
We welcome all nationalities to apply for the role. If you do not have the existing right to work in Denmark, DRC will support with applying and paying for a work permit.

**Further information**

For questions regarding the vacancy please contact: Georgie Horn, Senior Associate Korn Ferry: **DRC\_PAER@KornFerry.com**

For more information about the Danish Refugee Council, please visit our website [**drc.ngo**](https://drc.ngo/).

**Danish Refugee Council is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive and positive work environment based on mutual respect for all employees. All applicants are considered for employment regardless of personal characteristics or attributes.**

jobs.title: 22969 Protection Officer (P)
jobs.description:
The International Organization for Migration (IOM) in Liberia is working in close collaboration with the Government of Liberia, United Nations agencies, Civil Society Organizations (CSOs), and international partners to address the complex migration, humanitarian, and development challenges exacerbated by decades of conflict, displacement, and instability.

Under the supervision of the Chief of Mission and in close cooperation with relevant departments at Headquarters (HQs) and Regional Office (RO), the Protection Officer will be responsible and accountable for managing, coordinating and overseeing the Country Office’s (CO) Protection Programme activities and strategies, including child protection, counter-trafficking, violence against women and girls, men and boys, Disability Inclusion, assistance to vulnerable migrants, and overall specialized protection programming in the CO.

**Responsibilities**

1. Provide technical advice to CO management and programme teams on the design and delivery of protection programming and support in leading the protection Mainstreaming across relevant programme activities to strengthen safe programming and the protection capacity of staff and partners.
2. Contribute to the design of, implement, and monitor migrant protection interventions in line with IOM protection standards, protection principles, and rights-based approaches, providing inputs on strategic options to the COM and positioning IOM's response to the evolving needs of migrants.
3. Provide technical guidance on protection case management, vulnerability screening, protection assessments, and assistance to migrants in vulnerable situations to raise the quality and consistency of case handling across the CO.
4. Develop and maintenance referral pathways and coordination mechanisms with governmental, UN, Non-Governmental Organisations (NGOs) and civil society protection actors to widen vulnerable migrants’ access to specialised services.
5. Facilitate protection risk analysis and integrate mitigation measures throughout programme design and implementation to embed protection mainstreaming across operational activities and reduce risks to affected populations.
6. Review and monitor compliance with IOM protection standards, data protection principles, Protection from Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PSEAH) commitments and other relevant institutional policies and frameworks to identify gaps and recommend corrective action.
7. Conduct CO protection assessments and analyses of protection risks, service gaps, and emerging trends affecting migrants and vulnerable populations to generate evidence that informs CO strategy and programme adjustments.
8. Manage the implementation of protection projects by monitoring activities, expenditures and deliverables, and bringing issues to the attention of the Resources Management Officer (RMO) and the COM with proposed solutions for timely corrective action.
9. Provide operational management, guidance, supervision , and mentorship to relevant programme staff, advising on programmatic strategy and implementation, resource allocation and operational challenges, and deliver trainings that builds team performance and capacity.
10. Participate in technical coordination meetings, protection working groups and inter-agency forums to promote IOM’s technical positions that strengthen partnerships and the coherence of the collective protection response.
11. Prepare technical inputs for donor reports, concept notes and project documentation and share programme information with relevant stakeholders for donor confidence and transparency.
12. jobs.title: External Endline Evaluation Consultancy for Promoting Access to Water and Education (PAWE) Project Mandera County.
jobs.description:
**Terms of Reference**

**External Endline Evaluation Consultancy**

**Promoting Access to Water and Education (PAWE) Project Mandera County**

**IRK/PAWE/CONSUL/002/10/2026**

**ISSUED ON: Friday, 16th October 2026**

**CLOSING DATE: Thursday, 22nd October 2026 at 11:00 AM**

**October, 2026**

**Project: Promoting Access to Water and Education (PAWE) Project**
**Activity: External Endline Evaluation**
**Location: Mandera County**
**Duration: 28 days**

**1.0 BACKGROUND**
IR Kenya started operations in Kenya in 1993 through a local CBO in Mandera District, Northern Kenya. It opened its fully-fledged office in March 2006 at the height of the drought in the Horn of Africa. Since then, it has been providing humanitarian and development assistance to vulnerable communities. Over these years, IRK has remarkably changed the lives of the vulnerable and disadvantaged communities. In January 2010 and October 2011, IRK extended its operation to Wajir County and Garissa County, to serve both the local community and refugees at Dadaab Camp. Islamic Relief Kenya is currently implementing programmes in the following sectors: Health and Nutrition; WASH (Water, Sanitation and Hygiene); Sustainable Livelihoods and Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR); Child Welfare/Protection & Education; and Emergency Response. Over the years, IR Kenya has implemented various development and relief activities which have remarkably changed the lives of vulnerable and disadvantaged communities in Garissa, Wajir, Mandera, Kilifi, Marsabit, Tana River and Kajiado Counties.
IR Kenya commits to standards which ascribe to program quality and improved programming. This obliges us to conduct an end-line evaluation study for PAWE Project – Mandera County, focusing on the specific areas of the project interventions to document intended and unintended changes that can be attributed to the project.
**2.0 PROJECT SUMMARY**
The Promoting Access to Water and Education (PAWE) Project is an 18-month integrated community support initiative implemented by Islamic Relief Kenya (IRK) in Mandera County. The project aims to empower vulnerable communities by addressing critical gaps in Education and Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH). It seeks to improve access to inclusive, safe and accessible education for children while increasing the availability of clean and potable water for households, schools and food production, thereby contributing to improved well-being and resilience among targeted communities.
The project combines infrastructure development with service improvement and capacity strengthening. Key interventions include the construction and rehabilitation of school infrastructure and boreholes, provision of education and learning materials, improvement of school WASH facilities, and installation of solar-powered water systems and associated infrastructure. Sustainability and community ownership are embedded in the project through capacity building of beneficiaries and relevant community structures, alongside active engagement of government departments at national, county and sub-county levels in the monitoring and technical supervision of Education and WASH interventions. The project is aligned with the Mandera County Integrated Development Plan (CIDP) 2023–2027, IR Kenya's strategic priorities, and relevant NDMA plans.
Project goal/impact: Improved learning outcomes for children and enhanced access to clean, potable water for households in Mandera County
Project outcomes:
**Outcome 1:** Improved education facilities and materials for schools in Mandera County
**Outcome 2:** Increased access to potable water for targeted households and schools
Project outputs:
**Output 1.1:** 1500 pupils have access to quality education
**Output 2.1:** 3,000 households and 2 schools have access to clean portable water for household and livestock use
**3.0 Purpose and Objectives of The Endline Evaluation**
As the project approaches completion, IRK seeks to engage a qualified consultant/consultancy firm to conduct an independent external endline evaluation which will assess the extent to which the PAWE Project has achieved its intended objectives, outcomes and results against the established baseline and results framework. The evaluation will examine the relevance, effectiveness, efficiency, impact and sustainability of the interventions, identify intended and unintended results, and document key achievements, challenges, good practices and lessons learned. The findings and recommendations will support accountability to project rightsholders and stakeholders and provide evidence to inform the design and implementation of future integrated Education and WASH programming by IRK.
**4.0 Evaluation Scope**
The evaluation will assess the overall performance, results and sustainability of the 18-month PAWE Project, with particular focus on the following areas:
1\. Implementation and achievement of results across the project’s key thematic areas of Education and WASH, including the extent to which planned outputs, outcomes and objectives were achieved against the project results framework and baseline findings.
2\. Relevance, effectiveness, efficiency, impact and sustainability of the project interventions, including the extent to which they responded to the priority needs of targeted communities and the likelihood that benefits will continue beyond the project period.
3\. Quality and functionality of project-supported infrastructure and services, including constructed or rehabilitated education facilities, WASH facilities, boreholes, solar-powered water systems and other associated infrastructure.
4\. Community perspectives and satisfaction regarding the relevance, timeliness, appropriateness, quality and adequacy of the assistance and services provided, including perceived changes resulting from the project.
5\. Cross-cutting considerations, including gender, disability and social inclusion, safeguarding, protection, conflict sensitivity and Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP), with particular attention to equitable access and participation of vulnerable and marginalized groups.
6\. Effectiveness, accessibility, confidentiality and perceived safety of IRK's feedback and complaints mechanisms, including community awareness and utilization of available channels and the extent to which feedback was received, responded to and used to improve implementation.
7\. Community ownership, institutional capacity and sustainability, including the effectiveness of capacity-building initiatives, participation of community structures, and engagement of relevant county and sub-county government departments in monitoring, management and continued support of project interventions.
8\. Key lessons, good practices, challenges and unintended results arising from implementation, with practical and actionable recommendations to strengthen the design and delivery of future integrated Education and WASH programmes.
**5.0 Methodology**
The consultants will propose the most suitable study design, sampling methods and approach, sample size, data collection, and analysis approaches that are suitable for this project at the endline. This should be clearly outlined in the bidding document/proposal, and if qualified, at the interview stage, to have further discussion with the evaluation management team. The consulting team should propose respondents' interviews or data sources that can answer the log frame indicators and provide comparable statistics (meaningful comparison between baseline/needs assessment and endline) to document any changes.
**6.0 Expected Deliverables**
The following are the expected deliverables.
1\. Inception report and data collection tools.
2\. Draft report to be validated by the Islamic Relief Kenya and Islamic Relief Worldwide technical team.
3\. Final Report after addressing inputs from both IRK and IRW technical teams (the report must be submitted in MS Word and PDF format as well as three printed copies, which should be handed to the IRK team upon completion of this activity).
4\. Datasets for quantitative data in Excel format and KII and FGD transcripts in Word. Beneficiary data is personal data and MUST be protected within the IRK data protection policy, which will be shared with the consultant.
5\. A PowerPoint presentation which summarises the entire study
In performing the activities related to the evaluation, the consultant is expected to strictly adhere to IRK, data protection and privacy policy, Child safeguarding, and the IRK code of conduct.
**7.0 Roles and Responsibilities**
**Role/Responsibilities of the Consultant**
• Develop an inception report detailing the study design, methodology, indicators, data collection tools, and work plan schedule for carrying out the assignment agreed in consultation with the MEAL coordinator
• Conduct a desk review of relevant project documents
• Develop quantitative and qualitative data collection tools in consultation with the MEAL Coordinator
• Conduct training for the data collection teams, including pre‐testing/piloting of tools
• Plan and coordinate quantitative and qualitative data collection
• Work with the IR Kenya project team in planning study logistics
• Conduct data quality assurance
• Review, clean, and analyze data collected
• Presentation of the preliminary findings for input from the IRK team and stakeholders
• Incorporate input from project stakeholders and submit a final report
• Produce Endline study report
**Role of IRK**
• Recruit an external consultant for the endline study
• Review and provide input on the consultant’s deliverables
• Guide on the engagement with the consultant
• Provide consultants with background documents, reports and available secondary data for review
• Provide oversight during data collection
• Ensure smooth flow of consultancy engagement processes, including all contractual obligations
Reporting
The consultant will report to the MEAL Coordinator and work closely with the IRK Mandera field office -Field Coordinator, MEAL and other project staff. The Project staff will support the coordination of the data collection process.
**8.0 Duration of the Assignment and Logistics**
The consultant should describe the evaluation’s overall schedule (i.e., duration, phasing, and timing of different activities), required preparations for work, conditions that might affect data collection, analysis and reporting. However, below are some suggested timelines owed to the urgency of this assignment and are open for deliberation.
**ITEM # of days to complete Suggested dates**
Selection of the consultant -
Inception meeting between IR Kenya and the consultant to discuss the understanding of the assignment **1**
Review of project documents and submission of the inception report, including data collection tools **5**
Finalize the inception report and data collection tools based on feedback received **3**
Planning & actualization of consultancy logistics **2**
Conduct training for enumerators, including pre-testing and preparing for fieldwork **2**
Conduct data collection **6**
Data cleaning, analysis and submission of data tables and syntax files **3**
Developing a draft evaluation report **6**
Drafting and submission of the final draft report after incorporating input on the preliminary report and from the validation workshop **3**
Validation workshop with IR Kenya and stakeholders **1**
Incorporation of final report review comments and submission of final report to IR **3**
**TOTAL** **35**

**9.0 Consultants Qualifications, Skills and Experience**
The Consultant/s will possess the following minimum skills.
• A minimum master’s degree in social sciences or a relevant field
• At least 6 years’ experience undertaking evaluations and/or assessments for Food security, livelihoods, WASH, Education and integrated projects
• Must have led at least two to three similar/assignments in the past 3 years
• Proven skills in research, monitoring and evaluation
• Proven experience in conducting qualitative, quantitative and mixed methods evaluation studies
• Computer proficiency with good knowledge of MS Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and SPSS is desirable
• Experience in undertaking evaluations in ASAL areas will be an added advantage
• Excellent analytical and report writing skills
• Excellent written and spoken English
• Excellent time management skills
• Ability to work well both independently and in a team
• Excellent conflict-sensitive approaches and able to work in highly sensitive environments
**10.0 ETHICAL CONSIDERATIONS**
The below ethical considerations will be adhered to during the evaluation survey:
• IRW recognizes the personal dignity and rights of children and vulnerable adults, towards whom it has a special responsibility and duty of care and respect. The consultant is expected to adhere to the IRW Safeguarding policy and sign as an appendix to their contract of engagement and agree to conduct themselves by the provisions of these documents.
• The evaluation will be conducted by an independent and impartial external consultant, assisted by the IR Kenya MEAL Teams.
• Quantitative data will be obtained from a randomly selected representative population sample.
• Assert that their participation in the survey will be voluntary, and they are aware that they can opt out at any time. (Note that participants may leave or refuse to answer any question at any time, and that this will not affect their standing with the organization.)
• Anonymity, confidentiality and safeguarding of survey data will be guaranteed.
• There will be no risks and benefits for individual participants
• The culture, norms and traditions of study populations will be respected.
• Consent will be sought before commencing data gathering
• Views and opinions of the different survey subjects will be respected.
• For interviews with children, there will be an informed consent process to ensure that all children, their parents/guardians and vulnerable adults are fully aware of all aspects of the evaluation process and voluntarily provide their consent to take part. All caregivers/guardians will be asked to provide informed consent for children’s participation in the study, in line with UNCRC’s recognition of children’s evolving capacities and a parent/guardian’s responsibility to ensure a child’s well-being and safety.
• All the respondents’ data will be kept confidential and shared only with the consent of IR Kenya
**11.0 Product rights and ownership**
The ownership of the evaluation reports and associated products will belong to IR Kenya, and any documents or publications related to this evaluation will not be shared externally except with the consent of the IRK country director
**12.0 Evaluation Criteria**
The evaluation committee shall evaluate the proposals based on their responsiveness to the Terms of Reference, through the following stages:
• Preliminary/mandatory evaluation
• Technical evaluation
• Financial evaluation
**Preliminary/mandatory evaluation**
The following shall form the basis for the preliminary evaluation. Interested bidders MUST attach the following.
• Certificate of registration (applicable to consultancy firms – CR12) and ID of proprietor or ID for individual consultant.
• Copy of VAT/PIN certificate from KRA.
• Valid Tax compliance certificate
• Should be a firm/individual consultant with office/operational establishments within Kenya (attach business permit).
A proposal shall be rejected at this stage if it does not have all the valid preliminary/mandatory documentation.
**Technical evaluation.**
The evaluation committee shall evaluate the proposals based on their responsiveness to the Terms of Reference, with keen interest in the following:
1\. Experience in conducting similar services within the last five years. Attach contracts, LPOs, or recommendations, etc. - **20 points.**
Demonstrable consultancy experience working in similar assessments with NGOs focused on livelihoods, WASH and Education development sectors. - **10 points**
**Maximum points 30**
2\. The lead consultant must have a minimum of 5 years’ experience in conducting evaluations, development of strategic plans, Outcome harvesting, etc., with international NGOs, preferably with a broad understanding of livelihoods, WASH and Education development sectors. - **20 points**
The lead consultant/applicant must have a master’s degree in project planning and management, Development Studies, or other Social Sciences fields. (Attach academic certification and CV). -**10 points**
**Maximum points 30**
3\. Adequacy of methodology in responding to the terms of reference and proposed work plan. (**20 points** will be awarded for an adequate methodology and **10 points** for an adequate work plan)
**Maximum points 30**
4\. Attach at least two samples of similar work done, preferably for an international non-governmental organisation with programming around livelihoods, WASH and Education development sectors, etc., will be an added advantage.
**Maximum points 10**
Each responsive proposal will be given a technical score. A proposal shall be rejected at this stage if it does not respond to important aspects of the Terms of Reference or if it fails to achieve the minimum technical score of 80%.
**Financial evaluation**
Bids determined to be substantially responsive to the requirements of the terms of reference shall be subjected to financial evaluation.

jobs.title: Legal Migration Expert
jobs.description:
## I. Background

Seefar implements Raising Awareness of the Dangers of Irregular Migration II (RADIM II) across four governorates in Federal Iraq including Baghdad, Basra, Dhi Qar, and Al-Muthanna. RADIM II aims to reduce irregular migration by strengthening awareness at individual and community level, providing targeted psychosocial and practical support to at-risk youth, and connecting individuals to viable local and overseas alternatives.

A core element of RADIM II is ensuring that young people who are considering irregular migration and have the potential to migrate legally, are supported to do so.

## II. Objective of the Position

Seefar plans to appoint a Legal Migration Advisor to deliver specialist advice to programme participants with strong prospects of successfully obtaining work or study visas abroad. The assignment is part-time and deliverables based. It is expected to run from October 2026 to March 2027, with the potential to convert to a full time position during that period. The Advisor must be based in Federal Iraq.

## III. Key Responsibilities

1. Support the development of a legal advisory training curriculum. This will include conducting 10-12 interviews with potential candidates and two focus group discussions to help us understand how best to position the service.
2. Build rapport with 15-30 candidates who have been screened for legal mobility. You will collaborate with the MEL Analyst to select the candidates, then set up tailored engagement plans which seek to remove the barriers to mobility for each one and identify a high-prospect pathway to migration.
3. Across 1:1 advisory sessions and ad-hoc follow up, provide the candidates support with their applications and help them to succeed.
4. Complete monitoring forms as requested and provide regular feedback to the team, so we can continually improve the service.
5. Conduct a short exercise to test the willingness of candidates to pay for the service in the long term, as part of the service’ plan for longer term sustainability. (Note: this is only a test and candidates will not be charged.)
6. Take part in training and coaching as required by your supervisor.

The Legal Migration Expert shall provide guidance across some or all the following pathways, and may propose additional legal routes based on demand and their expertise:

- Legal labour migration and overseas employment
- Investment-based migration routes
- Student visa applications and study-abroad pathways
- Scholarships and funded study opportunities
- Family reunion.
- Other legal migration or mobility pathways relevant to youth

Sessions will be delivered online and in person.

## IV. Remuneration

You will be paid GBP 900 (approx. USD1,200) per month for a maximum of five months, with an expectation that you work approximately 20 hours per week. In each month, you’ll be expected to handle a caseload of 8 -10 ongoing and new candidates. Conversion to a full time contract depends on performance and external funding.

In addition, you will receive an additional bonus of GBP 90 (approx. USD120) for every successful application, up to a maximum of five education and five work applications. The maximum bonus payable is GBP 900.

We will make space available for in-person meetings.

## V. Qualifications and Experience

You should apply if you meet most or all of the following criteria:

- Proven experience in an advisory or counselling role. You’ll need to address the psychological, social, and practical barriers they are facing to legal mobility.
- Empathy, emotional intelligence, and passion to help people achieve their dreams. Your friends and family probably describe you as optimistic.
- Recognised university-level qualification in law, social studies, humanities, or a related field.
- Knowledge of how work and study visas work.
- Fluency in Arabic and English is required. Other Iraqi languages are an advantage.
- Availability for both online and in-person sessions.
- Based in Federal Iraq, with a preference for Baghdad or Basra. In exceptional cases, where all other requirements are met, candidates based in KRI may be considered.
- Successfully completed at least one of the following:
- Study or work (non-study) visa application to any country in the region
- Application (or scholarship application) to a [top 2,000 University](https://cwur.org/2026.php)

jobs.title: Provision of Scoping Additional Capacity Building and Finance- Alternative Financing Consultancy
jobs.description:
DRC has been operational in Kenya since 2005 and has been working with refugee and host communities. DRC protects, advocates, and builds sustainable futures for refugees and other displacement-affected people and communities. It provides protection and life-saving humanitarian assistance; supports displaced persons in becoming self-reliant and included into hosting societies; and works with civil society and responsible authorities to promote protection of rights and peaceful coexistence. DRC is present in Garissa (Dadaab & Garissa), Turkana (Kakuma, Kalobeyei & Lodwar), Nairobi and Mandera counties.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Denmark and Grundfos Foundation have granted funding to a consortium led by DRC, comprising Dan Church Aid (DCA) and Turkana Pastoralists Development Organization (TUPADO) to implement the Pathways to Prosperity (P2P) project. The project intends to promote self-reliance and resilience interventions in Turkana West Sub-County targeting both refugees and the host community population. The project targets both refugees and host community populations. Under financial inclusion, the project seeks to explore alternative financing mechanisms and broader business development services that are more flexible, inclusive, and responsive to the diverse needs of entrepreneurs as they scale and sustain their ventures.

**Purpose**

DRC Kenya is looking to explore wider entrepreneurship services that would be useful beyond formal finance access to support further business development activities. While access to formal financial services such as bank loans and participation in business training programs have supported many entrepreneurs, these services often remain insufficient for certain businesses, particularly those with high-growth potential, non-traditional models or operating in informal or fragile settings. The purpose of this consultancy is to go beyond a traditional review of financing options and instead conduct a targeted gap analysis, followed by a collaborative design process, to create new, innovative financing programs for businesses in the Kakuma context. This will provide DRC with a strong position to advocate for more relevant and effective financing strategies with partners.

**Objectives**

The consultant will be responsible for the following key objectives:

1\. **Conduct a comprehensive gap analysis:** Identify what financing and business services are available to entrepreneurs, what is not available, and most importantly, why existing options are not suitable or accessible to them. This will include an analysis of business models, affordability, and the stage and industry of businesses, with a specific focus on sectors like climate, livestock, agriculture, and small businesses.

2\. **Analyse past funding initiatives:** Conduct a stock-taking exercise to understand what happened to businesses that received funding from previous grant or challenge funds, such

as KKCF and Spark Fund. The goal is to understand the challenges they faced in continuing their business and securing further investment.

3\. **Integrate a climate focus:** Include an analysis of businesses with a positive climate impact, such as those in the clean cooking and renewable energy sectors, to understand their specific financing needs for expansion.

4\. **Facilitate a co-design session:** Organize and lead a workshop with key stakeholders, including investors, financiers, implementing partners, and refugee entrepreneurs, to present the findings and collectively design new, more suitable financing models. This will ensure the final output is an actionable, unified ecosystem model.

**Scope of Work**

The consultant will undertake a phased approach with the following specific tasks:

**● Phase 1: Gap and Needs Analysis**

○ Conduct primary data collection through surveys, focus groups discussion, and interviews with a diverse group of entrepreneurs in Kakuma, categorized by business size and sector.

○ Identify specific gaps in access to finance and business support that are not being met by formal loans or existing training programs.

○ Validate assumptions about why past funding models have not been widely effective or sustainable for businesses.

**● Phase 2: Investor and Stakeholder Mapping**

○ Map out potential investors and funders who may be interested in financing structures relevant to the Kakuma context, particularly for businesses in the identified priority sectors.

○ Identify and document which investors could be interested in supporting businesses with a climate angle.

○ Develop a tool or a strategy for connecting entrepreneurs with these potential funders.

**● Phase 3: Co-Design and Reporting**

○ Facilitate a workshop/roundtable session with a diverse group of stakeholders in Nairobi and Kakuma.

○ Lead the stakeholders in a co-design process to develop new financing models based on the findings of the gap and needs analysis.

○ Develop a final, comprehensive report that is not just a study, but an actionable roadmap. The report should include the needs analysis, an evaluation of mechanisms, and a clear implementation strategy for the newly designed financing model

**Expected Outputs**

The expected deliverables are summarized as below: **Phase**

**Expected deliverables**

**Indicative description of deliverables**

**Timelines**

Component 1: Inception

• Detailed Inception Report outlining the consultant’s understanding of the assignment, proposed methodology, and overall approach.

• Develop an Inception report that outlines the general approach to the assignment, schedule of activities and their deliverables.

**Week 1**

Component 2: Gap and Needs Analysis

• Conduct validation sessions are based on the report submitted. • **Analysis and synthesis** of stakeholder feedback, identifying gaps and opportunities.

• A summary report of the identified gaps and needs in finance and business support

**Week 2 & 3**

Component 3: Investor and Stakeholder Mapping

**a. Mapping of Investors and funders**, including non-traditional financiers, financial and non-financial service providers, Ecosystem actors

**b.** Analyse specific investors interested in supporting interventions in **climate, livestock production, skills development, MSMEs.**

**c.** Develop strategy for connecting entrepreneurs with potential funders

• A written summary of key findings and analysis from stakeholder consultations, data analysis, and service mapping, identifying relevant themes and insights to inform the financing strategy.

• Submitted strategy for connecting entrepreneurs with potential funders

**Week 4 & 5**

Component 4: Co-Design and Reporting

**Eligibility Criteria**

For this assignment, the Consultant should have extensive experience and knowledge in strengthening systems for BDS/FSP in Kenya that supports refugees and vulnerable host communities’ initiatives.

**Conditions**

jobs.title: Finance Manager
jobs.description:
**1. Position Summary**

The Finance Manager has overall responsibility for managing and overseeing the day-to-day financial operations of Feed the Children in the Philippines. The position provides financial leadership, technical guidance and oversight of accounting, financial reporting, budgeting, treasury and cash management, payroll reconciliations, procurement-related financial controls, audit and risk management, and statutory compliance. The role ensures that financial transactions are accurate, appropriately authorised, adequately supported by documentation and recorded in a timely manner. It also ensures that bank accounts, balance sheet accounts, payroll, budgets and expenditure are regularly reconciled and monitored, with discrepancies investigated and resolved promptly. The Finance Manager oversees the preparation and submission of monthly financial reports, budget-versus-actual (BVA) reports, accrual schedules, balance sheet reconciliations, cash forecasts and other required financial information. The position works closely with the Country Director, programme teams, Administration, Human Resources, Procurement and the International Office to ensure resources are appropriately managed, financial risks are mitigated, and management decisions are supported by reliable financial information. The role provides functional leadership to the Finance team and ensures that financial procedures, internal controls and reporting requirements are consistently applied across the Country Office.

**2. Essential Accountabilities**

**Financial Management and Accounting:**

- Oversee day-to-day financial operations, ensuring accurate, complete and timely recording of all financial transactions.
- Ensure compliance with Feed the Children financial policies, accounting procedures, donor requirements, applicable Philippine laws and regulations, and relevant accounting standards.
- Review monthly financial reports, general ledger transactions and expenditure records to identify errors, mispostings, unusual transactions, coding inaccuracies and potential compliance concerns.
- Monitor shared cost allocations, advances, receivables, payables and other balances
- Investigate abnormal or unexplained transactions and ensure corrective action.

**Audit and Risk Management:**

- Maintain and update the financial risk tracker, tracking risks, mitigation actions and progress against agreed actions.
- Identify financial, operational, compliance and control risks and recommend preventive and corrective measures.
- Ensure effective internal financial controls, segregation of duties and policy compliance.
- Coordinate audits, donor reviews and compliance assessments.
- Monitor implementation of audit recommendations and escalate irregularities, fraud risks or policy violations.

**Reconciliations and Financial Control:**

- Oversee payroll, bank, and balance sheet reconciliations, ensuring accuracy, documentation, and timely resolution of reconciling items.
- Monitor suspense accounts, advances, and inter-account balances, investigating abnormal transactions and ensuring compliance with reporting schedules and delegated authority.

**Procurement Oversight and Payment Pack Compliance:**

- Review procurement transactions and payment packs for compliance with policies, approval thresholds, budget availability, and delegated authority.
- Verify supporting documentation, contract compliance, coding accuracy, receipt of goods/services, and budget availability before payment processing.
- Monitor procurement commitments and supplier payments, maintain audit trails in SharePoint, and escalate procurement irregularities while providing financial compliance guidance.

**Cash and Treasury Management:**

- Review procurement transactions and payment packs for compliance with policies, approval thresholds, budget availability, and delegated authority.
- Verify supporting documentation, contract compliance, coding accuracy, receipt of goods/services, and budget availability before payment processing.
- Monitor procurement commitments and supplier payments, maintain audit trails in SharePoint, and escalate procurement irregularities while providing financial compliance guidance.

**Financial Reporting & Month-End Close:**

- Ensure timely and accurate monthly financial reporting and month-end close processes.
- Maintain accrual schedules, reconcile financial records, review balance sheet accounts, and ensure proper accounting for depreciation, prepayments, and deposits.
- Prepare financial dashboards, shared-cost reports, and budget-versus-actual (BVA) analyses, presenting key variances and recommendations to management.
- Ensure all supporting documentation is uploaded to SharePoint and reports are submitted according to established timelines.

**Payroll & Statutory Compliance:**

- Oversee payroll reconciliations, payroll cost allocations, statutory deductions, and payroll-related liabilities.
- Coordinate with HR to ensure payroll accuracy, compliance, timely payments, and secure maintenance of payroll records.

**Taxation & Regulatory Compliance:**

- Ensure accurate recording, reconciliation, filing, and payment of taxes and statutory obligations.
- Oversee BIR Form 2307 compliance, maintain supporting tax documentation, monitor deadlines, and liaise with tax authorities and advisers as required.
- Escalate compliance risks, penalties, or regulatory changes impacting operations.

**Budgeting & Financial Planning:**

- Review and consolidate departmental and project budgets, ensuring alignment with organizational priorities and funding requirements.
- Monitor budget utilization, analyze variances, support forecasts, revisions, and realignments, and identify funding gaps, restrictions, overspending, or underutilization.
- Provide financial analysis to support decision-making and cash-flow planning.

**Financial Systems & Records Management:**

- Ensure accurate transaction recording and reconciliation within QuickBooks Online and other approved systems.
- Maintain complete, accurate, and accessible financial records, payment packs, reconciliations, and supporting documentation in SharePoint.
- Safeguard confidential financial information and support continuous improvement of systems, reporting processes, and internal controls.

**Team Leadership & Stakeholder Engagement:**

- Provide leadership, supervision, coaching, and technical guidance to Finance staff, ensuring accountability and high-quality outputs.
- Foster understanding of financial procedures, controls, and compliance requirements across the team.
- Collaborate with HR, Procurement, Administration, Programme teams, and International Office stakeholders to support reporting, audits, cash management, compliance, and organizational objectives.
- Promote a culture of accountability, transparency, collaboration, and sound financial stewardship.

**3. Key Performance Expectations:**

**The following deliverables will be monitored through agreed performance indicators and the organisational reporting calendar.**

- **Risk Tracker and Internal Controls**
- **Frequency:** Updated and reviewed daily, with material risks escalated promptly.
- **Internal and External Audit Support**
- **Frequency:** As required, with audit recommendations tracked through to closure.
- **Bank Reconciliations (Eight Accounts)**
- **Frequency:** Daily monitoring, with formal reconciliation and approval in accordance with the financial close calendar.
- **Balance Sheet Reconciliations**
- **Frequency:** As per the reconciliation schedule, with prompt follow-up on abnormal or outstanding items.
- **Bank Statements Against QuickBooks Online (QBO)**
- **Frequency:** Daily.
- **Accruals, Journal Entries, Depreciation, Deposits and Prepayments**
- **Frequency:** As transactions arise and during the month-end close process.
- **Payroll Reconciliations and Payroll Tax Checks**
- **Frequency:** Monthly and in accordance with statutory deadlines.
- **Procurement Transactions and Payment Packs**
- **Frequency:** Reviewed as submitted, with daily monitoring of outstanding payments.
- **Monthly Wire/Fund Transfer Requests**
- **Deadline:** By the International Office's prescribed deadline.
- **Cash and Bank Balances**
- **Frequency:** Monitored daily, with funding requirements identified promptly.
- **Budget Versus Actual (BVA) Reporting and Budget Utilisation**
- **Frequency:** Monthly, with BVA reports presented to the Country Office team.
- **Budget Requests and Forecasts**
- **Deadline:** In accordance with the established budgeting calendar.
- **Month-End Reports and Checklist**
- **Deadline:** By the 10th day of each month.
- **Financial Documentation and SharePoint Uploads**
- **Frequency:** As financial transactions are processed.
- **BIR Form 2307**
- **Deadline:** In accordance with applicable statutory requirements.
- **International Office Financial Reporting**
- **Deadline:** In accordance with prescribed International Office reporting deadlines.

**4. Qualifications and Experience:**

**Required Knowledge, Skills and Competencies**

- Strong knowledge of accounting principles, financial management, financial reporting and internal controls.
- Experience in budgeting, cash-flow management, bank reconciliations, balance sheet reconciliations and financial analysis.
- Knowledge of procurement-related financial controls, payment verification and supporting documentation requirements.
- Understanding of payroll accounting, statutory deductions, taxation and applicable Philippine financial compliance requirements.
- Experience in audit coordination, financial risk management and implementation of audit recommendations. • Proficiency in accounting systems, preferably QuickBooks Online, and advanced Microsoft Excel skills.
- Ability to analyse financial data, investigate discrepancies and prepare accurate financial reports and management information.
- Strong planning, organisation, communication, problem-solving and deadline-management skills.
- Ability to communicate financial information to non-finance colleagues and collaborate across departments.
- Integrity, confidentiality, attention to detail, leadership and commitment to strengthening financial controls.

**5. Leadership Competencies:**

- **Accountability:** Takes responsibility for decisions, manages resources efficiently and holds self and others accountable.
- **Integrity and Ethical Judgement:** Demonstrates honesty, transparency, confidentiality and sound ethical decision-making.
- **Analytical Judgement:** Investigates discrepancies, assesses financial risks and uses evidence to recommend corrective action.
- **Collaboration:** Builds effective relationships across Finance, HR, Procurement, Administration, Programme teams and the International Office.
- **Team Leadership:** Develops staff capability, sets clear expectations and promotes quality and timely delivery.
- **Continuous Improvement:** Identifies opportunities to improve processes, documentation, reporting and internal controls.

**6. Other Role Requirements:**

- Primary location: Philippines Country Office in Cebu.
- Travel: As required for country operations.
- Other responsibilities: The employee may be assigned other job-related duties that are reasonable and consistent with the position's level, purpose and experience requirements.

**7. Standard Organisational Policy Statements:**

**Safeguarding and Child Protection**

Feed the Children is committed to preventing exploitation, abuse, harassment, child abuse and neglect and to responding promptly and appropriately to concerns. Employees must maintain high ethical standards, protect organisational integrity and comply with Feed the Children’s safeguarding, child protection and related policies and protocols. Violations may result in corrective action, up to and including termination of employment.

**Standards of Conduct:**

Employees are expected to act honestly, fairly and respectfully and in alignment with Feed the Children’s values and Standards of Conduct. These standards guide acceptable workplace behaviour and may form the basis for corrective or disciplinary action when violated.

**Commitment to Gender, Diversity and Inclusion:**

Feed the Children is committed to a diverse, inclusive, respectful and safe work environment in which all individuals are treated fairly and with dignity. Feed the Children prohibits discrimination, harassment, retaliation and workplace bullying and promotes equitable participation and opportunity across its workforce and operations.

**8. Review and Approval:**

This job description identifies the position’s principal purpose, accountabilities, authority and requirements. It is not all-inclusive and may be updated as organisational needs evolve. Annual objectives and performance measures are established separately through the performance planning process.

jobs.title: Request for Proposal AASHA Program County Consultants Kwale, Narok and Migori Counties
jobs.description:
## **Who We Are**

Girl Effect is an international non-profit that builds media that girls want, trust and need. From chatbots to chat shows and TV dramas to tech, our content helps adolescent girls in Africa and Asia make life choices and changes.

We create safe spaces for girls, sharing facts and answering questions about health, nutrition, education, and relationships, empowering girls with the skills to negotiate and redefine what they are told is possible “for a girl”.

Our reach is 50 million and counting. And we’re using technology to reach girls at scale so every girl can choose to be in control of her body, her health, her learning and her livelihood.

Because when a girl unlocks her power to make different choices that change her life, it inspires others to do so too. She starts a ripple effect that impacts her family, community, and country.

That’s the Girl Effect.

## **Background**

AASHA, the Age-Appropriate Sexual Health Approach, is implemented by Girl Effect in partnership with Kenya’s Ministry of Health. It seeks to improve access to age-appropriate sexual and reproductive health information and support for adolescents and young people aged 10–24 and contribute to reducing teenage pregnancy.

The programme works with national, county and community stakeholders. County delivery includes government and partner coordination, community and youth engagement, training and mobilisation, human-centred design activities, safeguarding and consent processes, data collection and programme learning.

Girl Effect seeks county-based individual consultants to coordinate and support these activities in Kwale, Narok and Migori counties.

## **Objective of the consultancy**

The consultant will serve as Girl Effect’s principal community-engagement and county-implementation focal point for AASHA in the assigned county.

The consultant will translate approved plans into safe, timely and well-documented delivery; strengthen government, partner and community coordination; support community champions and youth mobilisers; and provide reliable implementation information and learning to Girl Effect.

## **What You’ll Do**

The selected consultant will be responsible for the following tasks:

### **1. Project Implementation and Coordination**

- Serve as the main local liaison for Girl Effect in the County, and collaborate with local implementing partners and County Government teams to implement AASHA activities.
- Collaborate with the County Health Management Team to organize and facilitate community activities through community-owned resource persons, e.g. champions, child protection volunteers, community health promoters, etc and programme ecosystems, e.g. schools, health facilities, administrative units.
- Support planning and execution of training, community sessions, events, monitoring visits, and surveys/assessments.
- Support County in supervision and adaptation of tools and job aids, gather session feedback and share insights with the relevant project team(s) to inform continuous learning.
- Coordinate and co-facilitate training workshops building facilitation, mobilization, safeguarding, digital tool use and health messaging skills.

### **4. Government and Partner Engagement**

- Serve as the link between Girl Effect and county/sub-county offices (Child Protection, GBV, Health, Local Administration) as applicable
- Support and participate in TWGs (SRH, ACSM, M&E and Resource Mobilization) and Stakeholder meetings.
- Support rollout of SRH campaigns in the county, aligning with official reporting, referral and health service delivery structures.
- Facilitate collaboration between government ministries to implement AASHA activities to strengthen protection, reporting and priority behaviour uptake.

### **5. Monitoring, Learning, and Reporting**

- Document attendance, feedback, key discussion points, health service referrals and champions'/mobilisers' performance, by programme.
- Organize AASHA performance review meetings.
- Submit timely reports, work plans, and recommendations to the relevant programme team.
- Support Girl Effect’s Evidence & Insights team with data collection, ensuring community buy-in and data quality, including consent processes where research activities are involved.
- Capture stories of change and lessons learned for donor and partner reporting.

### **6. Flexible Surge Support**

- Be available for additional tasks such as extra training, launch events, urgent dialogues, troubleshooting or media rollouts to ensure responsiveness to evolving community needs.

## **Deliverables**

- **County Work Plan:** Detailed implementation plan, outlining how CHPs/facilitators, schools, parents and adolescents will be engaged in the counties.
- **Training/Meeting Reports:** Attendance sheets, training materials and post-training summaries for all champion and stakeholder training sessions.
- **Discussion Session Reports:** Session attendance, discussion summaries, feedback forms, and photo documentation (where appropriate).
- **Government Engagement Log:** Record of meetings, agreements and joint activities with the county's relevant government offices.
- **Monthly Report:** Comprehensive report summarizing activities, insights, challenges, outcomes and recommendations for scale-up.
- **Ad-hoc Deliverables:** Any additional reports or updates required to respond to emerging needs or opportunities during implementation.

## **Duration, Location and Level of Effort**

The consultancy is expected to run from November 2026 to September 2027, subject to contracting and programme requirements.

The consultant must be based in, or able to maintain a regular field presence in, the selected county.

This is a high-level-of-effort consultancy requiring consistent availability during agreed implementation periods. The consultant will manage their time against approved work plans, deliverables and an agreed monthly level of effort. The consultancy does not create an employment relationship or fixed working hours.

Travel within the assigned county will be required. Travel outside the county, exceptional activities or additional support must be requested in writing and delivered within the agreed level of effort or separately approved before the work begins.

## **Management and Working Arrangements**

The consultant will report to the designated Programme Manager and work closely with the Programme Lead and relevant Girl Effect teams, including:

- Programmes;
- Evidence and Insights;
- Safeguarding;
- Finance and Operations; and
- Communications and Digital Delivery.

Materials and reports will be prepared in English unless otherwise agreed. Girl Effect will provide programme guidance, approved tools and consolidated feedback through the designated focal point.

## **Who You Are**

## **Qualifications**

- Proven experience in communications, public relations, or a related field.
- Proven experience coordinating community-based projects focused on SRH, MNH, GBV, FGM, child marriage prevention, or similar social issues
- Strong background in community mobilization, facilitation, and stakeholder relationship management.
- Demonstrated experience working with county government structures and departments.
- Knowledge of participatory training methods and experience delivering capacity-building workshops.
- Skilled in documentation, basic reporting, and feedback collection.
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively with diverse community groups and adolescents.
- Commitment to safeguarding, gender equality, and child protection principles.
- Strong cultural awareness and sensitivity about the cultures within the counties.
- Excellent written and spoken English and Swahili.
- Commitment to realizing girls' potential and to the Girl Effect's vision and values.
- Bachelor’s degree in social sciences and related fields.
- 3+ years of experience.

## **Proposal Submission**

Applicants should submit a concise technical proposal of no more than five pages together with a separate financial proposal.

The application should include:

- A cover letter stating the county applied for, current location, availability and suitability for the assignment.
- A technical approach covering county coordination, community and youth engagement, government and partner engagement, champion support, safeguarding, monitoring and reporting.
- A proposed plan for the first 30 days and an approach to managing delivery risks.
- A current CV highlighting relevant assignments and county-level experience.
- Three professional references, including name, organisation, position, email address and telephone number.
- A separate financial proposal in Kenya shillings **(KES)** showing:
- The proposed all-inclusive monthly professional fee;
- The underlying daily rate or estimated level of effort;
- Applicable taxes shown separately.

## **Evaluation Criteria**

Proposals will be evaluated in the following order:

- Pre-screening;
- Technical evaluation; and
- Financial evaluation.

Girl Effect may establish a minimum technical score that applicants must achieve before their financial proposals are considered.

- Relevant qualifications and community engagement experience: 15%
- Experience in adolescent and youth health, SRH or related community programmes: 15%
- County knowledge, government engagement and multi-stakeholder coordination experience: 15%
- Quality and practicality of the proposed technical approach: 15%
- Safeguarding, monitoring, reporting and risk-management capability: 10%
- Value for money and clarity of the financial proposal: 30%

Girl Effect may request interviews, written clarifications, reference checks or a best-and-final financial proposal. The lowest-priced application will not necessarily be selected.

## **Procurement Timelines**

- Terms of reference published: 15th October, 2026
- Deadline for proposal submission: **26th October 2026**

## **General and Commercial Terms**

- **Contracting and Payment:** The successful consultant will sign Girl Effect’s standard consultancy agreement. Payment will be linked to the satisfactory delivery and approval of agreed outputs and supporting documentation.
- **Pricing, Taxes and Expenses:** Fees must be quoted in Kenya shillings, with applicable taxes shown separately. Girl Effect will deduct taxes where required by law. Only reasonable expenses approved in writing in advance will be reimbursable in accordance with the final agreement.
- **Confidentiality, Data and Intellectual Property:** The consultant must protect all confidential, personal and sensitive information. Deliverables and materials produced under the consultancy will be governed by Girl Effect’s intellectual property, confidentiality, and data protection provisions.
- **Safeguarding and Conduct**: Appointment is subject to satisfactory due diligence, reference and safeguarding checks. The consultant must comply with Girl Effect’s safeguarding, ethical, anti-fraud, information-security and code-of-conduct requirements.
- **Conflicts of Interest**: Applicants must disclose any actual or potential conflict of interest.
- **Equal Opportunity:** Girl Effect welcomes applications from qualified individuals of all backgrounds and particularly encourages candidates based in or with strong working knowledge of Nairobi County.
- **Right to Award**: Girl Effect may seek clarification, interview or negotiate with applicants, amend or cancel the process, reject any or all proposals, or make no award. Girl Effect is not liable for costs incurred in preparing an application.
- **Proposal Validity**: Proposals must remain valid for 90 days from the submission deadline.

## **Request for Proposal (RFP) On-Call IT Support Services**

**India**

## **Procurement Summary**

**Item Details**

RFP Title On-Call IT Support Services – India

Eligible Applicants India-based individual consultants and registered IT support agencies/firms

Location Remote support across India, with in-person coordination where required

Contract Period 12 months, with possible renewal subject to satisfactory performance and organisational need

Reporting To Senior IT & System Manager and India People and Operations Manager

## **Who We Are**

Girl Effect is an international non-profit that builds media and technology that girls want, trust and need. We use evidence-based social and behaviour change approaches to help adolescent girls make informed choices about their health, education and economic future.

In India, Girl Effect’s digital-first youth programme, Chhaa Jaa, reaches girls through social media, digital content, community spaces and interactive products, including Bol Behen. Reliable IT support is essential to the teams delivering this work.

## **Background**

Girl Effect India has approximately 28 staff working across locations including New Delhi, Mumbai, Hyderabad, Pune, Nagpur, Kolkata, Ahmedabad, Noida, Gurugram and Jaipur.

Girl Effect requires dependable on-call IT support to resolve hardware and software issues, coordinate repairs and warranties, and assist with approved IT sourcing.

### **What You will do**

The selected service provider will be responsible for:

- Providing remote, on-call IT support to approximately 28 users across India between 10:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m., Monday to Friday.
- Diagnose and resolve laptop, peripheral, operating-system, application, and connectivity issues within agreed service levels.
- Support IT setup and onboarding for new employees, including device configuration and troubleshooting access.
- Coordinating OEM warranty claims, repairs, and replacements, including clear communication on status, cost, and expected completion time.

## **Applicant Requirements**

### **Proposal Submission Requirements**
