**Terms of Reference: Recruitment Agency Services**

**1. Background**

Norwegian Church Aid (NCA) is establishing a regional Investigation & Compliance Support Team based in Nairobi, Kenya. To support the recruitment of qualified professionals for this function, NCA seeks to engage an experienced recruitment agency registered in Kenya to manage the recruitment process.

**2. Key responsibilities**

- Review NCA's job descriptions and agree on the recruitment process, workplan, and timetable.
- Advertise the vacancies and conduct targeted search in Kenya.
- Screen applications, verify eligibility and qualifications, conduct first-round interviews, administer agreed assessments and conduct second-round interviews together with NCA.
- Provide a ranked shortlist with brief candidate assessments.
- Coordinate candidate communication and interview logistics with NCA, and conduct reference and qualification checks.
- Submit final recruitment recommendations and support communication with selected candidates, as requested.

**3.General information**

**Name**:*External recruitment company-To be completed.*

**Title**: Recruitment Agency Services for the Investigation & Compliance Support Team

**Reporting to**:NCA’s designated HR and Finance representatives

**Office location**: Nairobi, Kenya

**Time frame:** The recruitment timetable will be agreed with the selected agency upon contract signature.

**4.Scope of services and deliverables:**

**Objective**

Identify, assess, and support the recruitment of qualified candidates for NCA’s Nairobi-based Investigation & Compliance Support Team.

**Positions to be recruited**

One Senior Investigator and one Investigator / Compliance Officer.

**Required candidate profile**

Candidates must meet the qualifications, experience, competencies, language requirements, and travel expectations specified in the approved job description for each position. Relevant experience may include investigations, compliance, audit, risk, governance, legal, or finance functions, preferably within NGOs, humanitarian organizations, or international organizations.

Detailed job descriptions will be provided to the selected agency upon contract signature.

**Deliverables**

- Agreed recruitment strategy and timeline
- Vacancy advertisements
- Ranked shortlist with candidate assessment summaries
- Reference and qualification check reports
- Final recruitment recommendation report

**5.Requirements for the recruitment agency:**

**Agency requirements**

The provider must be legally registered to operate in Kenya and demonstrate relevant recruitment experience. The provider must understand the Kenyan and East African labor markets and have a proven track record of recruiting professionals in investigations, compliance, audit, finance, legal, governance, or related fields, preferably for NGOs or international organizations.

**6**.**Proposal requirements**

The proposal should include a company profile, relevant experience, proposed methodology, workplan and timetable, proposed team, financial proposal, references from comparable assignments, and details of any guarantee or candidate replacement arrangements offered by the agency.

**Proposals should be evaluated based on**

**Relevant experience** of the firm conducting comparable recruitment assignments, particularly for investigations, compliance, audit, legal, finance, governance, NGO, or international organization positions.(40%)

**Understanding of the assignment** and quality of the proposed recruitment approach.(30%)

**Capacity and qualifications** of the proposed recruitment team.(20%)

**References** from comparable assignments, demonstrating successful delivery of recruitment services(10%)

**Total Technical Score:100**

Proposals will be evaluated using a combined technical and financial scoring method. The technical proposal will account for 80% of the total score, while the financial proposal will account for 20% of the total score.

**7.Success factors/risks and restraints**

**Success factors:** A timely and transparent recruitment process, a strong candidate pool, effective candidate communication, and qualified final candidates.

**Risks and restraints:** Limited availability of qualified candidates, candidate withdrawal, delays in the recruitment process. The agency must maintain confidentiality and disclose any conflicts of interest.

**8.Reporting**

The recruitment agency will report to the designated NCA representatives listed above, provide regular progress updates, and ensure that all information and deliverables are managed securely and confidentially.

jobs.title: East Africa Programme Officer
jobs.description:
**Job Title:** East Africa Programme Officer
**Reports To:** Africa Regional Manager
**Status:** Full-Time
**Direct Reports:** Interns/volunteers, where relevant. (At present, this role doesn’t have direct reports)
**Contract duration:** Two years (with the possibility of extension depending on funding)
**Compensation:** ETB 2,093,000–2,898,000 annually
**Location:** This post is based in Addis Abba, Ethiopia. Please note that IDC is unable to support relocation and the postholder needs to have the ability to work in Ethiopia.

**Background**

International Detention Coalition (IDC) is a unique global network, of over 200 civil society organisations and individuals in more than 75 countries, that coordinates with members and partners on advocacy, research, coalition and capacity building, to eliminate immigration detention and advance rights-based alternatives to detention.

**Role Purpose**

We are seeking a highly organized and motivated individual with a solid background in advocacy on migration and human rights. The ideal candidate will coordinate projects, initiatives and events efficiently, contribute to strategic advocacy efforts and support the development of the capacity of IDC members. Strong communications, organizational, planning, and stakeholder engagement skills are essential.

**Role Summary**

The Africa Programme Officer will play a key role in supporting IDC’s mission in the region by combining strong organizational and coordination skills with a solid understanding of advocacy on migration and human rights. Working closely with the Africa Regional Manager and other team members, the Programme Officer will contribute to the design and implementation of regional programs, events, initiatives and advocacy strategies. The role involves providing operational, administrative, research, and communications support, as well as helping to strengthen networks with members, partners, decision makers and other key stakeholders across the Africa region and specifically in Eastern Africa. The Programme Officer should be available to travel within the region as needed.

**Role Responsibilities**

**Project implementation, admin support and support to IDC members and partners**

- Contribute to the implementation of national and regional projects and events by providing technical, administrative, and logistical support to the Africa Regional Programme and in collaboration with relevant IDC staff and members
- Support the overall implementation of IDC’s mission and strategic priorities in the Africa region (with a priority focus on Easter Africa) through a balance of operational efficiency and advocacy engagement.
- Support IDC’s members in the region and support in network building.
- Maintain a high level of organization in managing project timelines, deliverables, and follow-ups in coordination with the Africa Regional Manager and other relevant team members.
- Support administrative processes related with finances in the Africa Programme.

**Advocacy and Stakeholder Engagement**

- Support the development and implementation of advocacy strategies related to immigration detention, alternatives to detention, and broader migrant and refugee rights.
- Engage effectively and in coordination with the Africa Regional Manager and other relevant team members with a wide range of stakeholders, including government representatives, civil society actors, UN agencies, and regional networks, to build partnerships and advance shared objectives.
- Contribute to drafting and disseminating advocacy materials, briefing notes, and strategic communications tailored to diverse audiences across the Africa region.
- Maintain regular contact with IDC members and partners to identify policy gaps, advocacy opportunities, and spaces for support, partnership and coordinated action.
- Assist in the planning and facilitation of stakeholder consultations, trainings, and regional events that promote rights-based alternatives, pathways and regional dialogue.

**Communication**

- Assist with developing print and digital communication materials for the region, including social media material for different platforms.
- Disseminate and share resources among members and other stakeholders through different platforms.
- Contribute to monitoring media platforms and keep track of reports and updates on relevant developments in the region.

**Internal Systems, Monitoring, Fundraising, and Institutional Support**

- Actively contribute to IDC’s fundraising efforts by providing background research, identifying potential funders, coordinating inputs, and play an active role in the drafting of proposals aligned with regional priorities
- Ensure accurate and timely monitoring and reporting of programmatic activities, supporting internal evaluation processes and donor accountability in line with IDC’s MEL systems.
- Maintain organized records of project outcomes, stakeholder engagement, and communications to support institutional memory and knowledge sharing.
- Assist in the preparation of high-quality reports, updates, and documentation for internal use, funders, and external dissemination.
- Support budget tracking, planning, and financial monitoring processes in collaboration with the Regional Manager, Executive Director, and relevant IDC staff.

**Core Responsibilities**

- Actively contribute to a culture of collaboration, teamwork, and support within the IDC team.
- Demonstrate a passion for and alignment with the IDC’s mission, vision and core values of innovation, collaboration, respect, representation and being solutions-focused
- Demonstrate an understanding of IDC policies including IDC Children and Vulnerable Adults Safeguarding policy to ensure a positive and safe working environment for all.
- Actively engage with organisational systems, processes, and infrastructure to ensure sustainability and appropriate safeguarding of institutional knowledge, assets and core activities over time

**Key Selection Criteria**

**Essential Criteria**

- Demonstrated understanding of the Africa contexts, particularly related to migration, human rights, and advocacy.
- A university degree in a relevant field such as international relations, law, migration studies, political science, or social sciences.
- A minimum of five years of professional experience, including project coordination, stakeholder engagement, and advocacy in the migration and/or human rights sectors.
- Proven experience in reporting and follow-up, including contributions to monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL) processes and reporting experience.
- Strong communication, writing, and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and work independently in a remote setting.
- Experience engaging effectively with diverse stakeholders, including civil society, government actors, and international organizations, to advance advocacy and collaboration.
- Demonstrated ability to plan, organize, and facilitate events such as meetings, workshops, and advocacy activities.
- Excellent organizational and coordination including good attention to detail. The ability to take initiative and to work remotely and autonomously, to manage competing deadlines, prioritise workload appropriately and work in a flexible manner. Proficiency in using digital communication tools and platforms, including social media.
- Ability to undertake travel in the region for the role
- Residing in Ethiopia with the legal right to work.
- Fluency in both English and Amharic (written and spoken) is mandatory. Fluency in Somali and/or Arabic is an added advantage.
- Strong commitment to IDC’s mission and values, including its safeguarding and child protection principles.

jobs.title: 22867 Senior Programme Coordinator (Humanitarian Response and Recovery) (P)
jobs.description:
The International Organization for Migration (IOM) – the United Nations (UN) migration agency – in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) implements a broad, integrated programme supporting crisis‑affected populations and national institutions in a context of protracted conflict, large‑scale displacement, and limited access to essential services. The programme combines humanitarian assistance, stabilization, durable solutions, peacebuilding, migration governance, and border management interventions across multiple provinces, targeting Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), returnees, host communities, ex‑combatants, vulnerable households, and government counterparts. Core activities include community‑based planning, rehabilitation of key infrastructure, livelihood and reintegration support, social cohesion initiatives, displacement tracking, protection services, and capacity building for national and local authorities. Through these efforts, IOM aims to strengthen resilience, restore basic services, enhance local governance, and advance sustainable solutions for displacement‑affected communities.

Under the overall supervision of the Regional Director of the Regional Office (RO) for East Horn and Southern Africa (EHSA) and direct supervision of the Chief of Mission (COM) in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), and in close coordination with the Regional Thematic Specialist (RTS) and relevant Divisions/Departments/Units at Headquarters, the Senior Programme Coordinator (Humanitarian Response and Recovery) will provide strategic leadership and oversight across the Country Office’s (CO) programme portfolio. This includes guiding programme development and implementation, leading strategic planning processes, strengthening donor and government engagement, ensuring coherence with One UN frameworks, overseeing programme support functions, and maintaining high‑level coordination with national authorities, UN agencies, partners, and stakeholders. The Senior Programme Coordinator (Humanitarian Response and Recovery) will also ensure integrated planning, quality assurance, knowledge management, and effective representation of IOM in inter‑agency fora, while supporting the COM in advancing the CO’s priorities and institutional objectives.

**Responsibilities**

1. Oversee the overall development, implementation, and monitoring of programme activities under areas of responsibility, including oversight of IOM’s cluster participation and ONE UN obligations. Identify potential and existing obstacles to programme delivery through continuous monitoring of new programme areas that reflect changes in host country and donor priorities.
2. Develop the CO’s programme overview, including all (or thematically relevant) programmes implemented by the CO, and schedule the major activities for the COM.
3. Lead the development of country strategic plans, which are in line with IOM’s global & regional strategies, the Country National Peace & Development Strategy, and the One UN Programme.
4. Lead the development of the CO’s donor and partner outreach strategies, taking into account priorities in DRC, Humanitarian Response and Recovery, and IOM’s regional and global strategic priorities and objectives; implement the strategies in close coordination with the COM and CO’s relevant units.
5. Develop and maintain Government working relationships with the ministries and international agencies involved in migration-related issues in DRC, and maintain regular liaison with key government officials and interlocutors. Serve as overall Focal Point for Humanitarian Response and Recovery.
6. In coordination with the COM and CO’s relevant units, establish liaison and maintain continuous dialogue with relevant stakeholders (i.e., national governmental authorities, donors, UN Agencies, national and international Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs), national and international institutions, Private sector) aiming at coordinating and facilitating the implementation of ongoing activities and promoting new activities and fundraising for new projects; identify synergies with IOM’s programmes and make recommendations on donor/partner engagement.
7. Lead the Programme Support Unit and supervise the Unit’s staff providing project development, public information, reporting, donor relations, government liaison and information management functions for the CO.
8. Ensure an integrated approach to CO’s programming, with required support functions such as project development, reporting, donor relations, public information and information management are provided to programme units in a timely manner.
9. Provide overall guidance to Programme Managers on project development, public information, donor relations, government liaison and information management; ensure consistency and coherence of project/ programme activities in accordance with the CO’s strategies and in coordination with the RO and relevant departments/units at HQ.
10. Provide guidance and support to the Heads of Sub-Offices on the CO’s priorities, policies and strategies.
11. Identify programme strategic priorities in relevant service areas and areas of interest in line with IOM mandate and expertise, aiming to further expand the CO’s partnership basis and the scope of activities.
12. Act as Focal Point for government liaison and oversee the CO’s correspondence and reporting to the government authorities; ensure that the CO’s interests are accurately communicated and promote IOM’s visibility.
13. Represent the CO in inter-agency fora, including but not limited to the Programme Management Team (PMT) and One UN, and One Programme.
14. Lead knowledge management and capacity building activities in the CO.
15. Prepare policy guidance notes, documentation and briefs for COM and senior management.
16. Perform such other relevant duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in International Relations, Political Science, Business or Public Administration, International Studies or a related field from an accredited academic institution with seven years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with nine years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Extensive experience in programme formulation, implementation and evaluation;
- Demonstrated supervisory experience in staff management;
- Proven record of establishing and maintaining good working relationships with governmental and diplomatic authorities, national, regional and international institutions, as well as civil society actors;
- Previous work experience in a rapid transition or post-conflict area;
- Demonstrated experience in liaising with governmental authorities, international agencies (i.e., UN), and civil society organizations;
- Experience in project development, implementation, and reporting, including financial and budgetary aspects; and,
- Familiarity with inter-agency programme regulations of the UN and other donors.

**Skills**

- In-depth knowledge of the broad range of migration-related subject areas dealt with by the Organization;
- Sound judgment, ability to analyze information and make decisions rapidly to resolve operational problems;
- Efficiency, flexibility, high level of professionalism and ability to adhere to strict deadlines;
- Strong leadership, management, and coordination ability;
- Sound communication and interpersonal skills;
- Ability to work effectively and harmoniously with colleagues from varied cultures and backgrounds;
- Familiarity with IOM’s Migrant Management Operational Systems Application (MiMOSA) and Project Information and Management Application (PRIMA) systems;
- Knowledge of the IOM project management cycle; and,
- Knowledge of IOM’s administrative and financial management.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

jobs.title: Business Development & Resource Acquisition Manager
jobs.description:
**The Organisation**

Plan International is an independent development and humanitarian organisation that advances children’s rights and equality for girls. We believe in the power and potential of every child but know this is often suppressed by poverty, violence, exclusion and discrimination. And it is girls who are most affected.

Working together with children, young people, supporters and partners, we strive for a just world, tackling the root causes of the challenges girls and vulnerable children face. We support children’s rights from birth until they reach adulthood and we enable children to prepare for and respond to crises and adversity. We drive changes in practice and policy at local, national and global levels using our reach, experience and knowledge.

For over 85 years, we have rallied other determined optimists to transform the lives of all children in more than 80 countries.

We won’t stop until we are all equal.

**The Opportunity**

We are seeking an ambitious, strategic and relationship-driven Business Development Manager to lead the growth and diversification of Plan International Liberia's funding portfolio and strengthen our position as a trusted partner for donors, National Organisations, foundations, UN agencies, NGOs and corporate stakeholders.

As a member of the Extended Country Leadership Team, you will play a pivotal role in shaping and delivering the country's resource mobilisation strategy, identifying and securing new funding opportunities that support sustainable, high-impact programmes for children and young people, particularly girls. You will lead strategic donor engagement, build high-value partnerships, provide market and donor intelligence, and position Plan International Liberia to compete successfully for institutional and private funding.

This is a unique opportunity to influence the future growth of the organisation, leading the full business development lifecycle from opportunity identification, donor mapping and consortium building through to proposal development, grant acquisition and donor stewardship. Working closely with programme, finance and technical teams, you will ensure the development of compelling, donor-compliant funding proposals that align with both donor priorities and Plan International's country strategy.

Key responsibilities:

- Develop and deliver Plan International Liberia's resource mobilisation strategy, ensuring alignment with organisational priorities, programme needs and income growth targets.
- Identify, assess and pursue funding opportunities from institutional donors, foundations, National Organisations and corporate partners.
- Build and maintain strategic relationships with donors, UN agencies, NGOs, National Organisations and consortium partners to strengthen Plan International Liberia's positioning and influence.
- Lead donor mapping, market intelligence and pipeline management to drive sustainable funding growth and diversification.
- Oversee the development of high-quality, donor-compliant concept notes, proposals and funding applications that align with organisational priorities and donor requirements.
- Lead decision-making on funding opportunities, including opportunity assessment, partner engagement and proposal strategy.
- Negotiate donor agreements and terms and conditions, ensuring strong financial sustainability, compliance and cost recovery.
- Act as the primary focal point for donor and National Organisation engagement, maintaining strong relationships throughout the grant lifecycle.
- Oversee donor reporting, grant compliance and funding performance, ensuring timely submission of high-quality reports and adherence to donor requirements.
- Provide strategic funding analysis, pipeline updates and recommendations to senior leadership, supporting informed decision-making and organisational growth.

**About You**

- Significant experience in business development, grants acquisition, fundraising or resource mobilisation within the international development or humanitarian sector.
- Strong understanding of the international development funding landscape and donor environment.
- Proven success securing funding from institutional donors such as the EU, USAID, World Bank, Global Fund, AFD and UN agencies.
- Demonstrated experience developing successful funding proposals and managing donor relationships.
- Excellent stakeholder management, influencing and negotiation skills, with the ability to build strategic partnerships.
- Strong analytical, planning and project management capabilities.
- Experience working within an international NGO or development organisation.
- A track record of translating funding opportunities into sustainable income and long-term programme impact.

**Location:** Monrovia, Liberia. This is a global search and therefore support with a relocation package is available if required.

**Type of Role:** Full-time position on a 12-month fixed-term contract, with the opportunity to extend.

**Reports to:** Country Director

jobs.title: DRR Project Manager / Team Leader
jobs.description:
**Miyamoto International (“Miyamoto”)** is in business to make the world safer. Miyamoto is a global engineering and disaster risk reduction firm that provides resiliency expertise that sustains industries and safeguards communities across the globe.

We are seeking a strategic, results-oriented **Disaster Response and Risk Reduction Specialist (Project Manager / Team Leader)** **based in the Philippines** to lead and coordinate the implementation of a national capacity-building project focused on emergency preparedness and response in the public works sector.

*Please note: This is a project-based, grant-funded consultancy position. Appointment is subject to project award and any required donor approvals.*

**This position is based in the Philippines. No relocation support will be provided.**

**Position Summary**

The Disaster Response and Risk Reduction Specialist (Project Manager / Team Leader) will be responsible for ensuring the successful implementation of the project in the Philippines, providing overall leadership, technical direction, and strategic oversight.

Success in this position requires strong leadership, advanced knowledge of Disaster Risk Reduction Systems, and proven experience managing complex, multi-stakeholder projects. The Team Leader will ensure compliance with donor requirements, timely delivery of outputs, and high-quality reporting.

This role will lead the comprehensive planning and execution of project activities, fostering collaboration with government counterparts, internal Miyamoto teams, and external partners to ensure effective and sustainable emergency preparedness and response systems.

**Key Responsibilities**

- Provide overall leadership and strategic direction for the project’s implementation.
- Manage and oversee all aspects of emergency preparedness, disaster response, and risk reduction programming.
- Lead and coordinate a multidisciplinary technical and administrative team.
- Develop, monitor, and adjust project implementation plans to ensure timely and high-quality delivery.
- Oversee the design and implementation of disaster risk reduction policies, preparedness frameworks, and response mechanisms.
- Maintain proactive coordination with government agencies (including public works authorities), local stakeholders, and international partners.
- Ensure compliance with donor requirements, including timely submission of high-quality technical and financial reports.
- Provide technical guidance on disaster response systems, preparedness planning, and institutional strengthening.
- Represent Miyamoto in high-level meetings, consultations, and coordination platforms.
- Contribute to strategic discussions related to Miyamoto’s operations and long-term engagement in the Philippines.

**Qualifications and Experience**

**Education:** Bachelor’s degree in engineering, disaster management or a related field is required. A Master’s degree in a relevant field is preferred.

- **Experience:**
- Minimum of ten (10) years of professional experience in disaster response, disaster risk reduction, emergency preparedness, or related fields.
- Preferably at least five (5) years of relevant experience in leadership roles managing complex, multidisciplinary projects.
- Demonstrated experience working with public sector institutions, preferably in public works or infrastructure-related contexts.
- Proven track record in capacity building, institutional strengthening, and policy-oriented programming

**Knowledge:**
- Strong familiarity with international donor regulations and project implementation requirements.
- Strong understanding of disaster risk reduction frameworks, emergency preparedness systems, and response coordination mechanisms.
- Familiarity with international donor-funded project implementation and compliance requirements.

**Skills:**
- Excellent leadership, organizational, and team management skills.
- Strong analytical, planning, and problem-solving abilities.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- Ability to engage effectively with senior government officials and diverse stakeholder groups.

**Languages:**
- Fluency in English (oral and written) is required. Knowledge of Filipino is an asset.

**Additional Requirements:**
- Demonstrated ability to work in complex, multi-cultural, and dynamic environments.
- Strong commitment to knowledge sharing, mentoring, and capacity development.

jobs.title: Recruiter
jobs.description:
**Location:** Kinshasa, DRC

**Consultancy**: Part time (up to 50%, or 4 hours per day)

**Duration:** 3 months with opportunity for extension, depending on need

**Compensation:** Rates competitive for DRC

**Start Date:** ASAP

**Background**

Global Outbreak Response Support (GORS), delivered by Global Emergency Group (GEG) under a cooperative agreement with the U.S. Department of State's Bureau of Global Health Security and Diplomacy (GHSD), provides rapid activation, surge response, and transition support to help countries detect, contain, and recover from infectious disease outbreaks. GORS combines 24/7 operational readiness, pre-vetted surge personnel, and technical expertise to translate outbreak alerts into coordinated, nationally led response action. The program supports governments and partners through rapid deployment, medical logistics, operational coordination, and transition planning to strengthen national outbreak response capabilities. Founded in 2007, GEG delivers GORS through a global network of regional response hubs, a pre-vetted surge roster, and embedded in-country teams that mobilize within hours of an authorized outbreak response.

**Reporting / Communication Lines**

The Recruiter reports to the Director Talent & Recruiting works closely with GORS HR & Surge Roster Coordinator.

**Scope of Work**

**Position Description**

The recruiter manages assigned local recruitments through a full recruitment or surge recruitment process as directed, from receipt of Position Descriptions/ Scope of Works to obtaining of 3 satisfactory written references for selected candidates

**Responsibilities**\*:\*

*The Recruiter will:*

- Create and coordinate posting of position adverts across various platforms.
- Adapt recruitment templates to specific positions, based on the Position Advert
- Screen CVs to evaluate qualifications and skills
- Schedule timed written tests to assess candidate suitability if position demands
- Coordinate and schedule interviews between candidates, Hiring Managers and Interview Panel.
- Evaluate candidates for suitability during the screening and interviewing process
- Conduct written reference checks
- Forward all relevant recruitment information of selected candidate to the HR and Surge Roster Coordinator for offer and contracting.
- Maintain a recruitment tracking system in excel
- Ensure position recruitment records are maintained
- Provide reports on hiring metrics.
- Build relationships with hiring managers and the operational team to understand job requirements.
- Participate in meetings as required
- Support GEG in meeting the highest levels of client satisfaction
- Other duties as assigned.

**Required Position Qualifications**

- Education and Experience: BS 2+ Years, MS 0+, or HS 6+
- Minimum 5 years of professional experience in HR management including recruitment
- 2 years proven experience in HR/recruitment in humanitarian emergencies
- A sound understanding of recruitment and human resources best practices, policies and systems within DRC
- Excellent written communication, and organizational skills.
- Strong attention to detail and ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines simultaneously.
- Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, SharePoint, Teams, and collaborative document-management systems.
- Ability to work independently while coordinating effectively with global teams.
- Fluent professional English and French required; additional languages are an asset.
- DRC nationality a prerequisite

**Competencies / Performance Criteria**

- Adherence to and promotion of the GEG Way.

**Travel Frequency**

The Recruiter may conduct occasional planned travel to support area specific local recruitments.

**Working Conditions**

The Recruiter will work from their home base in DRC. Working hours will be scheduled within the contracted 20-hour weekly allocation, with hours aligned to DRC operations and agreed overlap across relevant time zones. The Recruiter adheres to GEG security management directives and policies.

**Benefits**

As personnel dedicated to GORS delivery, the Recruiter will have access to those Global Emergency Group benefits available in DRC.

**About Global Emergency Group**

Founded in 2007, GEG is a benefit corporation that supports vulnerable people affected by crisis in more than 52 countries by providing a broad range of humanitarian support services to a wide range of organizations, including the United Nations, the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, donor governments, companies, major international and national NGO’s and local communities. Every day, these organizations and communities rely on GEG’s emergency response expertise, and on the combined capabilities and dedication of its people to implement strategies, find solutions and seize opportunities to assist the world’s most vulnerable people.

Global Emergency Group is committed to being an equal opportunity employer and recruiting people of diverse backgrounds and experiences. GEG does not discriminate on the basis of race, religion or belief, color, gender, sex, sexual orientation, marital status, family structure, age, medical condition, disability, ancestry, national origin or ethnic group. All recruitment decisions are made on the basis of qualifications, merit and business need.

jobs.title: Senior Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning Lead
jobs.description:
**Location:** DRC based/home based for DRC nationals
**Position Type:** Consultancy (40 hours per week)

**Length of contract:** 3 months with possibility of extension

**Compensation:** Rates competitive for DRC

**Start Date**: ASAP

**Background**

Global Outbreak Response Support (GORS), delivered by Global Emergency Group (GEG) under a cooperative agreement with the U.S. Department of State's Bureau of Global Health Security and Diplomacy (GHSD), provides rapid activation, surge response, and transition support to help countries detect, contain, and recover from infectious disease outbreaks. GORS combines 24/7 operational readiness, regional response hubs, pre-vetted surge personnel, and technical expertise to translate outbreak alerts into coordinated, nationally led response action. The program supports governments and partners through rapid deployment, medical logistics, operational coordination, and transition planning to strengthen national outbreak response capabilities. Founded in 2007, GEG delivers GORS through a global network of regional response hubs, a pre-vetted surge roster, and embedded in-country teams that mobilize within hours of an authorized outbreak response.

**Reporting/Communication Lines**

The Senior Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Lead reports to the GORS Senior Technical Director Program for GORS work planning, delivery and performance and works in close collaboration with the Program Director, Senior Operations Lead, Senior Public Health Lead, Senior Clinical Lead, A2A Hub Technical Lead, and deployed Response Team Leaders. The position supports learning and reporting requirements across all GORS readiness, activation, response, and transition activities.

**Scope of Work**

**Operational Readiness and Technology Support**

- Support the technology systems and services required to maintain GORS readiness, activation, response, and transition capabilities.
- Provide remote technical support to GORS personnel, regional response hubs, surge consultants, embedded teams, and deployed response personnel.
- Configure, deploy, maintain, troubleshoot, and recover laptops, mobile devices, communications equipment, and other technology assets supporting GORS operations.

- Maintain system reliability and assist with platform improvements that strengthen program efficiency and operational effectiveness.

**Field Technology and Deployment Support**

- Develop and test deployment communications packages with Operations and Security, including backup connectivity, power and low-bandwidth or offline arrangements. Coordinate equipment acquisition, shipment and recovery with Procurement, Logistics and Finance.
- Support deployment readiness of communications and information-management equipment maintained within regional response hubs and operational support locations.

- Maintain a technology readiness posture consistent with GORS activation and surge-response requirements.

- Support user access, onboarding, troubleshooting, training, and operational use of the GEG Analysis-to-Action (A2A) platform and related systems.
- Identify opportunities for workflow automation, process improvement, and enhanced use of existing technology capabilities.
- Contribute to organizational efforts to strengthen operational information management, digital readiness, and technology-enabled decision support.
- Coordinate with MEL Lead to ensure IT and communications systems effectively support field data collection, reporting, performance monitoring, and timely information sharing across program locations. This will include implementing appropriate data protection measures to safeguard sensitive program data and beneficiary information.

- Provide activation support through an agreed service-coverage plan specifying priority incidents, response expectations, backup personnel, escalation and additional surge capacity
- Support rapid establishment of communication, connectivity, and information-management capabilities during deployments.
- Contribute to continuity of operations during periods of heightened operational demand and emergency response activation.

jobs.title: Consultoría para la Evaluación Final del proyecto “Resilientes, Empoderadas, Sanas y Decididas (RESPOND)” – Venezuela
jobs.company: Plan International Latin America and the Caribbean
jobs.description:
Consulta los TDR completos aquí: [https://entintavioleta.com.ve/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/20261006_TdR_Evaluacion_Final_RESPOND.pdf](https://entintavioleta.com.ve/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/20261006_TdR_Evaluacion_Final_RESPOND.pdf)

Anexo Marco lógico: [https://entintavioleta.com.ve/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Anexo_1_Marco_Logico_RESPOND.pdf](https://entintavioleta.com.ve/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Anexo_1_Marco_Logico_RESPOND.pdf)

Anexo proyecto Respond: [https://entintavioleta.com.ve/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Anexo_2_MMR_RESPOND.pdf](https://entintavioleta.com.ve/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Anexo_2_MMR_RESPOND.pdf)

**Antecedentes**
El proyecto Resilientes, Empoderadas, Sanas y Decididas (RESPOND) se implementa en Venezuela con el
propósito de mejorar el ejercicio de la salud y los derechos sexuales y reproductivos (SDSR) de las mujeres
adolescentes y jóvenes (MAJ) y de las mujeres en edad reproductiva (MER) en los estados Anzoátegui y
Miranda.

El proyecto se desarrolla en nueve municipios: Simón Bolívar, Sotillo, Bruzual, Píritu y Guanta en Anzoátegui; y
Sucre, Cristóbal Rojas, Urdaneta y Tomás Lander en Miranda. RESPOND articula acciones orientadas a
fortalecer la demanda, reducir barreras en la oferta de servicios de SDSR y fortalecer la rendición de cuentas y
la incidencia de organizaciones de mujeres y organizaciones lideradas por jóvenes.
En el marco del proyecto se realizó una línea de base con enfoque antes-después para establecer valores
iniciales de indicadores del Marco de Medición del Rendimiento (MMR). La línea de base incluyó encuestas a
adolescentes y jóvenes, encuestas a mujeres en edad reproductiva, revisión de datos secundarios, encuestas a
líderes y lideresas comunitarias y evaluación de impacto organizacional a organizaciones de mujeres y de
jóvenes.

La línea de base se desarrolló entre diciembre de 2024 y abril de 2025 y alcanzó una muestra efectiva de 2.239
personas/entidades: 788 mujeres adolescentes y jóvenes, 838 hombres adolescentes y jóvenes, 422 mujeres
en edad reproductiva, 126 líderes y lideresas comunitarias y 65 representantes de organizaciones.
Adicionalmente, mediante la Evaluación de Necesidades de los Centros de Salud (ENCS), se establecieron los
valores iniciales de los indicadores 1200b y 1220a en los seis establecimientos de salud focalizados por el
proyecto (tres en Anzoátegui y tres en Miranda). Esta medición, realizada mediante entrevista estructurada y
observación con representantes responsables de infraestructura y de servicios e insumos, fue complementaria
y separada del estudio de línea de base. Dado que el instrumento original de la ENCS abarcó elementos
adicionales a los requeridos por los marcos de medición de estos indicadores, El equipo técnico del proyecto
revisará y acotará el instrumento para la medición final. La evaluación aplicará únicamente las variables
necesarias para calcular los indicadores 1200b y 1220a, manteniendo sus definiciones, reglas de cálculo y
comparabilidad con los valores iniciales. Además, profundizará cualitativamente en los cambios, barreras, uso
de recursos, protocolos, referenciación y sostenibilidad.
De cara al cierre del proyecto, se requiere una evaluación final mixta que combine: (i) la medición cuantitativa
de indicadores seleccionados del MMR; y (ii) un componente cualitativo que analice el desempeño y los
resultados del proyecto con base en criterios del Comité de Ayuda al Desarrollo (DAC por sus siglas en inglés)
de la Organización para la Cooperación y el Desarrollo Económicos (OCDE), complementando y explicando los
hallazgos cuantitativos.

**Objetivo general de la consultoría**
Realizar la evaluación final del proyecto RESPOND en Venezuela mediante la medición cuantitativa de
indicadores priorizados del MMR, y la evaluación cualitativa del desempeño, resultados, aportes y
sostenibilidad del proyecto con base en criterios CAD/OCDE (DAC), a fin de generar evidencia útil para la
rendición de cuentas, el aprendizaje y el diseño de futuras intervenciones.

**Objetivos específicos**
• Medir al cierre los indicadores cuantitativos priorizados del proyecto que fueron establecidos en la línea de
base, utilizando como referencia los instrumentos aplicados en esa medición, con ajustes menores
debidamente justificados.
• Obtener los valores finales de los indicadores 1200b y 1220a en los seis establecimientos de salud
focalizados, mediante la aplicación de un instrumento revisado y acotado por el equipo técnico del proyecto
que incluya únicamente las variables necesarias para su cálculo, preservando la comparabilidad con los
valores iniciales establecidos mediante la ENCS. Comparar los resultados finales con los valores de línea
de base y/o de mediciones previas disponibles y con las metas establecidas, identificando cambios,
avances, rezagos y hallazgos relevantes.
• Diseñar e implementar un componente cualitativo que permita evaluar el proyecto con base en criterios de
pertinencia, coherencia, eficacia, eficiencia, impacto y sostenibilidad, e integrar el análisis transversal de
género, derechos, protección e inclusión.
• Analizar factores facilitadores y limitantes del proyecto, incluyendo factores institucionales, operativos,
comunitarios, socioculturales, de género y contextuales que hayan influido positiva o negativamente en la
implementación y los resultados alcanzados, así como percepciones de participantes y actores clave sobre
la relevancia, calidad, resultados y sostenibilidad de las acciones del proyecto. Documentar conclusiones,
lecciones aprendidas, buenas prácticas y recomendaciones para futuras intervenciones en SDSR, igualdad
de género, prevención y respuesta a la violencia y fortalecimiento comunitario/organizacional.

***IDA is an international independent non-governmental organization providing medical and humanitarian assistance to people affected by conflicts, natural disasters and epidemics regardless of race, religion, gender or political affiliation.***

Participation and support in identifying individuals at risk of gender-based violence
Provide individual case management to clients in accordance with the survivor-centred approach and all relevant case management steps, tools and procedures: conduct needs and risk assessments, care planning, safety plans, case conferences, referrals, and provide emotional support to survivors as required.
Ensure proper documentation and compilation of case management forms according to the GBV Case Management System.

In collaboration with the supervisor, work closely with the other organization in order to ensure smooth referrals

Communicate regularly with the Program Officer for updates on achievements and challenges

At least one year of experience implementing GBV programmes, preferred social work or case management, in humanitarian or development settings

jobs.title: Project Manager – MEAL
jobs.description:
## Job Description

**Résumé du poste**

Le/La Project Manager, MEAL supervise et coordonne la conception et la mise en œuvre du système de suivi, évaluation, redevabilité et apprentissage (MEAL) du projet RAPID, conformément aux normes de qualité des programmes de CRS, aux exigences du bailleur et aux politiques et pratiques MEAL de l’organisation. Le poste veille à ce que des données de qualité, les retours des communautés et les enseignements tirés des activités soient générés, analysés et utilisés pour soutenir une prise de décision fondée sur des données probantes, la gestion adaptative et l’amélioration continue de la mise en œuvre du projet. En collaboration étroite avec l’équipe projet, les partenaires, les communautés et les autres parties prenantes, le/la Project Manager, MEAL renforce les capacités en MEAL, favorise la redevabilité envers les populations affectées et contribue à la mise en œuvre de programmes de haute qualité.

Le projet RAPID en Haiti vise à répondre à la crise humanitaire multidimensionnelle en Haïti en fournissant une assistance intégrée aux populations les plus vulnérables affectées par l’insécurité, les déplacements, et l’insécurité alimentaire. Il met en œuvre des interventions complémentaires dans les secteurs de l’assistance alimentaire, de la nutrition, de la santé, de l’eau, de l’assainissement et de l’hygiène, ainsi que du renforcement de la résilience face aux risques de catastrophe, en privilégiant une approche convergente qui soutient les mêmes ménages à travers plusieurs services essentiels afin d’améliorer durablement leurs conditions de vie et réduire leur vulnérabilité. RAPID est un programme d’urgence de 12 mois financé par Département d'État américain. Ce poste de PM - MEAL travaillera sous la supervision du Chief of Party pour assurer la qualité de suivi du projet.

**Rôles et principales responsabilités**

- Développer le système MEAL du projet et gérer les activités de mise en œuvre du MEAL tout au long du cycle du projet — démarrage, mise en œuvre et clôture — conformément aux principes et normes de qualité des programmes de CRS, aux exigences du bailleur et aux bonnes pratiques.
- Diriger l’appui technique pour une conception MEAL de qualité, y compris les outils et méthodes, adaptée à la portée, au contexte et aux exigences techniques du projet.
- Diriger l’appui technique à l’analyse des données MEAL qualitatives et quantitatives, tout en assurant la qualité des données et de bonnes pratiques de gestion des données. Utiliser l’ICT4D effectivement pour la collecte, gestion, numérisation et visualisation des données afin d’améliorer l'efficacité, la précision et le suivi de l'impact du projet.
- Intégrer l’analyse des données et la réflexion afin d’améliorer les activités du projet en cours.
- Assurer la conformité aux exigences MEAL du bailleur et de l’agence en appliquant systématiquement les normes établies et en suivant leur respect dans l’ensemble des activités.
- Communiquer l’approche de l’agence en matière de MEAL ainsi que les principaux résultats au personnel du projet et aux partenaires.
- Identifier les besoins de renforcement des capacités du personnel ainsi que les besoins d’assistance technique MEAL des organisations partenaires. Contribuer au renforcement des capacités et aux interventions nécessaires pour soutenir une mise en œuvre de qualité du projet. Former les parties prenantes du projet au système MEAL et aux exigences du bailleur.
- Gérer efficacement les talents et assurer la supervision. Gérer la dynamique de l’équipe et le bien-être du personnel. Fournir un accompagnement, adapter stratégiquement les plans de développement individuel, contribuer au processus de recrutement du personnel du projet et compléter la gestion de la performance pour les personnes sous votre supervision directe.
- Appuyer la production des rapports destinés au bailleur, en veillant à la disponibilité de données de qualité aux fins de rapportage.
- Diriger les événements trimestriels de réflexion MEAL avec le personnel de CRS et des partenaires.
- Maintenir des relations de collaboration avec les membres de la communauté et les parties prenantes clés en échangeant régulièrement avec eux, en favorisant une communication ouverte et en soutenant leur participation significative aux activités du programme.
- Contribuer à la planification, à la budgétisation et à la mise en œuvre d’activités MEAL de qualité grâce à des pratiques de gestion efficaces.
- Partager les apprentissages et expériences MEAL dans les discussions plus larges du programme pays.

***Connaissances, compétences et aptitudes***

- Bonne connaissancede MS Windows et des logiciels MS Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint), des logiciels standards d’analyse statistique (SPSS, Stata ou R), des applications de visioconférence et des systèmes de gestion de l’information.
- Capacités de pensée critique et de résolution créative de problèmes, avec aptitude à porter des jugements éclairés.
- Solides compétences en gestion des relations et capacité à travailler efficacement avec les parties prenantes locales.
- Compétences en analyse de données (quantitatives et qualitatives) et en gestion de bases de données.
- Excellentes capacités de communication et de rédaction pour des rapports efficaces en anglais et en français.
- Esprit proactif, axé sur les résultats et orienté vers le service.
- Souci du détail, précision et respect des délais dans l’exécution des responsabilités assignées.

**Langues requises** : Maîtrise du français et du créole haïtien requise ; la connaissance de l’anglais est un atout.

**Déplacements** :Doit être disposé·e et apte à voyager jusqu’à 40 % du temps.

**Responsabilités de supervision :** Oui.

## Qualifications

**Qualifications de base**

- Licence (Bachelor) en Sciences Sociologie, Statistiques, Science informatique ou dans un domaine connexe requis.
- Minimum de 5 ans d’expérience pertinente sur le terrain dans la coordination ou la gestion du MEAL sur des projets de complexes, de préférence au sein d’une ONG internationale.
- Minimum de 2 ans d’expérience en supervision des équipes
- Expérience en MEAL de projet, y compris dans l’élaboration d’indicateurs, d’outils et de méthodologies de collecte de données, ainsi que dans l’analyse et la présentation des données.

**Qualifications souhaitées**

- Une expérience de leadership en MEAL
- Expérience de travail avec des organisations partenaires.
- Expérience dans l’élaboration et la production de curricula, d’outils, de données probantes et d’autres produits pour appuyer le MEAL. Expérience démontrée dans le transfert de connaissances à des publics divers à travers la formation, le mentorat et d’autres méthodes formelles et informelles.
- Expérience en communication avec les communautés et en mise en œuvre de mécanismes de redevabilité.

**Agency Competencies (for all CRS Staff):**

- **Personal Accountability** – Consistently takes responsibility for one’s own actions.
- **Acts with Integrity** - Consistently models values aligned with CRS Guiding Principles and mission. Is considered honest.
- **Builds and Maintains Trust** - Shows consistency between words and actions.
- **Collaborates with Others** – Works effectively in intercultural and diverse teams.
- **Open to Learn** – Seeks out experiences that may change perspective or provide an opportunity to learn new things.

**Agency Leadership Competencies:**

- **Lead Change** – Continually looks for ways to improve the agency through a culture of agility, openness, and innovation.
- **Develops and Recognizes Others** – Builds the capacity of staff to reach their full potential and enhance team and agency performance.
- **Strategic Mindset** – Understands role in translating, communicating, and implementing agency strategy and team priorities.

**What we offer**

CRS offers U.S. based staff a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, life insurance, vision, and a generous retirement savings plan. Benefits packages for successful candidates employed outside the U.S. are based on the country of employment/in-country office where the candidate will perform the role. CRS´ work culture is a collaborative, mission-driven culture committed to improving the lives of the poor throughout the world.

## About Us

Catholic Relief Services is the official international humanitarian agency of the Catholic community in the United States. Catholic Relief Services works to save, protect, and transform lives in need in more than 100 countries, without regard to race, religion or nationality. Catholic Relief Services’ relief and development work is accomplished through programs of emergency response, HIV, health, agriculture, education, microfinance, and peacebuilding. We welcome as a part of our staff people of all faiths and secular traditions who share our values and our commitment to serving those in need. CRS’ processes and policies reflect our commitment to safeguarding children and vulnerable adults from abuse and exploitation.

jobs.title: Oficial de Proyecto – Asistencia en Especie y Recuperación Temprana - Venezuela
jobs.description:
**1. Contexto de la Organización**

CESVI es una asociación laica e independiente fundada en Italia en 1985 que trabaja por la solidaridad mundial y el ideal de la justicia social a través de acciones humanitarias de desarrollo. El mismo nombre CESVI, *Cooperazione e Sviluppo* (Cooperación y Desarrollo), expresa su filosofía de acción, basada en la promoción del protagonismo de sus beneficiarios en favor de su propio progreso, a fin de que la ayuda internacional no se reduzca a una acción temporal benéfica, sino que promueva un auténtico desarrollo sostenible de las poblaciones más necesitadas.

CESVI está presente en Venezuela desde 2019, desarrollando una respuesta humanitaria cada vez más integrada frente a la prolongada crisis socioeconómica y humanitaria del país en los estados de Amazonas, Distrito Capital, Falcón, Miranda, Sucre, La Guaira (Vargas) y Zulia. Durante este período, CESVI ha trabajado principalmente en Protección, incluyendo violencia basada en género (VBG), protección infantil, prevención de la explotación y la trata, gestión de casos, apoyo psicosocial y de salud mental (MHPSS), asistencia legal y salud sexual y reproductiva; Seguridad Alimentaria y Necesidades Básicas, mediante asistencia alimentaria, transferencias monetarias y cupones, y apoyo con artículos esenciales para los hogares; WASH, incluyendo acceso a agua segura, asistencia e iniciativas de promoción de higiene; y Medios de Vida y Recuperación Temprana, apoyando a hogares vulnerables para recuperar sus ingresos y fortalecer su resiliencia. A principios de 2026, CESVI puso en marcha un proyecto para la Movilidad Segura de los venezolanos que regresan al país. Los programas de CESVI en Venezuela cuentan con una base de financiamiento diversificada que incluye donantes institucionales, fundaciones y fondos privados, lo que permite a la organización implementar tanto intervenciones humanitarias a gran escala como respuestas más flexibles y focalizadas.

Tras el terremoto del 24 de junio de 2026, CESVI amplió significativamente sus operaciones de emergencia para incluir Alojamiento de Emergencia y Artículos No Alimentarios (NFI), WASH, Seguridad Alimentaria, asistencia monetaria multipropósito y sectorial mediante efectivo y cupones electrónicos, Protección y MHPSS, Movilidad Segura, Recuperación Temprana y Medios de Vida, combinando asistencia inmediata para salvar vidas con apoyo a la recuperación y resiliencia a más largo plazo.

**2. Objetivo Principal del Puesto**

El/La Oficial de Proyecto – Asistencia en Especie y Recuperación Temprana. será responsable de planificar, coordinar, supervisar y evaluar la implementación del modelo de Asistencia en Especie y Recuperación Temprana. en una comunidad asignada, acompañando su trayectoria completa desde la instalación y operación del Espacio de Bienestar y Autocuidado hasta la provisión a través de comercios aliados y el acompañamiento en la fase de reconstrucción. El puesto asegura que las intervenciones cumplan con los estándares técnicos internacionales (Esfera), nacionales y las directrices de calidad y salvaguarda de CESVI.

- **Lugar de trabajo:** Comunidad asignada – Miranda / La Guaira / Distrito Capital
- **Duración del contrato:** 3 meses (prorrogables)
- **Fecha prevista de inicio:** Noviembre del 2026

**3. Responsabilidades y Funciones Principales**

**Instalación y operación del Espacio de Bienestar y Autocuidado**

1. Planificar, implementar y monitorear la instalación y operación del Espacio de Bienestar y Autocuidado en la comunidad asignada, de acuerdo con las estrategias de CESVI, los Estándares Esfera y los requisitos de los donantes.
2. Identificar y gestionar la adecuación del espacio en coordinación con las autoridades locales, la administración del albergue y los liderazgos comunitarios, asegurando condiciones de accesibilidad, privacidad y seguridad para las personas participantes.
3. Construir, actualizar y mantener el catálogo de productos y la tabla de valores en puntos, asegurando la coherencia entre las existencias disponibles y las asignaciones definidas para cada hogar.
4. Supervisar técnicamente a la persona voluntaria administradora del espacio y garantizar su formación en manejo de existencias, atención con enfoque diferencial, protección y PSEA.
5. Gestionar el control de existencias, la planificación de reposición y la disposición del inventario residual al cierre, conforme a los procedimientos institucionales de entrega y registro.
6. Asegurar el funcionamiento de la modalidad de entrega asistida a domicilio para hogares con integrantes de movilidad reducida, personas mayores sin acompañamiento o personas con discapacidad.

**Análisis de necesidades y adecuación del catálogo**

1. Aplicar e interpretar los instrumentos de caracterización de necesidades y preferencias de los hogares, y analizar la información de consumo registrada por producto para ajustar periódicamente la composición del catálogo.
2. Identificar brechas de disponibilidad de productos en el mercado local y proponer alternativas o sustitutos aprobados, en coordinación con el área de logística.

**Provisión a través de comercios aliados**

1. Realizar el mapeo, la evaluación y la selección de comercios de la comunidad con capacidad de abastecimiento, reposición y condiciones adecuadas de almacenamiento, aplicando criterios técnicos claros y documentados.
2. Negociar y suscribir acuerdos de suministro con listas de productos y precios pactados, y realizar el seguimiento periódico de precios y del cumplimiento de las condiciones acordadas.
3. Formar a los comercios aliados en el uso de la plataforma de registro y trazabilidad de entregas, en trato digno y no discriminatorio a las personas participantes, en salvaguarda y en el funcionamiento del mecanismo de quejas.
4. Acompañar la transición operativa de la comunidad desde el Espacio de Bienestar y Autocuidado hacia la provisión en comercios aliados, garantizando continuidad en la atención y comunicación clara a los hogares participantes.
5. Articular la asistencia con los procesos de retorno y reparación de viviendas durante la fase de reconstrucción, asegurando coherencia entre las modalidades activas en la comunidad.

**Protección, monitoreo, coordinación e informes**

1. Asegurar que todas las actividades integren la protección, el género, la inclusión, la rendición de cuentas a las poblaciones afectadas (AAP), la prevención de la explotación y el abuso sexual (PSEA) y las consideraciones ambientales.
2. Garantizar la aplicación de criterios de priorización claros, confidenciales y no discriminatorios, así como el resguardo de los datos personales de las personas participantes conforme a los procedimientos institucionales.
3. Realizar seguimiento periódico sobre el terreno y Monitoreo Post-Distribución (PDM), recabando la opinión de la comunidad e identificando necesidades adicionales y oportunidades de mejora del modelo.
4. Coordinar con las autoridades locales, la administración del albergue, los liderazgos comunitarios y los socios humanitarios para garantizar una implementación armonizada y evitar duplicidades.
5. Participar activamente en las reuniones del Clúster de WASH y en los grupos de trabajo técnicos pertinentes, asegurando que la orientación técnica y las acciones acordadas se reflejen en la implementación del proyecto.
6. Preparar informes periódicos de actividades, actualizaciones de seguimiento e insumos para los informes a los donantes, y documentar los hallazgos operativos que alimenten la sistematización de la experiencia.

**4. Perfil Requerido**

- Título universitario en Ciencias Sociales, Economía, Administración, Ingeniería, Desarrollo Comunitario o campo afín.
- Al menos 3 años de experiencia en implementación de proyectos sociales o humanitarios, preferiblemente en asistencia en especie, WASH, seguridad alimentaria o medios de vida.
- Experiencia en relacionamiento, evaluación y contratación de proveedores o comercios locales.
- Experiencia en manejo de existencias, control de inventario y procedimientos de entrega de asistencia humanitaria.
- Conocimiento de los Estándares Esfera, CHS, AAP y PSEA.
- Manejo de herramientas digitales de registro y recolección de datos en campo (KoboToolbox u otras plataformas equivalentes).
- Experiencia en la realización de encuestas, PDM y consultas comunitarias.
- Sólidas habilidades de negociación, coordinación institucional, comunicación e informes.
- Capacidad para redactar informes técnicos claros y precisos en español (el dominio de inglés intermedio/avanzado será un activo valioso).
- Disponibilidad para viajar frecuentemente a zonas de trabajo.
- Preferiblemente residenciado en los estados Miranda (Charallave o Plaza), La Guaira (Corralito, Catia la mar o Caraballeda) o Distrito Capital (Junquito, la pastora).
- Habilidad comprobada para trabajar en equipos multiculturales y entornos de seguridad complejos.

**5. Salvaguarda y Políticas Institucionales**

CESVI mantiene una política de cero tolerancias frente a cualquier forma de daño, abuso, explotación, acoso (bullying) o negligencia contra niños, niñas, adolescentes, personas adultas vulnerables o cualquier participante en sus programas.

El compromiso de CESVI como organización segura se aplica desde el proceso de selección de personal, que incluye verificaciones rigurosas, referencias profesionales, posibles controles de antecedentes y revisión de comportamientos previos. Todo el personal contratado deberá firmar y cumplir estrictamente la Política de Salvaguarda Infantil, el Código de Conducta, la Política PEAS y el Código Ético de la organización.

El puesto asegura que las intervenciones cumplan con los estándares técnicos internacionales (Esfera), nacionales y las directrices de calidad y salvaguarda de CESVI.

- **Lugar de trabajo:** Comunidad asignada – Miranda / La Guaira / Distrito Capital
- **Duración del contrato:** 3 meses (prorrogables)
- **Fecha prevista de inicio:** Noviembre - 2026

**3. Responsabilidades y Funciones Principales**

1. Mantener presencia en cada jornada de atención del Espacio de Bienestar y Autocuidado, apoyando su apertura, operación y cierre conforme a los procedimientos establecidos.
2. Realizar el registro de los hogares participantes, la verificación de criterios de elegibilidad y la actualización de la información de composición familiar en las plataformas institucionales.
3. Gestionar los turnos, la organización de filas y el flujo de personas, asegurando condiciones de orden, respeto, privacidad y atención prioritaria a personas mayores, mujeres embarazadas o lactantes, personas con discapacidad y personas con movilidad reducida.
4. Realizar la verificación de identidad y el procesamiento de las entregas en la plataforma de registro y trazabilidad, garantizando la exactitud del registro de cada producto entregado.
5. Orientar a las personas participantes durante la selección de productos, brindando información clara sobre las opciones disponibles y sobre el uso adecuado de los artículos, sin inducir sus decisiones.
6. Ejecutar el conteo de existencias al inicio y cierre de cada jornada con firma conjunta, registrar entradas, salidas y mermas, y alertar oportunamente sobre productos próximos a agotarse.
7. Apoyar la conciliación entre las existencias físicas y los registros de entrega, y colaborar en la preparación del inventario de cierre.
8. Ejecutar la modalidad de entrega asistida a domicilio para hogares que no puedan desplazarse al espacio, aplicando el procedimiento de selección por catálogo en visita previa.
9. Realizar visitas domiciliarias de seguimiento y aplicar los instrumentos de Monitoreo Post-Distribución (PDM), evaluando el uso real de los productos entregados y la satisfacción de los hogares.
10. Recopilar datos de campo para encuestas de línea base, evaluaciones y monitoreo, asegurando el control de calidad del dato y su consolidación oportuna para los indicadores del proyecto.
11. Canalizar dudas, peticiones y quejas a través del Mecanismo de Respuesta y Rendición de Cuentas (AAP) de la organización, y registrar la retroalimentación recibida de las personas participantes.
12. Realizar visitas periódicas a los comercios aliados durante la fase de provisión en comunidad, verificando existencias, precios acordados y condiciones de atención, y apoyando la conciliación de las entregas registradas.
13. Atender y escalar oportunamente las incidencias operativas que se presenten en el espacio o en los comercios aliados, y recoger la retroalimentación de participantes y comerciantes.
14. Apoyar la socialización del modelo en la comunidad, la comunicación de fechas y horarios de atención, y el enlace cotidiano con liderazgos comunitarios y con la administración del albergue.
15. Aplicar en todas sus funciones los estándares de protección, género, inclusión, AAP y PSEA, y resguardar la confidencialidad de los datos personales de las personas participantes.

**4. Perfil Requerido**

- Estudios universitarios o técnicos en carreras humanistas, administrativas, sociales o afines (NO LIMITATIVO). En su defecto, una experiencia comprobada de al menos 3 años en roles similares podrá ser considerada.
- Experiencia mínima de un (01) año en trabajo comunitario, jornadas de distribución humanitaria, atención a público o registro de participantes.
- Manejo de dispositivos móviles y formularios digitales de recolección de datos (KoboToolbox u otras plataformas equivalentes).
- Conocimientos de Microsoft Office, en particular hojas de cálculo.
- Rigurosidad y atención al detalle en el manejo de datos, registros y existencias.
- Excelentes habilidades de abordaje comunitario, relacionamiento personal y trato respetuoso con población en situación de vulnerabilidad.
- Se valorará experiencia previa en manejo de inventarios o en puntos de atención a público.
- Disponibilidad para realizar misiones frecuentes sobre el terreno.
- Preferiblemente residenciado en la comunidad de intervención o en los estados Miranda, La Guaira o Distrito Capital.

**5. Salvaguarda y Políticas Institucionales**

jobs.title: Logistics coordinator (F/M) - Syria
jobs.description:
Do you want to join a committed, activist-driven organization and take meaningful action for social justice?
For over 40 years, Médecins du Monde has been delivering healthcare to the most vulnerable, challenging barriers to access, and driving long-term change in health policies.

In France and across nearly 30 countries, our work is built around six core missions:

- Sexual and reproductive health and rights (including access to safe abortion)
- Migration, exile, human rights and health
- Harm reduction
- Health and the environment
- Healthcare systems
- Humanitarian spaces

**MdM in Syria**

Since December 2024, about 1.8 million refugees and 2 million internally displaced people have returned to their areas of origin (UNHCR, 1 October 2026, indicative), and many others remain displaced. Many return to areas where roads, public services, and health facilities are damaged or only partially functional. Humanitarian needs remain high, while access, administrative procedures and security conditions can change quickly from one area to another.

Médecins du Monde (MdM) works in Syria to protect vulnerable people's access to essential health care, including returnees and displaced communities. Our programs are run from the coordination office in Damascus, with teams and partners in several governorates.

MdM is currently operating in Aleppo and Idlib governorates, supporting three health facilities. Since 2026, program activities have been extended to Rural Damascus and Daraa governorates, where MdM will support two health centers.

**About the role**

You will provide strategic and technical leadership to the logistics team, support program planning and proposal development, manage logistics risks and ensures compliance with MdM France procedures, donor requirements, and applicable Syrian regulations.

**What you’ll do**

Under the supervision of the general coordinator, you define, plan and implement all supply and logistics activities, while ensuring budget compliance and respect of MdM’s protocols and procedures. You lead and manage the logistics team.

More specifically, your main responsibilities are:

- Define, plan and budget logistical needs for the mission and monitor logistical activities
- Define, implement and adapt procurement plan and procedures
- Manage contracts related to logistics and supply activities
- Recruit and manage the logistics team, set objectives, define training needs, ensure skills management
- Ensure monitoring and reporting on logistical activities, adapt indicators when needed
- Supervise and manage the transportation of goods and people
- Supervise the installation and maintenance of office and accommodation areas
- Define and monitor IT and communication resources
- Ensure that the archiving system for logistics documents is respected
- Participate in the definition, implementation and monitoring of the safety and security standards
- Provide logistics guidance, training, advising and technical support to all field teams

**Who you’ll work with**

You will work closely with the logistics advisor at HQ, the program coordinators and the health managers, the support coordinators, the MEAL team and the security focal point, among others.

**You are the right match if you:**

- Hold a Master’s degree in the following : logistics, supply chain management, procurement, business administration or a related field.
- Have at least 5 years of relevant professional experience, including experience in a coordination or management role in a humanitarian or international NGO setting.
- Have experience managing local and international supply chains, preferably including medicines and health commodities.
- Have a previous experience with Médecins du Monde (strong asset)
- Speak English fluently, Arabic is highly appreciated

**This role may not suit you if you:**

- Don't have experience in premises management, infrastructure, energy systems and rehabilitation or renovation works.
- Don't have the ability to work under pressure, in complex, restrictive and volatile operational environments.
- You are not aligned with MdM’s values and activist approach

**Recruitment process**

If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow during the month of October.

Please note: as part of our anti–money laundering and counter-terrorism policy, international background checks may be conducted. Data is processed confidentially and securely. More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)
All successful candidates must provide a criminal record extract (B3).

**Ready to apply?**

We only need your CV and a cover letter.
If this role sounds like the right fit for you, apply now – we’d love to hear from you!

**Employment conditions**

**Contract & status:**

- Gross monthly salary: 3 392 €
- Fixed-term contract for 6 months starting as soon as possible
- Single posting

**Work environment:**

- Position based in Damascus, Syria
- Regular field visits

**Benefits:**

- 13th-month salary (for employees with more than 6 months’ seniority)
- Expatriation allowance: 10% of gross monthly salary
- Coverage of travel (home – mission), visas, and vaccinations
- Accommodation: guesthouse
- Health insurance (50% covered by MdM and 50% by the employee)
- Repatriation insurance
- MdM promotes training and internal mobility.

**Essentials:**

- 5 weeks paid leave + 22.5 RTT days per year
- Strong commitment to inclusion and fighting all forms of discrimination
- More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)

**Our commitment to diversity and inclusion**

MdM is committed to the inclusion of people with disabilities and to fighting all forms of discrimination.
If you are officially recognized as a person with a disability and/or require workplace accommodations, please let us know.

jobs.title: Programme Officer - WASH, Marsabit County
jobs.description:
**Job Title:** Programme Officer-WASH, Marsabit County

**Reports to:** Area Manager

**Job Location:** Marsabit

**Contract Details:** Fixed Term

**Salary Range:** Kes 173,208 per month

**Requirements:** Up to 50% travel to project locations in Marsabit County

**Important Notice:** This recruitment is being conducted in anticipation of funding, and any appointment is subject to funding confirmation.

**About Concern:** Established in 1968, Concern is a non-profit, non-governmental humanitarian organisation, dedicated to the reduction of suffering and the ultimate elimination of extreme poverty in the world’s poorest countries.

Concern’s vision, our mission and our work are all defined by one goal – ending extreme poverty, whatever it takes. Concern strives for a world free from poverty, fear and oppression.

Our culture is values driven and we believe that our people are central to all that we do and are key to delivering on our goal of Reaching the Furthest Behind First. We are committed to ensuring a workplace where everybody feels valued and are enabled to succeed in their work and contribute to delivering on our mission.

**Job Purpose:**

The principal objective of the WASH Officer is to support implementation of WASH activities at the field level. The role involves coordinating partners and providing technical support to Concern and partner staff working on WASH activities to ensure they develop, deliver, and monitor all WASH activities in line with the proposals and ensure implementation is compliant with both Concern and Donor policies and procedures and in line with international standards. The WASH Officer will also be responsible for the successful delivery of all the outputs of WASH in the programme in his or her area as specified in the project documents. S/he will ensure integration with other sectors like Health and Nutrition happens at activity implementation level and cross cutting issues are mainstreamed and integrated.

**Responsibilities:**

**1. To coordinate implementation of all WASH related activities in the programme area within agreed plans, budgets, and timeframe and donor guidelines by:**

- Ensuring all the software component (hygiene promotion activities, water transportation & storage facilities distribution etc.) are implemented as per the signed project agreement and the sphere standards.
- Preparing project documentation including bills of quantities, detailed implementation work plans for planned activities, procurement plans and supplies requests for materials
- Coordinating community mobilization and sensitization activities.
- Taking lead in formation and training of water and sanitation committees for specific water / sanitation facilities to be developed
- Ensuring cross cutting issues are considered during tactical planning of WASH activities and are implemented with the participation of communities.
- Promoting effective integration of Health and Nutrition activities at community level placing programme beneficiaries at the heart of Concern programmes

**2. To carry out accurate and timely assessments and tests to ensure the project is in line towards expected results by:**

- Liaising with all stake holders in conducting periodic operation and maintenance assessments of water and sanitation facilities to ensure functionality and usefulness of the facilities.
- Soliciting innovative ideas of implementing sustainable and appropriate safe water and sanitation solutions.
