jobs.title: CDD - Gestionnaire Regional Projet F/H
jobs.description:
La Fondation Mérieux œuvre de manière indépendante au service de la santé mondiale depuis sa création, en 1967. Reconnue d’utilité publique, elle se spécialise dans la lutte contre les maladies infectieuses, en particulier auprès des populations vulnérables dans les pays à ressources limitées.

La Fondation Mérieux inscrit ses actions dans une démarche de renforcement des capacités locales, notamment en biologie clinique, afin d’améliorer la surveillance, la réponse aux épidémies et l’accès aux soins. Au plus proche des besoins des populations, la Fondation agit aux côtés des acteurs locaux dans une logique de collaboration et de réseau, indispensable pour mobiliser les compétences et les énergies nécessaires à la mise en œuvre d’actions efficaces et pérennes.

Elle s’implique particulièrement autour des thématiques de santé publique les plus impactantes de ses pays d’intervention, comme la résistance aux antimicrobiens, la tuberculose, les infections respiratoires aiguës, le VIH ou encore les pathogènes émergents.

Engagée dans une démarche de santé globale, la Fondation Mérieux intègre, au-delà de son expertise en biologie, les principaux enjeux impactant l’accès aux soins et les conditions de vie des populations dans les pays où elle intervient. Nous opérons directement dans plus de 25 pays à travers le monde, en lien étroit avec les acteurs locaux, nous permettant d’adapter nos programmes et actions aux réalités du terrain et aux besoins des populations.

Misant sur des activités transversales et internationales, nous contribuons à l’atteinte de plusieurs Objectifs de développement durable, dont les ODD n°3 « Bonne Santé et bien-être », n°4 « Éducation de qualité », n°9 « Industrie, innovation et infrastructures » et n°17 « Partenariats pour la réalisation des objectifs ».

Nous rejoindre, c’est intégrer une équipe de près de 150 collaborateurs répartis dans 16 pays, en Afrique, en Asie, au Moyen-Orient et dans l’Océan Indien, réunis autour de valeurs communes : solidarité internationale, engagement, expertise et collaboration.

## En Afrique, la Fondation Mérieux dispose :

- *D’une équipe de coordination regroupée au sein d’un Bureau Afrique basé à Dakar ;*
- *D’un Bureau Afrique de l’Ouest qui coordonne les projets du Sénégal, du Mali, du Niger, du Burkina Faso et de Guinée Bissau (basé à Dakar) ;*
- *D’un Bureau Golfe de Guinée qui coordonne les projets du Togo, Bénin, Nigeria, Guinée-Conakry (basé à Lomé) ;*
- *D’un Bureau Afrique centrale qui coordonne les projets de RDC, Burundi, Tchad, RCA, Cameroun (basé à Kinshasa).*

## Objectif général de la fonction

En Afrique, la Fondation Mérieux et ses partenaires accompagnent le renforcement des systèmes de laboratoire. Sous la supervision hiérarchique du Chef de Projet Régional et sous la supervision fonctionnelle du Référent Gestion de Projets Afrique & de la Responsable Administratif et Financier Golfe de Guinée, le Gestionnaire Régional assure la gestion financière, budgétaire, administrative et contractuelle de projets régionaux dans la sous-région.

Il garantit la gestion financière des projets conformément aux procédures de la Fondation Mérieux, aux exigences du bailleur, aux réglementations applicables ainsi qu’aux principes de transparence, de redevabilité et de bonne gouvernance.

Il coordonne le dispositif de gestion financière des projets, accompagne les équipes logistique et administratives travaillant sur les projets et produit les analyses financières nécessaires au pilotage des projets et contribue à une utilisation efficiente des ressources.

## Missions principales

### Mission 1 : Assurerla gestion, financière, budgétaire et logistique duprojet

- Élaborer, consolider et assurer le suivi budgétaire global du projet en collaboration avec la Cheffe de Projet Régional ;
- Préparer les prévisions et révisions budgétaires périodiques, ainsi que les exercices de replanification ;
- Assurer le suivi financier des missions, des divers ateliers régionaux ;
- Superviser la gestion des immobilisations, des inventaires et des équipements financés par le projet.

### Mission 2 : Garantirla conformité financière et contractuelle

- Veiller au respect des procédures administratives et financières de la Fondation Mérieux ;
- Garantir la conformité des dépenses aux règles du bailleur et de la Fondation Mérieux ;
- Coordonner, avec le responsable juridique, la préparation des contrats et des conventions ;
- Veiller au respect des obligations fiscales, sociales et réglementaires applicables dans les pays d’intervention.

### Mission 3 : Assurer la coordination financière régionale

- Coordonner et accompagner les Administrateurs finances et logistique des quatre pays.
- Harmoniser les pratiques de gestion financière entre les pays.
- Organiser des réunions régulières de coordination financière.
- Renforcer les capacités des équipes nationales en matière de procédures financières.

### Mission 4 : Assurer le contrôle interne et la gestion des risques

- Mettre en œuvre les dispositifs de contrôle interne du projet afin d’identifier les éventuels risques de gestion ;
- Formuler des recommandations permettant de limiter les risques ;
- Assurer le suivi de la mise en œuvre des recommandations issues des audits ;
- Appuyer les audits internes et externes du projet.

### Mission 5 : Assurerle reportingfinancier

- Préparer les rapports financiers destinés au bailleur, au siège et aux partenaires ;
- Analyser et consolider les demandes de fonds conformément au calendrier du projet ;
- Consolider les informations financières transmises par les quatre pays ;
- Assurer la fiabilité des données financières du projet ;
- Fournir aux responsables du projet les analyses financières nécessaires à la prise de décision.

## Profil

### Formation initiale

- Diplôme universitaire de niveau Master (Bac+5) en finance, comptabilité, audit, contrôle de gestion, gestion des organisations, administration des affaires ou domaine équivalent.

### Formationcomplémentaire / spécialisation

- Formation en gestion financière des projets financés par des bailleurs internationaux.
- Une certification professionnelle (expertise-comptable, ACCA, CIMA, CPA ou équivalent) constitue un atout.
- Une formation en contrôle interne, en audit ou en gestion des risques constitue un atout.

### Expérience souhaitée

- Au moins 8 ans d’expérience professionnelle en gestion financière de projets de développement.
- Au moins 5 ans d’expérience en gestion financière de projets financés par des bailleurs internationaux.

### Compétences métiersrequises

- Maîtrise avancée du Pack Office, en particulier Excel (tableaux de bord, suivi budgétaire, analyses)
- Bonne maîtrise des outils numériques (Internet, messagerie professionnelle, outils collaboratifs)
- Bonne compréhension et utilisation des logiciels de gestion (ERP) ;
- Solide maîtrise du suivi budgétaire et du reporting financier ;
- Connaissance des exigences des bailleurs de fonds et des règles de conformité

### Compétences comportementales requises

- Rigueur et fiabilité
- Autonomie et sens des responsabilités
- Capacité d’analyse et de synthèse
- Aptitude au travail en équipe dans un environnement multiculturel
- Capacité d’anticipation, de priorisation et de gestion des délais
- Bon relationnel et capacité à interagir avec des interlocuteurs variés

### Langues

Excellente maîtrise du français et de l’anglais, à l’oral comme à l’écrit Maîtrise de l’anglais professionnel

jobs.title: PRF33834 Request for Proposals to Conduct Baseline Evaluation Strengthening Gender and Disability-Inclusive Climate Action in Bungoma County(Phase II)
jobs.description:
[https://kenyaredcross-my.sharepoint.com/:b:/g/personal/tenders_redcross_or_ke/IQADcP_o5VapSLdp7-4uz8sKAeF9zakl_iM0GTydw1Ty7YM?e=BeQ06q](https://kenyaredcross-my.sharepoint.com/:b:/g/personal/tenders_redcross_or_ke/IQADcP_o5VapSLdp7-4uz8sKAeF9zakl_iM0GTydw1Ty7YM?e=BeQ06q)

**Request for Proposals to Conduct**

**Baseline Evaluation**

**Strengthening Gender and Disability-Inclusive Climate Action in Bungoma County (Phase II)**

**Document Release Date: 14/10/2026**

**Last Date for Receipt of Proposals: 28/10/2026**

**Time: 11:00 HRS**

**Tender Number: PRF33834**

**Submission Method: email to tenders@redcross.or.ke**

**Tender Opening Venue and Time: Virtually via Microsoft Teams at 1200hrs**

1. **Summary of the baseline survey**
1. **Purpose**:

The baseline evaluation aims to establish the benchmark statistics for the project “Strengthening Gender and Disability-Inclusive Climate Action in Bungoma County” (Phase II), a new phase of the Kenya Red Cross Society (KRCS)/CBM Global “Promoting Inclusive Climate Change Resilience in Bungoma County” project (Phase I). It will document the current situation of target communities, including persons with disabilities, women, youth and other marginalized groups, against the Phase II results framework, validate the relevance and measurability of the log frame indicators and targets, and provide a robust reference point against which the project's future mid-term review and end-term evaluation will measure change.

**Partners**

CBM Global Disability Inclusion (CBM Global), Kenya Red Cross Society (KRCS), Disability Empowerment Network (DEN), National Government, Bungoma County Government and relevant departments (Directorate of Climate Change, Ministry of Water, Tourism, Environment and Natural Resources, Ministry of Youth, Gender and Social Development, Ministry of Health, Ministry of Labor and Social Protection, National Council for Persons with Disabilities (NCPWD), Association for Persons with Disability Kenya (APDK), Kenya Meteorological Department, Organizations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs)).

**Duration**

35 days

**Estimated Dates**

5/11/2026 – 9/12/2026

**Geographical Location**

Bungoma County, Kenya - focusing on Tongaren, Bumula and Webuye East sub-counties

**Target Population**

Persons with disabilities (men, women, boys and girls), women- and youth-headed households, older persons, indigenous and other marginalized community members, Organizations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs), Ward Climate Committees, Village Savings and Loan Association (VSLA)/self-help groups, County and Sub-County Government departments (climate change, disaster management, health, social protection), and Kenya Red Cross Society/DEN staff and volunteers.

**Deliverables**

Inception report and tools, cleaned datasets and codebook, draft and final baseline report, PowerPoint presentation, dissemination/validation workshop, and an easy-read version of the report.

**Methodology**

Mixed methods - quantitative and qualitative, disability- and gender-inclusive data collection approaches.

**Evaluation Management Team**

KRCS MEA&L team, KRCS Project representatives, and CBM Global representative(s).

1. **Background Information**

Climate Change is a threat to the development of the global economy and the greatest impediment to the achievement of sustainable development goals. Current global weather extremes affect millions of people, resulting in food and water insecurity in addition to affecting agricultural productivity. In Kenya, Climate Change has resulted in extreme weather events that have led to loss of lives, reduced agricultural productivity, displacement of populations, and destruction of infrastructure, among other adverse impacts. Bungoma County has also not been spared, with increased cases of flooding, landslides, and drought resulting in displacement of people, damage to infrastructure and low agricultural yields.

According to the 2019 Kenya census report, an estimated 40,186 persons with disabilities live in Bungoma County, representing 2.4% of the population. This population continues to face disproportionate risks due to structural barriers such as limited access to climate information, restricted mobility, limited access to services, and exclusion from planning and decision-making spaces at community and county levels. Barriers to their full participation in society prior to disasters and other emergencies tend to be exacerbated by climate-related hazards, and failure to consult persons with disabilities and their representative organizations in the development of plans to respond to emergencies increases their risks and vulnerabilities.

With support from and in partnership with CBM Global, Kenya Red Cross Society implemented a 3-year project dubbed “Promoting Inclusive Climate Change Resilience in Bungoma County” (Phase I, 2023-2025) in Cheptais, Kopsiro and Bungoma South (Kanduyi) sub-counties. Phase I demonstrated the feasibility and value of disability-inclusive climate action: it empowered more than 800 persons with disabilities to participate in climate resilience processes and reached over 20,000 community members through early warning dissemination, climate-smart livelihood activities, and community-led advocacy.

The Phase I end of project findings informed the design of Phase II, reflecting the learnings the results and the current needs. Building on the achievements, lessons and gaps identified under Phase I, KRCS and CBM Global have designed a new phase - “Strengthening Gender and Disability-Inclusive Climate Action in Bungoma County” (Phase II, 1st July 2026 - 31st December 2028) - implemented by KRCS as lead implementing partner in partnership with the Disability Empowerment Network (DEN) as the primary sub-partner. The project will be implemented in Tongaren, Bumula and Webuye east sub-counties. Phase II adopts a rights-based, gender-responsive, disability-inclusive, and community-led approach that tackles the root causes of vulnerability while enhancing adaptive capacities. It combines: strengthened Inclusive Early Warning and Early Action (EWEA) systems using multiple, accessible communication channels for different disability groups; climate-smart livelihood interventions targeting women, youth, and persons with disabilities, including underrepresented and indigenous communities; capacity building of county institutions and community structures to institutionalize inclusive climate governance; and integration of Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) to address the emotional and social impacts of climate-related stressors.

As the project design form notes that a baseline assessment is planned within the first quarter of project implementation, this baseline survey is required to establish reliable starting values for the Phase II log frame indicators, sharpen the theory of change, and inform the Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEA&L) plan to be finalized within three months of project commencement.

1. **Project Objectives**

Overall Project Goal: To reduce the impacts of climate-related risks for communities by strengthening their capacity for preparedness, early action, and inclusive disaster risk management, while ensuring full participation and protection of persons with disabilities and other at-risk groups.

- Specific Objective 1: To strengthen the ability of at-risk communities to apply inclusive, climate-adaptive approaches and engage in advocacy mechanisms that enhance their participation and resilience to climate-related shocks.
- Specific Objective 2: To improve adaptive livelihoods, access to services, and social protection for persons with disabilities and at-risk households.
- Specific Objective 3: To strengthen evidence generation, advocacy and learning for inclusive climate action.

1. **Key Project Stakeholders**

The project is implemented in close coordination with the National and Bungoma County Governments and their departments, including the Directorate of Climate Change, the Ministry of Water, Tourism, Environment and Natural Resources, the Ministry of Youth, Gender and Social Development, the Ministry of Health (rehabilitation and physiotherapy departments), the Ministry of Labor and Social Protection, the National Council for Persons with Disabilities (NCPWD), the Kenya Meteorological Department, and the Association for Persons with Disability Kenya (APDK).

Key implementing partners are Kenya Red Cross Society (KRCS), as lead implementing partner, and the Disability Empowerment Network (DEN), as primary sub-partner. The project also works with Organizations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs), Ward Climate Committees, women-led organizations, grassroots community structures, VSLA/self-help groups, and National Government Administrative Officers. At the regional/global level, the project engages with the Early Warnings for All (EW4ALL) pillar leads (UNDRR, NDOC, WMO, ITU, CA, IFRC, KRCS).

1. **Baseline survey Purpose & Scope**
1. **Purpose.**

The baseline survey aims to establish the current status of the target population and systems against each Phase II log frame indicator, ahead of project implementation. It will provide a credible evidence base against which project progress and impact will be measured at mid-term and end-term.

The baseline survey will establish the pre-intervention values for the Phase II log frame indicators in Tongaren, Webuye East and Bumula sub-counties. These values form the benchmark against which change will be measured at mid-term and end-term. The survey will also confirm that the indicators, targets and monitoring arrangements are realistic and measurable, so that the project can track and demonstrate its results from the start.

1. To establish baseline values for key project outcome and output indicators, including climate-related risks, community adaptive capacity and existing resilience practices across the three sub-counties.
2. To assess community perceptions and experiences of participation, disability inclusion, feedback, accountability and safeguarding mechanisms, and identify key gaps.
3. To identify priority project risks, assumptions and monitoring requirements that may affect implementation and achievement of results.
4. To provide practical recommendations to refine programme targeting, implementation, monitoring and learning.
5. **Key Questions**

The consultant will develop key questions to enable the baseline survey to generate the information needed on the project's starting context and indicators. The following are proposed key questions; the consultant may suggest changes/additional questions at the inception stage:

**Baseline values and indicators**

- What are the baseline values for each Phase II log frame indicator?
- Are the current indicators and targets realistic, measurable, and appropriately disaggregated (sex, age, disability, geography)?
- What data sources and collection methods are most appropriate for tracking each indicator going forward?

**Context and needs analysis**

- What is the current level of climate risk awareness, preparedness, and early warning access among target communities, disaggregated by gender and disability?
- What livelihood strategies do households, including persons with disabilities, currently use, and how climate-adaptive are they?
- What is the current status of VSLA/self-help groups, microenterprises, and access to rehabilitation and assistive devices in the target areas?
- What is the level of functioning of Ward Climate Committees, DRM coordination platforms, and OPD engagement in county governance processes?

**Capacity assessment**

- What is the current institutional and technical capacity of KRCS, DEN, OPDs, and county departments to deliver and monitor a disability-inclusive climate resilience project?
- Key MEA&L capacity gaps within DEN that require strengthening to enable DEN to meaningfully support MEA&L functions within the project.

**Community Engagement, Accountability and Safeguarding**

- What complaints and feedback mechanisms currently exist in the target communities, and how accessible are they to persons with disabilities?
- What safeguarding risks (including GBV, exploitation, and exclusion of persons with intellectual or psychosocial disabilities) are present in the target context, and what systems currently exist to mitigate them?
- To what extent are community members, including persons with disabilities and women, currently involved in decision-making processes relevant to climate resilience?

**Gender and Disability Inclusion**

- What specific barriers do women, men, persons with disabilities (by type), youth and older persons currently face in accessing climate information, livelihoods, and services?
- How are gender relations, decision-making power, and leadership currently distributed within target communities and OPDs?

**Risks and Assumptions**

- Are the key assumptions in the log frame (e.g. continued institutional commitment, market functionality, community adoption of livelihood diversification) currently valid in the project context?
- What additional risks (climate, security, political, or operational) should be considered in the project's risk register?

1. **Survey Methodology**

The consultant will be expected to propose the most appropriate study design, sampling methods, sample size, and data collection and analysis approaches for the baseline survey. These should be clearly outlined in the bidding document/proposal and will be further discussed with the assessment management team if the firm qualifies for the oral stage. The firm should identify and justify the target respondents or data sources that can effectively address the log frame indicators. The proposed methodology should incorporate triangulation of findings and ensure an adequate, representative sample of the target beneficiaries, with clearly defined sampling procedures, disaggregated by sex, age, and disability status (using, for example, the Washington Group Questions).

All log frame indicators should be given operational definitions in the bid submission. A detailed data analysis plan should also be included, indicating how each indicator will be analyzed, and how baseline values will be presented and structured to allow direct comparison at mid-term and end-term.

Additional documents that can be used during the baseline survey include the following, in additional to any other relevant documents/literature to inform the survey process:

- Phase I End-Term Evaluation report and Phase I project reports.
- Phase II project design form, theory of change, and log frame.
- Phase II project risk register and safeguarding risk assessment.
- Existing needs assessments and contextual analyses for Bungoma County.
- Documents, policies and frameworks by partners, county and national government (e.g. Bungoma County Integrated Development Plan (CIDP) 2023-2027, Kenya Climate Change Act 2016, National Climate Change Action Plan (NCCAP) 2023-2027, Disability Inclusion Policy).

The project's Overall Objective, Specific Objectives and Results-level indicators are shown in the table below:

**Hierarchy of Objectives**

**Objectively Verifiable Indicators (OVI)**

**Overall Objective (Impact):**

**Strengthened disability-inclusive, gender-responsive, and community-led climate resilience systems in Bungoma County.**

**Specific Objective 1 (Outcome):**

**Communities at risk of climate shocks in Bungoma County apply inclusive coping, early warning, and advocacy mechanisms that reduce vulnerability and strengthen resilience.**

% of supported communities implementing inclusive early warning and coping mechanisms. (Survey reports)

% of persons with disability, women, and marginalized persons accessing and responding to early warning information. (Surveys)

% of supported households reporting diversified and climate-adaptive livelihoods (Surveys)

**Result 1.1 (output):**

**Coping mechanisms of communities at risk of climate shocks are strengthened.**

Number of at risk households supported with inclusive climate-adaptive livelihoods.

Number of strengthened VSLA groups which are functional.

**Result 1.2 (output):**

**Participatory, community-led Early Warning Early Action (EWEA) systems accessible to all (including persons with disabilities) are strengthened.**

% of persons with disabilities reporting access to timely and understandable early warning information.

Number of functional DRM coordination platforms at ward, sub-county and county levels. Baseline (Phase I):

Number of persons accessing rehabilitation, assistive devices and referral services.

**Result 1.3 (output):**

**Strengthened gender, age and disability-inclusive climate governance through OPD-led advocacy.**

Number of OPDs actively participating in county climate and DRM governance processes.

Number of OPD-led advocacy initiatives on inclusive climate action.

Number of county plans, policies or processes influenced by OPD advocacy.

**Result 1.4 (Output**

**Project accountability, safeguarding, monitoring and learning systems strengthened.**

Number of joint monitoring visits conducted.

% of beneficiaries reporting satisfaction with project services.

Number of learning and advocacy products developed.

**Specific Objective 2 (Outcome):**

**Improve adaptive livelihoods, access to services, and social protection for persons with disabilities and at-risk households.**

% of targeted households demonstrating improved income and livelihood diversification.

% of people (persons with disabilities/women) reporting increased access to social protection or adaptive livelihood schemes.

Number of persons with disabilities, women, and marginalized persons engaged in climate-smart livelihood initiatives.

**Result 2.1 (Output):**

**Persons with disabilities, women and other marginalized groups have improved access to adaptive, climate-smart livelihoods and initiatives.**

Number of livelihood interventions designed with inclusive adaptation measures.

Average household income of participants.

Number of persons with disabilities, women, and marginalized persons participating in climate-smart livelihood projects.

**Result 2.2 (Output):**

**Rehabilitation and assistive technology services are scaled up and linked to livelihood and resilience initiatives.**

Number of livelihood initiatives integrating access to rehabilitation or assistive services.

Number of beneficiaries accessing assistive devices to support participation in livelihood activities.

Number of partnerships established between service providers and livelihood programmes.

**Result 2.3 (Output):**

**Households demonstrate improved economic resilience through inclusive VSLA and microenterprise support.**

% of VSLA members reporting increased savings and business income.

Number of inclusive VSLA groups formed/strengthened with persons with disability and gender representation.

Number of microenterprises initiated or scaled by persons with disability and women.

**Result 2.4: Output**

**Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) and GBV protection integrated into livelihood and community resilience programming.**

% of persons with disabilities and women reporting access to psychosocial and protection services.

**Specific Objective 3 (Outcome):**

**Strengthen evidence generation, advocacy and learning for inclusive climate action.**

Number of inclusive advocacy initiatives or policy dialogues influenced by project evidence.

**Result 3.1 (Short-term Outcome):**

**Data on disability inclusion, gender, and climate impact systematically collected and shared.**

Number of inclusive data collection tools developed and used.

Number of county climate reports that include disaggregated data (sex, age, disability).

Number of data-sharing platforms or repositories established and maintained.

**Result 3.2 (Short-term Outcome):**

**Policy briefs, learning papers, and evidence disseminated to inform county, national, and regional platforms.**

Number of policy briefs, case studies, and learning papers developed and disseminated.

Number of forums/events where inclusive climate data/evidence is presented. Baseline (Phase I): 1.

Number of instances where evidence informs policy decisions or planning processes.

**Result 3.3 (Short-term Outcome):**

**OPDs and county actors demonstrate improved capacity for inclusive advocacy and monitoring.**

Number of OPDs applying advocacy and monitoring skills in county planning processes.

Number of OPD and county actors reporting improved capacities.

1. **Quality & Ethical Standards**

The consultant shall take all reasonable steps to ensure that the survey is designed and conducted to respect and protect the rights and welfare of the people and communities involved and to ensure that the assessment is technically accurate and reliable, is conducted in a transparent and impartial manner, and contributes to organizational learning and accountability. Therefore, the survey team shall be required to adhere to the assessment standards and applicable practices as recommended by the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies.

- **Utility:** Assessments must be useful and used.
- **Feasibility:** Assessments must be realistic, diplomatic, and managed in a sensible, cost-effective manner.
- **Ethics & Legality:** Assessments must be conducted ethically and legally, with regard for the welfare of those involved in and affected by the assessment.
- **Impartiality & Independence:** Assessments should be impartial, providing a comprehensive and unbiased assessment that considers the views of all stakeholders.
- **Transparency:** Assessment activities should reflect an attitude of openness and transparency.
- **Accuracy:** Assessments should be technically accurate, providing sufficient information about the data collection, analysis, and interpretation methods so that its worth or merit can be determined.
- **Participation:** Stakeholders should be consulted and meaningfully involved in the assessment process when feasible and appropriate.
- **Collaboration:** Collaboration between key operating partners in the assessment process improves the legitimacy and utility of the assessment.
- **Inclusion:** The assessment must include clear steps to ensure meaningful engagement and participation of all sections of the community, including persons with disabilities and women.

It is also expected that the assessment will respect the seven Fundamental Principles of the Red Cross and Red Crescent: 1) humanity, 2) impartiality, 3) neutrality, 4) independence, 5) voluntary service, 6) unity and 7) universality.

5. Must have led at least five participatory assessments. Experience of conducting evaluations, monitoring and assessment work in the target or similar communities (preferred).
6. High level of professionalism and an ability to work independently and in high-pressure situations under tight deadlines.
7. Strong interpersonal, facilitation, and communication skills
8. The team must have a statistician able to analyze quantitative and qualitative data, as well as key technical team members to handle specific components of the project baseline.
9. The team must have experience in participatory data collection methods and using mobile phone technology for data collection, monitoring and reporting.

11. Availability for the period indicated and ready to carry out the assignment and deliver results within the specified period/time.

Availability of experts in each of the subject areas, with experience and relevant qualifications for the assignment, will be highly preferred.

jobs.description:
**La Fondation Mérieux**

La Fondation Mérieux œuvre de manière indépendante au service de la santé mondiale depuis sa création, en 1967. Reconnue d’utilité publique, elle se spécialise dans la lutte contre les maladies infectieuses, en particulier auprès des populations vulnérables dans les pays à ressources limitées.

La Fondation Mérieux inscrit ses actions dans une démarche de renforcement des capacités locales, notamment en biologie clinique, afin d’améliorer la surveillance, la réponse aux épidémies et l’accès aux soins. Au plus proche des besoins des populations, la Fondation agit aux côtés des acteurs locaux dans une logique de collaboration et de réseau, indispensable pour mobiliser les compétences et les énergies nécessaires à la mise en œuvre d’actions efficaces et pérennes.

Elle s’implique particulièrement autour des thématiques de santé publique les plus impactantes de ses pays d’intervention, comme la résistance aux antimicrobiens, la tuberculose, les infections respiratoires aiguës, le VIH ou encore les pathogènes émergents.

Engagée dans une démarche de santé globale, la Fondation Mérieux intègre, au-delà de son expertise en biologie, les principaux enjeux impactant l’accès aux soins et les conditions de vie des populations dans les pays où elle intervient. Nous opérons directement dans plus de 25 pays à travers le monde, en lien étroit avec les acteurs locaux, nous permettant d’adapter nos programmes et actions aux réalités du terrain et aux besoins des populations.

Misant sur des activités transversales et internationales, nous contribuons à l’atteinte de plusieurs Objectifs de développement durable, dont les ODD n°3 « Bonne Santé et bien-être », n°4 « Éducation de qualité », n°9 « Industrie, innovation et infrastructures » et n°17 « Partenariats pour la réalisation des objectifs ».

Nous rejoindre, c’est intégrer une équipe de près de 150 collaborateurs répartis dans 16 pays, en Afrique, en Asie, au Moyen-Orient et dans l’Océan Indien, réunis autour de valeurs communes : solidarité internationale, engagement, expertise et collaboration.

En Afrique, la Fondation Mérieux dispose :

- D’une équipe de coordination regroupée au sein d’un Bureau Afrique basé à Dakar ;
- D’un Bureau Afrique de l’Ouest qui coordonne les projets du Sénégal, du Mali, du Niger, du Burkina Faso et de Guinée Bissau (basé à Dakar) ;
- D’un Bureau Golfe de Guinée qui coordonne les projets du Togo, Bénin, Nigeria, Guinée Conakry (basé à Lomé) ;
- D’un Bureau Afrique centrale qui coordonne les projets de RDC, Burundi, Tchad, RCA, Cameroun (basé à Kinshasa).

1. **Contexte du projet**

La fragilité des systèmes nationaux de gestion des risques biologiques engendre des vulnérabilités critiques, notamment face aux risques d’exposition accidentelle du personnel de santé, de contamination environnementale ou de détournement malveillant d’agents pathogènes transmissibles. Pour relever ces défis, les pays du Réseau d’Afrique de l’Ouest des Laboratoires de biologie médicale (RESAOLAB) ont identifié le renforcement de la biosécurité et de la biosûreté comme une priorité majeure pour la sûreté des interventions en biologie médicale dans leurs pays.

La Fondation Mérieux, en soutien au Groupe de travail sur la sécurité biologique du G7/GP, sur financement d’Affaires mondiales Canada, initie le projet de Renforcement de la biosécurité et biosûreté dans quatre pays, à savoir le Bénin, la Guinée, le Sénégal et le Togo, tout en appuyant le RESAOLAB.

**La Fondation Mérieux appuie les systèmes de laboratoireselon l’approche One Health et la dimension de genre, en renforçant laqualité et la Biosécurité/Biosûreté, dans le cadre de ce projet d’une durée de 20 mois.**

1. **Objectif généralde lafonction**

Sous la supervision hiérarchique du Chef de projet pays et sous la supervision fonctionnelle du Gestionnaire financier du bureau d’affectation, l’Administrateur Finances & Logistique assure la gestion administrative, financière, comptable et logistique du projet à l’échelle nationale.

Il garantit la conformité des opérations financières et administratives aux procédures de la Fondation Mérieux, aux exigences du bailleur et à la réglementation nationale applicable. Il contribue au pilotage financier du projet en produisant des informations fiables, en assurant le suivi budgétaire et en veillant à une utilisation optimale des ressources mises à disposition.

1. **Missions principales**

**Mission 1 : Assurer la gestion financière et comptable du projet**

- Assurer la gestion comptable quotidienne du projet conformément aux procédures de la Fondation Mérieux et aux normes comptables applicables.
- Vérifier la conformité, l’exhaustivité et la validité des pièces justificatives avant leur comptabilisation.
- Enregistrer les opérations comptables dans le système d’information financier de la Fondation Mérieux.
- Assurer le suivi de la trésorerie, des opérations bancaires et de la caisse.
- Préparer les états de rapprochement bancaire et les arrêtés périodiques de caisse.
- Assurer le suivi des paiements aux fournisseurs, aux consultants et aux prestataires.

- Contribuer à la préparation des rapports financiers destinés au niveau régional et au bailleur.

**Mission 3 : Assurer la gestion administrative et contractuelle**

En Afrique, la Fondation Mérieux et ses partenaires accompagnent le renforcement des systèmes de laboratoire. Les capacités encore insuffisantes en matière de gestion des risques biologiques constituent une vulnérabilité importante, avec notamment des risques d’exposition accidentelle du personnel de santé, de contamination de l’environnement ou encore de détournement d’agents pathogènes à des fins malveillantes.

Pour répondre à ces enjeux, la Fondation Mérieux, aux côtés de ses partenaires, met en œuvre plusieurs projets visant à renforcer durablement la biosûreté et la biosécurité dans différents pays d’Afrique de l’Ouest et d’Afrique centrale.

## Objectif général de lafonction

Sous la supervision hiérarchique de l’Adjoint technique Afrique, l’Expert Régional Biosûreté et Biosécurité est le référent technique des projets BSS de la Fondation Mérieux en Afrique.

Il garantit la qualité technique des activités des projets BSS, veille à assurer l’alignement des interventions sur les normes internationales et règlementations nationales, la qualité et l’harmonisation des pratiques, tout en accompagnant les équipes dans leur mise en œuvre, leur amélioration continue et leur montée en compétences. Il entretient des relations fonctionnelles étroites avec le Responsable Biosûreté, Biosécurité et Qualité SIGL, basé au siège, ainsi qu’avec les différents Chefs de projets BSS en Afrique.

## Missions principales

Mission 1 : Fournir une expertise et un accompagnement techniques sur l’ensemble des volets BSS des projets

- Conseiller les Chefs de Projet travaillant sur toutes les questions relatives à la biosûreté, à la biosécurité.
- Veiller à l’application des référentiels internationaux, des règlementations nationales et des bonnes pratiques de biosécurité et biosûreté dans l’ensemble des interventions.
- Assurer une veille scientifique et réglementaire sur les évolutions internationales en matière de biosûreté et de biosécurité.

Mission 2 : Élaborer, contrôler et superviser l’ensemble des livrables techniques de biosécurité et biosûtreté des projets BSS.

- Contrôler la qualité et la conformité : vérifier l’exactitude, la cohérence et le respect des exigences et normes des projets.
- Superviser les revues et la validation : organiser les revues techniques, intégrer les observations et assurer la validation finale.

- Constituer, former et accompagner un vivier régional de formateurs.
- Assurer le mentorat technique auprès des équipes nationales.
- Coordonner et superviser l’accompagnementdes laboratoires dans l’amélioration continue de leurs pratiques.
- Contribuer au développement d’une communauté régionale de pratiques en matière de biosûreté et de biosécurité.

Mission 4 : Appuyer les interventions techniques dans les pays

- Appuyer l'évaluation des infrastructures et des équipements des laboratoires.
- Formuler des recommandations techniques pour améliorer les conditions de biosûreté et de biosécurité des projets.
- Accompagner l’intégration des exigences techniques lors du déploiement de LabBook, en collaboration avec l’Assistant SIL.
- Veiller à l’alignement de l’ensemble des interventions menées dans les quatre pays sur les règlementations nationales et les standards internationaux de la BSS.

Mission 5 : Contribuer au suivi technique

- Participer aux missions de suivi, de supervision et d’évaluation, en veillant au respect des normes et procédures applicables en matière de biosécurité et de biosûreté.
- Contribuer à l’analyse des résultats techniques, à l’identification des risques biologiques et à la capitalisation des enseignements tirés des projets.
- Participer à l’élaboration et à la diffusion de publications techniques et scientifiques, en intégrant, lorsque cela est pertinent, les enjeux de biosécurité et de biosûreté.

Mission 6 : Contribuer au développement des partenariats techniquesde la Fondation Mérieux

- Participer activement aux travaux des groupes techniques régionaux dédiés à la biosécurité et à la biosûreté.
- Contribuer à la préparation, à l’organisation et au suivi des réunions techniques régionales des projets.
- Favoriser le partage d’expériences, de bonnes pratiques et d’enseignements entre les pays de mise en œuvre des projets sur les enjeux de biosécurité et de biosûreté
- Contribuer à l’identification et au développement de nouvelles opportunités de partenariat et d’intervention pour la Fondation Mérieux dans les domaines de la biosécurité et de la biosûreté.

Formation complémentaire / spécialisation

- Formation spécialisée en BSS, idéalement la certification de l’IFBA “Professional Certification in Biological Risk Assessment”.

- Une expérience dans les pays d’Afrique de l’Ouest constitue un atout.

- Maîtrise des référentiels internationaux applicables aux laboratoires.
- Évaluation et renforcement des systèmes nationaux de laboratoire.
- Conception et animation de formations techniques.
- Analyse des risques biologiques et formulation de recommandations.
- Collecte, analyse et interprétation de données techniques.
- Excellentes capacités de rédaction scientifique et technique.

Compétences comportementales requises Esprit d’analyse et rigueur scientifique.

Sens de l’organisation et autonomie. Excellentes aptitudes pédagogiques. Esprit d'équipe et collaboration.

Langues

- Excellente maîtrise de l’anglais & du français, à l’oral comme à l’écrit.

jobs.title: Consultancy to Validate and Synthesize Existing Market Evidence for Women’s Economic Inclusion, Livelihoods and Market Systems in Kenya
jobs.description:
**About RefuSHE**

RefuSHE Kenya protects, educates and empowers orphaned, unaccompanied and separated refugee girls and young women to build healthier and more resilient futures for themselves and their children. The organization works across protection, education, skills development, livelihoods and economic empowerment.

**Background Context**

RefuSHE is embarking on a four-year Angaza program delivered by a consortium of implementing partners , seeking to advance economic and financial inclusion for diverse refugee and host community young women aged 18–35, including persons with disabilities, operating within the informal economy in camp and urban contexts. To bypass systemic barriers to formal employment, the program scales refugee-led, gender-responsive models through a multi-pronged strategy combining market-relevant skills training, apprenticeships, access to capital, and market linkages to strengthen young women-led micro-enterprises and livelihoods.

Kenya has an established body of research on refugee livelihoods, labour markets, market systems and economic inclusion. To avoid duplication, this assignment will not undertake a new broad market assessment; rather, it will critically assess and validate existing evidence against the current operating context. We seek a consultant to test that evidence against the 2026 context, fill critical gaps with targeted primary research, and translate findings into clear, evidence-scored livelihood pathways.

**Core question:** *What can Angaza confidently rely on from existing evidence about young women’s economic opportunities in the target locations; what has changed; what remains uncertain; and which economic pathways should Angaza prioritise?*

**SCOPE OF WORK AND DELIVERABLES**

The consultant will deliver the following workstreams and associated deliverables.

**Workstream**

**1. Inception**

Kick-off, review of Angaza documentation, stakeholder mapping, refined methodology, sampling frame and tool design.

Inception report with detailed workplan;

validation tools (employer, women worker/entrepreneur, KII and FGD guides)

**2.Evidence mapping & quality review**

Catalogue market, labor, value-chain, socioeconomic, financial-inclusion, digital and programme-evaluation evidence; grade each source for recency, method, geography, gender/refugee lens and 2026 relevance.

Evidence inventory; evidence quality/validity matrix; electronic evidence library

**3. Evidence synthesis**

Extract findings into a structured matrix; identify common findings, trends, contradictions and gaps; classify findings as valid, changed, outdated, contradicted or inconclusive.

Evidence synthesis matrix; evidence gap matrix

**4. Targeted primary validation**

Proportionate fieldwork to test priority findings and close critical gaps with employers, market actors, women workers/entrepreneurs, key informants and selective FGDs. No large household survey.

Stakeholder validation matrix; clean primary datasets and codebook

**5. Thematic validation**

Labour market (roles, skills, wages, hard-to-fill jobs); enterprise and value chains (demand, profitability, upgrading); financial inclusion; digital economy (online work, BPO, e-commerce).

Thematic findings within interim and final reports

**6. Women’s inclusion & barriers lens**

Access, participation, earnings, progression, agency, dignified work and resilience; barriers incl. childcare, mobility, safety, harassment, documentation, licensing, language, finance and social norms.

Women’s economic inclusion and barriers analysis

**7. County comparison**

Compare locations on demand, employment, enterprise, income potential, women’s and refugee accessibility, barriers and partnership potential.

County market comparison matrix

**8. Sector scoring & programme validation**

Score existing, adjacent and new sectors (weighted 1–5 framework with High/Medium/Low evidence rating); test Angaza partners’ programmes (beauty, dressmaking, ICT, artisan, entrepreneurship) from training to income.

Sector opportunity and validation matrix; programme validation matrix; new/untapped opportunity analysis (at least five sectors)

**9. Reporting & validation**

Decision-support interim report; validation workshop with the Angaza consortium to test findings.

Interim validation report (25–35 pages.); validation workshop and presentation

**10. Strategic translation**

Pathway-level recommendations: target group, intervention model, partners, KPIs, risks and indicative resources; each classified Scale / Continue / Redesign / Pilot / Explore / Do not prioritize.

Final assessment report; strategic opportunity matrix; 2026–2030 investment recommendations; PowerPoint of key findings

**WHAT YOUR TECHNICAL PROPOSAL SHOULD COVER**

We encourage applicants to go into depth. The technical proposal should cover:

1. **Understanding of the assignment** and of the refugee economic-inclusion context in Kenya, including the Refugees Act 2021 and the Shirika Plan.
2. **Evidence-synthesis methodology:** search strategy, inclusion criteria, how evidence strength and 2026 validity will be graded and how contradictions will be resolved.
3. **Primary validation approach:** proposed sample sizes and sampling by location, stakeholder group, refugee/host and disability status; tools; interpretation for Somali, Arabic, French and other refugee languages; data quality assurance.
4. **Approach to each scope workstream and annex tool,** including how sectors will be scored, how new sectors will be identified and tested, and how the training-to-income pathway of existing programmes will be assessed.
5. **Detailed 8-week workplan:** week-by-week activities and milestones, timing of each deliverable, review and feedback points, level of effort per team member, and risks (access, permits, security, timelines) with mitigation.
6. **Ethics, safeguarding and data protection:** informed consent, Department of refugee services clearances, do-no-harm and referral procedures, and compliance with the Kenya Data Protection Act.
7. **Team composition and CVs** (with a strong focus in economic inclusion/livelihoods; market systems/value chain; labour market; gender and women’s economic empowerment; quantitative and qualitative research).

**CONSULTANT LEAD REQUIREMENTS**

- Postgraduate degree in economics, labour economics, development studies, business, livelihoods or a related field.
- At least 8 years’ experience in market systems, livelihoods and economic inclusion research, including validating or synthesising evidence across multiple locations.
- Proven experience in labour-market and value-chain analysis, refugee economic inclusion in Kenya/East Africa, and gender-responsive research.
- Strong mixed-methods and data-analysis skills; ability to translate evidence into practical programme and investment recommendations.
- Fluency in English and Swahili; working knowledge of Arabic and French desirable. Certification as a data processor with the ODPC.

jobs.title: GBV Policy & Advocacy Technical Advisor
jobs.description:
**Job Title:** GBV Policy & Advocacy Technical Advisor

**Location:** Erbil, Kurdistan Region, Iraq (KRI), with occasional travel to other areas of KRI.

**Type of position:** Employment Contract/ Expat or National Contract

**Length of Contract:** 12 Months

**Compensation and Benefits:** Competitive salary and benefits commensurate with skills and experience. Local/Expatriate Compensation Package: includes relocation expenses and housing and local transportation allowances

**About SEED:** SEED is a women-led, local NGO in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq, working to **create a future where everyone can thrive by protecting rights, empowering communities, and strengthening systems.** We promote gender equality and work to end gender-based violence; protect children and promote the healthy development of children, adolescents, and youth; combat human trafficking and uphold survivor rights; and improve mental health and well-being. Through transformational services, community development, capacity building, and policy and advocacy, we support individuals, communities, and institutions to create sustainable impact.

**Role of the GBV Policy & Advocacy Technical Advisor:** The GBV Policy & Advocacy Advisor will provide technical expertise and leadership for SEED’s policy and advocacy work on promoting gender equality and combating GBV. The GBV Policy & Advocacy Advisor will identify institutional and “on the ground” gaps and needs in the KRI, and advocate for legislative and regulatory reforms as well as improved policies, processes, procedures, and practices to protect human rights. The Advisor will lead diverse initiatives – including advocacy, technical assistance, and capacity-building – to strengthen prevention and response strategies among governmental and non-governmental protection actors, and will lead or participate in relevant sector coordination mechanisms and working groups. The Advisor will also support the design and delivery of complementary training for service providers, contribute to messaging for public awareness campaigns on gender equality and GBV, and participate in program development. The Advisor will act as a strong advocate for universal access to human rights and identify opportunities to strengthen SEED’s impact on behalf of vulnerable groups.

**Specific Tasks:**

***Policy and Advocacy (60%)***

- Conduct research as necessary on gender equality deficits and GBV in Kurdistan, and identify gaps in prevention and response.
- Analyze relevant laws, regulations, policies, and procedures, and track developments.
- Examine international frameworks and best practices to inform approaches, adapting tools, resources, and guidance as necessary for the local context.
- Consult with diverse protection actors to understand current processes and practices related to GBV prevention and response, and conduct capacity and/or needs assessments.
- Conduct technical discussions with thematic experts and protection actors to enhance cross-organizational learning, harmonize tools and approaches, and standardize care.
- Identify opportunities to partner with government and other protection actors to strengthen prevention and response, build capacity, and support effective coordination of GBV services, and develop strategic plans to support engagement.
- Design and execute advocacy, technical assistance, and capacity building initiatives to achieve legislative and regulatory reform, and to strengthen systems, approaches, and services for the protection of human rights.
- Draft and disseminate materials to support advocacy, technical assistance, and capacity-building initiatives, such as policy briefs, issue analysis, assessments, reports, strategies, protocols and procedures, guidance, and tools.
- Prepare presentations, speeches, and talking points as needed to support high-level engagements on GBV initiatives.
- Plan and organize workshops, roundtables, and other events as needed to convene protection actors and decision-makers, secure agreements, and support uptake of key information, skills, or resources.
- Cultivate positive, responsive relationships with service providers and stakeholders across the response architecture, maintaining strong communication and ensuring effective management of expectations.

***Coordination and Organizational Representation (15%)***

- Lead or participate in relevant sector coordination mechanisms and working groups, including the national Technology Facilitated GBV Task Force, Regional GBV Sector, and GBV Working Groups.
- Represent SEED in coordination fora, with KRG and other stakeholders, and with donors
- Identify opportunities for collaboration, develop strategic partnerships, and maintain effective working relationships with all key stakeholders.
- Provide resources, information, and support to external audiences, as requested.

***Technical Leadership (25%)***

- Participate in program design and development to ensure that SEED’s GBV policy and advocacy work is responsive and calibrated for impact
- Support program monitoring and evaluation, including development of tools, to build strong feedback loops on GBV policy and advocacy interventions and facilitate course correction as needed.
- Ensure proper documentation of GBV policy and advocacy activities and contribute to quality reporting.
- Support the design, development, review, and delivery of SEED’s GBV trainings for service providers and other stakeholders.
- Contribute to the development of strategies and messaging for awareness campaigns on gender equality and GBV.
- Develop content and provide input on communications related to SEED’s GBV work, including website articles and social media, and ensure compliance with SEED’s storytelling policy.

**Essential Criteria:**

- Master’s Degree in social work, public policy, gender studies, psychology, law, international development, human rights, or another related field.
- At least five years of international development and/or humanitarian experience in GBV programming, including supervision of services and advocacy for improved legislative and policy protections.
- At least three years of experience working in a senior technical or programmatic role.
- Experience implementing donor-funded international development and/or humanitarian assistance programs.
- Familiarity and previous experience with the UN-led cluster coordination system, mechanisms, and tools.
- Direct and demonstrable experience working with government actors to achieve institutional change.
- Strong belief in gender equality and human rights.
- Strong people and project management skills.
- Strong leadership skills.
- Good interpersonal, communication, time management and team-building skills.
- High standard of spoken and written English, with Arabic and/or Kurdish a plus.
- Experience in Iraq and/or Kurdistan Region is a plus.
- Ability to work in a stressful setting and adapt quickly to changing environments.

jobs.title: Financial Planning & Analysis Advisor
jobs.description:
**Selection Criteria:** The Financial Planning and Analysis Advisor position is open to candidates residing in countries where Medical Teams International can legally employ staff, either directly or through an approved third-party Employer of Record (EOR). To support collaboration with global teams, candidates must be located within the UTC-8 to UTC+3 time zone range.

The Financial Planning and Analysis Advisor contributes to the calling of Medical Teams International by providing financial and business analytics support to drive financial planning and help make informed business decisions. This senior level role serves as a strategic business partner to executive and departmental leadership by providing forward-looking financial insights, enterprise performance analytics, and decision-support tools that optimize organizational resources and advance strategic priorities. The Financial Planning and Analysis Advisor leads organization-wide forecasting, scenario planning, performance measurement, and financial modeling activities to support sustainable growth, operational effectiveness, and mission impact.

**Medical Teams International Calling:**

Daring to love like Jesus, we boldly break barriers to health and restore wholeness in a hurting world.

Medical Teams International holds strict child and vulnerable adult safeguarding principles and a zero tolerance policy for misconduct related to sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse in the workplace and other places where the organization’s activities are rendered. Parallel to technical competence, recruitment & selection, hiring decisions will give due emphasis to assessing candidates’ eligibility, thorough background checks, police clearance, and professional reference check processes.

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Reporting and Analysis**

- Manage the financial planning and analysis (FP&A) process. This includes financial reporting, creating various financial metrics and dashboards, and scenario and predictive modeling.
- Lead indirect cost rate calculations and create cost recovery models across all business units.
- Prepare reports for Negotiated Indirect Cost Rate Agreement (NICRA).
- Develop and report monthly, quarterly, and annual metrics pertaining to departmental efficiencies, cost recovery, labor optimization, revenue, etc.
- Review, analyze, and distribute financial reports to budget holders and support interpretation of financial results.
- Create presentations for senior and executive management that provide insightful analysis, identify required action items, and effectively frame decisions to be made.
- Identify and research discrepancies and variances to forecast, budget, and prior-year and proactively identify opportunities for improvement across the enterprise
- Develop and maintain multi-year financial forecasts and strategic planning models to support organizational sustainability and growth initiatives.
- Establish and monitor enterprise key performance indicators (KPIs) and operational scorecards aligned with strategic objectives.
- Lead financial scenario analyses and sensitivity modeling to support executive decision-making, risk assessment, and resource prioritization.
- Partner with Development, Global Programs, and Executive Leadership to analyze funding trends, grant pipelines, donor concentration risks, and revenue sustainability.
- Prepare financial and operational analyses for executive leadership, Board committees, and senior management meetings.

**Budget**

- Oversee and coordinate data collection and input feeding into the annual global budget process.
- Create guidance documentation, and templates for budget holders, budget models for decision making, prior year analysis, current year projections plus providing budget system support and training.
- Identify foreign exchange exposure to include monitoring, reporting, and hedging as appropriate during annual budget and reforecasting cycle.
- Reconcile budget revisions and manage budgets in the ERP system. Input the finance department budget into the ERP system while offering educational assistance to other departments as needed.
- Lead quarterly reforecasting and rolling forecast processes across the organization.
- Evaluate investment proposals, staffing requests, and strategic initiatives through financial analysis and business case development.
- Partner with departmental leaders to identify opportunities for operational efficiency, cost optimization, and resource alignment.

**ERP and Financial Systems Support**

- Serve as a Finance ERP champion and the primary focal point for coaching, support and troubleshooting.
- Identify opportunities for financial process improvements by leveraging the ERP platform and other modules alongside the IS department.
- Develop training material and facilitate knowledge sharing and training on the use of digital tools for budget and reporting evaluations.
- Lead finance data governance initiatives to ensure consistency, integrity, and reliability of enterprise financial data.
- Collaborate with Information Systems to expand business intelligence capabilities through dashboards, automated reporting, and advanced analytics tools.
- Identify and implement automation opportunities to reduce manual effort and improve financial reporting efficiency.

**Other Duties**

- Support safeguarding of program participants and employees through promoting an environment of awareness and upholding the code of conduct provisions of Medical Teams Protection from Sexual Exploitation, Abuse & Harassment, Child & Vulnerable Adult protection, and harassment-free workplace policies. Incumbents will remain alert and responsive to any child and adult safeguarding risks, acquire relevant knowledge and skills which will enable you to promote strong safeguarding practices, understand the child and adult safeguarding policy and procedures, and conduct yourself in a manner consistent with the Safeguarding code of conduct and behavior expectations.
- Support the Finance department as needed, while having a line of sight into the financial metrics and performance of Philanthropy, Marketing & Mobilization, Global Programs, and Executive Management.
- Facilitate cross-functional financial reviews and business performance discussions with organizational leaders.
- Support enterprise risk assessment activities by identifying financial, operational, and funding risks and recommending mitigation strategies.
- Participate in organizational transformation initiatives and support change management efforts related to finance systems, processes, and reporting.
- Participate in and support strategic projects as requested.
- Utilize volunteers when appropriate.
- Additional duties as assigned.

## **Qualifications**

**EDUCATION, LICENSE & CERTIFICATIONS**

**Required:**

- Bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, business, economics, or closely related fields
- Valid passport

**Preferred:**

- Master’s degree and/or finance/accounting related certification
- Certified Corporate FP&A Professional (FPAC), CPA, CMA, CGMA, CFA, or equivalent professional designation
- Training or certification in business intelligence, data analytics, or financial systems administration

**EXPERIENCE**

**Required:**

- Minimum 6 years’ relevant experience in an NGO context
- 4 years’ financial planning, analysis, and non-profit budgeting experience
- 4 years’ indirect cost rate / NICRA modeling and reporting
- Prior experience in public accounting, audit, data analytics, business operations or relevant field
- Experience with Power BI, Tableau, Adaptive Planning, Workday Adaptive, or equivalent platforms
- Experience leading process improvement, automation, or finance transformation initiatives

**KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & ABILITIES**

**Knowledge:**

- US-GAAP
- Non-profit financial statements and corporate finance reports
- Financial planning, forecasting, budgeting, and variance analysis principles
- Nonprofit accounting, restricted funding, grant budgeting, and donor compliance
- Indirect cost allocation, cost recovery, and NICRA principles
- ERP-based financial reporting and data structures
- Internal controls, financial policies, and audit-ready documentation practice
- Strategic planning and enterprise performance management frameworks
- Business intelligence, data governance, and analytics best practices
- Financial risk assessment and scenario planning techniques

**Skills:**

- Spreadsheet proficiency
- Data manipulation
- Data visualization
- Building business, operational, or financial reports
- Financial modeling from multiple data sources
- Strategic financial analysis and decision support
- Long-range financial planning and enterprise forecasting
- ERP/NetSuite, expense management systems, and Microsoft Office
- Facilitation and stakeholder management
- Data visualization and storytelling
- Exceptional communication skills, especially with executive and non-financial audiences

**Abilities:**

- Commitment to Medical Teams International Calling statement and Values
- Ability to manage multiple and shifting priorities while meeting deadlines
- Strong ability to analyze details, identify issues, and communicate with courage
- Strong Ability to learn new technologies quickly
- Ability to navigate complex business environments
- Ability to work proactively and collaboratively
- Ability to communicate difficult or detailed issues with courage
- Ability to translate complex financial information into actionable insights for executive and non-financial audiences
- Ability to think strategically while maintaining operational excellence
- Ability to influence organizational decision-making through data-driven recommendations
- Ability to lead change initiatives and drive adoption of new processes and technologies
- Ability to anticipate emerging financial and operational challenges and proactively recommend solutions

**Compensation:**

The anticipated hiring range for this position is **$86,000-$92,000 USD annually**. Final compensation will be determined based on the selected candidate's qualifications, relevant experience, internal equity considerations, and geographic location.

While the salary range listed applies to candidates residing in the United States, compensation for candidates located outside the U.S. will be determined using Medical Teams International's international compensation framework and may vary based on local market conditions and organizational compensation practices.

jobs.title: Response Program Manager

This position works closely with Miyamoto, the Sistema Nacional de Protección Civil (SINAPROC), relevant government ministries, local partners, and international stakeholders.
