jobs.title: Food Security and Agriculture Program Coordinator
jobs.company: International Association for Relief and Development
jobs.description:
## **About ONSUR:**

The International Association for Relief and Development (ONSUR) is a non-governmental organization established in early 2012 and registered in Syria. ONSUR is dedicated to implementing relief and development projects that empower local communities and promote a dignified life for vulnerable populations. , the organization operates through a network of execution offices in Syria, Lebanon, Iraq, Turkey, and Yemen. ONSUR delivers humanitarian assistance and sustainable development initiatives in conflict-affected regions, with a focus on transparency, community engagement, and long-term impact.

**Location:** **Damascus**

**POSITION SUMMARY:**

The Food Security and Agriculture Program Coordinator leads the technical design, delivery and quality assurance of ONSUR’s food security and agricultural programming .

The role supports crisis-affected households and communities to meet immediate food needs, restore and strengthen crop and livestock production, protect productive resources, and build resilient, sustainable local food systems. Programming is informed by food availability, access, utilization and stability, and adapted to seasonal, market, climate and conflict-related risks.

The Coordinator is accountable for food-security results and the technical quality of agricultural interventions from emergency food assistance, crop and livestock inputs, agricultural extension and irrigation to animal health, post-harvest practices and the resilience of farming systems.

In ONSUR’s integrated programming, agricultural commercialization, farmer-to-market linkages, producer-enterprise development, SME support, small grants and agribusiness financing are led by the Early Recovery and Livelihoods (ERL) Program Coordinator and requires high level of coordination between the FSA and ERL programs.

This position provides the agricultural and food-security technical inputs to such initiatives and ensures interventions are complementary and well-coordinated.

**Duties and Responsibilities**

**Key Responsibilities**

**1. Program strategy, technical assessments and design**

**•** Lead food security and agriculture Program planning in line with ONSUR priorities, national and local context, humanitarian principles, area-based approaches and applicable donor and sector guidance.

**•** Oversee household food-security assessments, agricultural needs and capacity assessments, market and price analysis, seasonal calendars, crop and livestock production assessments, water-resource considerations and conflict-sensitivity reviews.

**•** Develop context-specific responses that address urgent food gaps while linking, where feasible, to recovery of agricultural production, natural resources and local food systems.

**•** Lead technical inputs to concept notes, proposals, theories of change, log frames, budgets, implementation plans and sector-specific SOPs, working closely with Program , Finance, Supply Chain and MEAL colleagues.

**2. Emergency food security and household access to food**

**•** Provide technical leadership for appropriately targeted food assistance, including in-kind food distributions, food vouchers and cash-based food assistance where needs, markets, donor rules and risk analysis support the modality.

**•** Guide selection of transfer or food-basket content, adequacy, frequency, distribution arrangements and monitoring in relation to household needs, local diets, food prices, market functionality and dignity of recipients.

**•** Ensure sound beneficiary targeting and verification, safe and accessible delivery, appropriate food quality and shelf-life controls, post-distribution monitoring and effective community feedback processes.

**•** Promote nutrition-sensitive food security, food safety, dietary diversity and practical links with WASH, Health and Protection services; identify referral needs without duplicating specialist nutrition or health functions.

**3. Crop production, seed systems and farmer support**

**•** Design and technically supervise agricultural recovery packages covering quality seeds and seedlings, tools, appropriate fertilizers, soil inputs, home gardens, field crops, horticulture and protected agriculture, based on agroecological suitability.

**•** Strengthen smallholder production through agricultural extension, demonstration plots, farmer field schools, crop calendars, soil management, integrated pest management and safe input handling.

**•** Ensure agricultural inputs meet agreed quality specifications, locally appropriate varieties and planting seasons; coordinate verification, transparent distribution and post-assistance technical follow-up.

**•** Assess and support rehabilitation of essential on-farm productive assets and community agricultural services where feasible, with due attention to safe land access, tenure, affordability and maintenance.

**4. Livestock production and animal-source food security**

**•** Lead technically appropriate support for small-scale livestock, poultry and other relevant animal production systems, focusing on household food supply, herd or flock productivity and resilience.

**•** Coordinate animal feed and fodder assistance, veterinary outreach, vaccination, animal-health services, husbandry training and disease-prevention measures through suitably qualified veterinary personnel and responsible authorities.

**•** Promote animal welfare, biosecurity, adequate water provision, safe handling of animal-source foods and environmentally responsible livestock management.

**•** Monitor seasonal feed availability, animal health risks, local service capacities and the practical sustainability of supported livestock assets.

**5. Irrigation, climate resilience and natural-resource stewardship**

**•** Provide technical direction for agricultural water access and irrigation rehabilitation, including water-efficient equipment and practices, in coordination with qualified engineers and relevant authorities.

**•** Integrate climate-smart and resource-efficient farming practices, drought preparedness, crop diversification, soil and water conservation and other locally suitable risk-reduction measures.

**•** Ensure proposals are grounded in water availability, environmental and social risk screening, feasibility, safe maintenance arrangements and avoidance of harm to other water users.

**•** Coordinate infrastructure interfaces with WASH, Shelter and other technical teams without duplicating engineering approval or sector-specific accountabilities.

**6. Agricultural services, post-harvest management and integrated technical support**

**•** Strengthen agricultural extension networks, community seed systems, farmer technical training and access to essential agricultural inputs, veterinary support and production-related services.

**•** Improve on-farm and post-harvest handling, safe storage, food safety, produce quality and loss reduction to protect agricultural output and food availability.

**•** Assess agricultural input availability, production constraints, crop and livestock service gaps, seasonal risks and food losses, and translate findings into technically sound food security and agricultural recovery interventions.

**•** Coordinate with the ERL Program Coordinator on initiatives involving agricultural commercialization, farmer-to-market linkages, producer organizations and enterprises, SME support, small grants, business incubation or agribusiness finance. The ERL Program Coordinator leads the economic empowerment components; this role provides technical oversight of agricultural production, livestock systems, input quality and food-security outcomes.

**7. Implementation quality, operations and risk management**

**•** Provide technical oversight to project teams on workplans, activity sequencing, procurement specifications, bills of quantities, distribution protocols, supplier quality and seasonal delivery timelines.

**•** Develop or review technical guidelines, SOPs, eligibility criteria, site assessments and inspection checklists for agricultural assistance, food commodities and productive-asset rehabilitation.

**•** Conduct regular field visits and technical reviews; track progress, expenditure implications, input performance and implementation risks; agree corrective actions with project teams and management.

**•** Coordinate with Supply Chain and Finance on due diligence, commodity and input traceability, transport, storage, distribution documentation and appropriate segregation of duties.

**•** Enforce ONSUR and donor requirements on safeguarding, PSEA, accountability, anti-fraud, data protection, conflict sensitivity, environmental responsibility and safe access for women and marginalized groups.

**8. MEAL, results measurement and reporting**

**•** Work with MEAL colleagues to establish baselines, outcome indicators, field verification, beneficiary feedback, seasonal follow-up and suitable post-distribution monitoring systems.

**•** Measure food-security changes using context-appropriate indicators (for example Food Consumption Score, reduced Coping Strategies Index and dietary diversity), alongside agricultural production, yields, asset functionality and adoption of improved practices.

**•** Analyze food prices, crop and livestock outcomes, access barriers, environmental risks and sustainability; adjust programming based on evidence and community feedback.

**•** Prepare accurate technical and narrative inputs for donor reports, proposals, learning notes and internal performance reviews, reconciled with MEAL and financial records.

**09. Team leadership, coordination and partnerships**

**•** Provide technical leadership, mentoring and quality assurance for food security and agriculture staff and implementing partners, including capacity-building plans and field coaching.

**•** Maintain effective working relationships with agriculture and veterinary directorates, local authorities, farmers and community agricultural structures, research and extension bodies, UN agencies, NGOs and relevant agricultural service providers.

**•** Represent ONSUR in appropriate Food Security and Agriculture coordination platforms and technical working groups, as delegated by the Programs Manager.

**•** Advance integrated and area-based programming with the ERL Program Coordinator and other relevant sector teams, ensuring complementary interventions, clear technical accountabilities and appropriate referral or coordination pathways.

**10. Safeguarding and Compliance**

• Ensure all interventions are designed and implemented with due consideration of **protection, gender, age, disability inclusion**, **housing-land-and-property rights**, conflict sensitivity, and the **do-no-harm principle**.
• Promote safe, accessible, and accountable programming and ensure staff, contractors, and communities understand feedback and reporting mechanisms for misconduct or abuse.
• Ensure compliance with **ONSUR's Code of Conduct**, Child Safeguarding Policy, **PSEA standards**, procurement rules, technical approvals, and donor requirements.
• Report safeguarding, fraud, safety, environmental, or compliance concerns through established organizational procedures and support timely corrective action.

**Note:**

The above responsibilities are illustrative and not exhaustive. Additional tasks may be assigned based on organizational needs and evolving program requirements.

## **Required Qualifications & Experience**

**Education:**

- Education: Bachelor’s degree in agriculture, Agronomy, Agricultural Engineering, Animal Science, Veterinary Medicine, Food Security, Rural Development or a closely related field. A relevant postgraduate qualification is an advantage.

**Experience:**

- Experience: At least 04 years of relevant experience in food security and/or agriculture Programs, including at least two years of program management, technical supervision or sector coordination.

**Technical Skills**

- Technical expertise: Practical knowledge of food assistance modalities, agricultural inputs and extension, crop or livestock production, seasonal planning, food-price and agricultural-input availability assessments, and rural community-based programming.
- Experience with agricultural irrigation, climate-smart practices, producer services, post-harvest systems or natural-resource management is highly desirable; specialists should demonstrate the ability to coordinate complementary disciplines.
- Strong capability in proposal and budget preparation, technical specifications, donor compliance, risk analysis, MEAL frameworks and constructive engagement with local institutions and communities.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint; experience with data collection, GIS or analytical dashboards is an asset.

**Core Competencies**

- Strong **coordination, communication, negotiation, leadership**, and decision-making skills.
• Ability and willingness to travel within Syria and to ONSUR's project locations as required.
• Commitment to upholding the highest standards of **safeguarding, accountability**, technical integrity, impartiality, and professional ethics

**Languages:**

- Excellent verbal and written communication skills in **Arabic and English**.

**Child Protection Policy**

ONSUR maintains a strict **zero-tolerance policy** toward all forms of child abuse and exploitation. The organization is fully committed to creating and maintaining a **child-safe environment** across all areas of its work. All employees are expected to uphold the highest standards of behavior to ensure the safety and well-being of children, and any breach of this policy will result in immediate disciplinary action.

**Anti-Discrimination, Harassment, and Abuse Policy**

ONSUR is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering a safe, inclusive, and respectful workplace for all. Discrimination, harassment, or abuse of any kind — whether based on race, ethnicity, religion, gender, age, disability, marital status, citizenship, or military status — is strictly prohibited and will not be tolerated.

All staff are expected to **promote a culture of respect** and integrity. Participation in any form of abuse, harassment (verbal, physical, or sexual), intimidation, or exploitation — whether inside or outside the workplace — is a violation of ONSUR’s core values and policies.

**Diversity & Inclusion**

ONSUR is strongly committed to gender equality and **encourages qualified female candidates** to apply for this position.

## **About ONSUR:**

The International Association for Relief and Development (ONSUR) is a non-governmental organization established in early 2012 and registered in Syria. ONSUR is dedicated to implementing relief and development projects that empower local communities and promote a dignified life for vulnerable populations. , the organization operates through a network of execution offices in Syria, Lebanon, Iraq, Turkey, and Yemen. ONSUR delivers humanitarian assistance and sustainable development initiatives in conflict-affected regions, with a focus on transparency, community engagement, and long-term impact.

**Location:** **Damascus**

**POSITION SUMMARY:**

The Early Recovery and Livelihood Program Coordinator provides technical and operational leadership for ONSUR’s early recovery, livelihoods, and economic empowerment portfolio . The postholder leads the development and implementation of market-informed interventions that restore productive assets, strengthen local economies, create decent employment and self-employment opportunities, and help crisis-affected households move towards sustainable income and greater economic self-reliance.

A core responsibility of the role is to lead ONSUR’s economic empowerment initiatives across multiple complementary modalities: micro, small and medium-sized enterprise (MSME/SME) development; small business and start-up grants; entrepreneurship and business recovery support; agricultural and rural economic development; vocational skills and employment pathways; and market and value-chain linkages.

The coordinator ensures that these interventions are inclusive, economically viable, accountable, compliant with donor requirements, and tailored to local market conditions.

**Duties and Responsibilities**

**Key Responsibilities**

**1. Skills development, employment and community economic recovery**

**•** Oversee market-driven vocational and technical training, apprenticeships, employability skills, job placement and business start-up pathways, ensuring curricula and trades reflect realistic employment and enterprise demand.

**•** Connect graduates to employers, mentorship, relevant business networks, start-up toolkits or eligible enterprise grants, with follow-up that tracks transition from training to sustainable work or self-employment.

**•** Provide technical oversight of cash-for-work and labor-intensive rehabilitation initiatives that restore community or productive assets while promoting safe working conditions, fair and transparent worker selection, and appropriate employment standards.

**•** Coordinate with Shelter, WASH, FSL, Protection and other ONSUR sectors to link rehabilitation of services and productive infrastructure with livelihood restoration and area-based economic recovery.

**2. Agricultural livelihoods and rural economic recovery**

**•** Lead agricultural economic empowerment and agribusiness interventions, working with Food Security and Livelihoods (FSL) colleagues and sector specialists to support viable farming, livestock-related activities, food processing and other rural enterprises.

**•** Design support packages for smallholder producers and agricultural businesses, which may include productive inputs, machinery and tools, irrigation improvements, climate-smart practices, post-harvest handling and income-generating agricultural assets, based on local feasibility.

**•** Strengthen producer groups, cooperatives and agricultural value chains through technical assistance, business planning, aggregation, storage, processing, marketing and buyer connections.

**•** Ensure interventions account for agricultural seasons, water-resource constraints, environmental sustainability, land and tenure risks, input availability, market demand and potential negative effects on local markets.

**3. Economic empowerment, SMEs and small-grant initiatives**

**•** Lead the design, rollout and technical oversight of economic empowerment interventions for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, including business establishment, recovery, expansion, formalization support where feasible, and entrepreneurship development.

**•** Design and manage small-grant and start-up assistance schemes (cash and/or in-kind), including clear eligibility and selection criteria, business-plan review, enterprise viability assessment, due diligence, approval workflows, grant documentation, disbursement coordination and post-grant verification.

**•** Ensure that grant packages are paired, where appropriate, with tailored business development services, financial literacy, basic bookkeeping, market research, coaching, mentorship, and follow-up support to improve business continuity and growth.

**•** Develop enterprise support interventions that strengthen productive capacities through tools, equipment, working capital or other eligible inputs, based on demonstrable business needs and donor-approved programme modalities.

**•** Facilitate linkages between supported enterprises and relevant suppliers, customers, buyers, business networks, chambers of commerce and service providers; promote local procurement and sustainable market participation.

**•** Promote equitable access to opportunities for women, young people, returnees, displaced populations, persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups, with appropriate protection safeguards and market-based targeting.

**4. Strategy, programme design and resource mobilization**

**•** Lead the technical direction and planning of ONSUR’s Early Recovery, Livelihoods and Economic Empowerment programming, aligned with organizational priorities, area-based recovery approaches, and relevant coordination frameworks.

**•** Oversee household economic assessments, labour-market studies, market-system and value-chain assessments, business feasibility analysis, and context/risk analysis to identify viable livelihood and enterprise opportunities.

**•** Design integrated, evidence-based interventions and implementation models; develop theories of change, results frameworks, activity packages, technical specifications, detailed budgets, and operational plans.

**•** Lead the technical development of concept notes and proposals for livelihoods, MSME support, small grants, agribusiness, cash-for-work and other early recovery interventions, in coordination with Programs, Finance, Supply Chain and MEAL teams.

**5. Implementation quality, grant controls and risk management**

**•** Guide project teams in preparing realistic workplans, procurement requirements, cash forecasts, technical guidelines, beneficiary-targeting tools and implementation schedules; monitor delivery, budgets and results against approved plans.

**•** Develop and maintain fit-for-purpose Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and quality-assurance processes for livelihood assistance, enterprise support and grant mechanisms, including transparent selection, verification, approvals, documentation and follow-up.

**•** Coordinate closely with Finance and Supply Chain on grant transfers, vendor or beneficiary payments, procurement, asset handover, financial documentation and verification, maintaining appropriate segregation of duties.

**•** Carry out regular field monitoring and technical reviews, identify delivery bottlenecks and emerging economic or protection risks, and agree corrective actions with project teams and management.

**•** Ensure activities follow ONSUR policies, donor rules, anti-fraud measures, safeguarding/PSEA requirements, conflict-sensitive and do-no-harm approaches, accountability to affected people, data protection and inclusion standards.

**6. MEAL, reporting, sustainability and learning**

**•** Work with the MEAL team to establish baselines, realistic outcome indicators, market monitoring plans, beneficiary feedback mechanisms, post-distribution monitoring and, where relevant, follow-up/tracer assessments.

**•** Monitor meaningful economic outcomes such as enterprise survival or growth, income improvement, employment or self-employment, grant utilization, productive capacity, agricultural earnings and sustained access to markets—not only activity completion.

**•** Analyze performance, delivery costs, inclusion and sustainability risks; use evidence and lessons learned to adapt Program design and improve results.

**•** Consolidate accurate technical inputs for donor and internal reporting, success stories and learning products, ensuring consistency with verified data, expenditure information and donor requirements.

**7. Team leadership, partnerships and representation**

**•** Provide technical supervision, mentoring and quality assurance to ERL project managers, officers and field teams; identify capacity gaps and deliver practical training on business development, grants, agriculture and market-based programming.

**•** Build working relationships with relevant local authorities, agricultural and economic directorates, private-sector actors, financial-service and business-development providers, producer groups, NGOs and community representatives.

**•** Represent ONSUR in relevant Early Recovery, Livelihoods, FSL and economic empowerment coordination structures and technical discussions, as delegated by the Programs Manager.

**•** Ensure meaningful participation of communities and foster coordination across Programs to avoid duplication, support complementarity and strengthen locally led recovery.

**8. Safeguarding and Compliance**

• Ensure all interventions are designed and implemented with due consideration of **protection, gender, age, disability inclusion**, **housing-land-and-property rights**, conflict sensitivity, and the **do-no-harm principle**.
• Promote safe, accessible, and accountable programming and ensure staff, contractors, and communities understand feedback and reporting mechanisms for misconduct or abuse.
• Ensure compliance with **ONSUR's Code of Conduct**, Child Safeguarding Policy, **PSEA standards**, procurement rules, technical approvals, and donor requirements.
• Report safeguarding, fraud, safety, environmental, or compliance concerns through established organizational procedures and support timely corrective action.

**Note:**

The above responsibilities are illustrative and not exhaustive. Additional tasks may be assigned based on organizational needs and evolving program requirements.

## **Required Qualifications & Experience**

**Education:**

- Education: Bachelor’s degree in Economics, Business Administration, Agriculture, Agribusiness, International Development, Development Studies or another relevant discipline. A postgraduate qualification is an advantage.

**Experience:**

- Experience: Minimum 03 years of relevant experience in humanitarian, early recovery, livelihoods or economic development programming, including Program/project management or technical coordination responsibilities.

**Technical Skills**

- Technical experience: Demonstrated practical experience in economic empowerment, ideally spanning at least two modalities such as MSME/SME development, small-business or start-up grants, entrepreneurship support, agricultural livelihoods/agribusiness, vocational training or employment creation.
- Knowledge: Strong understanding of market-based livelihoods approaches, business feasibility and selection, grant-management controls, private-sector engagement, risk management and sustainable income-generation pathways. Familiarity with Syria’s economic and agricultural context is a strong asset.

**Core Competencies**

- Strong **coordination, communication, negotiation, leadership**, and decision-making skills.
• Ability and willingness to travel within Syria and to ONSUR's project locations as required.
• Commitment to upholding the highest standards of **safeguarding, accountability**, technical integrity, impartiality, and professional ethics

**Languages:**

- Excellent verbal and written communication skills in **Arabic and English**.

**Child Protection Policy**

ONSUR maintains a strict **zero-tolerance policy** toward all forms of child abuse and exploitation. The organization is fully committed to creating and maintaining a **child-safe environment** across all areas of its work. All employees are expected to uphold the highest standards of behavior to ensure the safety and well-being of children, and any breach of this policy will result in immediate disciplinary action.

**Anti-Discrimination, Harassment, and Abuse Policy**

ONSUR is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering a safe, inclusive, and respectful workplace for all. Discrimination, harassment, or abuse of any kind — whether based on race, ethnicity, religion, gender, age, disability, marital status, citizenship, or military status — is strictly prohibited and will not be tolerated.

All staff are expected to **promote a culture of respect** and integrity. Participation in any form of abuse, harassment (verbal, physical, or sexual), intimidation, or exploitation — whether inside or outside the workplace — is a violation of ONSUR’s core values and policies.

**Diversity & Inclusion**

ONSUR is strongly committed to gender equality and **encourages qualified female candidates** to apply for this position.

jobs.company: Plan International Latin America and the Caribbean
jobs.description:
Ver términos de referencia completos aquí [https://plan-international.org/uploads/sites/56/2026/10/TdR_Business_Development_and_Partnership_Specialist.pdf](https://plan-international.org/uploads/sites/56/2026/10/TdR_Business_Development_and_Partnership_Specialist.pdf)

Antecedentes
Venezuela enfrenta una crisis humanitaria prolongada desde 2016, caracterizada por la contracción económica, el deterioro de los servicios básicos, la inseguridad alimentaria y crecientes riesgos de protección. Los terremotos del 24 de junio de 2026 agravaron estas necesidades, ante lo cual Plan International desplegó un equipo de emergencia y amplió su respuesta con el objetivo de alcanzar hasta 200.000 personas afectadas, con especial énfasis en la niñez y la igualdad de género. Las intervenciones abarcan agua, saneamiento e higiene; protección de la niñez; educación en emergencias; salud mental y apoyo psicosocial; y asistencia de emergencia. Desde 2019, Plan International implementa su respuesta en Venezuela a través de organizaciones socias nacionales e internacionales, promoviendo el liderazgo local, la complementariedad y la toma de decisiones compartida. Este modelo se complementa con consultores en el país y asistencia técnica regional y global. Plan International coordina la respuesta y asegura la calidad programática, la rendición de cuentas y la articulación humanitaria. La ampliación de las intervenciones hace necesario fortalecer la gestión de grants, los procesos de reporte a donantes y el seguimiento y acompañamiento a los socios implementadores.

En este contexto, Plan International requiere fortalecer su capacidad estratégica y operativa para la gestión de grants, el desarrollo de negocios y la gestión de organizaciones socias en Venezuela. La consultoría tendrá como prioridad inmediata coordinar y ejecutar los procesos de la cartera vigente, incluyendo reportes a donantes, FAD, convenios y seguimiento a socios, y contribuirá al relacionamiento con donantes institucionales y al diseño y redacción de propuestas junto con el equipo de Programas. Asimismo, permitirá transferir progresivamente los procesos actualmente acompañados por el equipo regional, asegurando la continuidad, calidad y cumplimiento oportuno de los compromisos.

Objeto de la consultoría
Brindar apoyo operativo y administrativo a la gestión de grants y organizaciones socias en Venezuela, contribuyendo a la continuidad de la cartera y al cumplimiento oportuno de los compromisos con donantes y socios. La consultoría comprenderá la preparación y actualización de FAD y registros de grants, la recopilación y organización de insumos para reportes y propuestas, la tramitación de convenios y adendas, la organización de expedientes y el seguimiento de plazos, entregables, trámites y documentación pendiente, conforme a las orientaciones y prioridades validadas por Plan International. La revisión y validación técnica, las aprobaciones, el relacionamiento estratégico con donantes y la toma de decisiones corresponderán a Plan International y al referente senior designado. La persona consultora mantendrá la trazabilidad de los procesos y comunicará oportunamente retrasos, inconsistencias y otras incidencias que requieran atención.

jobs.description:
About : Action contre la Faim

Créée en 1979, Action contre la Faim est une organisation non gouvernementale internationale qui lutte contre la faim dans le monde. Sa charte des principes humanitaires - indépendance, neutralité, non-discrimination, accès libre et direct aux victimes, professionnalisme, transparence - fonde son identité depuis 45 ans. Sa mission est de sauver des vies en éliminant la faim par la prévention, la détection et le traitement de la sous-nutrition, en particulier pendant et après les situations d'urgence liées aux conflits et aux catastrophes naturelles. Action contre la Faim coordonne ses programmes autour de 7 domaines d'activités : Nutrition et Santé - Santé Mentale, Soutien Psychosocial - Sécurité Alimentaire et Moyens d'Existence - Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène - Plaidoyer - Climat - Recherche. En 2024, Action contre la Faim est venue en aide à plus de 26 millions de personnes dans 57 pays à travers le monde. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

Mission :

Sous la supervision du Responsable Terrain, votre mission sera de mettre en place une prise en charge médicale et nutritionnelle de qualité pour les enfants souffrant de malnutrition aiguë sévère.
Dans ce cadre, vos responsabilités seront de :
Mettre en place et superviser la qualité des activités des projets Nutrition-Santé
Assurer une gestion de projet efficiente et contribuer aux développements des programmes Nutrition-Santé mis en oeuvre à l'Est
Former, encadrer et manager les équipes ACF Nutrition-Santé
Participer à la coordination de la crise à l'Est, représentation et au partenariat d'ACF auprès des partenaires et autres acteurs dans sa zone d'intervention
Représenter ACF et développer les partenariats locaux

Profile :

Vous êtes titulaire d'un diplôme d'Infirmier·ère ou de Médecin, complété par une expérience en PCIMA, PCIME et SSR dans des contextes d'urgence.
Vous justifiez d'au moins 5 ans d'expérience dans le secteur humanitaire au sein d'une ONG internationale, en tant que Responsable de Projet ou de Programme, incluant le management d'équipes et le renforcement des capacités.
Vous avez une expérience confirmée dans la coordination des réponses aux urgences sanitaires et nutritionnelles, en collaboration avec d'autres ONG, des partenaires étatiques et des organisations communautaires.
Vous êtes organisé·e, autonome et capable de prioriser vos activités, et de vous adapter à des environnements complexes.
Une expérience dans des centres de santé, dans des zones isolées ou difficiles d'accès, dans un contexte sécuritaire instable, ainsi qu'une expérience au Tchad, constitueront des atouts appréciés.

Salaire mensuel brut : de 2130 à 2475 euros en fonction de l'expérience, incluant 13ème mois

jobs.title: Monitoring and Evaluation Advisor
jobs.description:
## About the Role

All Hands and Hearts is seeking an experienced Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Advisor to build and lead the monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning systems for its humanitarian response in Gaza. Operating in a fast-changing environment with constrained access, AHAH needs reliable, timely evidence on what is reaching communities, what is working, and where programs must adapt. The successful candidate will focus primarily on nutrition Monitoring and Evaluation, ensure quality data collection and reporting to leadership and donors, and put in place mechanisms that let affected communities give feedback and hold the organization accountable.

## Key Responsibilities

- **M&E Systems and Frameworks:** Design and roll out AHAH's M&E framework for Gaza nutrition program, including results frameworks, data collection and analysis, indicator reference sheets and performance monitoring plans aligned with donor requirements and cluster standards.
- **Distribution and Commodity Monitoring:** Establish post-distribution monitoring, commodity tracking and verification processes to confirm that AHAH assistance reaches intended civilian beneficiaries, and flag diversion or access risks to leadership.
- **Data Collection and Management:** Develop data collection tools and lead the use of mobile data platforms; ensure data quality, security, beneficiary data protection and safe storage.
- **Assessments and Evaluations:** Lead or support needs assessments, baseline and endline surveys, and periodic program reviews; manage external evaluations where required.
- **Reporting and Learning:** Produce timely, accurate reports and dashboards for AHAH leadership and donors; document lessons learned and use findings to guide program adaptation.
- **Coordination:** Represent AHAH in inter-agency information management and assessment working groups; contribute data to cluster reporting, as appropriate.
- **Capacity Building:** Train and mentor field staff, on M&E methods, data collection and ethical data practices.
- **Resource Mobilization:** Contribute M&E plans, indicators and budgets to proposals for institutional and private donors.

## Qualifications & Experience

- Master's degree in Monitoring and Evaluation, Statistics, Public Health, Development Studies, Social Sciences, or a related field.
- Minimum 8–10 years of M&E experience, including at least 5 years in humanitarian or emergency settings.
- Demonstrated expertise in designing M&E systems, quantitative and qualitative methods, and donor reporting.
- Proficiency with mobile data collection platforms and data analysis tools
- Excellent analytical, communication and report-writing skills.
- Language requirements: Fluency in Arabic and English (written and spoken).
- Candidates must be willing to undergo a thorough background and security check prior to a final offer. Must demonstrate commitment to neutrality and community service.

## Salary

This is an 18-month, fixed-term contract/consultancy with compensation that will be competitive based on experience and location.

jobs.title: Senior Nutrition Advisor
jobs.description:
All Hands and Hearts is seeking an experienced Senior Nutrition Advisor to lead the design, delivery and quality of its emergency nutrition programming in Gaza. Acute malnutrition among children under five and pregnant and lactating women has risen sharply amid prolonged conflict, displacement and severe restrictions on food access. The successful candidate will provide technical leadership on nutrition across All Hands and Hearts' humanitarian response, ensure programs meet international standards, and represent the organization with the Nutrition Cluster, UN agencies, donors and partner NGOs. The Advisor will also help integrate nutrition into AHAH's wider food distribution, community health, shelter and education programs, and build the capacity of local staff and community health workers.

## Key Responsibilities

- **Technical Leadership:** Serve as AHAH's lead technical expert on nutrition in emergencies, setting program strategy and ensuring all nutrition activities align with Sphere standards, Nutrition Cluster guidance and Ministry of Health protocols.
- **Program Design and Delivery:** Design, launch and oversee nutrition interventions, which may include community-based management of acute malnutrition (CMAM), MUAC screening and referral, supplementary feeding, micronutrient supplementation, and infant and young child feeding in emergencies (IYCF-E).
- **Integration with Food Assistance:** Advise AHAH leadership and logistics teams on the nutritional adequacy of food baskets and distributions, targeting of vulnerable groups, and safe handling of specialized nutrition commodities (RUTF, RUSF, LNS).
- **Assessment and Surveillance:** Lead or support nutrition assessments, screening campaigns and surveillance (including SMART-style surveys where feasible) to identify needs, track trends and guide program decisions.
- **Coordination and Representation:** Represent AHAH in the Nutrition Cluster and relevant working groups; build partnerships with UNICEF, WFP, WHO, health facilities and local NGOs to strengthen referral pathways and avoid duplication.
- **Capacity Building:** Train and mentor AHAH staff, partner organizations and community health workers on nutrition screening, counseling, IYCF-E and the Code on breastmilk substitutes.
- **Monitoring, Reporting and Accountability:** Develop indicators and monitoring tools, ensure quality data collection, and report program results to AHAH leadership and donors. Ensure feedback and accountability mechanisms are in place for affected communities.
- **Resource Mobilization:** Contribute technical content to proposals, budgets and donor reports for institutional and private donors (e.g., USAID/BHA successor mechanisms, ECHO, UN pooled funds, foundations and Gulf donors).

## Qualifications & Experience

- MD or Master's degree in Public Health, Nursing, Nutrition, or a related field.
- Minimum 8–10 years of experience in health or nutrition programming, including at least 5 years in humanitarian or emergency settings.
- Demonstrated technical expertise in nutrition programming.
- Proven experience managing teams, training staff and working through local partners.
- Excellent analytical, communication and representation skills.
- Language requirements: Fluency in Arabic and English (written and spoken).
- Candidates must be willing to undergo a thorough background and security check prior to a final offer. Must demonstrate commitment to neutrality and community service.

## Salary

This is a 18-month, fixed-term contract/consultancy with compensation that will be competitive based on experience and location.

jobs.title: National MEAL Coordinator
jobs.description:
## Background

The CORE Group Partners Project (CGPP) is a multi-country, multi-partner initiative that provides on-the-ground technical assistance and guidance to support host country efforts to strengthen immunization systems, disease surveillance, and essential community-based health services. Globally, CGPP works across five technical areas (polio, maternal and child health, nutrition, malaria, and global health security) through existing networks of international and local NGOs operating in hard-to-reach areas with low immunization coverage. At the country level, a Secretariat coordinates the work of CGPP partner organizations in a manner that complements the efforts of all implementing partners. In Indonesia, CGPP supports national health strategies by strengthening routine immunization and polio eradication efforts while promoting maternal and child health through integrated community-based interventions.

CGPP works with the Government of Indonesia to improve maternal and child health (MCH) outcomes and strengthen routine immunization and polio eradication in selected districts of Papua and East Java and other CGPP-supported areas.

The CGPP Indonesia Secretariat, led by the Secretariat Director based in Jakarta, coordinates with the Ministry of Health (MOH) and other ministries, US Department of State (US DOS) Foreign Assistance team, UNICEF, STRIDES (FHI 360), other Global Polio Eradication Initiative (GPEI) partners, and Wahana Visi / World Vision Indonesia. The Director regularly briefs these stakeholders on project performance. Those briefings depend on project data that is complete, validated, and consistent with national MOH indicators and US DOS reporting requirements.

## Purpose of the Consultancy

CGPP Indonesia will engage a National MEAL Coordinator as a full-time consultant to make every number, report, and presentation that the Secretariat Director takes to the MOH and the US DOS accurate, consistent, and on time.

The National MEAL Coordinator will provide oversight support to CGPP Indonesia to ensure quality data and reporting. Working under the guidance of the CGPP Indonesia Secretariat Director, the consultant will:

1. Ensure CGPP project data is complete, accurate, timely and consistent with national MOH guidelines and indicator definitions and with US DOS Foreign Assistance reporting guidelines.
2. Ensure the quality of all CGPP Indonesia reports, data summaries, and briefings before submission.
3. Prepare and quality-check the presentations and briefing materials the Secretariat Director uses with MOH, US DOS, GPEI partners, and other forums.
4. Strengthen MEAL systems and capacity across the Secretariat and partner teams so that data is used for decisions and learning.

## Scope of Work and Key Responsibilities

### 1. Data quality and alignment with MOH and US DOS guidelines

- Review the CGPP Indonesia MEAL framework, indicator reference sheets, and data collection tools; align to CGPP Global MEAL Framework, indicator definitions, disaggregation, and reporting periods with MOH national standards (immunization, MCH, and surveillance systems) and with US DOS Foreign Assistance reporting requirements.
- Map source of the CGPP data (community, health facility, district, and partner sources) and document data flows, responsibilities, and reporting timelines.
- Establish and run a routine data quality assurance system: monthly validation checks, periodic data quality assessments (DQAs), and spot checks during field visits.
- Reconcile CGPP-reported results with MOH district and provincial data; flag and resolve discrepancies with field teams and partners before results are reported.
- Maintain a single, version-controlled master dataset and indicator tracking table as the official source for all CGPP Indonesia figures.

### 2. Quality of reports

- Review all CGPP Indonesia reports before submission (monthly updates, quarterly and semi-annual reports, annual reports, and ad hoc donor requests) for data accuracy, internal consistency, correct use of indicators, and clear analysis.
- Validate monthly data updates, performance indicators, and partner-reported results, as required by the Secretariat Director.
- Develop standard reporting templates and a reporting calendar with internal deadlines that allow time for review.
- Write the results and data analysis sections of reports, including progress against targets and explanations of variance.

### 3. Presentations and briefings for the Secretariat Director

- Prepare data-driven presentations, briefing notes, fact sheets, and talking points for the Director's meetings with MOH, US DOS, GPEI partners, UNICEF, STRIDES, and other coordination forums.
- Ensure every figure in these materials matches the master dataset and the latest submitted report.
- Produce clear charts, maps, and dashboards that show progress, gaps, and priority actions.
- Attend key meetings with the Director when requested, capture data-related questions and action points, and follow up.
- As per guidance of the CGPP Indonesia Director, represent CGPP Indonesia in national-level platforms.

### 4. Monitoring, evaluation, and learning

- Support the design and management of planned CGPP assessments, surveys, and evaluations, including terms of reference, tools, data analysis, and reports.
- Lead regular data review and reflection meetings with the Secretariat and provincial teams to turn findings into program adjustments.
- Document lessons learned, success stories, and good practices for internal learning and external sharing.

### 5. MEAL systems and capacity strengthening

- Work with the CGPP National Program Manager and MEAL team to harmonize workflows and maintain common MEAL standards across all partners.
- Train and mentor national and provincial staff on indicators, data collection, data quality, and data use.
- Recommend practical improvements to digital data tools and dashboards, in line with MOH systems.

### 6. Accountability

- Support community feedback and accountability mechanisms so community concerns are recorded, analyzed, and reported to decision-makers.
- Ensure data protection, confidentiality, and ethical standards in all data collection and storage.

## Reporting and Working Relationships

- **Reports to:** CGPP Indonesia Secretariat Director, who sets priorities, approves deliverables, and certifies payment.
- **Technical guidance:** CGPP Global Secretariat MEAL team and Senior Technical Advisor, for global indicator and reporting standards and program quality.
- **Internal:** CGPP National Program Manager, CGPP Indonesia MEAL team, Provincial Team Leaders, Wahana Visi / World Vision Indonesia program and MEAL staff, and finance and grants teams.
- **External:** MOH (national, provincial, and district health offices), US DOS Foreign Assistance team, UNICEF, STRIDES (FHI 360), and other GPEI partners, for data-related coordination as delegated by the Director.
- **Supervisory responsibility:** None. As a consultant, the MEAL Coordinator provides technical guidance and mentoring but does not supervise staff.

## Qualifications and Experience

### Required

- Master's degree in public health, epidemiology, biostatistics, demography, or a related field.
- At least 8 years of experience in monitoring and evaluation of public health programs, including at least 3 years leading MEAL for donor-funded projects.
- Hands-on knowledge of Indonesian MOH health information systems and indicators, especially immunization, MCH, and surveillance.
- Proven experience in data quality assessment, data validation, and reconciliation with government data.
- Experience preparing donor reports and presentations for senior government and donor audiences; US Government reporting experience strongly preferred.
- Strong skills in Excel and at least one statistical or visualization tool (e.g. Stata, SPSS, R, Power BI, or Tableau); experience with DHIS2, KoboToolbox, or ODK is an advantage.

### Preferred

- Experience with polio eradication, routine immunization, and MCH or GPEI partner programs.
- Work experience in Indonesia.
- Experience designing and managing surveys and evaluations.

### Skills and Abilities

- Close attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy.
- Ability to turn complex data into clear messages, charts and briefings.
- Ability to work to tight deadlines and manage several reports at once.
- Strong interpersonal skills to work with government, donors and partners.

### Languages

- **English**: Professional proficiency required, with ability to communicate effectively in writing and speech and with excellent report-writing in English.
- **Bahasa Indonesia**: Professional proficiency required in speaking, reading, and writing.

### Travel

- Must be willing to travel approximately 25-35% of the time.

## Terms

- **Contract:** Full-time consultancy with CORE Group, Inc., November 1, 2026 – August 31, 2027, with possible extension based on performance and funding.
- **Payment:** Monthly fee, paid on submission and approval of the monthly activity report, timesheet, and deliverables due that month. Travel costs are covered per CORE Group, Inc. policy.
- **Data ownership:** All data, reports, and materials produced belong to CGPP and may not be shared without the Secretariat Director's written approval.
- **Safeguarding:** The consultant must comply with CORE Group codes of conduct, including safeguarding and prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse.

## Disclaimer

- This scope of work is not an exhaustive list of the skills, effort, duties, and responsibilities associated with the position.

jobs.title: Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Consultant
jobs.description:
**CONSULTANCY TITLE:** Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Consultant

**DURATION OF ASSIGNMENT:** 30 days from October 26, 2026, to June 30, 2027.

**EMAIL SUBJECT LINE**: *Consultancy – Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Expert*

**Background**

Population Council- Kenya (PC Kenya), a non-profit organization registered in Kenya, is leading an inter-regional consortium of Function-Oriented Impact Partner Organizations (IPOs) that comprises ThinkPlace Kenya, Le Barometre, and the Centre for the Study of the Economies of Africa (CSEA) (the IPO). The IPO supports Mastercard Foundation’s Impact Strategy by conducting impact measurement and evaluation activities, in addition to supporting program design and learnings across the Foundation’s program platforms, namely, the Pan-Africa Program (PANA), Scholars, Secondary Education and Transition (SET), Higher Education Collaboratives and Strategic Initiatives (HECSI), and Strategic Partnerships and Innovations (SP&I). The geographic scope of programs supported by the Foundation cuts across 35 countries in Africa. The IPO supports the Foundation and its partners through:

1. **Impact Technical Delivery**, which includes supporting robust monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL) processes that entail assessing the progress of programs in advancing the Foundation's charitable goals of financial inclusion and youth education, as well as achieving set targets across the various programmatic platforms.
2. **Program Support**, that entails supporting the development of strategies tailored to the unique needs of the Foundation’s partners and program participants through extensive evidence reviews, needs assessments, and participatory design methods to ensure interventions are designed to achieve impact in line with specific platform strategies and the Foundation’s charitable purpose.
3. **Cross-cutting Support**, which entails supporting field building and communications activities through training and knowledge sharing and reflection to promote adoption of best practices.

The IPO provides technical support to the Foundation and its implementing partners on strategies that strengthen theories of change (ToCs) and monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL) frameworks, including supporting refinement of ToCs, MEL key performance indicators (KPIs) and learning questions, in addition to tracking partners’ MEL capabilities, and providing technical support to strengthen those capabilities.

**Scope of Work**

PC Kenya is seeking the services of a professional consultant to support the IPO, the Foundation and its implementing partners. The purpose of the assignment is to support the IPO to establish and deliver a structured MEL accompaniment programme for Foundation implementing partners. The programme will strengthen partner-level MEL infrastructure, governance, systems, processes, capabilities and use of evidence for decisions and reporting. Support will be tailored to documented partner needs and will cover theories of change, MEL plans, indicators, learning questions, data architecture, participant-level records, data quality, data governance, analysis, reporting, learning and adaptive management. The consultant will work with the IPO to perform the following tasks:

**Workstream 1: Inception, partner universe and prioritisation**

1. Review the Platform framework, partner portfolio, IPO plans, relevant MEL guidance, Shared Measures 2.0 requirements, Comprehensive Approach to Reviews and Evaluation (CARE), Program Outcomes Assessment/ Data Quality Assessment (POA/DQA) findings, Fluxx/Daraja reporting requirements and existing partner MEL documentation.
2. Confirm the partners and programmes covered by the assignment.
3. Establish a partner-level MEL support register and prioritisation methodology.
4. Prepare a detailed workplan showing partners, needs, activities, dates, responsibilities, level of effort, intended results and dependencies.

**Workstream 2: Partner MEL capability and system diagnostics**

1. Assess the MEL capability, infrastructure and operational readiness of agreed partners.
2. Review partner ToCs, results chains, MEL plans, indicators, targets, learning questions, data tools, participant-management systems, reporting arrangements and evidence-use practices.
3. Integrate relevant DQA, POA and review findings into each diagnostic.
4. Produce an agreed improvement plan for each partner or coherent partner cluster.

**Workstream 3: MEL framework and infrastructure strengthening**

1. Support partners to refine and operationalise ToCs, MEL plans, indicators, learning questions, tools, protocols and reporting calendars.
2. Strengthen data architecture, participant-level records, data dictionaries, indicator reference sheets, collection processes, storage, access controls, cleaning, validation and documentation.
3. Clarify data flows and accountabilities between lead partners, sub-partners, collaboratives, IPOs, programme teams and the Foundation.
4. Support partners to establish practical DQA and data-correction routines.

**Workstream 4: Measurement alignment**

1. Support operational alignment with Shared Measures 2.0 and applicable Work-Enabling Outreach (WEO), Youth-in-Work (YiW), transitions, inclusion, institutional strengthening and systems-change measures.
2. Confirm indicator applicability, targets, disaggregation, sources, frequency, aggregation, attribution and reporting responsibilities.
3. Identify and address gaps between partner records, programme designs and Fluxx/Daraja reporting requirements.
4. Support credible treatment of collaborative contributions and risks of double counting.

**Workstream 5: Learning and adaptive management**

1. Support partners to strengthen learning agendas and routine evidence reflection.
2. Facilitate or support partner-specific working sessions, coaching and communities of practice.
3. Establish decision logs linking evidence and insights to adaptations.
4. Harvest cross-partner learning and prepare decision-ready briefs for programme and platform discussions.

**Workstream 6: Monitoring, reporting and handover**

1. Maintain the live partner support register and evidence repository.
2. Prepare monthly dashboards and quarterly analytical reports.
3. Document capability improvements, outstanding risks, decisions requiring escalation and support still needed.
4. Prepare an end-of-assignment synthesis, partner handover notes and recommendations for sustaining improved MEL functions.

**Key deliverables**

The consultant will document monthly progress, implementation and adaptations at partner level without replacing partner MEL staff or assuming Foundation programme-management responsibilities; will work through the IPO’s consortium governance; will tailor support where partner needs differ; and will distinguish clearly between partner action, IPO support, consultant input and Foundation accountability. The consultant will not certify data as credible without documented review; will not treat attendance at socialisation sessions as evidence of operational readiness; will not mark DQAs or MEL plans as complete without agreed closure evidence; and will not request personally identifiable data without authorised arrangements. A summary of key tasks, deliverables and projected due dates are outlined in the table below:

**Activity 1: Inception, partner universe and prioritisation**

**Deliverable:** Inception package (inception note, delivery methodology, quality assurance plan, support for MEL/impact work)

**Projected due date:** October 30, 2026

**Activity 2: Partner MEL capability and system diagnostics**

**Deliverable:** Partner MEL support register (a live tool containing ToC/MEL status, agreed support, planned/completion dates, evidence link and next actions)

**Projected Due Date**: November 15, 2026

**Activity 3:** **MEL framework and infrastructure strengthening**

**Deliverable:** Partner diagnostic and improvement plans (assessment findings, agreed improvements, success measures, evidence required, completion date, and sustainability requirements)

**Projected Due Date**: December 15, 2026

**Activity 4: Measurement alignment**

**Deliverable**: Strengthened partner MEL products (refined ToC/MEL plans, learning agenda, data collection tools, and reporting templates

**Projected Due Date**: March 31, 2027

**Activity 5: Learning and adaptive management**

**Deliverable:** Capability accompaniment and evidence of application (coaching and technical session records; participation records; adapted materials; completed partner assignments)

**Projected Due Date:** May 31, 2027

**Activity 6: Monitoring, reporting and handover**

**Deliverable:** Monthly and quarterly reporting (monthly dashboard, quarterly analytical report per partner and in aggregate), and final synthesis and handover.

**Projected Due Date:** Monthly, quarterly, end of assignment by (June 30, 2027) as appropriate

1. **Roles and Responsibilities**

The consultant will work as part of the IPO delivery structure and will not operate as an independent parallel support channel to Foundation partners. Partner engagement will be coordinated through the designated IPO lead and relevant Foundation Impact Delivery and programme focal points. Foundation teams retain responsibility for strategic direction, approval of Foundation standards and programme decisions. The IPO retains responsibility for consortium management, technical delivery, quality assurance and contractual performance. The consultant provides specialist technical capacity within this structure.

**Quality Assurance**

All partner diagnostics, MEL products, status updates and reports will undergo documented IPO technical, format and document quality assurance before submission. The review should assess completeness; internal consistency; alignment with agreed standards; traceability to source evidence; proportionality of claims; data protection; usability; clarity; alignment with required formats; and disclosure of any use of AI.

**Ethical Requirements**

The consultant will apply the Foundation’s approved ethical, responsible-data, safeguarding and data-protection requirements across all activities. The consultant must not request, receive, retain or transfer personally identifiable information unless this is specifically authorised and supported by approved arrangements. Any data governance, consent or safeguarding concern must be documented and escalated through the agreed mechanism.

**Qualifications and Experience**

The consultant should have the following minimum qualifications:

- Advanced degree in program monitoring and evaluation, statistics, economics, development studies or social sciences.
- Minimum 5 years prior experience working in MEL, impact evaluation, or strategic planning.
- Prior experience designing and tracking theories of change, MEL frameworks, performance indicators, and adaptative management.
- Experience mentoring or training teams or partner organizations on development of theories of change and MEL frameworks.
- Excellent diplomatic, representational, problem-solving, management, and interpersonal skills.
- Excellent written and oral communications skills in English, including quality writing and presentation skills.
- High sense of attention to details and ability to work collaboratively with diverse teams across Africa.
- Experience working with international organizations, NGOs, or in Africa.

**Duration of Assignment**

The contract period will run from October 26, 2026 to June 30, 2027. The maximum consultant level of effort will be 30 working days, distributed across the contract period in accordance with the approved workplan and agreed deliverables.

**Travel**

The consultant may be expected to travel with all travel costs covered directly by PC-Kenya.

**Compensation**

The compensation will be based on the existing consultancy rates for the IPO-supported activities.

**Payment Terms**

Payments shall be output-based and made within thirty (30) calendar days following receipt of a valid invoice and the PC-Kenya's written approval of the corresponding deliverable. No payment shall be made for outputs not approved as satisfactory by PC-Kenya.

jobs.title: Communications Intern/Volunteer
jobs.description:
**Location:** The Hague, the Netherlands
**Period:** 6 months, 15 November 2026 – 15 May 2027, Monday to Thursday

## **About us**

The Dr. Denis Mukwege Foundation (MF) is an international rights-based, survivor-centred organisation, dedicated to ending sexual violence as a weapon of war globally. The Mukwege Foundation supports survivors’ demands for a world where sexual violence as a weapon of war is no longer tolerated, and bears consequences for individual perpetrators and states. We work for a future where survivors receive the holistic care and compensation they need to rebuild their lives. We create opportunities for survivors to speak out and be heard, and where they can organise to create change, influence policies, and demand justice and accountability.

## **Background**

At the Mukwege Foundation, everything we do is guided by a five-year strategy (2024–2028) and a mission that matters: supporting survivors of conflict-related sexual violence and changing the global response to the use of sexual violence as a weapon of war. Communications are how that mission reaches people, helping them to understand and engage with the change we are working to achieve.

As our Communications Intern/Volunteer, you’ll help organise our communications assets, from powerful photos and videos to the archives and systems behind them. Your work will make our stories easier to share and use for years to come, so the voices of survivors keep reaching the people who need to hear them.

## **What you’ll do**

You will work side-by-side with our Communications Specialist on two fronts. First, you’ll help bring our social media campaigns to life. Second, you’ll play a central role in building our new media library: organising, cataloguing, indexing and migrating our communications assets so that everything is properly classified, easy to retrieve and accessible to colleagues across the organisation.

## **What you’ll gain**

This is your chance to get real, hands-on experience in a dynamic international non-profit organisation. You’ll learn what survivor-centred, ethical communications look like in practice across social media, newsletters and our website, and you’ll leave knowing that your work has lasting impact on how our mission is shared with the world

## **Tasks**

The Communications Intern/Volunteer will:

- Assist with the development of flagship communications materials, including the Annual Activity Report, social media posts, video scripts, news items and press releases.
- Support the maintenance, organisation and clean-up of the Mukwege Foundation media libraries, including the migration of photo and videos between SharePoint environments.
- Contribute to campaign content creation, including social media copywriting, design, and video editing, as well as scheduling, planning, and campaign coordination.

## **Profile of the candidate**

**Mandatory**

- The candidate must either be enrolled in or have recently graduated from a degree in Communications, Media, Journalism, Graphic Design, Marketing or a related field.
- Strong interest in the topic of armed conflict, gender-based violence, human rights, and/or conflict-related sexual violence.
- Proficient in Microsoft 365 tools, particularly SharePoint, Excel, Word.
- Attentive to detail, highly organised and autonomous.
- Ability to prioritise and work under pressure.
- Hands-on attitude and proactive mindset.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.
- Ability to manage large volumes of information accurately and systematically.

**Desirable**

- Experience managing databases, datasets, media libraries or digital repositories
- Experience with content migration
- Familiarity with WordPress (or similar CMS platforms)
- Experience using social media scheduling tools (e.g. Hootsuite)
- Experience in social media content creation
- Strong design skills

## **Reporting and Management**

The Communications Intern/Volunteer will report to the Communications Specialist.

## **Conditions of the internship/volunteer opportunity**

The internship/volunteering will be conducted under the following terms and conditions:

- The candidate undertakes this role on a volunteer basis or as an intern
- A small monthly allowance can be offered, based on Dutch law
- The candidate must be based in the Netherlands with occasional commute to the Foundation’s office in The Hague
- The candidate shall adhere to the Code of Conduct of the Mukwege Foundation
- Duration: 6 months, ideally starting on 15 November

jobs.title: Americas Officer
jobs.description:
Front Line Defenders is recruiting an **Americas Officer** to join our team. This is a one-year fixed term contract based in the region reporting to the Head of Americas.

**Overview**

The Regional Team leads Front Line Defenders’ work in the Region, with responsibility for defining priorities, directing organisational protection responses, and ensuring that resources are deployed where they have the greatest impact for human rights defenders (HRDs). Grounded in sustained engagement with HRDs and regional ecosystems, the team determines where the organisation acts, who and how it supports, and how it responds to evolving risks. The Regional Team plays a central role in shaping organisational direction by ensuring that strategies, approaches and interventions are driven by regional priorities, while contributing directly to global strategy and positioning.

The Americas Officer will support the Protection Team’s direct response to human rights defenders at risk in the Americas. This position will involve collaboration with all colleagues working in the region, and in particular close coordination with Americas Protection Coordinators, Head of Protection, Senior Advocacy Lead, and HRD Memorial Coordinator, offering assistance with documentation, research, administrative and logistic duties in relation to Front Line Defender’s work with human rights defenders in the Americas. Responsibilities include, but are not limited to, documentation, verification and research on risks faced by defenders, drafting various briefing papers, reports and appeals, regular update of the Front Line Defenders' database, taking minutes of meetings, direct communication with defenders, coordination with other civil society organizations as well as providing occasional language support through in-house translation of sensitive documents, as well as in online and in person meetings.

**Background**

Front Line Defenders is an international organisation based in Ireland that works exclusively for the protection of human rights defenders at risk. Human rights defenders are people who are persecuted because of their peaceful work for the rights of others. Front Line Defenders provides practical help through protection grants, physical and digital protection training, lobbying, advocacy and campaigning.

**Role responsibilities**

**Key duties include:**

- Provide support to the Protection Coordinators in outreach and correspondence with defenders, incl. responding to defenders’ queries and following-up on their requests with different FLD program areas
- Input HRD-related and case information (case updates, outcomes) to the Front Line Defenders' database and ensure that it is kept up to date
- Provide regional coverage on behalf of Protection Coordinators when they are on mission, or not available for other reasons, including attending meetings with various stakeholders and allies
- Gathering documentation for work with human rights defenders cases;
- Support Human rights defenders at risk connecting and liasing with other organizations with specific expertise relevant for their protection needs
- Undertake desk research on cases of defenders, situation of HRDs at risk in the region; assist with gathering and verification of information
- Compile and draft as requested briefings, reports, urgent appeals/updates, statements, or other materials;
- Taking notes at meetings with defenders, other organisations representatives and at internal FLD meetings;
- Close daily collaboration with the regional team (staff working in the Americas from different
- FLD program areas, including Advocacy, HRD Memorial, Grants, Digital Protection,
- Communications and Capacity Building);

For further information, please view:

[https://www.frontlinedefenders.org/sites/default/files/americas_officer_jd_october_2026.pdf](https://www.frontlinedefenders.org/sites/default/files/americas_officer_jd_october_2026.pdf)

**Salary & Benefits**

- €34,128 - €55,094 per annum
- 26 annual leave days
- Pension
- Paid Health Insurance
- Income Protection & Life Assurance
- Employee Assistance Scheme (EAP)
- Monthly Well-Being Provisions

**Requirements**

**Interested applicants must have:**

- Solid knowledge of the situation facing human rights defenders in the Americas
- At least 4 years of experience working directly with human rights defenders and/or civil society in the region
- Experience working with human rights defenders in the context of land, environmental, indigenous, campesino and/or black communities rights
- Analytical skills, ability to search for information throughout different sources, verify it and organise into advocacy documents
- Good writing skills, including ability to produce high-quality reports and correspondence.
- Fluent written and spoken Spanish;
- High level of written and spoken English;
- Good time management, ability to plan and prioritise work on the tasks, and ability to accommodate emergency tasks within the workplan
- Ability to work independently and as part of the team
- Good level of political judgment, especially in the context of casework, e.g. ability to defend the case based on the analysis of the context and FLD mandate.
- Self drive, initiative and capacity to pro actively support HRDs;
- Ability to manage high-pressure situations while maintaining professionalism and responding to emotionally demanding challenges.
