jobs.description:
**WE ARE HIRING AN EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR!**

**ABOUT TICAH**
TICAH is a feminist organization that works to promote health, equitable relationships, and
community action. We dream of safe and just societies where barriers to equitable health and social outcomes are removed including for the most marginalized populations, where rights are realized, holistic health is attained and where the beauty of culture and diversity is celebrated.

Our definition of health recognises the links between health, values and culture, the role of art in activism and social change and the elevation of marginalised voices and ideas, that there is much to be gained by engaging with our traditional cultures, that access to quality health information services is critical and the power of nutrition and herbs in overall wellness cannot be overlooked.
We work toward communities driving and owning all implementation through our tried and tested methodologies: Listening and Co-Creation of interventions with communities, Creation of Safe Spaces for Values Clarification and Training of Trainers; Advocacy, where we raise our voices to advocate for better laws, policies and practices to protect rights, access to holistic health services, freedom of expression and sexual &amp; reproductive health rights. We celebrate the beauty and diversity of ideas, ethnicities, religions, sexuality, music, art, genders, indigenous cultures, and traditions as expressions of a healthy society.

Our priority areas are Gender Justice, Climate Justice and Holistic Health.
TICAH’s 4 program areas are:
 Art for Connection & Healing: Working with artists and through arts practices to build community, raise marginalized voices, activate and revitalize public spaces, and find
healing and wellness.
 Healthy Households working with households to build wellness and prevent illness by
incorporating practical, affordable, and sustainable practices by focusing on food and
herbal remedies.
 Indigenous Knowledge and Culture: Working closely with cultural practitioners and
elders to bring positive indigenous knowledge, practice and culture into holistic health
and solving community challenges.
 Our Bodies, Our Choices, a SRH program encouraging more honest and healthy
approaches to sexual life through curricula, trainings, peer discussions and a hotline. With
like-minded organizations we advocate for comprehensive sexuality education, and
access to safe legal abortion.

From our beginnings in 2003, TICAH has been rooted in health, healing, culture, and justice.
Deeply embedded in the communities we work with, ours has always been a story of us, for us - walking alongside communities, listening, staying curious, and learning as we go. We wanted to be an organization that itself embodies the values and tenets of wellness, rights, and connection that we aimed for in our work.This grounding continues to shape how we work, how we lead, and where we are going next.
Over the years, TICAH has evolved from providing information and programs to empowering communities to take control of their health, rights, and futures. Our early work connected health with culture, rights, relationships, and indigenous knowledge, fostering open conversations on sexuality, HIV, nutrition, traditional medicine, and social justice.

By 2019, we further strengthened our focus on women and girls, gender equality, community leadership, and advocacy.
We’ve seen impact not just in numbers reached, but in people making informed choices,
changing practices at home, indigenous women leading, artists driving social change, and
communities shaping policies. By 2025, communities were reorganizing after disruptions, young women were influencing policy, families were blending nutrition with local knowledge, indigenous women were leading on land and climate justice, and artists were creating spaces for healing.

In addition, TICAH also plays a strategic movement-building role, convening and hosting
networks advancing SRHR and other rights nationally and regionally, including MAMA Network (a regional network of 70+ organizations in 26 African countries), and various national networks in Kenya.

In so doing TICAH creates the connective infrastructure that enables organisations and activists to organise, learn, respond and act collectively. Through these networks, we help turn individual organisations and community action into collective power capable of influencing systems at scale.

The 2022-2026 Strategic Plan further solidified TICAH's commitment and methodology for
building power and systems change. With a team of 25, TICAH’s work has impacted over
407,000 people, equipping them with the knowledge, agency, and collective power to lead
change. In this period, TICAH began to see communities not just as participants, but as leaders with collective power and agency. Our focus has thus moved from providing information to supporting informed choices, advocacy, and collective action. Our programs have become more integrated, connecting health, rights, gender, climate, art, and indigenous knowledge through an intersectional approach. This has led to greater influence on policies and systems at all levels. By the end of the strategy, TICAH’s role will be less about delivering solutions and more about creating conditions for communities to lead, systems to listen, and people to shape their own
futures.

As our current Strategic Plan comes to an end, we are looking ahead with ambition and curiosity, asking ourselves what is possible as TICAH enters its next strategic plan cycle: how do we hold on to the depth, creativity and community-rootedness that have always defined us, while growing our ability to scale and influence the systems that shape people’s health and lives. How do we build an even stronger, more resilient and sustainable organisation, one that can navigate an increasingly complex political and funding environment, deepen our impact, strengthen our partnerships and continue to challenge conventional ways of thinking about health and
wellbeing?

TICAH’s next Executive Director will have the exciting responsibility of helping us imagine, shape and lead this next chapter building on more than two decades of learning and impact while taking the organisation boldly into its future.
Learn more: [https://www.ticahealth.org/](https://www.ticahealth.org/)

TICAH’S SHARED LEADERSHIP MODEL:
TICAH has adopted a shared leadership model where the Executive Director and Deputy
Executive Director share responsibility, authority, and decision-making for the organization.

Rather than a traditional hierarchical structure centered on a single leader, shared leadership emphasizes collaboration, mutual accountability and complementary strengths.
In addition, shared leadership is embedded in TICAH’s DNA through listening and consensus- building, trust and delegation, a highly collaborative Leadership Team and cross-functional committees that steer program development, MEL, fundraising, communications, staff welfare, procurement and more.

This model is deeply aligned with TICAH’s values in a number of ways:
● Shared leadership reflects feminist values by promoting shared power, equality, and
inclusive decision-making.
● Indigenous principles emphasize collective leadership, inclusive stewardship, and
respect for relational decision-making.
● Sustainability: Sharing leadership responsibilities reduces burnout, builds institutional
memory, and supports healthier, more stable operations over time.
● Better outcomes for communities: Shared Leadership brings complementary skills and
insights, enhancing strategic thinking, innovation, and the overall impact of TICAH’s
mission.
As a result, the ED role includes both, shared leadership responsibilities and areas of sole
ownership, which are outlined below to provide clarity on roles and accountability.

ROLES SHARED BETWEEN ED & DEPUTY ED (20%):
Strategy Development
 Lead the expansion of TICAH’s vision & advance opportunities to realise its unique
mission &amp; approach in Kenya, regionally and globally.
 Hold the SP’s vision and goals, steer implementation and learning through 2027–2030,
and lead the development of the SP 2030+.
 Provide technical leadership for the annual reviews of the Strategic Plan. Ensure all
Programs and MELS strategies, frameworks, and SOPs align with the Strategic Plan and
its revisions
 Provide effective representation of TICAH’s transformative agenda and goals to influence
relevant actors and actions in Kenya, regionally and globally.
Governance / Board Management &amp; Development
 Lead board development as needs evolve.
 Coordinate Board Meeting Schedule.
 Prepare for, attend and ensure follow-up from board meetings.
 Ensure board decisions are documented and implemented.

Legal
 Oversee the organization’s legal and compliance matters, including emerging issues and
risk management, working closely with legal counsel and the board as needed.

**EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR ROLES:**
Fundraising & Donor Communication &amp; Engagement (25%):
● Hold overall accountability for TICAH’s fundraising and donor engagement, working
closely with the Head of Partnerships and Deputy Executive Director to ensure adequate,
sustainable and values-aligned resource mobilisation.
● In collaboration with the Head of Partnerships, cultivate and steward strong relationships
with current and prospective donors, effectively communicating TICAH’s distinctive value,
impact and relevance to health and social justice priorities in Kenya, the region and globally.
● Ensuring donor relationships are held by the organisation rather than concentrated in any one individual. Donor relationships may be primarily led by the Executive Director, Deputy Executive Director, Head of Partnerships or other relevant team members, while ensuring that each key donor has meaningful relationships with more than one person within TICAH.
● Provide strategic leadership for the retention of existing donors and Cultivation and
progressing onboarding of new donors in close collaboration with HoPa to ensure that
donors understand the value and relevance of TICAH’s uniqueness to a range of current
topical health and social issues in Kenya, regionally and globally.
● Ensure adequate funding to support the SP through Donor Relations with all current
donors and high-value prospects. (progressive onboarding of new donors and retention
of current donors)
● Ensure strategy- and value-aligned communication with all donors through the review of
key donor communication tools (grant applications, donor reports, annual reports, pitch
decks).
● Maintain overall oversight of TICAH’s donor portfolio and relationships, including those
managed day-to-day by other members of the team, and ensure emerging opportunities,
risks and relationship needs are appropriately managed.

Organizational Leadership, Talent & Culture (20%):
● In collaboration with the Leadership Team, spearhead the organizational design, talent
management strategy, culture, and structure in service of our Mission and Strategic Plan,
in line with our values.
● Ensure wellness, self-care and collective care are deeply embedded in the organizational
culture through policy and practice.
● Oversee staff development to realize TICAH’s strategic plan, strengthen its ability for
impact and growth, and stay responsive to evolving realities and needs.
● Support and manage the Deputy ED, Head of Partnerships and Head of Finance and
Operations, and enable them to drive the organizations results through their teams.
● Committees of the ED: Actively participate in the Communications and Fundraising
Committee and opportunity to join MELS or Programs Committee as needed.

External Influence, Communications & Visibility (10%):
In collaboration with Head of Partnerships & Communications:
● Lead effective representation of TICAH’s transformative agenda and goals to influence
relevant actors and actions in Kenya and the region and globally.
● Build relevance and visibility in key spaces by representing TICAH and our beliefs, and
provide thought partnership externally through strategic speaking engagements, industry
networking, and collaboration on op-eds, articles, research, publications, reports, media
engagements, etc.
● External Communications Oversight:
○ Ensure strategic and value-aligned external communications.
○ Provide strategic leadership in moments of crisis communication.
○ Act as the main spokesperson and ensure oversight of external communications
by the team.

● Strategic Internal Communication:
○ In collaboration with the leadership team ensure that information flows
transparently, clearly and consistently across teams, fostering collaboration,
alignment, and a strong organisational culture

Partner & Stakeholder Engagement (15%):
● Engage regularly with diverse audiences and communities across our programs and
methodologies, building relationships, deepening understanding of our work in action,
and staying grounded in community realities through presence and listening.
● Cultivate relationships with partners and stakeholders to ensure they understand the
value and relevance of TICAH’s unique approach to current topical health and social
issues in Kenya, the region and globally.
● Grow non-funding partnerships in service of Strategic Goals, e.g., replication of our model, advocacy efforts, organizational and technical learning, etc.
● Steward relationships with strategic partners hosted by the organization, ensuring strong
collaboration, alignment and mutual value creation. Join strategy committees, oversee
operational plans and staff as needed.

Financial Management (10%):
● In collaboration with the Head of Finance;
○ Oversee the overall budgets, grant management, and systems that comprise
TICAH’s financial direction, sustainability, and practice.
○ Provide strategic oversight of TICAH’s financial health and stewardship of
resources, ensuring funds are used responsibly, effectively, and in alignment with
organizational priorities, while the DED leads operational decisions related to
grants, expenditures, and reporting

● Steward a long-term financial sustainability strategy, including diversifying revenue
streams through innovative models such as social enterprise, strengthening reserves and
investment strategies, and ensuring the organization is positioned for long-term resilience
and independence.

**WHO ARE LOOKING FOR:**
We are looking for a deeply mission-aligned, bold feminist leader with demonstrated
conviction and experience in rights-based programming and advocacy, who believes
communities own their challenges, solutions and decisions and is committed to self-
determination, bodily autonomy, holistic health, human rights, and addressing the intersections of health, culture, art, climate, and inequality.
You have a robust understanding of SRHR issues in East Africa and in-depth knowledge of
relevant laws, policies, regulations, and trends, including anti-rights actors and are comfortable working on access to safe abortion and the rights of LGBTQI+ people.
You embody a deeply relational worldview: You have a deep appreciation for culture and
creativity and understand the interconnectedness of people, community, wellbeing, justice, truth, beauty, and everyday life. And you bring this whole-person perspective to leadership and in how you listen, create and lead decisions on the role of the creative sector in social change.
And you move fluently across worlds: You have lived and worked across diverse contexts, and cultures and know how to move between with humility, curiosity, and ease.

EXPERIENCE & TRACK RECORD:
● Fundraising: You have successfully led fundraising across a diverse portfolio of
institutional, philanthropic, and individual donors, including securing significant multi-
year and unrestricted funding, and worked closely across fundraising and programme
teams to translate programme priorities into compelling funding opportunities and
proposals.
● Relationship-led donor stewardship:
○ Demonstrated track record of representing an organization compellingly, building
and retaining long-term donor relationships, with strong retention while building
the credibility and partnerships needed to resource complex systems-change
work. Recognizes that fundraising at TICAH is fundamentally relationship-based
rather than proposal-based.
○ Strategic resource mobilisation: Understands the changing funding landscape,
thinks beyond traditional fundraising and explores diverse approaches to
resource mobilisation and long-term organisational sustainability.

● Team size: You have experience leading an organisation of 20+ staff, including a senior
leadership team of at least three people, with an appreciation for building and managing
well motivated and self-driven diverse teams and navigating organisational transitions and
evolving leadership structures.
○ People leadership: Strong influencing, coaching, conflict resolution and
performance management skills, with the ability to support managers lead and
build self-driven motivated, healthy teams that achieve their goals

○ Experience promoting a culture of wellness, self- and collective care through
practices that support staff well-being, while modeling these values through your
own leadership and working style.

● Financial Management: Sound understanding of financial management, budgeting,
planning, accountability, and organizational systems, with a track record of ensuring
resources are used effectively and sustainably towards organization’s strategic goals.
○ Has managed an organisational budget of at least $1M, ideally in an organisation
of comparable size and complexity.
○ Demonstrated long-term thinking about organisational financial sustainability
and resilience, with an interest in diversifying revenue and exploring innovative
approaches to building greater financial independence.

● Programme complexity: Experience working across multiple, multidisciplinary
programmes, ideally spanning areas such as SRHR, health, food systems, climate justice,
art and culture.
○ Programmatic curiosity and credibility: Brings sufficient depth in at least one of
TICAH's areas of work and stays connected to the wider conversations, networks
and emerging thinking shaping holistic health, gender justice, climate justice and
rights-based work. Working with indigenous communities is an added advantage.
○ Program leadership: Ability to provide strategic leadership to ensure TICAH’s
programs evolve with learning, respond to emerging opportunities and needs, and
remain deeply aligned with the organization’s mission, strategy and long-term
vision.

● Movement building: Experience working within or alongside diverse social Justice
movements and advocacy spaces, particularly in SRHR and gender justice, including
navigating politically complex environments and advancing work beyond conventional
approaches.
● Government & policy: Experience engaging with government ministries, technical
working groups and/or policy spaces, and bringing technical or programmatic expertise
into these spaces.
● Conference & network engagement: Demonstrated ability to use conferences and
convenings strategically for fundraising, partnerships, and influence.

**LEADERSHIP SKILLS:**
1\. Strategic and grounded leadership
● You have a track record of 10+ years of leadership advancing social justice work in East
Africa, with experience working alongside community-focused organizations.
● Strategic leadership: You have proven senior leadership experience, ideally as an ED or
equivalent, with the strategic thinking and judgment to guide TICAH through its next
stage of growth and deepen its contribution to systems change.
● Complexity & adaptability: You have proven ability to hold complexity and connect the dots across global, national, and local contexts, balancing scale and systems change with TICAH’s bespoke, community-centred approach. You know when to challenge,
when to steady and when to listen and learn before changing.
● Organizational stewardship: You have the ability to translate strategy into effective planning, execution and ways of working, while strengthening organisational systems
and maintaining high standards of accountability, transparency, financial stewardship and operational effectiveness.

2\. Relationship-centred, people-powered leadership
● Trust-based and developmental: You intentionally build trust, listen deeply, understand people and their strengths, and create an environment where the team and all stakeholders feel supported, connected to leadership and empowered to grow.
● Shared and participatory: You believe in shared leadership and distributed power, with
the emotional intelligence and facilitative skills to navigate difficult conversations, bring diverse perspectives together and enable collective decision-making.
3\. Deep cultural and values alignment
● Humility, integrity & generosity: You lead with authenticity and integrity, and bring
generosity to colleagues, partners and allies.
● Learning &amp; growth: You are curious and committed to your own development, with the self-awareness to reflect, learn and evolve their leadership and ways of working.
● People & organisational wellbeing: You care deeply about the long-term sustainability
of the organisation and the conditions in which people thrive, creating psychological
safety, transparency and an environment where people can do their best work.
4\. Movement-builder and ecosystem leader
● Movement-minded: You understand TICAH’s distinctive role across feminists,
indigenous, SRHR, health and social justice movements, and its role as a convener, weaver and incubator.
● Builds across boundaries: You bring people together around shared purpose, build
coalitions and lasting relationships, and inspire collective action beyond organisational
boundaries.
● Generous collaborator: You have proven ability to nurture relationships, including inherited ones and you see collaboration (not competition) as a way to strengthen the wider movements and ecosystem.

**OTHER INFORMATION:**
Anticipated start is the first half of 2027. The role will be based in our Karen office with two days working from home flexibility. The role will involve regular travel within Kenya, regionally and internationally (approximately 5 international and 7 local/regional trips annually, in addition to regular engagements in/around Nairobi) to engage with communities, partners, donors, movements and other strategic spaces relevant to TICAH’s work.

We are looking for candidates who are excited to make a long-term commitment in seeing TICAH through its next level of growth.
There will be a six-month probationary period and we will agree on performance and learning objectives.

jobs.title: Director, Protection of Civilians (PoC) Division (Geneva)
jobs.description:
**About CIVIC**

Center for Civilians in Conflict (CIVIC) Center is an international nonprofit and nongovernmental organization with offices around the world working to improve protection for civilians in conflict zones. Our mission is to support communities affected by conflict in their quest for protection and strengthen the resolve and capacity of armed actors and relevant institutions to prevent and respond to civilian harm. We are advocates who believe that no civilian caught in conflict should be ignored, and advisors who provide practical solutions to preventing and responding to civilian harm. Learn more at [civiliansinconflict.org](https://www.civiliansinconflict.org/).

**About the Position**

The **Director of the Protection of Civilians (PoC) Division** leads CIVIC's technical, strategic, policy, and programmatic support on Protection of Civilians across all country programs and global initiatives. As a key member of the Senior Management Team (SMT), the Director ensures technical excellence, drives innovation, strengthens organizational capacities, and reinforces CIVIC's positioning as a global leader on PoC. The Director oversees the organization's team of technical advisors, ensuring coherent and high-quality support to field programs throughout the programme cycle—from strategy and programme design to implementation, learning, and policy influence. The Division translates global policy and normative frameworks into practical operational guidance while ensuring that evidence, lessons learned, and emerging protection trends from field operations systematically inform CIVIC's research, policy development, humanitarian diplomacy, and multilateral engagement, thereby strengthening the organization's field-to-policy feedback loop and strategic influence.

**Location:** Geneva (Switzerland). Candidates must be fully authorized to work without the need for sponsorship now or in the future.

**Travel:** As required

**Reporting to:** Director, Global & Field Programs

**Staff reporting:** Yes

**Key Responsibilities**

**1. Strategic, Technical and Programmatic Leadership**

- Provide high-level technical advice and oversight to field programs, ensuring alignment with evolving PoC standards, operational realities, and emerging protection challenges.
- Lead the strategic planning and evolution of the PoC Division, identifying new thematic priorities, partnerships, and areas of organizational growth.

**2. Supervision and Technical Management**

- Directly supervise the team of technical advisors (Gender & Children, MEAL, Community-Based Protection, Military Engagement, Research and other thematic advisors), ensuring high-quality technical support across the organization.
- Foster collaboration, accountability, professional development, and integration of technical expertise across programs, policy, and humanitarian diplomacy.

**3. Organizational Positioning and External Representation**

- Strengthen CIVIC's global positioning as a leading organization on Protection of Civilians through technical leadership, policy engagement, strategic partnerships, and external representation.
- Represent CIVIC in high-level engagements with donors, governments, multilateral organizations, security actors, academic institutions, and policy forums.

**4. Technical Support, Organizational Learning and Capacity Strengthening**

- Lead organization-wide capacity strengthening initiatives and promote continuous learning on CIVIC's thematic priorities.
- Support country teams throughout the programme cycle, including strategy development, proposal design, implementation, monitoring, evaluation, and adaptive learning.
- Promote effective knowledge management by capturing lessons learned, documenting good practices, and strengthening organizational learning.

**5. Bridge Between Programs, Policy and Humanitarian Diplomacy**

- Ensure a continuous two-way feedback loop between field operations and headquarters by translating policy and normative developments into practical operational guidance, while
- ensuring field evidence and operational learning inform CIVIC's research, policy development, humanitarian diplomacy, and multilateral engagement.
- Identify cross-cutting protection trends emerging from country programs and translate them into organizational priorities, policy products, advocacy initiatives, and technical guidance.

1. **Innovation and Thought Leadership**

- Drive innovation in Protection of Civilians by exploring emerging issues such as civilian harm mitigation, community-led protection, new technologies, artificial intelligence, misinformation, and evolving conflict dynamics.
- Promote interdisciplinary collaboration across humanitarian, peacebuilding, development, defense, and security sectors to advance innovative and practical approaches to civilian protection.
- Serve as CIVIC's technical lead on Protection of Civilians, guiding programmatic strategy, design, implementation, and learning across country programs.

**Key Qualifications**

- Minimum **10 years of progressively senior experience** in humanitarian protection, protection of civilians, civilian-military engagement, peacebuilding, security sector engagement, or related fields.
- Master's degree in International Relations, Humanitarian Affairs, Peace and Conflict Studies, International Law, Human Rights, Political Science, Security Studies, Development Studies, Public Policy, or another relevant field required. An advanced degree or equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.
- **Deep expertise in Protection of Civilians**, including operational approaches, community-based protection, civilian harm mitigation, and relevant international norms and best practices.
- Proven experience **engaging state and non-state armed actors, security institutions, and government authorities** to promote the protection of civilians, international humanitarian law, and improved civilian outcomes in conflict settings.
- Demonstrated experience providing **strategic, technical, and programmatic support** to field operations throughout the programme cycle, including strategy development, programme design, implementation, and learning.
- Proven experience leading **multidisciplinary and multicultural technical teams**, fostering collaboration, innovation, and professional development.
- Strong experience in **research, policy development, humanitarian diplomacy, and multilateral engagement**, with the ability to translate field evidence into policy influence and operational guidance.
- Proven track record of **strategic thinking, innovation, organizational learning, and external representation** at senior level.
- Strong understanding of **international humanitarian law, international human rights law, UN Protection of Civilians frameworks, civilian harm mitigation, and other relevant international policy and normative frameworks.**
- Excellent interpersonal, communication, negotiation, and diplomatic skills, with experience engaging governments, donors, multilateral organizations, security actors, and civil society.
- Demonstrated experience contributing to **business development**, including technical input to proposals, donor engagement, and programme growth.
- Fluency in **English and French** required; additional languages are an asset.
- **Valid authorization to work in Geneva at the time of this application without the need for current or future visa sponsorship. Nationals preferred.**

**Additional Details**

**Application Deadline: November 4, 2026**

Due to the high volume of applications, only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted. ***Shortlisted candidates will receive an email invitation from TestGorilla to submit their resume. Please complete this step promptly to ensure your candidacy is fully considered.***

CIVIC is an Equal Opportunities Employer committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive environment, and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or any other protected characteristic.

Note to Recruiters and Placement Agencies: CIVIC does not accept unsolicited agency resumes and does not pay placement fees for candidates submitted by agencies other than its approved partners.

jobs.title: Technical Mentor - Consultancy
jobs.description:
**Strengthening Media Capacity and Civil Oversight for Accountability in Lebanon**

## **Project Background**

Lebanon's governance environment is heavily impacted by systemic crises and erosion of the national integrity system. This project aims to strengthen the organizational capacity of six Lebanese media and civil society organizations (CSOs) to evaluate public data sources, apply advanced analytical workflows, and execute evidence-based accountability work.

The project integrates cutting-edge technology, AI-assisted research routines, and automated data monitoring workflows to enhance the analytical capacity of independent media and CSOs scrutinizing public procurement, registries, and financial data in Lebanon.

This project is implemented by the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH in partnership with Media in Cooperation and Transition (MiCT). It is funded by Germany through the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ).

- **Duration:** 10 months
- **Level of Effort:** 5 days per month per mentor (across 6 mentors)

**Role Objective**

Technical Mentors work directly with assigned organizations to build, refine, document, and embed custom data tools, AI workflows, and monitoring routines into regular organizational operations until complete operational independence is achieved.

## **Key Responsibilities & Scope of Work**

- **Hackathon Support & Working Sprint:** Guide assigned teams during the Beirut Hackathon event. Provide at least two structured technical check-ins per week during the 4-week working sprint to unblock obstacles in coding, data fetching, and prototyping.
- **Mentorship Opening & Workplan:** Conduct an opening 1-day in-person session in Beirut. Co-draft a binding mentorship workplan with assigned organization specifying technical tasks, staff training targets, and output timelines.
- **Fortnightly Mentorship & Site Visits:** Hold bi-weekly remote sessions and at least two in-person site visits per organization. Train at least two designated staff members to independently operate and maintain the tool/agent.
- **Technical Log & Verification:** Maintain running technical logs documenting software architecture, code repositories, user manuals, digital safety protocols, and editorial integration.

## **Key Deliverables**

1. Approved Mentorship Workplan and baseline technical diagnosis for assigned organization.
2. Fortnightly mentorship meeting notes and technical progress updates.
3. Completed Technical Log, source code documentation, and User Manual for the custom tool/workflow.
4. Final assessment report confirming that at least two staff members can independently operate the tool without external support.

## **Qualifications & Requirements**

- Degree or equivalent professional experience in Data Journalism, Software Development, OSINT, Data Analysis, or Computational Media.
- 5 to 7 years of demonstrated experience in mentoring, capacity building, or training non-technical staff in digital tools.
- Expertise in tools such as Python, SQL, web scraping, LLM APIs, visualization platforms, or security protocols.
- Fluency in Arabic and English.

jobs.title: Cash and Markets Project Manager Sudan Khartoum (Open for Sudanese only)
jobs.description:
**Background:**

The Cash Project Manager sits in the Country Office Cash & Markets team, reports to the Cash & Markets Programme Manager, and works at middle-management level. The role leads the day-to-day management of a portfolio of CVA grants across several Area Offices. It supervises the Cash & Markets Project Coordinator(s) and is the technical reference point for Area Office cash and market staff. It is the main link between the Country Office, Area Office teams, partners and support functions, turning strategy and donor commitments into on-time, compliant, quality delivery.

**What you will do:**

The Cash Project Manager leads the oversea of NRC's cash and markets projects from start to close-out. The role owns project cycle management across multiple grants and Area Offices: planning, budget follow-up, quality assurance, reconciliation of reach figures, and timely donor reporting. It ensures cash reaches people most in need safely and in line with NRC standards, and that market functionality and risk inform every modality decision.

The position sits in the Country Office Cash & Markets team and is a key link between the Programme Manager, Area Office teams, partners, the Sudan Collective technical unit and support functions.

General Responsibilities:

1. Line management responsibilities for directly reporting staff. This includes the
- Performance management process; setting clear goals aligned to country strategy and priorities, and to follow up and support staff’s achievement.
- Responsible for key processes as workforce planning, recruitment, staff induction and development and ensure Duty of Care for own staff
- Manage cash projects (activities, budgets, procurement, partners, documentation) in line with proposals, strategy and donor requirements.
2. Report on progress regularly and on an ad-hoc basis, meeting all internal and donor deadlines.
3. Coordinate across NRC departments and Area Offices involved in delivery

**Specific responsibilities**

1. Project cycle management
- Engage with AO teams to develop and maintain work plans, spending plans, MEAL plans and procurement plans for each CVA grant.
- Lead grant opening, project review and grant closing meetings with Grants, Finance and Area Offices.
2. Cash and voucher delivery – Field based.
- Oversee MPCA, sectoral cash, voucher delivery, both direct and partner led.
- Ensure Area Office teams apply NRC Sudan SOPs: targeting, registration, verification, payment and complaints handling.
3. Markets and feasibility
- Lead or support cash feasibility, market and risk assessments ahead of each response.
- Identify opportunities for market-support interventions and integration with other Core Competencies.
4. Grants, budgets and reporting
- Oversee CVA project budgets with AO teams and Finance: forecasting, BvA follow-up, and timely reallocation requests.
- Reconcile reach and distribution figures across Area Offices, NRC systems, in close collaboration with the Information Management Coordinator.
5. MEAL, quality and learning
- Work with MEAL on baseline, post-distribution monitoring and market monitoring, and act on findings.
- Ensure complaints and feedback are tracked, referred and closed on time.
6. Partnership and coordination
- Support partner capacity assessments and capacity building for local partners on CVA.
- Represent NRC in the Cash Working Group and CCS technical meetings as delegated.
7. People management
- Line-manage the Cash & Markets Project Coordinator(s) and provide functional guidance to Area Office cash staff.
- Identify capacity gaps and deliver or arrange CVA training for NRC staff.

**Please refer to the** [**Job Description**](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQC6dQo7nbPSR5_U1Cn2kmuxAZK1nDO9GHQDXompx5lhLDk?e=DxdFER) **for detailed information as the above responsibilities are just a snapshot.**

**What you will bring:**

1. **Generic professional competencies:**

- Bachelor's degree in economics, business administration, social sciences, development studies or a related field. A Master's degree is an asset.
- At least 4 years of humanitarian experience, including a minimum of 3 years of experience managing Cash and Voucher Assistance (CVA) projects or similar interventions.
- Proven project cycle management: planning, budget management, risk management and reporting on multiple grants at once.
- Experience working in complex, insecure and fast-changing contexts.
- Line management experience, including recruitment and performance management.
- Documented results related to the position's responsibilities.
- Fluency in Arabic and English, written and spoken. Able to draft donor-quality reports in English.
- Advanced Excel skills. Experience with KoBo/ODK, Power BI or beneficiary data systems (e.g. LMMS, RedRose) is an asset.

**2. Context related skills, knowledge and experience:**

- Strong knowledge of the Sudan context, including displacement dynamics, the economic situation and access constraints.
- Knowledge of Sudanese markets, financial service providers and digital payment options (e.g. mobile money, bank apps).
- Experience with cash consortia or the Sudan Cash Working Group.

- **Your most updated Cover Letter**
- **Do not attach certificates or any other documents apart from the two mentioned above.**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

jobs.title: Head of Operations, Myanmar
jobs.description:
**Job Summary**

As a member of the Country Program’s (CP) Senior Management Team (SMT), the Head of Operations is responsible for providing leadership and management of the operational functions - Finance, Human Resources (HR), Supply Chain Management (SCM), Administration, Information and Communication Technology, Security and Audit - in support of the CRS mission to serve the poor and vulnerable. You will promote stewardship of resources, ensure principled compliance, proactively manage risk, prevent fraud, and lead (continuous) operational improvements including from a Climate Action lens. As part of the SMT you will proactively manage and mitigate security risks.

**Roles and Key Responsibilities:**

- Contribute to the CP strategic planning and programming on needed investments in operations capacity – systems, processes and staffing – that meet CRS’ standards, donor requirements, and local regulations and support high-quality programming. Represent CRS, as needed.
- Plan, integrate, coordinate, and monitor day-to-day operations to ensure all support services are delivered with high-quality in an efficient manner. Address issues where operations support needs to be adapted for complex programming. Oversee the piloting of new operations initiatives that require the setting of new standards and systems
- Effectively manage and supervise talent. Lead the development of clear staff development and sucession plans within the Operations team to meet growth needs. Manage team dynamics and staff well-being. Provide coaching, strategically tailor individual development plans, and complete performance management for direct reports. Monitor and assess performance to ensure adequate capacity for successful support of high quality programming. Contribute to staffing plans and recruitment process of senior staff.
- Ensure the program is adequately staffed to meet CP needs and HR systems, policies and practices support a high-performance culture, staff development and retention. Ensure quality personnel administration and a work environment that truly reflects the agency’s guiding principles.
- Oversee compliance with agency and donor requirements and local laws and regulations through periodic systems checks, review and assessment of CP’s operations policies and procedures. Act as lead contact and responder to issues that emerge from internal and external audits and provide recommendations and guidance to implement improvements.
- Oversee financial processes in accordance with policies and ensure proactive service delivery, advice, and support to managers, staff, and subrecipients in relation to the project cycle (Design, Start-up, Implementation, Close-out). Ensure efficiency and compliance with CRS’ policies and procedures, Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP), donors’ rules and regulations, and legal requirements. Ensure effective and appropriate use of CRS’s finance and supply chain management systems and other technical solutions.
- Collaborate with programming leads to ensure appropriate project expenditures in line with financial plans and proper stewardship of material sources. Promote effective use of CRS’ Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system for budget management and general oversight. Anticipate, identify and address challenges that affect the proper stewardship, risk, and optimal utilization of program assets and resources (financial, human, and material).
- Promote safeguarding at the CP level. Ensure quality implementation of CRS safeguarding policy and principles across operations at both CRS and partner level. With support from technical advisors, ensure capacity building efforts and technical guidance to CRS staff and partners, in line with CRS principles and standards, donor guidelines, and industry best practices.
- Oversee Health, Safety, and Security management. Ensure all staff understand and adhere to CRS staff safety and security trainings, policies and plans and ensure the updating of such plans.
- Lead the operational aspects of a CP’s Climate Action strategy with support from the SMT including: implement action plans and monitor progress, prioritize entry points and investments for operational efficiency and the reduction of Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions and waste.
- Effectively manage and supervise talent. Manage team dynamics and staff well-being. Provide coaching, strategically tailor individual development plans, and complete performance management for direct reports. Monitor and assess performance to ensure adequate capacity for successful support of high quality programming. Contribute to staffing plans and recruitment process of senior staff.
- With the Country Representative, oversee the preparation of annual budget plans and grant/project budgets to ensure they reflect maximum operational efficiency and budgetary compliance and mitigate risks. Set and provide technical oversight of internal processes for approving expenses, monitoring spending, and making budget adjustments in line with operational and programmatic needs and with donor requirements.
- Create and maintain the proper conditions for learning. Establish a safe environment for the sharing of ideas, solutions, and difficulties and the capacity to detect, analyze and respond quickly to small deficiencies. Provide capacity strengthening guidance for project teams and partners, which includes cross-departmental learning.

**Basic Qualifications:**

- Bachelor's degree in International Development, Business Administration, Finance or relevant field required.
- Minimum of 5-8 years work experience in a management position with progressive responsibilities with at least 2 years supervisory experience. Experience with an international NGO and experience outside country of origin preferred.
- Additional experience may substitute for some education; additional education may substitute for some experience.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

- Knowledge of multiple public donors’ regulations highly preferred.

***Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:***

- Understanding of financial systems, including budgeting and budget/expense analysis experience.
- Knowledge of procurement and office administration/management issues.
- Ability to represent the agency at high levels.
- Knowledge of Oracle ERP or similar financial reporting software.
- Staff management experience and abilities that are conducive to a learning environment.
- Proficient in MS Office package (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Visio), Web Conferencing Applications, and information and budget management systems.
- Excellent strategic, analytical, systems thinking, and problem-solving skills, with capacity to see the big picture and ability to make sound judgment and decisions.
- Strong relations management abilities. Ability to work collaboratively.
- Team leadership abilities.
- Ethical conduct in accordance with recognized professional and organizational codes of ethics.
- Proactive, resourceful, solutions-oriented and results-oriented.

***Required Languages***: Fluent English is required. Working proficiency in Burmese is a plus.

***Travel**:* Must be willing and able to travel up to 30% in Myanmar or within the Europe, Middle East, Asia (EMEA) region.

**Supervisory Responsibilities:** Yes

**Agency Competencies (for all CRS Staff):**

- **Personal Accountability** – Consistently takes responsibility for one’s own actions.
- **Acts with Integrity** - Consistently models values aligned with CRS Guiding Principles and mission. Is considered honest.
- **Builds and Maintains Trust** - Shows consistency between words and actions.
- **Collaborates with Others** – Works effectively in intercultural and diverse teams.
- **Open to Learn** – Seeks out experiences that may change perspective or provide an opportunity to learn new things.

**Agency Leadership Competencies:**

- **Lead Change** – Continually looks for ways to improve the agency through a culture of agility, openness, and innovation.
- **Develops and Recognizes Others** – Builds the capacity of staff to reach their full potential and enhance team and agency performance.
- **Strategic Mindset** – Understands role in translating, communicating, and implementing agency strategy and team priorities.

**What we offer**

CRS offers U.S. based staff a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, life insurance, vision, and a generous retirement savings plan. Salary and benefits packages for successful candidates employed outside the U.S. are based on the country of employment/in-country office where the candidate will perform the role. CRS´ work culture is a collaborative, mission-driven culture committed to improving the lives of the poor throughout the world.

## About Us

Catholic Relief Services is the official international humanitarian agency of the Catholic community in the United States. Catholic Relief Services works to save, protect, and transform lives in need in more than 100 countries, without regard to race, religion or nationality. Catholic Relief Services’ relief and development work is accomplished through programs of emergency response, HIV, health, agriculture, education, microfinance, and peacebuilding. We welcome as a part of our staff people of all faiths and secular traditions who share our values and our commitment to serving those in need. CRS’ processes and policies reflect our commitment to safeguarding children and vulnerable adults from abuse and exploitation.

CRS welcomes candidates from the countries and regions in which we work. In the event the successful candidate is an expatriate, the anticipated duration of the assignment is informed by a term limit, based on the type and level of the job and the needs of the agency.

CRS is committed to safeguarding program participants, community members, staff and volunteers from all forms of exploitation and abuse. The successful candidate is expected to sign and adhere to CRS´ Code of Conduct.

CRS talent acquisition procedures reflect our commitment to safeguarding the rights and dignity of all people - especially children and vulnerable adults - to live free from abuse and harm.

*Disclaimer: This job description is not an exhaustive list of the skill, effort, duties, and responsibilities associated with the position.*

CRS is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

**General Requirements**

CRS offers are contingent on the selected candidate’s ability to legally work where the position is to be performed. Every government has a unique set of work permit eligibility requirements\*\*.\*\* All positions requiring residence or frequent travel outside a home country must undergo and clear a pre-employment medical clearance; some work permit processes require clearing a separate government administered medical examination.

CRS prioritizes candidates who are citizens/ permanent residents of the countries where we have CRS offices.

jobs.title: Finance & Administration Manager
jobs.description:
**Position:**

Finance & Administration Manager (FAM) (100%)

**Duty station:**

Damascus, Syria, with travel within Syria as required and as security conditions allow

**Reporting line:**

Country Director, Syria (direct supervision)

**Technical liaison:**

Finance Department, Solidar Suisse Headquarters, Zurich

**Contract type / duration:**

12 months, renewable

**BACKGROUND INFORMATION**

Solidar Suisse is a Swiss NGO founded in 1936 (then known as Swiss Labour Assistance), committed to social justice and decent working conditions worldwide. Today, Solidar Suisse is active in 16 countries, implementing both development cooperation and humanitarian assistance programs.

In Syria, Solidar Suisse has been operational since 2023, primarily responding to the 2023 earthquake in Northwest Syria. The country program has focused on Protection, Shelter, WASH, and Livelihoods and is now formulating a new strategy incorporating both humanitarian and recovery components. With the evolving political and humanitarian dynamics, and new opportunities for engagement across Syria, Solidar Suisse is establishing an operational presence in Damascus to expand its support for recovery, resilience, and development efforts throughout the country. A Country Director is now in post in Damascus. Solidar Suisse is in the process of, but has not yet completed, official registration with the relevant Syrian authorities.

**GENERAL POSITION SUMMARY**

The Finance & Administration Manager is a core member of Solidar Suisse’s start-up team in Syria. Working alongside, and under the direct supervision of, the Country Director, the FAM will play a central role in establishing Solidar Suisse’s operational presence in Damascus and in building the finance, administration, human resources, logistics and procurement systems that the Syria program will rely on as it grows.

The FAM is responsible for the finance, human resource management, administrative, logistics and procurement functions of the Damascus office. S/he ensures effective implementation of Solidar Suisse’s financial and administrative policies and procedures, in compliance with donor requirements and Syrian laws and regulations. He/She will also provides guidance and support to both Solidar Suisse project staff and to the staff of local partner organisations. The FAM liaises closely with Solidar Suisse Headquarters, particularly the Finance Department in Zurich.

In the start-up phase the Country Director and the FAM will be the first staff of Solidar Suisse in Syria. The position therefore requires a hands-on professional who is willing to work flexibly across functions and to take on tasks beyond those listed below as the needs of the start-up require. As the Syria program expands, the role is expected to evolve towards the supervision of a finance, administration and logistics team and increased oversight of partner financial management.

**MAIN TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Finance**

- Take over and manage the day-to-day operation of the interim finance and cash management system, including working advance requests, the bank and cash transaction registers (USD and SYP), supporting documentation, cash counts, bank reconciliations, monthly closing and timely settlement of advances to Headquarters.
- Prepare monthly cash projections and fund requests, and provide support in developing and following up on project and office budgets, including financial forecasts and relevant financial analysis.
- Support the transition from interim arrangements to full financial systems, including the opening of an organisational bank account, the set-up and application of accounting software, and the adaptation of Solidar Suisse’s Field Financial and Administrative Guidelines (FFAG) and Finance Policy to the Syrian context, in cooperation with the Country Director and Headquarters.
- Provide timely reporting to MoFA and further line ministries, ensure adherence to national laws on income tax, social insurance and other applicable obligations as the legal status of Solidar Suisse in Syria develops, and ensure applicable payments are made on time.
- Prepare budgets and financial inputs for concept notes and proposals and prepare or consolidate financial reports required by Headquarters and donors.
- Conduct orientations for local partner organisations and continuously guide and advise them on correct finance procedures and documentation; review partner financial reports and financial management and procedures on a regular basis; and support any audit by external entities.

**Administration & Human Resources**

- Support the Country Director in all administrative matters related to the registration of Solidar Suisse in Syria, including the preparation, translation and follow-up of documentation with the legal representative and the relevant authorities.
- Be the responsible for contact and communication with line ministries in Syria to ensure organizational and programme related permissions are obtained and compliance in reporting ensured
- Manage and follow up all contractual office matters, including the office lease, utilities and service contracts, and ensure timely payment of all office-related bills and fees.
- Provide advice to the Country Director on Syrian labour law and support the development of HR procedures and staff regulations for the Syria program in line with Solidar Suisse policies and local legislation.
- Support the recruitment and onboarding of staff and consultants, including drafting job descriptions and Terms of Reference, advertising, organising interviews and preparing contracts; maintain personnel files, timesheets and leave records, and administer payroll once established.
- Ensure that financial, HR and administrative records and filing are comprehensive, accurate, secure and up to date. This includes, but is not limited to, all financial plans, budgets, contracts, agreements and key correspondence.
- Record bills, advances, invoices and payments accurately and on time, ensuring every transaction is properly authorised, supported and filed in line with the Approval Authority Matrix.
- Support and guide partner Finance staff on administration and HR related issues and check compliance with internal and external rules and regulations (e.g. staff policy, payroll, labour law).

**Logistics & Procurement**

- **Office set-up:** support the identification, assessment and set-up of suitable office premises in Damascus, including the application of agreed selection criteria (location and security, condition of the property, electricity supply and back-up/solar arrangements, internet and telephone connectivity, furniture and work-space layout), market assessment of available premises, and negotiation with landlords on lease terms and any required works.
- **Works and fit-out:** prepare or review itemised cost estimates and work plans for any adaptations needed to make premises fit for purpose (e.g. electrical work, partitioning, minor repairs, connectivity, furnishing), and follow up on their completion.
- **Procurement:** manage procurement of goods and services in strict accordance with the Interim Finance and Cash Management Manual, the applicable procurement thresholds and the Solidar Suisse Supplier Code of Conduct, including sourcing comparative quotations, preparing bid analyses and procurement committee documentation, and ensuring procurement files are complete and properly filed.
- **Assets and inventory:** establish and maintain the asset register and inventory records, and ensure the delivery, installation, tagging and safe-keeping of equipment and supplies.
- **Contracts and suppliers:** prepare contracts engaged by Solidar Suisse with third parties (landlords, service providers, suppliers and consultants) and develop a list of reliable local suppliers and service providers.
- **Partner procurement:** support, monitor and review procurement processes carried out by partner organisations and ensure compliance with applicable procurement policies.
- **Movement and travel:** organise travel arrangements, accommodation, local transport, meetings and other events for the team and visitors.

**Safety, Security & Duty of Care**

- Support the Country Director in implementing safety, security and duty of care measures in coordination with Headquarters, including staff contact lists, emergency communication arrangements and the security of the office, cash and assets.

**Internal Coordination & Reporting**

- Work in close day-to-day coordination with the Country Director and maintain regular contact with the Finance Department and Desk Officer at Headquarters.
- Perform any other tasks assigned by the Country Director.

**WORKING ARRANGEMENTS AND FLEXIBILITY**

- The FAM will join a two-person team and will work in close partnership with the Country Director to set up Solidar Suisse’s operational presence in Damascus. Roles will be shared pragmatically, and the FAM is expected to take on tasks outside the core finance and administration functions where needed, including general office, program and representation support, liaison with local stakeholders, and Arabic–English translation.
- During the start-up phase the work will be dynamic and priorities may change at short notice. The FAM is expected to show flexibility in working arrangements, including occasional work outside normal office hours and work from temporary premises until a permanent office is established.
- With a small initial team, the Country Director and the FAM will work together to maintain sound internal control and an appropriate segregation of duties (for example, independent review of transactions), in line with Solidar Suisse policies.
- In the absence of the Country Director, the FAM will act as the focal point for operational, finance and administrative matters in Damascus, within delegated authority.
- The scope of the position will evolve as the Syria program grows and further staff are recruited.

**REQUIRED PROFILE AND EXPERIENCE**

- University degree in finance, accounting, business administration or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
- At least 5 years of experience in finance and administration, ideally with an international NGO, UN agency or similar organisation; experience of office or program start-up is a strong advantage.
- Solid knowledge of the Syrian legal, tax, banking and labour law environment; familiarity with NGO registration procedures in Syria is an advantage.
- Practical experience in procurement, logistics and asset management.
- Experience of donor-funded project budgeting and financial reporting; experience with Swiss or European donors is an asset.
- Excellent computer skills, especially Excel and accounting software.
- Fluency in Arabic and Advanced English (written, spoken and reading).
- Syrian national or resident of Damascus, with good knowledge of the city and its service providers.
- Strong initiative and the ability to plan, organise and prioritise work independently, cope with stress and respect deadlines.
- Able to work independently as well as in a very small team; flexible, adaptable and comfortable with the uncertainty of a start-up environment.
- A high degree of integrity, discretion, loyalty and commitment.

**DURATION AND STARTING DATE**

Solidar Suisse is looking for a candidate who can start as soon as possible. The position is offered on an initial 12-month contract, subject to a three-month probationary period. The contract may be extended based on satisfactory performance and organizational requirements.

jobs.title: Consultancy Services of Graphic designer in shift asia learning session
jobs.description:
## TERMS OF REFERENCE FOR CONSULTANCY SERVICES

### Graphic designer in shift asia learning session

***Oxfam is committed to preventing any type of unwanted behaviour at work including sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse, lack of integrity and financial misconduct; and committed to promoting the welfare of children, young people and adults. Oxfam expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment through our code of conduct. We place a high priority on ensuring that only those who share and demonstrate our values are recruited to work for us.***

**Shaping a stronger Oxfam for people living in poverty.**

**BACKGROUND**

The Supporting Humanitarian Initiatives for Transformation in Asia (SHIFT Asia) Project is a critical regional initiative building upon the success of the first phase of Women’s Local Humanitarian Leadership (WLHL) implemented in 2022–2023. SHIFT Asia now operates across Indonesia, Bangladesh, the Philippines, and Myanmar, and is focused on advancing women’s leadership by positioning their organizations at the center of humanitarian decision-making.

The project operates based on the reality that women and girls are disproportionately affected by crises yet remain severely underrepresented in leadership. By applying a feminist and participatory approach that fosters regional networks and solidarity, SHIFT Asia aims to transform humanitarian systems to be more inclusive, representative, and effective in achieving gender-transformative disaster preparedness and response.

Central to this second phase is the SHIFT Asia Learning Agenda (2025–2027). This agenda promotes feminist learning spaces, peer-to-peer exchanges, and collective capacity enhancement in key areas such as program design (Theory of Change - TOC) and robust Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) systems. Grounded in Oxfam’s Common Approach to MEAL, the Learning Agenda is designed to generate evidence, capture lessons, and drive accountability and social change across local, national, and regional levels. To effectively communicate these lessons, we require a professional Graphic Designer to transform technical content into engaging visual assets.

**PURPOSE**

The primary purpose of this assignment is to secure a professional Graphic Designer to produce high-quality visual learning materials for **eight (8) design packages**. The goal is to ensure complex humanitarian and feminist concepts are accessible and shareable across regional networks.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

The selected graphic designer shall be responsible for:

- **Visual Design:** Creating cohesive and culturally sensitive designs that align with Oxfam’s branding and the feminist principles of the SHIFT Asia project.
- **Layout & Illustration**: Developing infographics and layouts that simplify technical MEAL and program design concepts.
- **Revision:** Incorporating feedback from the SHIFT Asia team to ensure technical accuracy and visual clarity.
- **Technical Compliance:** Ensuring all files are delivered in high-resolution print-ready and web-optimized formats.

**EXPECTED RESULTS**

*It must be noted that the copyright for all the plans and reports and other intellectual property created as a part of this project shall vest exclusively to Oxfam which would be free to use all such material, without restrictions.*

For each of the **eight (8) design packages**, the consultant will provide:

1. **One (1) Learning Paper Design:** A detailed A4-sized document of 5–6 pages summarizing the key findings and technical data of the topic.
2. **Two (2) Social Media Designs:** Two separate carousels (4–6 slides each) designed for platforms like LinkedIn, Instagram, or Facebook to promote the learning highlights.
3. **Posting the social media design via Oxfam Asia social media platform**

**DELIVERABLES AND TIMELINE**

The implementation period will be for **approximately 6 months** starting from **19 November 2026**.

***Deliverable - Description - Quantity***

1. ***Learning Papers -*** 5-6 page A4 Infographic/Learning Paper per package - 8 Total
2. ***Social Media Assets -*** Carousel (4-6 slides) per package (2 versions each) - 16 Total

**DURATION OF THE ASSIGNMENT**

The intended start date is 19 November 2026 and the period of implementation will be for approximately 6 monthsfrom this date.

Note: Specific session dates will be confirmed upon contracting.

**CONTRACT SUPERVISION**

The consultant will work closely with and under day-to day supervision of the of the SHIFT Asia MEAL Coordinator to fulfil the objectives of this consultancy.

**REQUIREMENTS AND QUALIFICATIONS**

The consultant’s proposal shall demonstrate the following refined capabilities to ensure alignment with the visual and technical needs of the SHIFT Asia project:

- **Language Proficiency:** Near-native or native fluency in English and professional working proficiency in either Indonesian (Bahasa) or Bengali (Bangla).
- **Technical Experience:** A minimum of 3 years of professional experience providing graphic design services for international development or humanitarian organizations.
- **Portfolio:** A strong portfolio demonstrating a proven ability to create similar tasks, specifically transforming technical data and concepts into digestible 5-6 page learning papers and social media carousels.
- **Software Proficiency:** Proven ability to use **Canva** or other professional design and conferencing platforms (e.g., Adobe Creative Suite, Zoom, MS Teams) with access to reliable high-speed internet.
- **Oxfam Branding:** Prior experience working with **Oxfam branding guidelines** and visual identity is highly preferable to ensure seamless integration with existing project materials.

**KEY ATTRIBUTES**

- Ability to demonstrate sensitivity to cultural differences and gender issues, as well as the commitment to equal opportunities.
- Ability to demonstrate an openness and willingness to learn about the application of gender/gender mainstreaming, women’s rights, and diversity for all aspects of development work.
- Commitment to Oxfam’s safeguarding policies to ensure all people who come into contact with Oxfam are as safe as possible.

**ORGANISATIONAL VALUES**

- Accountability – Our purpose-driven, results-focused approach means we take responsibility for our actions and hold ourselves accountable. We believe that others should also be held accountable for their actions.
- Empowerment – Our approach means that everyone involved with Oxfam, from our staff and supporters to people living in poverty, should feel they can make change happen.
- Inclusiveness – We are open to everyone and embrace diversity. We believe everyone has a contribution to make, regardless of visible and invisible differences.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

The selected Interpreter(s) shall be responsible for:

- Interpretation: Providing accurate and simultaneous (preferred) or high-quality consecutive interpretation between English - Indonesian (Bahasa) and English - Bengali (Bangla) for all four virtual learning sessions. These two languages are recommended to delivered by different providers in the each country based.
- Preparation: Reviewing all session materials (agendas, presentations, technical guides) provided at least 48 hours in advance to familiarize themselves with the subject and technical jargon.
- Testing: Participating in a brief technical check prior to each session to ensure optimal audio and virtual platform settings (e.g., Zoom/MS Teams interpretation feature).
- Impartiality: Maintaining strict confidentiality, professionalism, and impartiality throughout the assignment.

**EXPECTED RESULTS**

*It must be noted that the copyright for all the plans and reports and other intellectual property created as a part of this project shall vest exclusively to Oxfam which would be free to use all such material, without restrictions.*

The success of the interpretation service will be measured by its contribution to the technical quality and participatory nature of the learning sessions, specifically:

1. High Comprehension of Technical Content: Approximately 95% of all core technical content delivered by the facilitator are accurately conveyed and understood by Indonesian and Bangladeshi participants, minimizing the need for extensive clarification loops.
2. Facilitation Efficiency: The interpretation services do not introduce significant delays; the session concludes within the scheduled 2-hour timeframe, maintaining the flow and pacing set by the facilitator.

**DELIVERABLES AND TIMELINE**

The Interpreter(s) are expected to deliver interpretation services for the following four virtual sessions:

***Deliverable - Description - Estimated Session Date - Estimated Duration (Each)***

*D1 -* Rapid Gender Analysis (RGA) – internal review of RGA methodologies applied and tracked against MTR commitments -19 November 2026 - 2 Hours

*D2 -* Partnerships, Policy & Advocacy – sharing Year 1 partnership models and policy wins with donors and allies - 21 January 2027- 2 Hours

*D3 -* Rapid Care Analysis (RCA) – evaluating implementation of the new RCA method addressing unpaid care work - 18 March 2027 - 2 Hours

*D4 -* Women Local Humanitarian Leadership – evaluating how women’s organizations and leaders improve humanitarian outcomes - 20 May 2027 - 2 Hours

Note: Specific session dates will be confirmed upon contracting.

**DURATION OF THE ASSIGNMENT**

The intended start date is 19 November 2026 and the period of implementation will be for approximately 6 monthsfrom this date.

**CONTRACT SUPERVISION**

The consultant will work closely with and under day-to day supervision of the of the SHIFT Asia MEAL Coordiantor to fulfil the objectives of this consultancy.

**REQUIREMENTS AND QUALIFICATIONS**

We need **two providers from each country** based that have a team of appropriately qualified personnel with a broad range of skill mixes that allow it to deliver the tasks identified above. The consultant’s proposal shall demonstrate the following capabilities:

- **Language Proficiency:** Near-native or native fluency in English and professional working proficiency in either Indonesian (Bahasa) or Bengali (Bangla).
- **Technical Experience**: A minimum of 3 years of professional experience providing interpretation (simultaneous or consecutive) for international development or humanitarian organizations.
- **Technical Setup:** Proven ability to use virtual conferencing platforms (e.g., Zoom, MS Teams) and access reliable high-speed internet and high-quality audio equipment essential for simultaneous interpretation.
- **Professionalism:** Demonstrated ability to maintain strict accuracy, professionalism, and neutrality during high-stakes internal discussions.

**KEY ATTRIBUTES**

- Ability to demonstrate sensitivity to cultural differences and gender issues, as well as the commitment to equal opportunities.
- Ability to demonstrate an openness and willingness to learn about the application of gender/gender mainstreaming, women’s rights, and diversity for all aspects of development work.
- Commitment to Oxfam’s safeguarding policies to ensure all people who come into contact with Oxfam are as safe as possible.

**ORGANISATIONAL VALUES**

- Accountability – Our purpose-driven, results-focused approach means we take responsibility for our actions and hold ourselves accountable. We believe that others should also be held accountable for their actions.
- Empowerment – Our approach means that everyone involved with Oxfam, from our staff and supporters to people living in poverty, should feel they can make change happen.
- Inclusiveness – We are open to everyone and embrace diversity. We believe everyone has a contribution to make, regardless of visible and invisible differences.

**Fixed term | 6 months | November 2026**

## Acted

**Who we are**
Acted works with 19 million people across 43 countries at the intersection of humanitarian, development, climate and environmental programming. We draw on deep contextual knowledge and embrace emerging technologies to save lives, alleviate suffering, and protect and restore our planet. Working in collaboration with a growing ecosystem of local, national and international partners, we pursue one shared objective: a 3Zero World – Zero Exclusion, Zero Carbon and Zero Poverty.

**Who we are looking for**
You bring the core competencies required for classical humanitarian and development work, alongside an active climate and environmental conscience, and you can navigate the challenges that arise when human and environmental suffering intersect. You have an entrepreneurial mindset: you see opportunities, connect dots, adapt your approach to different environments, and take measured risks in pursuit of results. You balance principles with pragmatism, and ambition with humility.

## Acted Occupied Palestinian Territory - OPT

Acted has been present in the West Bank since 2007 and in the Gaza Strip since 2008. With its office in Jerusalem, Acted has been responding to humanitarian needs and development challenges in the Occupied Palestinian Territory through an integrated approach. In view of the worsening of the humanitarian situation in recent years, and even more so since 7 October 2023, Acted is mobilized to respond to the basic needs of the populations affected by the conflict.

## You will be in charge of

The Country Security Manager is responsible for overseeing daily security management of all Acted premises and project sites, ensuring a permanent monitoring and assessment of the security situation in country, as well as reviewing and implementing Acted security management guidelines and protocols. He/she will also advise the Country Director and Senior Management Team on all issues of safety and security and provide appropriate security training and mentoring.

***Main duties***

1\. Department management

2\. Context & Risk analysis

3\. Develop and update Country Security Plans, SOPs and Contingency Plans

4\. Daily Security Management

5\. Crisis management

- *Adapt crisis management protocols to the local situation;*
- *Act as a key member of the Crisis Management Team so that safety policies and procedures are implemented;*

6\. Reporting

7\. Training and briefing

- *Conduct security briefing for each new international staff arriving in country;*
- *Design security training modules for Country Director’s approval and HQ endorsement;*

8\. Develop and maintain a security network

9\. Ensure external representation

## Expected skills and qualifications

- At least 3-5 years of working experience in insecure environments; preferably in Africa, Asia, or the Middle East;
- Extensive experience in security management and procedures;
- Demonstrated communication and organizational skills;
- Ability to train, mobilize, and manage both international and national staff Flexibility and ability to multi-task under pressure;
- Ability to work well in unstable and frequently changing security environments;
- Willingness to work and live in often remote areas under basic conditions;
- Proven ability to work creatively and independently both in the field and in the office;
- Advanced proficiency in written and spoken English;
- Knowledge of local language and/or regional experience highly desirable.

## Terms of reference

For more information about the position, [click here ](https://www.acted.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/csm-opt-2026.pdf).

## Conditions

- Salary between 3300 and 4500€ monthly (before income tax), depending on the level of education, security level, etc as well as a monthly living allowance of $300
- Accommodation and food provided in Acted guesthouse
- Pension, health insurance, life insurance and repatriation assistance (& unemployment insurance for EU citizens)
