jobs.title: Liaison and Partnership officer
jobs.description:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a highly qualified **Liaison and Partnership officer**.

## **About the job**

The Liaison and Partnership Officer supports DRC's access, operations, and partnerships across East (and South Libya when needed), under the line management of the Country Director and the technical supervision of the Partnerships Coordinator. This includes helping to build and maintain relationships with local authorities, civil society actors, humanitarian partners, and community leaders to support current and future programming.

The role requires a strong communicator who can navigate administrative systems and foster collaboration to support humanitarian goals, and who supports partner mapping, contract/sub-grant agreement (SGA) tracking, documentation and field follow-up in close coordination with the Partnerships Coordinator.

Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

**1. Liaison and Representation**

- Serve as a focal point with local authorities including ministries and municipalities, and relevant entities in East and South Libya.
- Facilitate approvals, permits, and coordination required for operations, staff movement, and program implementation.
- Represent DRC in relevant coordination meetings and stakeholder forums to promote organizational interests and ensure alignment with local frameworks.
- Monitor and interpret local administrative and context developments that may impact operations.
- Jointly with DRC's partnership unit, liaise with sub-grant partners to ensure the process is clear and all documents are received and updated on the system.
- Demonstrate competencies in drafting official letters in both languages (Arabic and English).

**2. Operational and Program Support**

- Support field teams in obtaining timely approvals for program activities, site access, and logistical facilitation.
- Assist in resolving access challenges, bureaucratic bottlenecks, and operational impediments.
- Coordinate with logistics, security, and program teams to ensure smooth field operations and staff deployments.

**3. Engagement and Entry Point Analysis**

- Identify and assess opportunities for expanding or initiating programming in under-served or priority areas.
- Provide contextual analysis, local dynamics, and potential partners or entry points.
- Support needs assessments, field visits, and donor missions by organizing meetings and access arrangements with local actors.

**4. Partner Mapping, Contract and SGA Tracking**

- Support the mapping and regular updating of information on current and potential partner organizations (national/local NGOs and CSOs) operating in the area of coverage.
- Maintain and update the partnership database/tracker, ensuring partner profiles, capacity information and contact details are accurate and up to date.
- Ensure proper filing and archiving of partnership-related documents (MoUs, agreements, amendments, assessments, correspondence) in line with DRC's document management procedures.
- Maintain an up-to-date tracker of partner agreements/SGAs, including start and end dates, budget lines, deliverables and reporting deadlines.
- Follow up with partners and relevant internal teams on the status of agreement modifications, amendments, no-cost extensions and renewals, flagging any delays to the Partnerships Coordinator.
- Support the collection and compilation of documentation required for partner selection, due diligence and capacity assessment processes.

**5. Field Monitoring and Partner Follow-up**

- Support field visits to partner-implemented activities to follow up on progress against agreed targets and identify implementation challenges.
- Follow up on partners' compliance with agreement commitments and action points arising from monitoring visits, review meetings and audits.
- Document field visit findings and share reports/updates with the Country Director, relevant teams and the Partnerships Coordinator.

**6. Reporting and Documentation**

- Maintain records of key meetings, communications, and agreements with stakeholders.
- Support drafting of MoUs with partners, routing them for review and validation, and following up until finalization.
- Provide regular updates and analysis on access, coordination, and liaison matters to senior management.
- Contribute to reporting requirements for donors, clusters, and internal management as needed.
- Support the collection and follow-up of partner and community feedback related to partnership activities.
- Contribute inputs to internal partnership reports, trackers and dashboards for the Country Director and the Partnerships Coordinator.
- Flag any irregularities, compliance concerns or incidents identified during field visits or partner engagement to the line and technical manager.

**Note:** this job description must remain flexible, to respond to additional tasks or changes as identified by the line and/or technical manager.

## **About you**

To be successful in this role we expect you to have At least 2-3 years of relevant experience in humanitarian or development sectors, with exposure to liaison, coordination, external relations or partnership/grants support functions.

Moreover, we also expect the following:

**Required**

- Strong understanding of the context and humanitarian landscape in East and South Libya.
- Experience engaging with local authorities, community leaders, and civil society actors.
- Experience maintaining trackers/databases and working with Excel or similar tools for data and document tracking.
- Excellent communication, negotiation, cultural sensitivity, and interpersonal skills.
- Willingness to travel frequently and work in dynamic field environments.

**Desirable:**

- Experience working with both government and INGOs and/or UN agencies in a liaison role.
- Prior experience in access negotiation, humanitarian coordination, or partnership/grant support.
- Knowledge of humanitarian principles and operational standards; knowledge of donor compliance basics is an asset.

In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies:

- **Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.
- **Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.
- **Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.
- **Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.
- **Demonstrating integrity:** You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

## **We offer**

- Contract length: Open Ended Contract
- Band: NMH2
- Designation of Duty Station: Benghazi Based (with regular travel to South and West of Libya plus Tunis when needed)
- Suggested Start date: 01 Nov 2026

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of Employment for national employees; please refer to [our website](https://drc.ngo/about-drc/vacancies). For questions regarding the vacancy please contact Us.

## **Application process**

All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV (no longer than four pages) in English. Applications sent by email will not be considered.

**Closing date for applications: 27 October 2026**

For further information about the Danish Refugee Council, please consult our website [drc.ngo](https://drc.ngo/).

jobs.title: ICLA Project Manager CAR Bouar
jobs.description:
**Contexte**

La République centrafricaine continue de faire face à d’importants besoins humanitaires, de protection et de relèvement, résultant de plusieurs années de conflit, de déplacements de populations et d’un accès limité aux services de base. NRC est présent en RCA depuis 2014 et continue de mettre en œuvre ses programmes à travers une présence réduite mais stratégique.

Les principaux secteurs programmatiques qui seront renforcés au cours de la prochaine période comprennent **l’Information, le Conseil et l’Assistance juridique (ICLA), l’Éducation, les Abris et l’Eau, l’Hygiène et l’Assainissement (WASH), ainsi que la Protection contre la violence (PfV)**.

**Le programme ICLA** est au cœur de l’action du NRC en RCA. Il vise à renforcer la protection juridique des personnes déplacées internes, retournées ou affectées par des crises, en facilitant leur accès aux droits liés au Logement, à la Terre et à la Propriété (LTP), à l’identité juridique, tout en soutenant la prévention et la résolution pacifique des conflits fonciers. En RCA, ces enjeux sont particulièrement critiques en raison de la complexité des systèmes fonciers, de la faiblesse des mécanismes de sécurité d’occupation, des risques d’expulsions forcées et du manque de reconnaissance juridique des documents essentiels. Dans ce cadre, NRC joue un rôle de premier plan en tant que Lead au sein du Groupe de travail Logement, Terre et Propriété (LTP), coordonné au sein du nouveau Cluster SLSC. NRC joue également un rôle clé dans le cadre du processus de redynamisation de la plateforme nationale de coordination de l’état civil en RCA.

Dans le contexte de la transition RCA–Cameroun, NRC passera d’un modèle de bureau pays autonome en RCA à une présence opérationnelle intégrée sous la responsabilité du bureau pays du Cameroun. Cette transition représente une adaptation du modèle opérationnel visant à maintenir une présence ciblée, conforme aux exigences de NRC et orientée vers les programmes, tout en améliorant l’efficacité des coûts, la supervision et la durabilité.

Afin de contribuer à répondre aux défis de protection et de garantir la continuité d’une mise en œuvre efficace et de qualité de ses projets, NRC recrute un(e) Responsable de Projet ICLA, en appui aux opérations terrain en RCA et dans la façade Est du Cameroun.

**Ce que nous cherchons**

Le/la Project Manager ICLA est chargé(e) de la mise en œuvre de la stratégique opérationnelle et technique du programme d’Information, Conseil et Assistance Juridique (ICLA) en RCA et dans la façade Est du Cameroun en appui au projet SOLID II si confirmé. Il/elle est responsable de la planification, de la mise en œuvre, du suivi et du reporting des activités ICLA conformément aux standards de qualité, aux lignes directrices de NRC, ainsi qu’aux exigences des bailleurs. En étroite collaboration avec les spécialistes techniques et sous la supervision du Responsable de Programme de zone/Area Programme Manager, il/elle encadre les équipes ICLA sur le terrain, renforce leurs capacités et garantit la pertinence, l’impact et la conformité des interventions. Ses responsabilités couvrent notamment deux des domaines de compétence clés du programme ICLA, à savoir les droits liés au logement, à la terre et à la propriété (LTP), ainsi que l'identité juridique.

**1.Rôles et responsabilités**

1. Assurer la gestion hiérarchique du personnel de projet, y compris le recrutement, et veiller au bon encadrement des équipes.
2. Le processus de gestion de la performance; définir des objectifs clairs alignés sur la stratégie et les priorités de la mission, puis assurer le suivi et l’appui nécessaires pour permettre au personnel d’atteindre ces objectifs.
3. Être responsable des processus clés tels que la planification des effectifs, le recrutement, l’intégration et le développement du personnel, et veiller au respect du devoir de protection (*Duty of Care*) envers son propre personnel.
4. Contribuer à l’élaboration des stratégies pays, de zone et du programme ICLA ; initier et participer au développement des projets pertinents dans le domaine ICLA. 2.
5. Mettre en œuvre les projets ICLA dans les zones concernées, en garantissant une qualité technique élevée, conforme aux stratégies ICLA en RCA et assurant des synergies avec les autres compétences sectorielles.
6. Appuyer la préparation des propositions de projets (aspects techniques, financiers et narratifs) pour les zones d’intervention et le bureau pays.
7. Développer, gérer et suivre les budgets conformément au Manuel financier du NRC et aux exigences des bailleurs, en coordination avec le Responsable de programme de zone et les coordinateurs ICLA.
8. Fournir des rapports d’avancement réguliers au Responsable de programme de zone, au Responsable de zone et au Spécialiste ICLA, en mettant en avant les réussites et les défis opérationnels.
9. Évaluer, revoir et assurer le contrôle qualité des projets ICLA en cours et achevés dans la zone concernée.
10. Veiller à ce que les projets ciblent les bénéficiaires ayant les besoins de protection les plus urgents ; identifier et proposer des approches plus efficaces d’assistance.
11. Renforcer les capacités du personnel du projet et des partenaires et assurer le transfert des compétences clés.
12. Représenter ICLA dans les forums internes et externes; développer des partenariats au sein de la communauté humanitaire dans la zone concernée et coordonner avec les autorités locales.

**2.Compétences**

**Compétences professionnelles**

- Diplôme de Master (BAC+4/5) minimum en sciences sociales, droit ou tout autre domaine pertinent des sciences humaines.
- Minimum de 3 ans d’expérience professionnelle pertinente dans le domaine d’expertise ICLA.
- Solides connaissances techniques du secteur humanitaire.
- Expérience préalable dans des contextes complexes et instables.
- Capacité avérée à travailler de manière autonome dans un environnement multiculturel, multitâche et orienté vers les résultats.
- Expérience dans les programmes d’assistance juridique et/ou de droits humains, avec une bonne compréhension des enjeux de protection et des compétences liées aux responsabilités du poste.
- Expérience dans la gestion d’équipe.
- Maîtrise des applications Microsoft.
- Excellente maîtrise du français, tant à l’oral qu’à l’écrit.
- La connaissance de l’anglais constitue un atout.

***Compétences techniques et expériences spécifiques requises***

- Connaissance du contexte de la RCA, de la dynamique des mouvements et besoins humanitaires en présence le long de la frontière avec le Cameroun (Façade Est)
- Expérience dans les processus de réforme légale en RCA dans le cadre de l’identité juridique et sur le foncier
- Expérience en matière de genre et d’intégration de la dimension genre dans la mise en œuvre des projets.
- Expérience avérée dans les domaines de la protection et du plaidoyer, notamment dans le cadre du programme ICLA ou d’assistance juridique ou d’un programme similaire.
- Solide expérience dans la mise en œuvre de réponses ICLA, tant en contexte volatile que de relèvement.
- Expérience confirmée en gestion des projets liés à l’assistance juridique, aux droits fonciers et à la documentation civile suivant une dimension transfrontalière notamment avec le Cameroun
- Expérience de travail avec des bailleurs de fonds et maîtrise de leurs cadres techniques, priorités stratégiques et exigences en matière de rapports (ex. : ECHO, UE, NORAD, SIDA, etc.).
- Compréhension approfondie des processus de suivi-évaluation (M&E) et capacité à concevoir et adapter des outils pertinents au contexte.
- Expérience dans la production des outils de visibilité et de capitalisation des réalisations du programme
- Expérience dans la conduite d’évaluations multisectorielles et d’analyses contextuelles.
- Aptitude à travailler en étroite collaboration avec les équipes terrain et intersectorielles.
- Excellentes compétences en communication, représentation, flexibilité et négociation.
- Capacité démontrée à transmettre des connaissances à des publics variés, à travers des formations, du mentorat et d’autres méthodes formelles ou informelles.
- Sensibilité aux dynamiques politiques et culturelles.

**Compétences comportementales**

- Capacité à travailler en équipe.
- Aptitude à évoluer dans des environnements sécuritaires instables.
- Réflexion stratégique.
- Capacité à responsabiliser les autres et à instaurer la confiance.
- Proactivité et capacité à initier des changements.
- Esprit d’analyse.

***Profil de leadership***

- Construire des relations solides et significatives
- Agir avec intégrité
- Donner aux équipes les moyens d’agir
- Obtenir des résultats

Veuillez trouver la [JD - ICLA PM CAR Bouar.pdf](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQD1k3mu8bRfSoq1o5kwVXoCAYV-HFIKbnyJLFk31OrV-c8?e=EQ5OUU)

**Ce que nous offrons**

Le Conseil norvégien pour les réfugiés (NRC) est une organisation humanitaire indépendante qui vient en aide aux personnes contraintes de fuir. jobs.title: Watsan Mobile Support Specialist (MSS)
jobs.description:
## **MSF Ubuntu is looking for a Watsan Mobile Support Specialist (MSS)**

*Do your skills and experience not precisely match the requirements? At MSF EA, we strive to create a safe, diverse and inclusive workplace, recognising the need to increase access to professional opportunities for historically underrepresented groups. If you're interested in this position but your experience doesn't align perfectly with the selection criteria, we encourage you to apply anyway. You might be the ideal candidate for this or other positions.*

*Firmly committed to safeguarding patients, community members, staff, and all those in contact with the organisation from all forms of abuse, including sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment (SEAH), we will take all necessary steps, through rigorous vetting processes, to ensure that confirmed perpetrators of abuse do not join the organization.*

*For this position, contact level with patients and children is categorized as **Low** risk and will be monitored with this in regard.*

## ***Introduction***

Médecins Sans Frontières/Doctors Without Borders (MSF) is an international independent medical humanitarian organisation that provides assistance to people affected by conflicts, epidemics, and natural or human-made disasters and excluded from healthcare. We provide this assistance without discrimination, irrespective of race, religion, creed or political affiliation.

## ***About MSF Ubuntu***

**MSF Ubuntu** is the newest Operational Directorate of Médecins Sans Frontières, grounded in the philosophy of Ubuntu – “I am because we are”. With a strong emphasis on interdependence, interoperability, and locally grounded action, MSF Ubuntu aims to strengthen medical humanitarian response by placing communities at the centre of decision-making.

## ***Rationale/Objective for Position***

The Watsan MSS is the technical focal point for Water Supply, Hygiene, Sanitation and Vector Control (WHS and VC) within the Med-Ops Cell. S/he provides 1st and 2nd line (remote and/or in person) technical support to MSF Ubuntu country programs within their Med-Ops Cell, covering both operational implementation of activities and the strategic definition of Watsan approaches and priorities across the portfolio, in line with the Logistics & Watsan Strategy.

The role supports country programme staff in the design, planning, implementation and review of Watsan interventions, ensuring that programme proposals are technically sound, context-appropriate, and aligned with MSF protocols, standards and procedures, the MSF Ubuntu Strategic Plan, including Med-Ops programming priorities, and the Logistics & Watsan Strategy 2026–2028.

The Watsan MSS contributes to capacity building of country programme staff through the application and transfer of technical know-how, to strengthen programme quality, support country programs in optimal working conditions and maximize the impact of MSF Ubuntu's projects.

This position will be ***hierarchically*** accountable to the ***Cell Logistics & Supply Advisor*** and ***functionally*** accountable to the **Watsan Technical Coordinator** and **Deputy Med-Ops Cell Manager (Med)** – joint functional line.

## ***Tasks & Responsibilities***

- Following up the Watsan activities in her/his portfolio countries within the Med-Ops cell.
- Reporting systematically on progress in implementing the MSF Ubuntu Logistics & Watsan Strategy 2026–2028, the application of related policies and performance against Watsan KPIs, to inform strategic and operational decisions.
- Ensuring understanding and alignment of the Watsan interventions with MSF Ubuntu priorities and standards, as per MSF Ubuntu’s Strategic Plan, including the “Logistics/Watsan Basics” minimum standard.
- Supporting and guiding the definition and the revision of the Watsan strategy for the country programs, in line with the MSF Ubuntu Logistics & Watsan Strategy 2026–2028 and medical priorities and advising on current and future medical and logistics operations when pertinent.
- Carrying out a functional evaluation of the Watsan set-up, assessing the applicable technical installations, systems, structures, equipment and HR set-up, the compliance with procedures, policies and guidelines, within the framework of MSF standards to identify the main areas for improvement.
- Assessing and validating local suppliers and local (sub-)contractors for quality of materials, systems, installations, parts etc. to ensure compliance with MSF quality standards.
- Developing and initiating the implementation of the improvement plan based on the recommendations arising from the functional evaluation.
- Assisting the logistics team with the design and installation of new (complex) systems and/or with the implementation of (new) protocols, tools etc.
- Monitoring and supervising established and ongoing work, systems and installations in the field of expertise and providing technical advice and solutions when necessary.
- Assisting the logistics team in their HR tasks such as recruitment & selection of technical staff, briefing and debriefing of focal persons and logisticians.
- Identifying training needs and contributing to the definition of training content for WHS and VC.
- Facilitating team training and providing on-the-job training on technical basics related to area of specialization according to MSF standards to enable effective implementation of relevant methodologies, systems and tools and ensure best practice is delivered.
- Upon request of the Watsan Technical Coordinator and in coordination with the Cell Logistics & Supply Advisor and Deputy Med-Ops Cell Manager, develop new policies, tools, protocols and SOPs related to his/her area of expertise (with a local, regional or even global approach).
- Drafting reports and action plans following field visits to capture experiences and “lessons learnt”.
- Contributing to the research and development of programme tools, practices, guidelines and policies based on insights gained in the job.
- Proposing and testing/piloting innovative solutions to overcome recurrent problems and technical challenges.
- Developing and maintaining knowledge of practices and approaches within the area of expertise and sharing this knowledge with others to enhance operational effectiveness.
- Carrying out field visits to the portfolio countries as needed or requested by the programme teams.
- Close collaboration with the IPC MIO advisor in relevant areas related to WASH and IPC, in line with MSF policies and standards.
- Participating in the Med-Ops Cell Health Programme Support Team (HSTP) meetings on a regular basis, ensuring a strong link and collaboration between medical and logistics strategies and priorities.
- Supporting emergency/outbreak WASH response primarily within their Med-Ops Cell portfolio; extending support to other Cells only upon request from the Head of Logistics or activation of the MSF Ubuntu Emergency Response Strategy.
- Ensuring WASH facilities and services are designed for privacy, gender-appropriateness, accessibility and safe usage, and are aligned with MSF Ubuntu's safeguarding and community-accountability approach .
- Mapping and engaging local WASH actors — public, community-based and private — in the portfolio, and contributing to targeted WASH partnerships for operational delivery where these strengthen or complement existing local systems .
- Acting as the Med-Ops Cell focal point and technical reference for Watsan, ensuring coherent, timely and context-appropriate technical guidance to country programmes across the portfolio.
- Reviewing and advising on country programme proposals, intervention designs and operational plans related to Watsan, to ensure technical quality, feasibility, relevance and alignment with MSF Ubuntu priorities, standards and strategies.
- Contributing to strategic discussions and decision-making within the Med-Ops Cell on Watsan priorities, approaches and operational orientations for the portfolio countries.

## ***Qualifications***

**Education**

- Essential: Degree in civil engineering, environmental sciences, environmental health, public health engineering, or a closely related technical discipline.
- Desirable: Postgraduate qualification in water and sanitation, public health, or humanitarian studies.
- Essential: Sphere Watsan standards; water treatment and quality testing; excreta and wastewater management; healthcare waste management; community Watsan methodologies; vector control principles.
- Desirable: MSF Watsan protocols and tools; GIS and EPANET.

**Experience**

- Essential: Minimum 2 years of NGO Watsan field experience; community and HCF Watsan, outbreak response; adult training facilitation; ability to work in remote and insecure settings.
- Desirable: MSF Watsan experience; EASTEN and southern Africa Experience in Watsan interventions or infrastructure design in climate-vulnerable or climate-affected contexts.

**Languages**

- Essential: English (fluent written and spoken).
- Desirable: French.

**Competencies**

- Commitment to MSF Principles
- Results and Quality Orientation
- Teamwork and Collaboration
- Flexibility
- Intercultural Sensitivity

***Conditions and Benefits:***

- The role requires regular travel to countries of operation and MSF Ubuntu hubs.
- Travel at short notice may be required during emergencies, assessments or critical incidents.
- The post-holder may be required to work extended or irregular hours during crises.
- The role requires high levels of discretion, resilience, political judgement and emotional intelligence.
- The position will operate in a growing Operational Directorate and will require adaptability as MSF Ubuntu’s structures, systems and portfolio evolve.
- **Job Location**: This position will be based in one of the countries within its portfolio (to be confirmed). For the initial two years, the duty station is expected to be in Harare (Zimbabwe), Johannesburg (South Africa), or Nairobi (Kenya). After two years, the successful candidate accepts flexibility to move to the final duty station, that is still to be confirmed.
- **Contract**: 1 year (renewable) full-time contract.
- **Start date**: As Soon As Possible.
- **Annual Salary and other benefits**: In line with MSF reward policy, Subjected to local conditions.

**If based in Nairobi, the benefits below shall apply:**

- **Salary:** An annual salary of **EUR 27,145 at HQ Grade 8** based on a full-time appointment with an annual increment of 2% every year up to a maximum of 10 years.
- **Work-life balance financial benefit;** ranging between **EUR 620 to 1,159/month** based on individual & administrative status. This amount may be used to cover accommodation and utilities, transportation, etc.
- **Other benefits include;**
- **Annual Leave:** 25 days of annual leave per year.
- **Other Holidays:** sick leave, circumstantial leave, maternity leave (21 weeks), paternity leave (4 weeks), own affairs days off, etc.
- **Employer Pension contribution**: 10% of basic salary:
- **International insurance** for both medical and disability**.**
- **Relocation support**; based on MSF EA terms/conditions.
- **Work-life balance**: Daily flexi-hours and 2 days working from home possible.
- **School fees benefits**: for eligible dependents, based on individual & administrative status.
- **Diverse team composition**; Collaborate with a global network of talented professionals, bringing diverse perspectives and expertise from around the world.
- **Career Development**: MSF provides many learning resources (online learning resources, regular trainings – including language, Peer to peer learning.
- **Mobility**: You will have opportunities to travel abroad for work, meetings, trainings and workshops; giving you a chance to experience different cultures and broaden your professional network.
- **Annual home leave ticket**: To be taken once every year for both staff and eligible dependents back to their home country for vacation. Only applicable to non-Kenyans and based on individual & administrative status.

**If based in Johannesburg, the benefits below shall apply:**

- **Salary:** An annual salary of **ZAR 520,889 at HQ Grade 7 based** on a full-time appointment with an annual increment of 2% every year up to a maximum of 10 years.
- 13th Cheque in November.
- 100% Medical aid contribution.
- 10% additional pension allowance.
- Transport allowance.
- Cell Phone Allowance.
- Work-life balance: Daily flexi-hours and 2 days working from home possible.
- Diverse team composition; Collaborate with a global network of talented
professionals, bringing diverse perspectives and expertise from around the world
- Resources needed such as working space, computer, internet, stationery, and other resources will be made available.

Field Office Manager CAR Paoua - Internal Applicants Only
jobs.description:
**Contexte**

La République Centrafricaine continue de faire face à d’importants besoins humanitaires, de protection et de relèvement, résultant de plusieurs années de conflit, de déplacements de populations et d’un accès limité aux services de base. NRC est présent en RCA depuis 2014 et continue de mettre en œuvre ses programmes à travers une présence réduite mais stratégique.

Les principaux secteurs programmatiques qui seront renforcés au cours de la prochaine période comprennent **l’Information, le Conseil et l’Assistance juridique (ICLA), l’Éducation, les Abris et l’Eau, l’Hygiène et l’Assainissement (WASH), ainsi que la Protection contre la violence (PfV)**.

Dans le contexte de la transition RCA–Cameroun, NRC passera d’un modèle de bureau pays autonome en RCA à une présence opérationnelle intégrée sous la responsabilité du bureau pays du Cameroun. Cette transition représente une adaptation du modèle opérationnel visant à maintenir une présence ciblée, conforme aux exigences de NRC et orientée vers les programmes, tout en améliorant l’efficacité des coûts, la supervision et la durabilité.

Pour atteindre ses objectifs pays, le NRC est à la recherche d'un/une Field Manager doté de solides compétences en gestion des Programmes/projets, un gestionnaire dynamique et engagé avec une vision de travail axée sur les résultats et ayant une solide compréhension du contexte Centrafricain et du paysage des bailleurs de fonds.

**Ce que nous cherchons**

Pour atteindre ses objectifs pays, le NRC est à la recherche d'un/une Field Manager doté de solides compétences en gestion des Programmes/projets, un gestionnaire dynamique et engagé avec une vision de travail axée sur les résultats et ayant une solide compréhension du contexte Centrafricain et du paysage des bailleurs de fonds.

**1.Rôles et responsabilités**

1. Responsabilités de gestion hiérarchique vis-à-vis des collaborateurs qui lui rendent directement compte. Cela comprend :

- Le processus de gestion des performances : définir des objectifs clairs, alignés sur la stratégie et les priorités nationales, et assurer le suivi et l’accompagnement des collaborateurs dans la réalisation de ces objectifs.
- La responsabilité des processus clés tels que la planification des effectifs, le recrutement, l’intégration et le développement du personnel, ainsi que la garantie du devoir de diligence envers ses propres collaborateurs

1. Fournir des analyses et des contributions spécifiques au terrain concernant les stratégies de l’Area Office.

3\. Assurer et maintenir une communication, une coordination et une collaboration efficaces avec les principales parties prenantes externes sur le terrain, notamment les communautés, les autorités locales et les acteurs humanitaires.

4\. Représenter le NRC dans toute interaction avec les parties prenantes externes sur le terrain, conformément aux pouvoirs délégués par le responsable régional.

5\. Assurer une coordination et une circulation de l’information efficaces entre les équipes de programme et de soutien au sein du bureau de terrain et avec le bureau régional.

6\. Être responsable des ressources du bureau de terrain, y compris les responsabilités de gestionnaire budgétaire pour les lignes budgétaires du bureau de terrain (programme et soutien), les achats et la gestion des actifs.

7\. Veiller à la mise en œuvre rapide, efficace et de qualité des opérations sur le terrain, conformément aux politiques et procédures de la NRC.

8\. Diriger la gestion de la sécurité au sein du bureau de terrain, y compris les négociations d’accès, les évaluations des risques et la mise en œuvre des procédures d’accès humanitaire et de sécurité.

9\. Veiller à la mise en œuvre effective du devoir de diligence de la NRC et des mécanismes de responsabilité envers le personnel et les populations touchées sur le terrain.

10\. Veiller au respect et à l’application des politiques, des directives et des procédures de la NRC.

**2.Compétences**

**Compétences professionnelles**

- Minimum niveau Master (Bac +4) en sciences sociales, gestion des projets ou tout autre domaine pertinent
- Expérience d'au moins deux ans dans le leadership humanitaire et la gestion des opérations, notamment dans des contextes de conflit et de post-conflit en Afrique.
- Expérience en matière de supervision de la mise en œuvre de programmes humanitaires multisectoriels et intégrés, de solutions durables et de programmes d'intervention d'urgence.
- Expérience en matière de leadership d'équipe et de développement des capacités
- Connaissance de ses propres compétences/profil de leadership
- Maîtrise du français, à l'écrit comme à l'oral
- Capacité à converser/communiquer en anglais
- Maîtrise des outils informatiques, notamment de Microsoft Office, et plus particulièrement de Word, Excel, PowerPoint et Outlook.

***Compétences techniques et expériences spécifiques requises***

- Expérience en matière de gestion des fonctions de soutien et des programmes humanitaires dans des contextes instables.
- Expérience en matière d'établissement de relations et de coordination avec les autorités gouvernementales et les chefs traditionnels.
- Expérience en matière de pilotage de programmes de gestion du changement dans le domaine humanitaire.

**Compétences comportementales**

- Capacité à travailler en équipe.
- Aptitude à évoluer dans des environnements sécuritaires instables.
- Réflexion stratégique.
- Capacité à responsabiliser les autres et à instaurer la confiance.
- Proactivité et capacité à initier des changements.
- Esprit d’analyse.

***Profil de leadership***

- Construire des relations solides et significatives
- Agir avec intégrité
- Donner aux équipes les moyens d’agir
- Obtenir des résultats

jobs.title: Chief of Party – ‘Catalyst Fund’ for Locally Led Humanitarian Response & Solutions
jobs.description:
**What we’re looking for:**

NRC is seeking an experienced **Chief of Party to lead the ‘Catalyst Fund’ for Locally Led Humanitarian Response & Solutions,** an ambitious new initiative transforming how humanitarian assistance is financed and delivered.

You will provide strategic leadership across countries, partners and workstreams, driving programme delivery, locally led partnerships, learning and humanitarian systems change. The Fund aims to strengthen local leadership in neglected displacement crises, initially in Africa, by combining rapid, flexible emergency response with locally led recovery, protection and sustainable pathways to solutions.

Beyond immediate impact, you will help shape a scalable model that strengthens local systems, promotes self-reliance, and influences wider humanitarian financing, policy and practice. The role is expected to begin with a six-month inception phase to establish the Fund’s operational model, partnerships, governance and learning systems, subject to final approval.

The ideal candidate must have a strong understanding of NRC’s internal systems, processes, and operational context.

**What you will do:**

**Strategy**

- Set the strategic direction of the Fund and ensure the effective functioning of its activation, assurance and accompaniment arrangements across all levels of governance and implementation.
- Working closely with the donor(s) and the Fund's governing bodies, develop and implement the Fund's multi-year strategy, including its results matrix, control measures and key performance indicators.
- Accountable for robust risk mapping of Fund activities and implementation of appropriate risk mitigation measures.
- Responsible for monitoring and reporting on progress against strategic objectives and KPIs to NRC leadership, donors, and the Fund's governing bodies.
- Co-responsible (with NRC Management and the donor) for identifying and developing additional funding opportunities and co-donor partnerships to grow the Fund.
- Responsible for the Fund's transition/continuity planning, including succession from the inception-phase support arrangements.

**Fund Management Team**

- Ensure the Fund has the appropriate capacity and expertise required for effective delivery, and lead/support the recruitment of dedicated Fund positions.
- Provide strategic and functional leadership to staff and functions supporting the Fund, through line management, and/or functional relationships, as appropriate to the final organisational set-up.
- Establish effective working relationships with relevant NRC functions and teams, including the Emergency Response, Operational Support and Governance, and Global Programme Sections, ensuring coherent and timely support to the Fund across programme, grants, partnerships, finance, MEAL, learning, communications, policy and advocacy, and other relevant functions.
- Maintain effective coordination with external or shared functions supporting the Fund, including the ICVA Local Coordination Adviser, as relevant.
- Budget holder for the Fund, managing its budget, assets and resources.
- Responsible for the review and submission of quality donor reports (programmatic and financial), evaluations, audits, and partner agreements/awards.
- Ensure Fund functions (grants, finance, MEAL, communications, learning) provide effective and timely support to country teams and partners.
- Ensure effective risk management, compliance and mitigation across the Fund Facility.
- Accountable for the Fund's legal and regulatory compliance, including donor agreements and relations with the donor.

**Governance**

- Convene and service the Fund's governing bodies (Steering Committee/Board), ensuring agreed courses of action are implemented, reported on and monitored.
- Responsible for presenting the Fund's roll-out and delivery to the Steering Committee/Board and participate in board discussions as the Fund's representative.

**Delivery**

- Review and sign off on Fund activations and awards, ensuring adherence to the Fund's proportionate due diligence and assurance model.
- Responsible for ensuring high-quality implementation of Fund-supported responses, and accountable for control measures for monitoring delivery, in coordination with the roving staff deployed and country-level structures.
- Ensure close coordination with Country Office management teams in the delivery of the response.
- Ensure that NRC policies on safeguarding, Safe and Inclusive Programming and community engagement, and equitable partnerships are upheld in the delivery of the response
- Ensure effective coordination with relevant NRC technical and thematic functions, drawing on their expertise and quality assurance to support delivery of the Fund's humanitarian response, localisation and solutions objectives.

**Representation, Learning and System Change**

Setting and Reporting The United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat) is mandated by the UN General Assembly to promote socially and environmentally sustainable towns and cities. UN-Habitat is the focal point for all urbanization and human settlement matters within the UN system. UN-Habitat works with partners to build inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable cities and communities. UN-Habitat promotes urbanization as a positive transformative force for people and communities, reducing inequality, discrimination and poverty. This position is located in the Regional Office for Latin America and the Caribbean (ROLAC), Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. The incumbent will report to the Regional Director for Latin America and the Caribbean and work closely with programme divisions, branches and units at Headquarters and across the region. Within delegated authority, the Programme Management Officer, Human Settlements will be responsible for the following duties: Responsibilities • Provide normative and technical leadership on adequate housing, sustainable urbanization and implementation of the New Urban Agenda across countries in Latin America and the Caribbean. • Promote the integration of adequate housing, basic services and informal settlements thematics into national policies in the region. • Support the Secretariat of UN-Habitat to MINURVI (Forum of Ministers and High-Level Authorities on Housing and Urban Development in Latin America and the Caribbean). • Lead regional/subregional portfolio development and implementation, with particular focus in the anglophone Caribbean subregion. • Lead Programme development and preparation of proposals for global vertical funds. • Supports connection of focus areas of UN-Habitat Strategic Plan with ROLAC strategic priorities. • Supports and advises development, implementation and evaluations to programmes/projects, in the subregion; supports monitoring and analysis of programme/project development and implementation; supports reviews of relevant documents and reports; identifies problems and issues to be addressed and initiates corrective actions; liaises with relevant parties; ensures follow-up actions. • Fosters partnerships and collaboration with donors and other international agencies to mobilize resources for projects and programmes on adequate housing and sustainable urbanization in assigned subregion. • Performs consulting assignments, in collaboration with the clients and counterparts, by planning facilitating workshops, through other interactive sessions and assisting in developing the action plan the client will use to manage the change. • Provides technical and management advisory on human settlements analysis, needs assessments and other activities, participating in advisory missions to carry out high level consultations and other activities aimed at development of human settlements policies, strategies and programmes. • Researches, analyzes and presents information gathered from diverse sources. • Coordinates policy development, including the review and analysis of issues and trends, preparation of evaluations or other research activities and studies, • Generates survey initiatives; designs data collection tools; reviews, analyzes and interprets responses, identify problems/issues and prepares conclusions. • Organizes and prepares written outputs, e.g. draft background papers, analysis, sections of reports and studies, inputs to publications, etc. • Provides capacity development support through documentation of knowledge management, tool development and facilitating networking with partners and programmes contributing to the enhancement of the policy dialogues at UN-Habitat and globally. • Provides substantive backstopping to consultative and other meetings, conferences, etc., to include proposing agenda topics, identifying participants, preparation of documents and presentations, etc. • Initiates and coordinates outreach activities; COMMUNICATION: Speaks and writes clearly and effectively; listens to others, correctly interprets messages from others and responds appropriately; asks questions to clarify, and exhibits interest in having two-way communication; tailors language, tone, style and format to match audience; demonstrates openness in sharing information and keeping people informed. CREATIVITY: Actively seeks to improve programmes or services; offers new and different options to solve problems or meet client needs; promotes and persuades others to consider new ideas; takes calculated risks on new and unusual ideas; thinks “outside the box”; takes an interest in new ideas and new ways of doing things; is not bound by current thinking or traditional approaches. Education Advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in Architecture, Civil Engineering Urban or Regional Planning, Political Science, Economics or a related field is required. A first-level university degree in combination with two (2) additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. Successful completion of both degree and non-degree programs in data analytics, business analytics or data science programs is desirable. Job - Specific Qualification Not available. Work Experience A minimum of seven (7) years of progressively responsible experience in adequate housing, human settlements (urban planning and management, human development initiatives, housing and slum upgrading, land and urban infrastructure) is required. A minimum of four (4) years of experience at the international level in stakeholder driven strategic planning and implementation processes is required. Experience working on governance, planning or policy related issues in the area of human settlements is required. Experience in planning, including strategic planning, and overseeing the implementation of the plans is desirable. Two (2) years or more of experience in data analytics or related area is desirable. Setting and Reporting The United Nations General Assembly resolution 71/251 established the Technology Bank for the Least Developed Countries and adopted its Charter on 23 December 2016. The objectives of the Technology Bank are : a. To strengthen the science, technology and innovation capacity of least developed countries, including the capacity to identify, absorb, develop, integrate and scale up the deployment of technologies and innovations, including indigenous ones, as well as the capacity to address and manage intellectual property rights issues; b. To promote the development and implementation of national and regional science, technology and innovation strategies; c. To strengthen partnerships among science, technology and innovation-related public entities and with the private sector; d. To promote cooperation among all stakeholders involved in science, technology and innovation, including researchers, research institutions and public and private sector entities, within and between least developed countries, as well as with their counterparts in other countries; e. To promote and facilitate the identification and utilization of and access to appropriate technologies by the least developed countries, as well as their transfer to the least developed countries, while respecting intellectual property rights and fostering the national and regional capacity of the least developed countries for the effective utilization of technology in order to bring about transformative change. The Technology Bank’s work is guided by the Strategic Plan 2025–2027, which sets out three core verticals of engagement: i) High-Impact Policy and Technical Advisory Services; ii) Capacity Building for Transformation; iii) Knowledge Services for Results. This position is located in the Programme Unit of the Technology Bank for the Least Developed Countries, Gebze, Türkiye. The Associate Programme Officer reports to Economic Affairs Officer, P-4. reviews relevant documents and reports; assists in anticipating implementation risks, identifying problems and issues to be addressed, proactively identifying practical solutions and recommending corrective actions; liaises with relevant parties; identifies and tracks follow-up actions. • Promotes adaptive management by continuously assessing project/programme performance and recommending improvements based on evidence and lessons learned; assists with design of data collection tools; issues data collection tools, reviews, analyzes and interprets responses, identifies problems/issues and prepares preliminary conclusions. • Assist in providing substantive support for policy coordination and evaluation functions, including the review and analysis of emerging issues and trends, participation in evaluations or research activities and studies. • Contributes to the identification, design and formulation of national, regional and multi-country projects aligned with the strategic plan of the Technology Bank and its mandate to strengthen technology transfer, innovation ecosystems, digital transformation and STI capacities in least developed countries, including the preparation of concept notes, project documents, and resource mobilization materials. • Supports the assessment and selection of partner organization; oversees project/programme implementation by grant recipients, ensuring compliance with contractual obligations and programme objectives. • Assists in preparing donor reports, funding proposals, briefings and resource mobilization materials under guidance of the supervisor. • Supports procurement and contracting processes related to programme implementation, including the preparation of terms of reference, technical specifications, evaluation inputs and contract management documentation, in accordance with applicable rules and procedures. • Assists in monitoring project/programme expenditures against approved budgets and work plans, ensuring efficient use of resources. Coordinates activities related to budget funding (programme/project preparation and submissions, progress reports, financial statements, etc.) and preparation of related documents/reports (pledging, work programme, programme budget, etc.). • Assists in performing consulting assignments, in collaboration with the client, by planning facilitating workshops, through other interactive sessions and assisting in developing the action plan the client will use to manage the change. • Assists in providing administrative and substantive support to consultative and other meetings, conferences, etc., to include proposing agenda topics, identifying and proposed participants, preparation of background documents and presentations, handling logistics, etc. • Carries out basic research on selected aspects of programmes, operations and other activities, etc., to include collecting, analyzing and presenting statistical data and other information gathered from diverse sources. • Contributes to the collection and analysis of data as well as identification of trends or patterns and provide draft insights through graphs, charts, tables and reports using data visualization methods for data-driven planning, decision-making, presentation and reporting. • Contributes to the preparation of various written outputs, e.g. draft background papers, analytical notes, sections of reports and studies, inputs to publications, etc • Contributes to knowledge management activities, including the documentation, dissemination and exchange of good practices, success stories, innovations and lessons learned to support programme scaling, replication and organizational learning. • Contributes to undertaking outreach activities; participates in the development of training workshops, seminars, etc.; participates in and makes presentations on assigned topics/activities. • Supports the production of promotional materials. • Performs other duties as required. Competencies • Professionalism: Knowledge and understanding of programme and project management concepts, approaches and methodologies, particularly in the areas of science, technology and innovation. Ability to support the planning, implementation, monitoring and reporting of development projects and programmes, including the application of results-based management principles. Ability to identify programme implementation issues, analyze and participate in the resolution of issues/problems. Ability to assist with data collection, analysis and interpretation. Ability to conduct independent research and analysis, including familiarity with and experience in the use of various research sources, including electronic sources on the internet, intranet and other databases. Ability to apply judgment in the context of assignments given, plan own work and manage conflicting priorities. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. • Planning& Organizing: Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies; identifies priority activities and assignments; adjusts priorities as required; allocates appropriate amount of time and resources for completing work; foresees risks and allows for contingencies when planning; monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary; uses time efficiently. • Client Orientation: Considers all those to whom services are provided to be “clients” and seeks to see things from clients’ point of view; establishes and maintains productive partnerships with clients by gaining their trust and respect; identifies clients’ needs and matches them to appropriate solutions; monitors ongoing developments inside and outside the clients’ environment to keep informed and anticipate problems; keeps clients informed of progress or setbacks in projects; meets timeline for delivery of products or services to client. Job - Specific Qualification Professional certification in project management (PMP, PRINCE2, or equivalent) or programme management is desirable. Work Experience A minimum of two years of progressively responsible international experience in project/programme management, project implementation or related area is required. Experience applying results-based management approaches is desirable. Experience working in the UN common system or similar international organization is desirable. Budget: A. Budget Preparation: •Provides support to managers with respect to the elaboration of resource requirements for budget submissions using the RBB framework •Reviews and analyze data with respect to the finalization of UNOCA cost estimates and budget proposals, in terms of staff and non-staff requirements, including programmatic aspects •Reviews, analyses and provides input into finalization of programme budget/financial implications to the Security Council statements in light of additional mandates. •Provides substantive support to relevant intergovernmental and expert bodies in their budget review; assists in securing approval from the General Assembly B. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. •Communication: Speaks and writes clearly and effectively; listens to others, correctly interprets messages from others and responds appropriately; asks questions to clarify, and exhibits interest in having two-way communication; tailors language, tone, style and format to match audience; demonstrates openness in sharing information and keeping people informed. •Planning& Organizing: Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies; identifies priority activities and assignments: adjusts priorities as required; allocates appropriate amount of time and resources for completing work; foresees risks and allows for contingencies when planning; monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary; uses time efficiently. •Accountability: Takes ownership of all responsibilities and honours commitments; delivers outputs for which one has responsibility within prescribed time, cost and quality standards; operates in compliance with organizational regulations and rules; supports subordinates, provides oversight and takes responsibility for delegated assignments; takes personal responsibility for his/her own shortcomings and those of the work unit, where applicable. •Client Orientation: Considers all those to whom services are provided to be "clients" and seeks to see things from clients' point of view; establishes and maintains productive partnerships with clients by gaining their trust and respect; identifies clients' needs and matches them to appropriate solutions; monitors ongoing developments inside and outside the clients' environment to keep informed and anticipate problems; keeps clients informed of progress or setbacks in projects; meets timeline for delivery of products or services to client. A first-level degree (Bachelor’s degree or equivalent) in the specified fields of studies with two additional years of relevant work experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. jobs.description: Org. Setting and Reporting This position is located in the United Nations Regional Office for Central Africa (UNOCA) in Libreville, Gabon. The Political Affairs Officer will work in the Reporting and Analysis Pillar of the Political Affairs Section and report through the Senior Political Affairs Officer to the Chief, Political Affairs Service. UNOCA covers Angola, Burundi, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Chad, Republic of the Congo, Democratic Republic of Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Rwanda and Sao Tome and Principe and works closely with the Economic Community of Central African States and other sub-regional organisations. Responsibilities Within delegated authority, the Political Affairs Officer will be responsible for the following duties: - Gathers, selects and analyses information contained in communications and publications received from different sources, in order to keep the leadership of UNOCA regularly informed of peace and security developments and trends in the sub region. - Carries out regular in-depth research on emerging or persisting peace and security challenges facing the Central Africa region or the countries under the purview of UNOCA and recommends options for good offices and other UN actions. - Monitors national and regional level political developments and provides advice to Headquarter and field mission/UN agencies active on the ground, through the preparation of regional, country-specific and thematic reports including, but not limited to weekly situation reports, briefing notes, analytical notes, options papers, code cables and reports of the Secretary-General to the Security Council, General Assembly or other bodies. - Compiles background notes and talking points for the SRSG’s engagements and that of the Chief, Political Affairs Section. - Supports the Chief, Political Affairs Service, in the overall coordination of the Section, especially in following up on the substantive issues requiring his attention/action. - Support activities organized by UNOCA in the framework of its partnership with ECCAS, the provision of secretariat services to the United Nations Standing Advisory Committee on Security Questions in Central Africa (UNSAC) or other activities to enhance the capacity of subregional actors in the field of prevention. - Maintains up-to-date knowledge of events relating to political issues, in general, and in particular as they affect the countries under the purview of UNOCA and thematic areas pertaining to the mandate of the Office. - Maintains contacts with other sectors of the UN, other international organizations and governments on coordination and policy matters. - Monitors actions taken by intergovernmental groups, UN organizations, government and non-governmental organizations. - Participates in fact-finding and other missions to countries within assigned area of responsibility. - Prepares meetings of visiting senior UN officials in the subregion or with officials from countries under the purview of UNOCA. - Performs other related duties as required. Competencies Professionalism: Demonstrates professional competence and in depth knowledge of political affairs; Strong analytical skills, and experience in information collection and management; excellent drafting and editing skills with the proven ability to complete in-depth studies and reach conclusions on possible causes and solutions to political problems in specific areas and/or countries; Shows pride in work and in achievements; Is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; Is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; Shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations; Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. Communication: Speaks and writes clearly and effectively; Listens to others, correctly interprets messages from others and responds appropriately; Asks questions to clarify, and exhibits interest in having two-way communication; Tailors language, tone, style and format to match the audience; Demonstrates openness in sharing information and keeping people informed. Teamwork: Works collaboratively with colleagues to achieve organizational goals; solicits input by genuinely valuing others' ideas and expertise; is willing to learn from others; places team agenda before personal agenda. Planning and Organizing: Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies; Identifies priority activities and assignments and adjusts priorities as required; Allocates appropriate amount of time and resources for completing work; Foresees risks and allows for contingencies when planning; Monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary; Uses time efficiently. Education An advanced university degree (Master’s or Doctorate degree, or equivalent) in political sciences or related fields is required. A first-level degree (Bachelor’s degree or equivalent) in the specified fields of studies with two additional years of relevant work experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. Job - Specific Qualification Not available. Work Experience A minimum of five years of progressively responsible experience in political science, international relations, law, disarmament, security, development management, conflict resolution or related area is required. Experience working in Africa on peace and security issues is required. Experience in conducting research and analyses on political or peace and security issues in Africa is required. Experience in front office is desirable. Experience on partnerships with regional or sub-regional organisations is desirable. Experience working in and/or on Central Africa is desirable. Languages English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this job opening, English and French are required. The table below shows the minimum required level for each skill in these languages, according to the UN Language Framework (please consult https://languages.un.org for details). Required Languages Language Reading Writing Listening Speaking English UN Level II UN Level II UN Level II UN Level II French UN Level II UN Level II UN Level II UN Level II Assessment Evaluation of qualified candidates may include an assessment exercise which may be followed by competency-based interview. jobs.title: DATA AND BEHAVIORAL SCIENTIST, P3
jobs.description: Org. Setting and Reporting This position is located in the CEB Secretariat, reporting to the Senior Inter-Agency Human Resources Advisor. The focus of the position is twofold: The first focus is to identify, structure and underpin data-and analytics-driven solutions in all areas of Inter-Agency Human Resources matters ranging from demographics and cost-related topics to behavioral aspects. A strong conceptual and scientific foundation is expected to underpin such solutions, in order to ensure objectivity and credibility of the proposed solutions. The second focus is to generate and communicate Human Resources-related data-driven analyses and insights in support of decision-making processes, by looking at historical trends, current data and predictions. Responsibilities Within delegated authority, the Data and Behavioral Scientist will be responsible for the following duties: • Works with stakeholders across the CEB organizations to identify opportunities for leveraging data to drive business solutions. • Develops and implements databases, data collection systems, data analytics and other strategies to optimize statistical efficiency and quality including automation scripts and internal software. • Applies causal inference and experimental methods such as randomized controlled trials, quasi-experimental designs, and causal modeling of observational data to estimate the impact of system-wide policies and inform evidence-based decisions. • Collects, mines, scrapes and analyzes data including those shared by organizations shared by organizations to drive optimization and improvement of inter-agency coordination in behavioral sciences, human resources, organizational management and compensation. • Assesses and tests the effectiveness and accuracy of new datasets and data processing procedures. • Develops custom predictive algorithms to apply to data sets. • Coordinates with different functional teams in CEB organizations to implement models and monitor outcomes • Performs other duties as assigned. Competencies Professionalism: Knowledge of the data analysis life cycle from ingest and wrangling to analysis and visualization to present findings. Excellent knowledge of statistical and computational methods, such as clustering, classification, correlation, dimension reduction, forecasting, machine learning, detecting outliers, and regression. Takes pride in the work for the organization and understands the impact that can be brought into the organization by allowing data-driven and evidence-based decisions. Ability to apply judgment in the context of assignments given, plan own work and manage conflicting priorities. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. Planning& Organizing: Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies; identifies priority activities and assignments; adjusts priorities as required; allocates appropriate amount of time and resources for completing work; foresees risks and allows for contingencies when planning; monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary; uses time efficiently. Accountability: Takes ownership of all responsibilities and honours commitments. Delivers outputs for which one has responsibility within prescribed time, cost and quality standards. Operates in compliance with organizational regulations and rules. Supports subordinates, provides oversight and takes responsibility for delegated assignments. Takes personal responsibility for his/her own shortcomings and those of the work unit, where applicable. A first-level university degree in combination with two additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. Job - Specific Qualification Not available. Work Experience A minimum of five years of progressively responsible experience in data science, data analytics, applied mathematics, information management or related area is required. Experience in combining data analytics and behavioral science (such as organizational psychology or behavioral economics) is required. Experience with data science and statistics-related programming languages such as R and Python, with SQL and relational database design and management is required. Experience with data governance, data quality, or data privacy and security practices is desirable. Experience with JavaScript and web frameworks, version control tools such as Git, containerization tools such as Docker and with API development and data integration are desirable. A first-level university degree in combination with qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. Job - Specific Qualification Not available. Work Experience A minimum of seven years of progressively responsible experience in public information, journalism, international relations, public administration or related area is required. Experience in providing media advice to an intergovernmental or expert body is desirable. Experience in or on the region is desirable. Ensure effective management and coordination of multidisciplinary teams, international and national personnel, contractors, and service providers to achieve organizational objectives. 3. Oversee the development and implementation of strategic work plans, technical standards, performance indicators, and resource allocation strategies in alignment with organizational priorities. 4. Ensure effective governance and control of project scope, budgets, schedules, quality, risks, and contractual obligations, promoting accountability and value for money. 5. Provide high-level technical advice and recommendations to senior management on infrastructure development, asset management, operational challenges, risk mitigation, and resource optimization. 6. Strengthen performance management, workforce development, capacity building, and knowledge transfer to enhance institutional effectiveness and operational sustainability. 7. Lead stakeholder engagement and interdepartmental coordination to facilitate decision-making, resolve complex technical and operational issues, and ensure timely delivery of organizational commitments. 8. Ensure the timely completion, commissioning, handover, and closeout of projects, supported by comprehensive technical documentation, financial accountability, and appropriate asset management records. Work Location Abyei Expected duration 6 months Duties and Responsibilities The United Nations Interim Security Force for Abyei (UNISFA), through the Facility Management Unit (FMU), manages the planning, development, construction, operation, maintenance, rehabilitation, optimization, and decommissioning of mission facilities and infrastructure across all camps and locations. These include accommodations, offices, power, water and sanitation systems, waste management, workshops, warehouses, drainage networks, and other mission-support facilities. The Project Manager serves as the FMU focal point for project management and compound maintenance operations, responsible for planning, managing, designing, coordinating, overseeing, and monitoring infrastructure projects and facility operations. The role ensures facilities are safe, functional, sustainable, and cost-effective while providing technical and managerial oversight throughout the project lifecycle, from planning and design through construction, commissioning, close-out, operation, maintenance, rehabilitation. Under the supervision of the Chief, FMU, the incumbent provides technical, operational, and advisory support in developing and implementing infrastructure strategies, camp development plans, maintenance programs, and project priorities in compliance with UN regulations, engineering standards, and mission requirements. Responsibilities The incumbent will be based at UNISFA Abyei Headquarters and will travel frequently to field locations. Administration • Lead assigned projects throughout the project lifecycle, ensuring delivery of approved scope, schedule, budget, quality, and safety requirements. • Develop project plans, schedules, resource requirements, risk registers, and monitoring tools. • Manage and oversee the construction, reconstruction, rehabilitation, operation, maintenance, and improvement of mission facilities and infrastructure. • Coordinate preventive, corrective, and emergency maintenance programs across mission camps. • Ensure compliance with UN engineering standards, environmental policies, and occupational health and safety requirements. • Coordinate and monitor the implementation of construction, alteration, repair and maintenance works, ensuring timely completion and effective utilization of available resources • Maintain accurate project, asset, contract, maintenance, and technical documentation. • Conduct technical inspections, condition assessments, and facility audits, recommending corrective actions where required. • Prepare and review Statements of Work (SoWs), Bills of Quantities (BoQs), technical specifications, cost estimates, and procurement documents. • Review contractor submissions, drawings, and technical documentation for compliance with approved specifications, contractual requirements, and applicable technical standards. • Utilize project management and other relevant tools for project tracking, procurement, asset management, and financial monitoring. • Advise management on project risks, resource requirements, operational constraints, and corrective actions. • Coordinate infrastructure priorities, workplans, budgets, and procurement plans with relevant mission stakeholders. Planning • Develop and implement construction infrastructure development, rehabilitation, maintenance and project management plans in support of camp operation. • Lead infrastructure projects from initiation through design, procurement, implementation, commissioning, handover, and closure. • Develop project plans, schedules, resource requirements, risk management strategies, and monitoring tools. Coordinate with engineering, logistics, procurement, finance, ICT, security, medical units, and other stakeholders to ensure integrated project delivery. • Conduct feasibility studies, technical assessments, site surveys, and infrastructure evaluations. • Assess changing operational requirements and recommend infrastructure improvements. • Prepare and review project scopes, designs, technical specifications, BoQs, and cost estimates for technical and operational suitability. • Identify project risks and implement mitigation measures. • Support annual and multi-year infrastructure investment and maintenance planning. • Develop contingency plans to ensure continuity of critical services and infrastructure. Operations • Manage contractor performance, ensuring compliance with contractual, safety, quality, and technical requirements. • Monitor project progress, costs, schedules, and resource utilization, recommending corrective actions where required. • Supervise multidisciplinary technical teams, contractors, consultants, and service providers. • Conduct site inspections, progress reviews, testing, commissioning, handovers, and acceptance activities. • Identify defects and non-conformities, coordinate corrective measures, and verify satisfactory completion of remedial works • Review completed works and verify quality, quantities, and compliance prior to acceptance or payment. • Coordinate infrastructure modifications, relocations, rehabilitation, and repurposing activities. • Coordinate construction and maintenance activities to minimize disruption to ongoing mission operations and ensure safe execution of works • Promote resource efficiency and sustainability initiatives in construction, maintenance, and facility operations. Ensure compliance of construction and maintenance operations with applicable environmental standards, regulations, and waste management requirements.. • Respond to technical emergencies and coordinate remedial actions. • Implement corrective action plans and continuous improvement initiatives. • Participate in technical evaluations, inspections, project reviews, and asset management activities. • Ensure completed projects are incorporated into mission asset inventories and maintenance programs. Reporting and Compliance • Prepare periodic reports on project implementation, camp operations, maintenance activities, risks, and contractor performance. • Maintain project monitoring and reporting systems, including progress tracking, risk management, corrective actions, and performance monitoring.Monitor KPIs related to infrastructure operations, maintenance, service delivery, and project performance. • Support audits, inspections, management reviews, and UN Headquarters reporting requirements. • Ensure project and operational records are complete, accurate, traceable, and audit ready. • Prepare technical briefings, management reports, presentations, and decision papers. • Monitor compliance with UN policies, engineering standards, environmental requirements, safety procedures, and contractual obligations. • Analyze recurring infrastructure and operational issues and recommend sustainable solutions. • Support mission planning, budget preparation, infrastructure strategies, and operational decision-making. Qualifications/special skills A minimum of Seven (7) years of progressively responsible experience in construction project management, facilities management, construction supervision, or infrastructure support operations in field or complex environments is required. A minimum of seven (7) years of progressively responsible experience in planning, design coordination, implementation, and supervision of construction and infrastructure projects is required. Experience in project scheduling, cost control and risk management is required. Experience in coordinating multi-disciplinary technical teams and contractors s is required.. Ability to prepare and evaluate technical reports and documentation is desirable Proficiency in computer-aided design (CAD), project scheduling and management software (e.g., AutoCAD, MS Project, Primavera P6), and standard office applications is desirable Knowledge of construction methodologies, materials, quality assurance and quality control, and applicable engineering standards is desirable. Driving License for cars is required. Languages English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For the post advertised, fluency in English is required.
