jobs.description: Org. Setting and Reporting This post is located in the Rule of Law, Accountability and Civic Space (RACS 1), Special Procedures (SP), Thematic and Special Procedures Division (TSP) in the Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR). The incumbent will work under the direct supervision of the Chief of Special Procedures Rule of Law, Accountability and Civic Space (RACS 1), and under the general supervision of the Chief of Special Procedures. Responsibilities Under the general supervision of the Chief of Special Procedures and the direct supervision of the Chief of Special Procedures Rule of Law, Accountability and Civic Space (RACS 1), the incumbent will: • Monitor the implementation of international human rights law and international humanitarian law, and support follow-up on recommendations from human rights mechanisms, including treaty bodies, the Universal Periodic Review, special procedures and investigative mechanisms, to advance compliance and accountability. • Collect, document and analyse evidence-based information on civil, cultural, economic, social and political rights, including the right to development, within assigned thematic or geographic areas to support in-depth analysis, early warning, accountability, and informed decision-making, ensuring that human rights data is discoverable, interoperable and appropriately shared, including from gender and leave-no-one-behind perspectives. • Draft, review and contribute to human rights reports, briefings, legal and policy analyses and other communications, and prepare analytical papers that inform strategies, policies, programmes and decision-making, with integration of gender and leave-no-one-behind considerations. • Collect, verify and analyse multi-source information on thematic and country-specific human rights situations, ensuring data quality, methodological compliance and gender-responsive analysis. • Provide substantive professional support to national and regional counterparts in strengthening human rights systems, institutions and frameworks, including complaints mechanisms, victim and witness support services, engagement with international human rights mechanisms, and implementation of recommendations. • Support the integration of international human rights norms and standards into political, peace and security, humanitarian, development and economic frameworks and processes, contributing to efforts to address impunity and structural human rights challenges. • Contribute to guidance and professional support to civil society actors on integrating human rights into protection, rule-of-law, development, transitional justice and accountability initiatives. • Engage with UN entities, UN Country Teams, regional coordination mechanisms and development and economic actors to integrate human rights, including gender dimensions, into policies, programmes and cooperation frameworks. • Support analytical, coordination and planning work related to protection of civilians, conflict-related sexual violence and child protection, including translating early-warning information into coordinated responses. • Provide research, coordination and follow-up support to treaty bodies, special procedures, the Universal Periodic Review and commissions of inquiry. • Contribute to the collection and analysis of data as well as identification of trends or patterns and provide draft insights through graphs, charts, tables and reports using data visualization methods for data-driven planning, decision-making, presentation and reporting. • Maintain confidentiality and integrity and handle sensitive information with discretion, ensuring compliance with the UN data privacy, security requirements, and standards. • Contribute to gender-focused sections of reports, studies, speeches and other written outputs for UN bodies and public communications by providing research inputs, background analysis and drafting support. Competencies • Professionalism: Knowledge of international human rights law, norms, and standards. Knowledge of human rights monitoring, documentation, analysis, research and reporting methodologies, including planning, coordinating and conducting field missions. Skills in drafting human rights reports, policy and other documents. Knowledge of regional and international human rights mechanisms. Knowledge of international humanitarian law and its application. Ability to conduct legal analysis. Skill in collecting, processing, and analysing large volumes of unstructured and structured data. Knowledge of global and regional gender equality frameworks and instruments. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. Able to analyze and interpret data in support of decision-making and convey resulting information to management. • Teamwork: Works collaboratively with colleagues to achieve organizational goals; solicits input by genuinely valuing others’ ideas and expertise; is willing to learn from others; places team agenda before personal agenda; supports and acts in accordance with final group decision, even when such decisions may not entirely reflect own position; shares credit for team accomplishments and accepts joint responsibility for team shortcomings. • Planning& Organizing: Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies; identifies priority activities and assignments; adjusts priorities as required; allocates appropriate amount of time and resources for completing work; foresees risks and allows for contingencies when planning; monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary; uses time efficiently. Education Advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in human rights, law, political science, international relations, social sciences, economics, public policy, sustainable development, humanitarian affairs or related field. A first-level university degree in combination with two additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. A first-level university degree and no experience will be accepted for candidates who have passed the Young Professionals Programme Examination (YPP), the United Nations National Competitive Recruitment Examination (NCRE) or the General Service to Professional Examination (G to P). Job - Specific Qualification Not available. Work Experience A minimum of 2 years of experience in human rights or related areas is required. Relevant experience may include, but is not limited to political affairs, public affairs, international relations, law, social sciences, economics, development, humanitarian affairs, or other related areas. (No experience is needed for candidates who have passed a United Nations Competitive Recruitment Examination.) Knowledge of international human rights law, norms, and standards is required. Ability to conduct legal analysis is required. Skills in drafting human rights reports, policy and other documents is required. Knowledge of regional and international human rights mechanisms is required. Knowledge of international humanitarian law and its application is desirable. Knowledge of human rights monitoring, documentation, analysis, research and reporting methodologies, including planning, coordinating and conducting field missions is desirable. Skill in collecting, processing, and analysing large volumes of unstructured and structured data is desirable. Knowledge of global and regional gender equality frameworks and instruments is desirable. Languages English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this job opening, English is required. French is desirable. The table below shows the minimum required level for each skill in these languages, according to the UN Language Framework (please consult https://languages.un.org for details). jobs.title: Analyste de Projet, Système d’Information Géographique (SIG) et en Gestion de base des données [ouvert aux candidats internes & externes]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

Conformément à l’engagement visant à préserver les capacités et à soutenir le personnel déjà au sein de l’Organisation, la majorité des postes vacants du PNUD, du FENU et des VNU sont publiés selon un processus de candidature par niveaux , selon lequel :

- Niveau 0 : Personnel international du PNUD/FENU/VNU titulaire d'un contrat permanent (PA) ou à durée déterminée (FTA), dont les postes seront supprimés, ou dont les contrats seront résiliés ou non renouvelés en 2026

- Niveau 1 : Autre personnel du PNUD/FENU/VNU titulaire d'un contrat permanent (PA) ou à durée déterminée (FTA)

- Niveau 2 : Personnel du PNUD/FENU/VNU titulaire d'un contrat temporaire (TA), personnel sous contrat PSA régulier, et Volontaires des Nations Unies Experts et Spécialistes

- Niveau 3 ou aucun niveau indiqué : Tous les autres types de contrat du PNUD/FENU/VNU et d'autres agences, ainsi que les candidats externes

Veuillez noter le(s) niveau(x) indiqués dans le titre du poste vacant, le cas échéant, et assurez-vous de remplir les conditions d’éligibilité pour postuly.

Description du bureau/de l’Unité/du Projet

La République Centrafricaine dans sa stratégie de protection de son patrimoine forestier exceptionnel qui couvrent plus d’un tiers du territoire national (environ 22.3 millions d’hectares de forêts, soit 45% du territoire national), avec une forte biodiversité et fournissant des services écosystémiques vitaux, et de lutte contre la pauvreté des communautés, entend changer de paradigme pour inverser la tendance à la perte du couvert forestier estimée annuellement à 0,26 % soit 58 000 hectares de couvert forestier. Pour cela, la mise en œuvre de l’axe 4 du Plan National de Développement (PND) 2024-2028 permettra de transformer la conservation de la forêt et la gestion durable des terres en une source de valeur financière directe pour les communautés locales. Le mécanisme des Paiements pour Services Environnementaux (PSE), tel que développé par CAFI, permet de concrétiser cette transformation en apportant aux producteurs et aux communautés qui adoptent des pratiques vertueuses, des incitations financières permettant de gérer durablement leurs terres et forêts.

L’Unité Environnement, Énergie et Changement Climatique (EE&CC) du PNUD soutient le Gouvernement dans la mise en œuvre des politiques environnementales, de développement durable et énergétique. À travers ses programmes et projets, elle promeut les énergies renouvelables en milieu rural, la conservation de la biodiversité, l’écotourisme dans les aires protégées, l’agroforesterie et la gestion durable des forêts. Elle appuie également l’accès à la finance climat et le renforcement des capacités nationales et locales pour la prévention des risques climatiques et la gestion des urgences.

En 2025, la RCA a bénéficié d’un Don préparatoire de l’Initiatives pour les Forêts d’Afrique Centrale (CAFI) d’un montant de 300 000 USD pour la formulation d’un Projet PSE Bangui et ses périphéries pour une durée de 5 ans (2026-2030). L’objectif principal du projet est de déployer des PSE au profit des communautés, de démontrer la nécessité et l’efficacité d’un système PSE en RCA, en l’ancrant dans la plateforme régionale de CAFI et en l’adaptant au contexte national.

Dans l’optique de mettre en œuvre le « Projet PSE Bangui et ses périphéries », le Bureau du PNUD en RCA recrute un(e) Expert(e) National(e) en SIG et en Gestion de base des données.

Portée des travaux

Sur la base de son expertise, le/la Analyste de Projet, Système d'Information Géographique (SIG) et en Gestion de base des données aura pour mission principale de soutenir efficacement la mise en œuvre des interventions du projet tant sur le plan institutionnel, programmatique qu’opérationnel, conformément au Document de Projet afin de contribuer à l’atteinte des résultats du Document de Programme Pays (CPD) 2023-2027 du PNUD qui est aligné sur les priorités nationales définies dans le Plan National de Développement (PND), en particulier l’Axe stratégique 5 : Durabilité environnementale et résilience face aux crises et aux effets du changement climatique. Sous la supervision et l'orientation générales du/de la chef(fe) de projet, il/elle sera chargé(e) de développer, gérer et analyser l’ensemble des données spatiales et non-spatiales nécessaires à la planification, au suivi-évaluation et à la vérification indépendante des activités du projet. le/la Analyste de Projet, Système d'Information Géographique (SIG) et en Gestion de base des données jouera un rôle clé dans l’opérationnalisation de la plateforme PSE du CAFI, en garantissant la fiabilité des bases de données, la production d’analyses spatiales et la génération de rapports techniques conformes aux standards CAFI et internationaux.

Principales tâches et responsabilités :

Développer et maintenir la base de données spatiales et non-spatiales du projet :

- Concevoir et mettre à jour des cartes thématiques pour la planification,

- Assurer la tenue des registres fonciers au sein du projet,

- Collecter et gérer les données socio-économiques,

- Assurer le suivi biophysique.

Assurer le géoréférencement et l’intégration des données issues des activités d’enrôlement :

- Reporter et archiver les limites des parcelles, forêts communautaires et blocs paysagers en réalisant le tracé géoréférencé des unités de gestion en utilisant des outils GPS, SIG et images satellites (orthophotos, imagerie haute résolution) ;

- Mettre en place un système d’archivage structuré permettant de conserver l’historique des limites (versions, dates, auteurs) ;

- Organiser le stockage des shapefiles, métadonnées et documents associés selon les normes reconnues en gestion de données spatiales ;

- Intégrer les données collectées dans la plateforme numérique CAFI et garantir leur qualité (contrôle, validation, cohérence)

Former les équipes de terrain et les agrégateurs à l’utilisation des outils de collecte mobile (KoboToolbox, GPS, tablettes) :

- Animer des sessions de formation sur l’utilisation des outils numériques de collecte,

- Développer des modules de formation adaptés aux différents profils d’utilisateurs (équipes de terrain, agrégateurs, responsables locaux).

- Former à l’utilisation avancée de KoboToolbox : création de formulaires, paramétrage, gestion des soumissions, synchronisation des données.

- Former à l’utilisation correcte des équipements GPS et tablettes : prise de coordonnées, enregistrement de traces, calibration, bonnes pratiques de terrain.

- Démontrer les procédures de collecte standardisées afin d’assurer l’homogénéité et la fiabilité des données.

- Assurer l’encadrement terrain des acteurs du projet en accompagnant les équipes lors des sorties terrain, et produire des rapports d’encadrement terrain comprenant les lacunes observées, les recommandations et les mesures correctives.

- Assurer la production de documents cartographiques et d’outils de visualisation destinés au suivi et à la communication des activités du projet (rapports cartographiques, d’infographies, et d’autres supports visuels adaptés), production d’analyses spatiales pour le suivi des interventions PSE, incluant l’agroforesterie, les activités de Régénération Naturelle Assistée (RNA), les mesures de conservation et les actions liées au bois-énergie.

Élaborer des supports techniques et visuels :

- Produire des analyses spatiales pour le suivi des activités PSE (agroforesterie, RN+A, conservation, bois-énergie) ;

- Assurer la production de documents cartographiques et d’outils de visualisation destinés au suivi et à la communication des activités du projet (rapports cartographiques, d’infographies, et d’autres supports visuels adaptés), production d’analyses spatiales pour le suivi des interventions PSE, incluant l’agroforesterie, les activités de Régénération Naturelle Assistée (RNA), les mesures de conservation et les actions liées au bois-énergie.

Assurer un appui technique à la vérification indépendante en fournissant un soutien technique complet aux processus de vérification indépendante, notamment à travers :

- La préparation et structuration des données cartographiques nécessaires à l’évaluation,

- La production et la mise à disposition de données statistiques et de preuves géospatiales vérifiables

- L’utilisation d’images satellitaires, de données issues de drones et d’autres sources d’observation de la Terre pour le suivi de la couverture forestière et la validation des résultats

Garantir la sauvegarde, l’archivage et la mise à disposition sécurisée des données aux partenaires du projet en garantissant la gestion rigoureuse et sécurisée des données géospatiales et statistiques du projet, incluant :

- La sauvegarde régulière et la prévention des pertes ou altérations de données ;

- L’archivage structuré et la documentation des jeux de données pour assurer leur traçabilité ;

- La mise à disposition sécurisée des données auprès des partenaires du projet, conformément aux procédures internes et aux normes de confidentialité.

Contribuer aux activités du Pilier en matière de Système d’Information Géographique (SIG).

- Contribuer au fonctionnement de l’Unité EE&CC, notamment par un appui conseil technique et à la promotion du travail d’équipe y compris le partage de connaissance en matière de système d’information géographique (SIG) et gestion des bases des données ;

- Contribuer à la préparation des plans de travail, de suivi et évaluation, des rapports annuels du pilier et autres exercices mandataires du bureau ;

- Fournir l’assurance qualité aux processus d’évaluation des projets / programmes du pilier

Faciliter le renforcement des connaissances et des capacités, le partage des connaissances et la sensibilisation dans le ou les domaines thématiques assignés

- Identifier, synthétiser et documenter les bonnes pratiques et les enseignements tirés du projet et des partenaires de mise en œuvreLe titulaire exécutera tout autres tâches jugées nécessaires au fonctionnement efficace du Pilier et de l'Organisation.

Impact des résultats:

- La base de données spatiales et non-spatiales du projet (cartes, registres fonciers, données socio-économiques, suivi biophysique) est développée et maintenue ;

- Les cartes thématiques pour la planification, le suivi et la communication du projet sont conçues et mis à jour ;

- Un appui technique à la vérification indépendante : préparation des données, cartographies, statistiques et preuves géospatiales est assuré.

- La capitalisation et le partage d’expérience en matière d’outils SIG et gestion des données sont renforcés.

Arrangement institutionnel

le/la Analyste de Projet, Système d'Information Géographique (SIG) et en Gestion de base des données du projet travaillera sous la supervision directe du Chef(fe) de Projet qui rend compte au Management du PNUD.

Compétences

Core

Obtenir des Résultats : LEVEL 1: Planifie et supervise son propre travail, fait preuve de minutie, fournit un travail de qualité dans le respect des délais

Penser de Manière Innovante : LEVEL 1: Ouvert aux idées créatives et aux risques connus, c'est un solutionneur de problèmes pragmatique qui apporte des améliorations

Apprendre en Continu : LEVEL 1: Ouvert d'esprit et curieux, partage ses connaissances, tire les leçons de ses erreurs, sollicite des retours d'expérience

S'adapter avec Agilité : LEVEL 1: S'adapte au changement, gère de manière constructive l'ambiguïté et l'incertitude, fait preuve de souplesse

Agir avec Détermination : LEVEL 1: Fait preuve de dynamisme et de motivation, capable de rester serein face à l'adversité, sûr de soi

S'engager et Collaborer : LEVEL 1: Fait preuve de compassion et de compréhension envers les autres, tisse des relations positives

Favoriser la Diversité et l’Inclusion : LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Compétences transversales et techniques

Gestion de organisation - Gestion axée sur les résultats : Être en mesure de gérer la mise en œuvre de stratégies, de programmes et de projets en mettant l’accent sur l’amélioration des performances et l’obtention de résultats démontrables. Connaître et comprendre les théories, les concepts, les méthodologies, les instruments et les outils pertinents.

Développement de l’organisation - Génération de connaissances : Savoir chercher des informations et les transformer en connaissances utiles, qui sont adaptées au contexte ou répondent à un besoin exprimé. Savoir appliquer des concepts existants à de nouvelles situations et définir de nouveaux concepts afin de mettre au point des solutions réalisables et de nouvelles approches. Connaître les théories, concepts et modèles conceptuels pertinents qui peuvent être utiles pour faire face à de nouvelles situations

Gestion de organisation - Communication : Communiquer de manière claire, concise et sans équivoque, à la fois à l’écrit et à l’oral ; adapter les messages et choisir les modes de communication en fonction du public. Savoir gérer la communication interne et externe, au travers des médias, des réseaux sociaux et d’autres canaux appropriés.

Numérique et innovation - Analyse des données : Capacité à extraire, analyser et visualiser des données (y compris des données en temps réel) afin de dégager des informations pertinentes et faciliter une prise de décision efficace.

Gestion des partenariats - Gestion des relations : Capacité à dialoguer avec un large éventail de partenaires publics et privés, d’établir, de maintenir, et/ou de renforcer les relations de travail, la confiance et la compréhension mutuelle.

Qualifications minimales du NPSA réussi

Exigences minimales en matière d'éducation

Un diplôme universitaire supérieur (Master ou équivalent) en en Géomatique, Sciences de l’information Géographique, Télédétection, Environnement ou Disciplines Connexes ; est requis, ou

Un diplôme universitaire de premier cycle (licence) dans les domaines susmentionnés

combiné à deux années supplémentaires d'expérience qualifiante sera pris en considération à la place du diplôme universitaire supérieur.

Années minimales d'expérience professionnelle pertinente

Les candidats titulaires d'un Master (ou équivalent) dans un domaine d'études pertinent ne sont pas tenus d'avoir une expérience professionnelle.

Les candidats titulaires d'une licence (ou équivalent) doivent avoir au moins deux (2) ans d'expérience professionnelle dans l’utilisation des SIG, de la télédétection et de la gestion de bases de données appliqués à la foresterie, l’agriculture ou la gestion des ressources naturelles ;

Compétences souhaitées

Expérience avérée dans la mise en place de systèmes de suivi basés sur les SIG et l’intégration de données spatiales et socio-économiques

Expérience et connaissance avérée des standards MRV, PSE ou REDD+ serait un atout ;

Excellente capacité d’analyse et de synthèse, avec un sens de la rigueur et de l’organisation ;

Avéré(e) capacité à former et accompagner des équipes pluridisciplinaires (agents de terrain, agrégateurs, institutions locales) ;

Une expérience en Gestion axée sur les résultats/Gestion du cycle de projet (GAR/GCP) sera un atout certain ;

Expérience et avoir une large connaissance des concepts de développement durable et du changement climatique centrées sur le principe de ne laisser personne pour compte ;

Connaissance et expérience pratique de l'application de l'intégration de la dimension de genre dans les projets internationaux ;

Expérience et avoir une bonne compréhension de la conservation de la biodiversité, de l'application de la loi, des moyens de subsistance durables et des questions connexes.

Langues requises

La maîtrise du français est requise.

La « connaissance pratique » de l'anglais est requise.

Voyage

Le/la titulaire du poste pourrait être amené (e) à effectuer des missions. Les frais de mission seront payés conformément aux règles et procédures en la matière.

Égalité des chances

En tant qu'employeur souscrivant au principe de l'égalité des chances, le PNUD valorise la diversité en tant qu'expression de la multiplicité des nations et des cultures où nous opérons et, à ce titre, nous encourageons les candidats qualifiés de tous horizons à postuler à des postes au sein de l'organisation. Nos décisions d'embauche sont fondées sur le mérite et l'aptitude au poste, sans discrimination.

Le PNUD s'engage également à créer un lieu de travail inclusif où tout le personnel est habilité à contribuer à notre mission, est valorisé, peut s'épanouir et bénéficie d'opportunités de carrière ouvertes à tous.

Harcèlement sexuel, exploitation et abus d'autorité

Le PNUD ne tolère pas le harcèlement, le harcèlement sexuel, l'exploitation, la discrimination et l'abus d'autorité. Tous les candidats sélectionnés sont donc soumis à des contrôles pertinents et doivent respecter les normes et principes respectifs.

Droit de sélectionner plusieurs candidats

Le PNUD se réserve le droit de sélectionner un ou plusieurs candidats à partir de cette annonce de vacance de poste. Nous pouvons également retenir les candidatures et prendre en considération les candidats qui postulent à ce poste pour d'autres postes similaires au PNUD, au même niveau et avec une description de poste, une expérience et des exigences éducationnelles similaires.

Alerte aux escroqueries

Le PNUD ne facture aucune redevance à aucun stade de son processus de recrutement. Pour plus d'informations, veuillez consulter www.undp.org/scam-alert.

jobs.title: Project Manager (Open to Internal and External Applicants)
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP is committed to achieving workforce diversity in terms of gender, nationality, and culture. Individuals from minority groups, indigenous groups and persons with disabilities are equally encouraged to apply. All applications will be treated with the strictest confidence.

UNDP does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of harassment, including sexual harassment, and discrimination. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks.

UNDP is the leading United Nations organization in fighting to end the injustice of poverty, inequality, and climate change. Working with our broad network of experts and partners in 170 countries, we help nations to build integrated, lasting solutions for people and planet. Learn more at undp.org or follow at @UNDP

Iraq is recognized as one of the most affected countries by the harmful effects of climate change. Iraq ratified the Paris Agreement on January 14, 2021. In October 2021, the Government of Iraq (GoI) signed their first National Determined Contribution (NDC), which has been presented at the COP26. The Government of Iraq has requested UNDP support in implementation of the NDC, including through capacity development, advisory for sectoral planning and formulation of related strategies, frameworks, and instruments.

UNDP is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP's policy work carried out at HQ, Regional and Country Office levels offers a spectrum of deep local knowledge to cutting-edge global perspectives and advocacy. UNDP invests in the Global Policy Network (GPN), a network of field-based and global technical expertise across a wide range of knowledge domains in support of the signature solutions and organizational capabilities envisioned in UNDP's Strategic Plan.

UNDP is an accredited Implementing Agency for the Global Environment Facility (GEF) Trust Fund and the family of funds such as the Least Developed Countries Fund (LDCF), the Special Climate Change Fund (SCCF), and the Global Biodiversity Framework Fund (GBBF). As an Implementing Agency, UNDP offers countries highly specialized services for eligibility assessment, project formulation and due diligence, co-financing mobilization, implementation oversight, results management and evaluation, and knowledge management.

Iraq faces significant environmental and public health risks associated with persistent organic pollutants (POPs), hazardous chemicals, obsolete pesticides, polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), unintentional POPs (UPOPs), industrial POPs (IPOPs), and chemically contaminated sites. Previous assessments identified substantial quantities of obsolete pesticides and potentially PCB-contaminated electrical equipment and highlighted significant technical and institutional capacity gaps in chemicals and contaminated-sites management.

The Government of Iraq is a Party to major international chemicals and waste conventions, including the Stockholm, Basel, Rotterdam and Minamata Conventions. Iraq has previously developed a National Implementation Plan (NIP) under the Stockholm Convention; however, the existing NIP requires updating to reflect newly listed POPs, improved inventories, updated risk information, institutional developments and current national priorities.

The Integrated Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs) and Chemical Hotspots Management Project, therefore adopts an integrated approach combining:

- strengthening the national framework for POPs and hazardous chemicals management;

- updating the national POPs inventories and National Implementation Plan;

- strengthening laboratory, inspection, monitoring and institutional capacities;

- environmentally sound management and disposal of obsolete pesticides;

- management and disposal/phase-out of PCB-contaminated equipment, oils and waste; and

- assessment and remediation planning for priority chemical pollution hotspots.

The project comprises three components. Component 1 focuses on improved management of POPs and hazardous chemicals; Component 2 focuses on high-risk POPs in the agriculture and power sectors; and Component 3 addresses chemical pollution hotspots and contaminated sites.

Implementation will require extensive technical assistance, consultancy services, procurement of laboratory and field equipment, hazardous waste management services, capacity building, site assessments, remediation planning and policy/regulatory development.

The project will be implemented by UNDP through an Output Agreement with the Ministry of Environment. The Project Manager will therefore be the principal day-to-day focal point for implementation and coordination within the project management structure.

Institutional Arrangement

The Project Manager will directly report to the Programme Specilaist with matrix reporting to the chief technical specialist of the Environment, Energy and Climate Change (EECC), UNDP Iraq. The position holder will be part of a dynamic team of national and international experts working on policy advocacy, capacity building, innovation and sharing best practices with national stakeholders on climate change, environmental management and POPs and Chemical Hotspots Management.

Duties and Responsibilities

Provide Strategic Technical Direction and Leadership

- Lead strategic planning for the project as well as formulation and periodic revisions of the project’s annual work plan (AWP), including plans for budget, HR and procurement that are developed in close coordination with UNDP’s Country Office Programme, HR, and Procurement teams. Lead development of detailed implementation plans.

- Lead the provision of high-level strategic and technical guidance to the project, ensuring alignment with UNDP corporate priorities, donor requirements, national development frameworks, and relevant international commitments.

- Advise UNDP management and project stakeholders on emerging technical issues, risks, opportunities, and strategic approaches to enhance project impact, sustainability, and policy relevance.

- Oversee the overall technical quality of project outputs, deliverables, studies, assessments, and knowledge products to ensure compliance with international standards and best practices.

- Provide leadership in the identification, design, and implementation of innovative technical solutions and approaches that support the achievement of project objectives and intended outcomes.

- Guide the integration of cross-cutting issues, including gender equality, environmental sustainability, social inclusion, human rights, and capacity development, into project planning and implementation.

- Support adaptive management by recommending strategic adjustments based on implementation progress, lessons learned, and changing contextual circumstances.

- Provide direction, guidance, and direct supervision to UNDP project personnel. Undertake technical review of project documents produced by the project team and partners, and ensure high technical standards are met.

- Ensure proper execution of all administrative activities associated with project implementation, including mobilizing goods and services, preparing Terms of Reference, completing contracting processes, recruiting/selecting consultants and experts, and managing financial arrangements/transactions and their correct authorization.

- Identify opportunities for synergies with other projects within UNDP and beyond, to advance the key objectives and grow its focus.

Lead Technical Quality Assurance and Programme Oversight

- Provide technical review and quality assurance of project work plans, technical reports, procurement specifications, Terms of Reference, training materials, policy products, and other project deliverables.

- Ensure that project activities are implemented in accordance with approved project documents, UNDP rules and regulations, donor requirements, and national priorities.

- Support the technical teams in maintaining high standards of project delivery, timeliness, and cost-effectiveness.

- Review technical outputs developed by consultants, contractors, service providers, and implementing partners and provide recommendations for improvement where necessary.

- Ensure consistency and coherence across project components and interventions to maximise results and avoid duplication of efforts.

- Provide technical support to the implementing partners and act as a liaison between UNDP and the partners.

- Support resource mobilization efforts and project development.

Support Strategic Partnerships and Stakeholder Engagement

- Facilitate technical dialogue and collaboration between UNDP, government institutions, development partners, academia, civil society organisations, and private sector stakeholders.

- Provide technical advice and support to implementing partners to strengthen ownership, coordination, and effective project implementation.

- Identify opportunities for strategic partnerships, resource mobilisation, and collaboration that can enhance project sustainability and scale-up successful interventions.

- Represent the project and provide technical inputs during meetings, workshops, consultations, conferences, and policy dialogues as required.

Monitor and report on progress in implementing project activities and achieving the targets set.

- Provide leadership and technical advice to the project in developing baselines and indicators for project monitoring and evaluation and coordinate the finalization of detailed results framework. Develop clear strategies and an effective system for data collection, means of verification, and information sharing and reporting.

- Lead the implementation of project monitoring, evaluation, and results framework to identify plan deviations and other problems; and make needed course corrections within agreed upon tolerances to achieve results. Conduct field visits as required to verify project activities relative to stated targets and provide regular field updates to UNDP management.

- Lead the development and conduct of mid-term and annual reviews, and end line assessment; and coordinate the conduct of independent evaluations. Organize project review and evaluation meetings. Follow up on the implementation of decisions, recommendations, and course corrections.

- Manage and monitor project risks, including social and environmental risks, initially identified and submit new risks to appropriate project governing bodies for consideration and decision on possible actions.

- Coordinate the preparation of corporate, donor and government reports in line with the reporting schedule and UNDP and donor requirements. Ensure provision of ad hoc reports and information requested by relevant entities.

- Ensure proper operational and financial closure of the project.

Facilitate knowledge and capacity building, knowledge sharing, and advocacy relevant to the assigned thematic areas.

- Provide technical guidance for the development and refinement of project indicators, monitoring frameworks, and reporting tools.

- Review project progress and results regularly and provide recommendations to address implementation challenges and improve performance.

- Contribute to the documentation of lessons learned, good practices, case studies, and knowledge products to support institutional learning and replication of successful approaches.

- Lead and support capacity-building initiatives, technical trainings, workshops, and knowledge-sharing activities for project staff, government counterparts, and stakeholders.

- Promote knowledge exchange and contribute to relevant communities of practice, technical networks, and learning platforms.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Competencies

Core

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

- People Management: UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site .

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Business Direction & Strategy

- System Thinking Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

2030 Agenda: Planet

- Nature Environmental Governance: Global Environmental Governance

Finance

- Budget Management Ability to support budgetary aspects of work planning process, drawing and management of team budgets.

Business Direction & Strategy

- Effective Decision Making Take decisions in a timely and efficient manner in line with one’s authority, area of expertise and resources.

- Negotiation and influence Reach an understanding, persuade others, resolve points of difference, gain advantage in the outcome of dialogue, negotiate mutually acceptable solutions through compromise, and create win-win situations.

Business Management

- Project management Ability to plan, organize, prioritize, and control resources, procedures, and protocols to achieve specific goals.

- Risk management Identify and organize action around mitigating and proactively managing risks

Minimum Qualifications of the Successful NPSA

Minimum Education requirements

- Advanced university degree (Master's degree or equivalent) in Environmental Management, Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Natural Resources Management, Development Studies, Project Management or a relevant related field is required, OR

- A first-level university degree (Bachelor's degree) in the above fields in combination with two additional years of relevant experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree

Minimum years of relevant work experience

- Minimum 5 years (with master’s degree) or 7 years (with bachelor’s degree) of progressively responsible professional experience at the national or international level in environmental management, chemicals and waste management, climate change and biodiversity, natural resources management, environmental safeguards, environmental policy and governance, and project management is required.

Required skills

- Demonstrated experience in project management, preferably in environmental, chemicals, hazardous waste, climate, natural resources or sustainable development projects.

- Demonstrated experience managing multidisciplinary teams and consultants.

- Experience managing projects involving Government institutions and international development partners.

- Proven Experience in the use of computers and office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc) and advanced knowledge of spreadsheet and database packages, and experience in handling web-based management systems

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section

- Experience in working, liaising, and collaborating with UN agencies, governments, NGOs, civil society organizations, and public international organizations.

- Proven knowledge of capacity building theory and capacity building/assessment methodologies

Required Language(s)

- Fluency in written and spoken English and Arabic is required.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

jobs.title: Field Security Associate (FSA)- Training, NPSA-6, DS-Kyiv, UNDSS, National position
jobs.description:
Background

The position is located in the Department of Safety and Security of Ukraine. This position is locally administered by UNDP and is financed by the United Nations Department of Safety and Security (UNDSS) from the Local Cost Share Security Budget (LCSSB) . The contract may be extended subject to the availability of funds, satisfactory performance, and continuing need for the post.

Under the supervision of the UNDSS Head of Training for training related matters and the Field Security Coordination Officer (FSC)) for security related matters; and overall guidance of the Chief Security Adviser (CSA), the Field Security Associate (Training) assists in the conducti of security training in Ukraine.

Duties and Responsibilities

Within limits of delegated authority and depending on location, Field Security Associate (FSA) - Training at this level may be responsible for the following duties: (These duties are generic and may not be performed by all Field Security Associates).

1. Facilitate knowledge sharing and Provide Security Trainings Coordination and Delivery

• Contributes to the planning, organization and delivery of security training courses including Safe and Secure Approached in Field Environment (SSAFE), Individual First Aid Kit (IFAK), Emergency Trauma Bag (ETB), Women Security Awareness Training (WSAT), and Field Security Associate (FSA) Training.

• Provides administrative and logistic support for all aspect of the training arrangements.

i. Liaises with conference manager for booking of training room and facility.

ii. Communicates in a timely manner with practical training ground manager.

iii. Assists in the preparation of IFAK/ETB/SSAFE training aids.

• Coordinates the co-facilitation of training with other trainer(s) from UN Agencies, Funds, Programmes and Organizations (UNAFPOs).

• Provides support in liaising with INGOs regarding security training assistance as part of Saving Life Together (SLT)_ framework.

• Assists in maintaining/updating training repository and data in SharePoint.

• Prepares and develops training package (including translation) as required.

• Conducts in-person IFAK/ETB/SSAFE training in field locations as required.

• Assists FSCO in preparing monthly training reports.

• Arranges IFAK sessions for the certification of new IFAK instructor candidate.

• Conducts practical and written assessment for IFAK and ETB.

2. Monitor Security Information and Coordination

• Assists the Chief Security Advisor/FSCOs in collecting, updating, and communicating information regarding the security situation in the Area of Responsibility (AoR):

i. Liaises and coordinates, as appropriate, with the host government security organizations and/or personnel, including national and local provincial authorities, military, and police officers, as well as non-governmental organizations in the area of operation;

ii. Helps to assess the security situation at the duty station and ensures adequate gathering and verification of security information that may be required for a proper analysis of the situation;

iii. Communicates information on security issues to the heads of United Nations agencies and provides host country security advice to UNDSS, as required;

iv. Maintains regular contacts with Security Focal Points of UN agencies;

v. May be requested to provide technical assistance at Area/Security Management Team meetings.

3. Assist in Security Planning and Monitoring

• Assists in maintaining the Security Plan, including updating staff lists:

• Helps in the preparation and review of the UN Security Plan;

• Supports actions during the implementation of the Security Plan, as required.

• Assists with the monitoring of the security measures implementation as recommended in the Security Risks Management (SRM) process for the AoR.

• Assists in reporting security incidents affecting UN staff, offices, and assets, and assists in the preparation of security reports, such as the Security Incident Report and other Security Assessments.

4. Monitor the security compliance of UNSMS premises and international staff residences

• Provides support in conducting security evaluations and provides advice on Residential Security Measures of UN staff, as well as on latest trends and threats to staff safety and security;

• Establishes and maintains warden system and keeps update of information related to UN offices and residences;

• Administers a pass and ID system;

• Maintains liaison with commercial companies used for UN security at offices and residences in order to facilitate the effective and efficient use of the guard force.

5 Provide General Administrative Support

• Maintains routine and confidential correspondence files/documents;

• Maintains a database on contact details of host country security authorities;

• Arranges appointments, receives visitors, places, and screens telephone calls with discretion, and takes minutes and/or notes at meetings.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

Under the supervision of the UNDSS Head of Training for training related matters and the Field Security Coordination Officer (FSC)) for security related matters; and overall guidance of the Chief Security Adviser (CSA), the Field Security Associate (Training) assists in the conduction of security training in Ukraine.

Competencies

Core

Achieve Results:

LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively:

LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously:

LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Adapt with Agility:

LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination:

LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner:

LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion:

LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Thematic Area

Name

Definition

Business Management

Communication

Communicate in a clear, concise, and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience. Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media, and other appropriate channels.

Business Management

Customer Satisfaction/Client Management

Ability to respond timely and appropriately with a sense of urgency, provide consistent solutions, and deliver timely and quality results and/or solutions to fulfil and understand the real customers' needs.

Provide inputs to the development of customer service strategy.

Look for ways to add value beyond clients' immediate

requests.

Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns

Business Management

Operations Management

Ability to effectively plan, organize, and oversee the Organization beyond processes in order to convert its assets into the best results in the most efficient manner.

Knowledge of relevant concepts and mechanisms

Security Services

Security training

Ability to design, contribute to, and/or facilitate meaningful security training programmes/courses.

Required Skills and Experience

Min. Education requirements

- Secondary Education is required.

- University degree (Bachelor’s degree) in Political Science, Military Studies, Security Management, Management or a relevant field will be given due consideration but it is not a requirement.

- Applicable security, police and/or military training is desirable.

Min. years of relevant work experience

- Minimum six (6) years (with secondary education) or three (3) years (with bachelor’s degree) of working experience in the field of safety and security management or security training in the public or private security service areas is required.

Required skills

- Experience using computers (MS Word, Excel and PowerPoint, etc.).

- A valid driver’s license (standard category B) within Ukraine is required.

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section

- Prior experience on conduction of IFAK or ETB training.

- Prior experience on support or conduction of other security training.

- Prior experience with the UN system or an international NGO.

- Prior UNDSS FSA certification.

Required Language(s)

- Fluency in English and Ukrainian are required.

- Knowledge of Russian is desirable.

Professional Certificates

IFAK ToT 2.0 or ETB ToT valid certificate is required.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Use of AI by candidates

Background

The United Nations Volunteers (UNV) programme contributes to peace and development through volunteerism worldwide. We work with partners to integrate qualified, highly motivated and well supported UN Volunteers into development programming and promote the value and global recognition of volunteerism. UNV is active in 160 countries every year. UNV is administered by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP). UNV is headquartered in Bonn, Germany, with a field presence comprising 6 regional offices and 50+ field units.

The Human Resources Section (HRS) provides a full range of HR services to the organization and its workforce. As part of the Human Resources Section, the Capacity Development Team (CDT) designs capacity development and learning programmes for UN Volunteers. The team supports the implementation of the UNV Learning Portfolio which consists of five comprehensive learning experiences: 1. onboarding 2. skills surge 3. empowerment for change 4. connect and learn 5. career craft.

Scope of Work

- Plan and design virtual and onsite learning activities

- Conduct training needs analysis to identify gaps and improvements, informing programme design. Develop detailed programme plans aligned with learning objectives, including curriculum design, content outlines, instructional strategies, and assessment methods, utilizing prototyping principles.

- Create or source high-quality accessible training materials and resources, incorporating appropriate learning technologies and methodologies. Coordinate with facilitators and subject-matter-experts to ensure accuracy, relevance, and quality.

- Ensure alignment with UNDP-UNV M&E Framework and implement data-driven improvements.

- Perform the full cycle of project management, including communication, timeline management, budget oversight, and scope control.

- Prepare terms of reference and procure professional services from vendors and consultants for volunteer learning activities and projects.

- Coordinate logistics, and administrative arrangements for the timely delivery of the thematic workshops.

- Organize and monitor the delivery of services by external consultants and vendors in line with project plans, timelines and budgets.

- Conduct a thorough review to capture lessons learned and best practices for future projects.

- Provide technical guidance and supervision to designated personnel supporting assigned learning portfolio activities.

2. Deliver virtual and onsite learning activities

- Facilitate in-person, virtual, and blended learning activities in collaboration with stakeholders and domain experts, and the capacity development team using appropriate platforms.

- Adapt learning delivery methods to meet the needs of diverse volunteer categories, incorporating interactive and participatory techniques to increase engagement and retention.

- Build and maintain relationships with key stakeholders to expand co-delivery of volunteer learning initiatives.

- Engage with facilitators to ensure understanding and finalization of learning content and methods for effective program delivery.

- Coordinate or provide technical and learner support for virtual, blended, and onsite learning activities.

- Monitor volunteer engagement during sessions, making real-time improvements to optimize learning outcomes.

- Conduct pre- and post-workshop evaluations, recommending data-driven improvements.

3. Design and maintain e-courses on Learning Management System

- Ensure catalogue e-courses are current, relevant and accessible on UNV Learning Management System (e-Campus);

- Track completion of e-courses, including mandatory ones in collaboration with relevant UNV sections;

- Stay abreast of the status of mutual recognition of mandatory learning programmes completion through the UN Inter-Agency Group;

- Design, develop, update or maintain priority digital and blended learning products on eCampus, using learning technologies and authoring tools, including storyboards, instructional scripts, interactive activities and multimedia resources..

- Liaise with external vendors to resolve technical issues with accessing and completing courses, while improving user experience and interface.

- Support the administration and continuous improvement of learning platforms and digital learning environments to strengthen learner access, usability, engagement and reporting.

4. Support the revision of and delivery of learning programmes

- Collaborate with stakeholders and domain experts to revise learning programme content and delivery, aligning with identified learning needs and corporate goals.

- Analyze learning evaluation data to identify areas of improvement and incorporate changes into learning programmes and products.

- Apply agreed quality standards, templates and review processes to learning products, digital content, facilitator materials and learner resources.

- Maintain version control, communicate updated/revised programme to stakeholders, and conduct Training of Trainers for relevant workshops.

5. Coordinate learning outreach, communications and engagement

- Plan and coordinate communications and learner-engagement activities for assigned learning portfolio and UNV region, using appropriate communication channels and digital platforms.

- Develop and implement programme information, guidance and stakeholder updates to support awareness, access to and participation in learning opportunities.

- Draft relevant reports on learning activities, outcomes and impact as required.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the section and the organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The Learning Specialist reports to the Team Leader, Capacity Development and Learning, and works closely with the rest of the CDT and as a member of the Human Resources Section.

Core Competencies

Achieve Results

- Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

Learn Continuously

Adapt with Agility

Act with Determination

Engage and Partner

Enable Diversity and Inclusion

People Management: The position has no direct supervisory responsibilities. The role is intended to provide technical leadership and vendor/resource oversight through subject matter expertise, architecture guidance, quality assurance, and management of vendor-delivered outputs, not through line management of UNV staff.

Background

For six decades, UNDP has shaped the progress of human development, working with its partners to lift millions from poverty and increase opportunities for all. Empowered by Member States with a mandate to work across the spectrum of human development, UNDP provides integrated support at scale to improve people’s lives worldwide. UNDP’s Strategic Plan 2026-2029 is grounded in the determination of UNDP to eradicate poverty, the greatest global challenge, indispensable to the 2030 Agenda and the Sustainable Development Goals. Through the Strategic Plan, UNDP will continue to support countries’ progress towards high human development, while protecting the planet. Four strategic objectives – prosperity for all, effective governance, crisis resilience, and healthy planet – define its strategic direction, powered by three accelerators: digital and artificial intelligence (AI) transformation; gender equality; and sustainable finance. All are underpinned by a commitment to human rights and to leaving no one behind, and rest on the recognition of UNDP as a trusted and transparent development partner.

Within UNDP, the Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) unites world-class policy expertise, flagship global programmes, and collaborative innovation and learning networks so UNDP is not only ready for the future— but helps build it with governments and partners. BPPS is where policy meets practice - for impact. From development to crisis contexts, BPPS helps countries navigate complexity, scale what works, and advance a more just, resilient, and sustainable future. The position of Director, Quality and Impact Hub is a member of the BPPS senior leadership team.

The Quality and Impact Hub aim to expand UNDP’s value position as an accountable, transparent and therefore trusted and neutral development partner. The Impact Hub serves as the corporate custodian and strategist driving continual improvement of UNDP’s institutional architecture that guides UNDP programming. The Impact Hub leads changes in UNDP policy instruments and quality assurance approaches to enable UNDP programming - spanning all funding sources, including core, non-core, and Vertical Funds (VFs) - that is risk-informed, agile, results focused and integrates social and environmental risks and opportunities. The Impact Hub brings together two existing units in BPPS: the Vertical Fund Hub (VF Hub), and the Quality Programming Team (QPT - including the Social and Environmental Team (SES) Team) to be the central pillar of trust and transparency in UNDP.

By consolidating policy custodianship, quality assurance, risk management, and results oversight, the Impact Hub will be better able to support UNDP in achieving higher accountability, fostering greater trust with partners, reduce fiduciary risks, be more adaptable, and achieve greater developmental quality and impact. A renewed focus on fit-for-purpose and relevant policies will enable and steer UNDP into new partnerships with the private sector, with IFIs, and with the VFs. The Impact Hub will also institutionalize quality assurance and oversight into UNDP, where risk management, results assurance, and policy coherence operate seamlessly through digital systems, enabling evidence-based decision-making and learning across all UNDP programming. The Impact Hub will drive continuous improvement internally while learning from external engagements with the UNDP Executive Board and Boards of the Vertical Funds amongst others to ensure UNDP remains fit-for purpose, dynamic, agile and relevant in an ever-changing international development landscape. The Quality and Impact Hub will continue to lead UNDP’s accountability and engagement with the VFs and ensure UNDP VF programming complies with VF policies and requirements, as well as continue to provide financial oversight of VF programming to ensure VF funds are used for their intended purpose as required by the VFs and VF fiduciary management, reporting and auditing as mandated by the VFs.

Position Purpose

The Director of the Quality and Impact Hub guides and informs areas within the Hub, drawing on their deep technical expertise, political acumen, and demonstrated leadership and managerial capacities. The Director leads cross-cutting efforts in UNDP programming policy reform, and accountability, thereby contributing to UNDP’s reputation as a trusted and transparent. The Director also provides advice and technical expertise for high level decision makers seeking UNDP’s support. Further, the position engages across multilateral processes and partners to position UNDP as a partner of choice in support of developing countries. The role also interfaces with the broader BPPS (other Hubs, Teams) UNDP’s other Bureaus and Offices, and with UN system and related offices, entities, agencies/programmes/funds. The Director is responsible for creating a culture and enabling systems and processes that motivate, engage, and build a coherent team across multiple geographies. The Director will be supported by a Deputy Director.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Duties and Responsibilities

1. Lead UNDPs engagement with the Vertical Funds including Policy alignment, Project Oversight and Compliance and Financial Oversight

- Develop political, technical, operational and financial strategy for UNDP’s engagement with the Environmental Vertical Funds (Global Environment Facility, Green Climate Fund and Adaptation Fund) and provide the substantive technical and managerial leadership required to implement it;

- Ensure effective collaboration and relationship management with the Secretariats of the Environment Funds.

- Represent UNDP in the Vertical fund partnerships engaging with the Governing Bodies of each Fund; the technical and advisory bodies of each Fund, and the Accredited Entities under each Fund;

- Prepare, implement, and monitor annual VF Fee budgeting and planning in close collaboration with the Director of the Planet Hub and technical teams, as well as Regional Team Leads to ensure organizational alignment;

- Develop and continuously enhance the internal UNDP VF oversight and compliance procedures to ensure VF policies are met in UNDP VF programming;

- Deliver on project and portfolio level VF monitoring, reporting and evaluation requirements;

- Provide dedicated financial oversight for each VF project, including nationally implement projects and specific global projects, as well as annual portfolio level Fund specific audits, as required by VF policy and procedures;

- Regularly engage with other UNDP Bureaus to ensure consistent application of oversight and compliance procedures across VF programming, and on policy, legal, risk and other strategic VF issues;

- Proactively monitor project and program level VF specific risks connected with UNDP’s relationship with the Vertical Funds and regularly engages with Planet Hub teams including at regional level to ensure efficient and effective oversight and risk management of VF programming.

2. Lead development of UNDP Programme, Portfolio and Project Management standards, approaches, and prescriptive content (PPM)

- Represent UNDP in relevant UNSDG programming working mechanisms, inter-agency task forces and other UN reform initiatives and provide strategic analysis and advice on emerging issues across the UN related to programme and project management, and programming standards, approaches and modalities (e.g. on QCPR, UNSDCF, UNSDG guidelines and programming principles); help establish programme-related priorities, positions and action;

- Lead and develop new and revised programme, portfolio and project standards, approaches, policies and procedures to improve the quality of UNDP programming, facilitate evidence-based decision making/feedback loops, reduce unnecessary transaction costs, respond to evaluation and audit recommendations, and maintain coherence with operational content;

- Lead on the roll-out, review and revision of programming and portfolio approaches to enhance programme effectiveness for achieving results;

- Lead the review of specific quality assurance tools and standards including Partner Capacity Assessment Tool (PCAT) and Private Sector Due Diligence (PSDD) to facilitate flexible, innovative and impactful programming in UNDP;

- Monitor implementation of policies, methods and tools and compliance by relevant UNDP units, and analyze performance to identify lessons learned and steps needed to incentivize improved organizational performance, compliance, and effectiveness;

- Manage and contribute to development of PPM-related capacity building guidance, training modules and other resources for staff.

3. Provide management leadership on quality country programming, SES, Transparency, and Risk Management to increase value add of UNDP programming

- Develop and update guidance and Standard Operating Procedures for the corporate HQ Programme Appraisal Committee (HQ PAC) for new country and regional programmes (CPDs and RPDs);

- Manage the nomination, appointment and orientation process of HQ PAC members and chairs;

- Oversee the quality assurance processes and oversight of the regional bureau cleared CPDs/RPDs, for onward submission to the Executive Board based on its adherence to the Programme Quality Appraisal recommendations;

- Leads the development of standard operating procedures, guidance and systems (VF and non-VF) to ensure UNDP provides high-quality oversight services and remains compliant with policies and procedures;

- Monitor project-level appraisal and VF pipeline development processes and quality assurance, including the implementation of the Quality Standards for Programming and the Social and Environmental Standards;

- In partnership with other Bureaus, update UNDP tools to embed risk management into UNDP programming and the escalation of implementation risks for enhanced oversight as needed;

- Lead UNDP’s transparency initiative by integrating and implementing the International Aid Transparency Initiative (IATI) standard in programme and project management;

- Lead enhancement of and application of UNDP Social and Environmental Standards across all UNDP programming.

4. Promote and lead innovation and substantive knowledge management

- Create an environment of creative and innovative thinking; and culture receptive to change to drive the development of future UNDP programming policy and procedures;

- Lead the evolution and adoption of digital tools to support the efficiency and efficacy of the work of the Quality and Impact Hub;

- Advise on the enhancement of organizational management information systems and digital tools (e.g. Quantum, PIMS +) to advance the integration and effective application of policies and procedures to meet strategic management needs;

- Position accountability and transparency and quality assurance as a key aspect of UNDP’s value proposition to its partners;

- Analyze data on the performance of programmes and projects, including quality assurance data, to advise management of programming reforms that would help to lift performance, using evidence-based approaches.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Hub, Bureau, and the Organisation.

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

Background

General Assembly Resolution 2186 (XXI) decided to “bring into operations the United Nations Capital Development Fund as an organ of the General Assembly which shall function as an autonomous organization of the United Nations. The UN Capital Development Fund (UNCDF) assists developing countries, especially least developing countries, in the development of their economies by supplementing existing sources of capital assistance by means of grants, loans, and guarantees. UNCDFs vision is to help mobilize and catalyze an increase of capital flows for SDG impactful investments to Member States to address the most pressing development challenges facing vulnerable communities in these countries and thereby contribute to sustainable economic growth and equitable prosperity.

As a Flagship Catalytic Blended Financing platform of the UN, UNCDF utilizes its unique capability in the UN system to deploy grants, loans and guarantees to crowd-in finance for the scaling of development impact. UNCDF focuses on where the needs are greatest, a deliberate focus and capability rooted in UNCDF’s unique investment mandate to support the achievement of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and the realization of the Doha Programme of Action for the least developed countries, 2022–2031.

As per its Strategic Framework, UNCDF works to deploy its functions as a hybrid development organization and development finance institution. UNCDF responds to Member States requests for assistance by providing targeted technical and financial advisory services on investments for development outcomes, designing bespoke financial structuring solutions, undertaking financial derisking of investments, and enhancing investment readiness of SDG aligned projects in partnership with private sector, United Nations Organizations, International and Local Finance Institutions, Development Finance Institutions as well as Foundations and Philanthropy, among others. UNCDF works to develop local financial systems, new markets and mobilize and crowd in capital from public and private sources. UNCDF is driven by a partnership mindset which enables it to deploy its different capital capabilities in highly tailored and responsive ways in order to mobilize investments flows from other sources, in particular from the private sector. By structuring transactions which are highly impactful, but also recognize the need for multiplying the impact of its own capital, UNCDF seeks to position itself as a preferred partner for different stakeholders. UNCDF’s work is focused on three priority areas, including:

• SME Finance

• Sub-National Finance

• Digital Finance

Within UNCDF’s thematic are of nature, climate and energy financing, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) Sustainable Energy 2 program, a 5 year program funded by the Central African Forestry Initiative (CAFI) and Fonds National de REDD+ (FONAREDD DRC), aims to scale up clean energy solutions to reduce deforestation and emissions, through building a diversified investment portfolio across clean fuels, renewable electrification, and sustainable biomass.

To continue driving these objectives, UNCDF seeks to hire an Administration and Finance Analyst for the Sustainable Energy 2 Program. The Administration and Finance Analyst will support the Energy Investment Program Manager in the day-to-day operations, reporting and activities, to ensure that the program is efficiently executed against donor-committed timelines.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Administration and Finance Analyst will provide support in the effective financial management, administrative support, and compliance with UNCDF/UNDP rules and procedures. The incumbent will play a critical role in supporting program operations, managing budgets, overseeing procurement, and ensuring transparent and efficient use of resources.

Key Duties and Responsibilities:

Support to Project Planning and Management

- Assist in standardizing finance and accounting systems in accordance with UNDP and UNCDF procedures.

- Support preparation of annual work plans, budgets, budget revisions, procurement plans, and ensure proper system entry.

- Review budget revisions, financial plans, and ensure timely reporting and submission to relevant stakeholders.

Financial Management and Reporting

- Assist in monitoring project expenditure and cash flows to ensure compliance with approved budgets.

- Support quarterly Fund Authorization and Certification of Expenditures (FACE) reviews, cashbook and bank reconciliations.

- Prepare and maintain detailed financial records and reports, ensuring accuracy and completeness.

- Prepare and monitor budgets, financial forecasts, and expenditure reports.

- Ensure support in compliance with UNCDF/UNDP financial regulations and donor requirements.

- Support the consolidation of investee financial reports to inform annual financial reporting and plans, to the donor and to UNCDF.

Procurement and Contract Administration

- Support procurement processes, including preparation of requests for quotations/proposals and contract management in adherence to procurement policies and procedures.

- Maintain accurate records of procurement activities and vendor performance in line with UNCDF standards.

Administrative Support

- Oversee office operations, logistics, and asset management.

- Assist with events management, travel arrangements, and documentation and records management.

- Facilitate communication between project teams and partners.

Audit and Compliance

- Facilitate internal and external audits, ensuring timely submission of required documentation.

- Support the implementation of risk management and compliance measures.

Program Support and Coordination

- Support data collection for companies during due diligence process, when necessary.

- Provide administrative and financial input for program planning and reporting.

- Liaise with partners, government counterparts, and stakeholders on financial and administrative matters.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.
